News.title: UK Budget 2026 Live: Millions to get £100 off energy bills as minimum wage increased and rise in bank tax
News.content:
Chancellor John Healey is delivering his first Budget of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government after a raft of early announcements including changes to the planned cash ISA allowance cut and gas bill standing charges

UK Budget 2026 Live: Millions to get £100 off energy bills as minimum wage increased and rise in bank tax

Chancellor John Healey has promised a "budget for the working people of Britain" as he announced energy bills discounts, help for state pensioners on low incomes, bank tax hikes and fuel duty freezes.

He said it is a budget "for British businesses, big and small", built on "fiscal discipline". He warned of "global economic storms" with trade tensions and Putin's illegal invasion of Ukraine as he opened his Budget statement in the House of Commons.

Directly blaming rising energy costs on Donald Trump's war with Iran, the Chancellor says he's taking immediate action and extending the VAT cut on electricity bills until the summer next year. Also 20 million households in council bands A-D will get a £100 energy bills discount - a £2.6billion scheme to take pressure off as winter bites. An announcement that crashed the government's council band checker website.

The Chancellor also announced the fuel duty freeze will be extended until July and the national minimum wage and national living wage will increase by 3.9% for 2.3 million workers. Mr Healey said he was "looking to our banks to help fund breathing space for British families", and hiked taxes on banks by an extra 3% for 15 months from January.

Mr Healey said Britain will commit £10 billion of additional economic and military support to Ukraine, and half a billion in urgent military funding this winter and said he is “getting work under way” to reach spending of 3% of GDP on defence by 2030.

State pensioners on low incomes have come out as winners from today's Budget and will be protected from paying income tax.

Follow our live blog for the latest updates.

News.title: Budget 2026 winners and losers revealed from energy bill payers to state pensioners
News.content:
Budget 2026 winners and losers revealed from energy bill payers to state pensioners

The Mirror rounds up the winners and losers from the Budget - from billpayers to state pensioners, and all the things that were missed out today

View 4 Images We reveal the winners and losers from the Budget

John Healey promised “a Budget for the working people of Britain” with help for rising energy bills and a fuel duty freeze for drivers - but who are the winners and losers?

‌



‌



Low-paid workers were also handed a pay rise, though the tax-free personal allowance remains frozen - which means people get dragged into paying tax for the first time, or pushed into higher tax rates, when their wages go up.

‌



However, it was announced that state pensioners will be shielded from paying income tax as the state pension is set to rise above the personal allowance for the first time next year.

‌



Stay up to date with everything announced in our Budget 2026 live coverage.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images The Budget announced help with energy bills and new schemes for first-time buyers (Image: Getty)

‌



Council tax band checker website crashes after Chancellor says millions will get £100 energy bill discount in Budget READ MORE :

WINNERS

Pensioners

Low income state pensioners will be protected from paying income tax, with their personal allowance set to match the full state pension. The state pension is set to rise to £13,036 a year from next April, in line with the triple lock. This means it will be above the £12,570 tax-free personal allowance. By increasing the personal allowance for state pensioners, it means anyone who only claims the state pension and no other sources of income will not have to pay tax. But those that have a private pension or a higher state pension - for example, through additional payments or if you deferred your state pension claim - will still be hit with a tax bill.

‌



Low-paid workers

The minimum wage will increase by 3.9% for 2.3 million workers. The minimum wage for workers aged 21 and over is currently £12.71 an hour and this will rise to around £13.20, while the rate for workers aged ‌18 to 20 will go up from £10.85 an hour to around £11.27. However, as the tax thresholds remain frozen, it means more of your income risks getting pushed into a higher tax bracket, depending on how much you earn.

‌



Energy bill payers

A new £100 payment has been announced for 20 million households living in council tax band A to D properties, to help with rising energy bills. This money will be paid into people's bank accounts. The government has also announced new measures to cut energy bills today. It was confirmed that standing charges on gas bills are being axed, in a move that is expected to save 60% of households an average of £45 off their annual bill. But the cost will be shifted to the unit rates, which means high-usage households could end up paying more. The changes will be introduced from January 2027. It comes after the Prime Minister removed VAT on electricity bills this month, though the saving was swallowed up by higher wholesale costs. The VAT cut had been due to end in March 2027, but this has now been extended until July 2031.

‌



View 4 Images John Healey with his ministerial team before the Budget (Image: Simon Walker / HM Treasury)

Drivers

‌



Drivers have seen the price of petrol and diesel soar since the start of the Iran war, with diesel hitting £2 per litre last month. In response to this, fuel duty has been frozen for a 16th year running. Fuel duty is a tax on petrol, diesel, biodiesel and bioethanol and is included in the price you pay for every litre of fuel you buy. It had been due to rise by 3p in January, then by another 2p in March - reversing a 5p cut that had been in place in 2022. The 5p will now not be reversed until July 2027. The headline fuel duty rate is 52.95p per litre.

Savers

‌



The planned cut to the cash ISA allowance from £20,000 a year to £12,000 has been axed, in a boost for savers. The cut had been due to happen next April for savers under the age of 65. The cutting of the cash ISA allowance was announced in the 2025 Budget by then-Chancellor Rachel Reeves, with government hoping that it would encourage younger savers to invest in the stock market instead. However, in not-so good news for savers, the tax on income from savings will rise to 24% for basic rate taxpayers from April 2027. It had been scheduled to rise to 22%. The savings higher rate will be 44%, and the savings additional rate will be 49%.

First-time buyers

‌



A new first-time buyer scheme called Your First Home scheme will help people get on the property ladder with a deposit of just 2.5%. The Government would then provide a loan worth 20% of the property value to help pay for the purchase. This equity loan will initially be interest-free. However, critics have warned of the risk of buyers falling into negative equity - when the amount of money you owe on your mortgage is greater than the current market value of your house - if the value of the property falls. The Lifetime ISA penalty is also being reduced from 25% to 20%. This means you will get back roughly what you have saved, plus interest, though not your bonus, instead of part of your original savings being wiped out. The Lifetime ISA allows you to save £4,000 a year and you get a £1,000 bonus from the government - but the money has to be used for your first home or retirement. There is also a new First Time Buyer ISA planned, which is replacing the Lifetime ISA. The bonus with the First Time Buyer ISA will only be paid out on completion of a property and this ISA cannot be used for your retirement.

Small businesses

‌



The threshold for small business rate relief for retail hospitality and leisure businesses will be increased from £12,000 ⁠to £18,000. The the shift takes an estimated 70,000 additional businesses completely out of paying business rates. In order to qualify for this relief, your business must occupy primarily one property.

View 4 Images Energy bill has been announced (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

‌



LOSERS

Taxpayers

The tax thresholds remain frozen, which mean as your salary increases, a larger portion of your income gets pushed into higher tax bands. This is something which is known as fiscal drag. The personal allowance - which is how much most people can earn before they start to pay income tax - is £12,570. It is currently set to be frozen at this level until 2031. You pay 20% tax on earnings between £12,570 and £50,270, then 40% on earnings between £50,270 and £125,140 and 45% on earnings over £125,140.

‌



Smokers and vapers

Vape shops will be excluded from business rates relief starting from April 2027. This means shops may have to increase prices to absorb the extra costs. As of this month, all vaping products are now subject to a new Vaping Products Duty. This change saw a flat rate tax of 22p per millilitre added onto vaping liquid, costing someone who buys a 10ml bottle of e-liquid an extra £2.20 in duty. Cigarettes also went up this month, in line with RPI inflation plus an additional 2 percentage points. Tobacco duty is normally increased at the Budget, but it was moved forward in line with the vape tax.

‌



Drinkers

The government will increase alcohol duty rates in line with RPI from next February. We don’t know for sure what month’s data for RPI will be used, but in the last three years, the tax on a bottle of wine has gone up by £1.32 and tax on a bottle of gin has increased by £1.65. However, the Chancellor also announced £10million in alcohol duty relief for around 2,000 small brewers and cider makers.

‌



Gamblers

An increase in taxes on gambling companies was announced, which will impact companies such as Ladbrokes and William Hill. The Chancellor announced he will increase Machine Games Duty, a tax on the net takings from some slot machines, to 25% from 20%.

Article continues below

Landlords

The tax landlords pay on profits from renting out homes will rise from next April. The basic rate will be 24%, the higher rate will be 44%, and the additional rate will be 49%.

News.title: Kevin Keegan to be given highest honour for the first time in Newcastle's history
News.content:
Kevin Keegan to be given highest honour for the first time in Newcastle's history

Newcastle City Council said it would "serve as a lasting tribute to a man who meant so much to the city" following the death of football legend Kevin Keegan in July

View 3 Images Kevin Keegan in his heyday at Newcastle United in 1999 (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Football legend Kevin Keegan will become the first person in history to be posthumously awarded the Freedom of Newcastle, the city's highest honour.

‌



‌



Newcastle City Council said it would "serve as a lasting tribute to a man who meant so much to the city. King Kev's legacy will 'continue to inspire people for many years to come,' civic chiefs said.

‌



The local authority confirmed Keegan had been due to be given the Freedom of the City earlier this year. It was not formally agreed upon, though, before he died in July after being diagnosed with cancer.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images Keegan managed his beloved Newcastle United in 2008 (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Goal King Kane crowned the best in the world and could now be set for a knighthood READ MORE :

Alan Shearer makes special trip to thank charity fundraisers READ MORE :

Council leader Colin Ferguson said: "We were all deeply saddened to learn of Kevin Keegan's death in July. You could see from the enormous amount of tributes left outside St James' Park what he meant to the city and the footballing world.

‌



"The stories shared about Kevin and the impact he made have been inspiring, showing just how much he was loved not only by our city, but across the world."

As a player, Keegan, who won the Ballon d'Or awards after being voted the world's best player in 1978 and 1979, scored 48 goals in 78 games after joining Newcastle in 1982 and helped secure promotion back to the First Division.

‌



Recipients of the honorary award have their name inscribed in the wall of the Banqueting Hall at the Civic Centre.

It is different to being a hereditary Freeman of Newcastle, a centuries-old group who swear an oath to defend the city and have traditionally had special rights and duties — including the right to graze cattle on the Town Moor.

‌



Newcastle lord mayor Henry Gallagher, a Magpies season ticket holder, said: "Kevin has a lasting legacy for the whole of the city, not just for the football club. "Looking at all the comments people have made about him, they all say the same thing — that Kevin always had time for people.

View 3 Images Tribute to the Newcastle United icon before the club's opening game of the season against Liverpool (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Article continues below

"He would always stop and chat, and make sure that everybody had a chance to talk to him. He brought such joy to our city. When he came here it was like we were taken notice of again and it was brilliant." Newcastle United CEO David Hopkinson added: "Kevin Keegan will always be, quite simply, one of the most important, influential and beloved figures in the history of Newcastle United. "His impact on our club, our city and generations of supporters is immeasurable. As both a player and manager, he helped shape some of the most memorable chapters in our history and created a bond with Newcastle that leaves a true legacy. "The proposal to make Kevin an Honorary Freeman of Newcastle, the highest civic honour, is a fitting recognition for one of the city's greatest icons."

News.title: Fiancé issues desperate plea for his wife-to-be who vanished without a trace
News.content:
Fiancé issues desperate plea for his wife-to-be who vanished without a trace

Vitoria Figueiredo Barreto, 31, has not been seen for eight months after CCTV captured a person believed to be her entering a boatyard, with her fiancé Janilson now making a fresh plea for help

View 3 Images Vitoria has been missing for eight months (Image: Police)

The heartbroken fiancé of a psychologist who disappeared without a trace eight months ago has today issued a desperate plea for information about her whereabouts.

‌



‌



Vitoria Figueiredo Barreto, 31, was last seen entering a boatyard in Brightlingsea, Essex, eight months ago. She was staying in nearby Southend-on-Sea but disappeared after visiting a friend at the University of Essex.

‌



Now, her fiancé Janilson Gomes Da Silveira Filho is urging police, the Government and local communities not to give up the search for the missing psychologist.

‌



He said: “As far as we know, there has been no sign of life from Vitoria since March and equally no indication that Vitoria wished to ‘start a new life,’ that all is well and that she is no longer needing help.

"Similarly, no body has been found — Vitoria is still missing. A young, vibrant psychologist, a daughter, a sister, a friend and a fiancée."

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



View 3 Images Vitoria was captured on CCTV (Image: PA)

Missing capybara Samba caught on camera more than six months after escape from Marwell Zoo READ MORE :

Janilson also appealed directly to people living in the area to report anything that could help establish what happened to Vitoria.

‌



He added: “I ask the habitants of these areas, if you see a woman unfamiliar to the region, an unknown woman, please pass all information to Essex Police. Please speak to others in your community so you can help us during this difficult time.

“Vitoria may be experiencing memory loss at the moment, she may be confused or unsure of where she is and in need of help. So we ask you as a community to please help us, she may be being held hostage somewhere and in need of help. I am asking the communities of Brightlingsea and Bradwell to please help us during this time — just as you helped us at the beginning.”

‌



Vitoria visited a friend at the University of Essex on March 3 before boarding the number 87 bus from Boundary Road in Wivenhoe shortly after 1pm. CCTV showed her getting off around half an hour later in Bellfield Avenue, Brightlingsea, before she was seen in the Hurst Green area at around 2.30pm.

View 3 Images Police believe a fishing boat was unmoored shortly after Vitoria was last seen (Image: PA)

‌



She was wearing a dark coat, blue turtleneck jumper, light-blue jeans and black trainers with light-coloured soles. She was also carrying a white shoulder bag marked ‘People over profit’.

Vitoria was later captured on CCTV at 12.16am on March 4, when a person believed to be her was seen jumping over a fence into a boatyard. Police believe a fishing boat was unmoored from a pontoon around 20 minutes later, although officers have previously said there was no clear footage conclusively showing Vitoria taking the vessel.

‌



The boat was later found drifting out of the harbour before coming to rest near Bradwell-on-Sea, Essex, at around midday. Five days later, Vitoria’s white shoulder bag was discovered near Copperas Road in Brightlingsea. Her laptop was then recovered in the town on March 14.

Police have carried out extensive searches since Vitoria disappeared and have urged residents in both Bradwell and Brightlingsea to check sheds, garages and outbuildings for anything which could help the investigation.

‌



Detective Superintendent Anna Granger previously said: “We would ask residents, particularly in Bradwell but indeed also Brightlingsea, to check sheds, garages and outbuildings on their properties. Even the smallest piece of information could be important.

“If you believe you saw Vitoria or have information that you have not yet shared with us, please come forward."

Article continues below

She added: “At the heart of all of this work is Vitoria and her loved ones. This continues to be a distressing time for her family and friends, and they remain at the forefront of our thoughts.

“Although significant work has already taken place, the passage of time does not lessen the importance of new information coming forward.”

News.title: Tommy Robinson found guilty of harassing two journalists telling them "I'm coming to get you"
News.content:
Tommy Robinson found guilty of harassing two journalists telling them "I'm coming to get you"

Tommy Robinson has been found guilty of harassing two Daily Mail journalists after a trial at Southwark Crown Court

Tommy Robinson found guilty of harassment at Southwark Crown Court

Far-right activist Tommy Robinson has been convicted of harassing two Daily Mail journalists and causing them to fear violence.

‌



‌



The 43-year-old, who told his trial his full name is Stephen Lennon, was labelled a “bully” by prosecutors after freelance reporter working for the title and a Daily Mail editor were forced to either leave their homes or employ extra security for fear of a “vigilante” attack.

‌



Jurors at Southwark Crown Court took 11 hours and 25 minutes to find Robinson guilty by a majority of 10 jurors to two of both charges of harassment causing fear of violence.

‌



His trial heard how the anti-migrant activist “retaliated” after the Daily Mail and its sister publication the MailOnline published a story about him “stoking riots from his sunbed” during unrest in the UK in August 2024 following the murders of three girls in Southport.

Robinson made a series of posts on social media about the unfolding situation while on holiday in Cyprus, prompting the newspaper to send the freelance journalist and a photographer to the island.

After the MailOnline published its story about him, Robinson posted criticisms on his X account of both journalists because of their involvement in the article. Robinson went on to hire private investigators to find the home addresses of his victims, as well as the editor-in-chief of the Daily Mail.

‌



View 2 Images A majority verdict was allowed in the trial of Tommy Robinson, with jurors reaching a 10-2 verdict of guilty (Image: Jeff Moore/Press Association)

The jury panel accepted the prosecution’s case that the decision to hire detectives was designed to “intimidate” his victims, with photographs of one journalist outside his home and cropped images of the other journalist's family posted online by Robinson.

‌



As well as social media posts and direct messages the defendant also became “increasingly menacing” on a telephone call with the freelance journalist on August 5, 2024 – telling the freelance journalist: “I’m coming to get you.”

Jurors rejected claims from the activist that the Daily Mail had put his family in danger by publishing the story, with the defendant weeping in the witness box on Thursday as he spoke about the relationship he had with his children.

‌



View 2 Images Tommy Robinson had sobbed in court while discussing his family earlier in the trial (Image: Elizabeth Cook/Press Association)

Prosecutor Ben Holt previously told the court the freelance journalist was given a close protection officer by the Daily Mail after photographs of his wife and children were posted on Robinson’s X account.

‌



The editor involved in the case had to move house because of the harassment. A third journalist, a Daily Mail correspondent, also felt the need to leave his family home after becoming concerned with the publicity surrounding his colleagues.

Police were provided with a of a voicemail sent from Robinson, who told a journalist: “I’ve already located every f****** one of you.”

Article continues below

The activist posted on X before the trial began to thank Tesla owner Elon Musk for funding his legal fees. He was granted bail ahead of his sentencing on December 16.

News.title: Martin Lewis gives State Pension £94 'you will not need to claim' update
News.content:
Martin Lewis gives State Pension £94 'you will not need to claim' update

Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey made the announcement in the Budget

View 2 Images Martin Lewis has discussed the changes to the State Pension tax allowance (Image: ITV)

Martin Lewis has explained how the new State Pension tax allowance system will work, following changes announced in the Budget. Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey confirmed in the Budget today (October 28) that there would be a new pension tax allowance.

‌



‌



It means that pensioners with income up to the value of the full new state pension will not pay income tax on it. There had been fears that pensioners collecting the full new State Pension would exceed the tax-free personal allowance of £12,570 for the 2026/27 tax year.

‌



That would be caused by the 3.9 per cent rise predicted next April thanks to the triple lock, which works by making sure that the state pension goes up by inflation, wages or by 2.5% - whichever is highest.

‌



Former Chancellor Rachel Reeves promised that pensioners earning slightly more than the personal allowance from their State Pension alone would not be chased by the Government for tax. Mr Healey has now changed the State Pension tax allowance, saying: “For pensioners, I am delivering the new pension tax allowance – so that pensioners with income up to the value of the full new state pension will not pay income tax in this Parliament."

How will it work?

Content cannot be displayed without consent

According to money-saving expert Mr Lewis: "From April 2027, if your total annual income is not more than full new State Pension (£13,037/yr) you will not pay tax. So this is £94 extra tax free. If your total income is slightly higher then for every £3 you earn above, you lose £1 of this extra allowance.

‌



"So if you earn £13,186 (£150 above) you would get a 'Pension Tax Allowance' meaning you pay £44ish less tax than otherwise (ie £94 minus £50) So by total income of £13,319 you won't receive any extra allowance. "

He also said that the changes will be applied automatically by His Majesty's Revenue and Customs (HMRC), so people do not need to fill anything in or apply for the new rate.

‌



"HMRC will automatically apply this allowance you will not need to claim it," he said.

The Government explains its changes in detail here.

‌



View 2 Images Prime Minister Andy Burnham is scrapping the triple lock as we know it (Image: WPA Pool, Getty Images)

In the future

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to end the triple lock in its current form from 2030 to help fund a new national care service.

‌



His plans would see the state pension increase every year at least by inflation or 2.5% - but remove the automatic annual link with average earnings.

The triple lock has long proved controversial, with many saying it favours pensioners and is unaffordable. It is forecast to be three times higher by the end of the decade than its original estimate, according to the Office for Budget Responsibility.

Article continues below

Prior to Mr Burnham's announcement of scrapping it, the annual cost of the triple lock policy is estimated to reach £15.5bn by 2030.

News.title: Prince Harry 'mindful' of King’s Caribbean tour and 'doesn’t set out' to overshadow royals
News.content:
Prince Harry 'mindful' of King’s Caribbean tour and 'doesn’t set out' to overshadow royals

It is understood that Prince Harry and Meghan Markle do not have any public engagements planned in the coming weeks while the King is on a delicate trip to the Caribbean

Harry and Meghan continue to row about how they want to be titled

Prince Harry is mindful of not distracting from the King’s Caribbean tour and does not set out to overshadow his royal relatives, it is claimed.

‌



‌



King Charles landed in The Bahamas yesterday for a nine-day tour of the region, which will also see him visit Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda. Harry’s father began the trip last night by acknowledging the “great suffering of the past” and confirmed Commonwealth leaders will discuss the legacy of slavery at a major summit next week, which he will open.

‌



But campaigners have argued this "falls far short of what justice requires" and have put pressure on the monarch to take further action during the trip. Traditionally, royals are careful not to undertake high-profile visits or appearances that would overshadow another's work, especially state visits carried out by the King.

‌



King Charles flies into Caribbean storm as minister calls slavery reparations 'unreasonable' READ MORE :

View 3 Images Prince Harry and Meghan in Nottingham earlier this month (Image: WireImage)

Yet, earlier this month, Harry and Meghan made their first joint public appearance together since moving back to the UK in Nottingham, in what resembled a royal engagement on the same day that the King and Queen opened the Welsh Parliament.

While last week, an interview with Harry by GQ magazine, where he issued a plea for reconciliation with his father, brother and Prince William, was published while the rest of the royals hosted the Sultan of Oman in a state visit at Windsor Castle — although the Sussex team say the timing was down to the magazine.

‌



However, it is understood that while Charles is in the Caribbean, the Sussexes do not have any public appearances lined up and are spending time with their children Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet during the half-term holidays. It is believed they do have one more public event together planned before the end of the year.

A source close to the couple told The Times: “Harry doesn't set out with an intention to try to pull focus or draw attention away from what his father is doing or what his brother is doing.

‌



View 3 Images The King at a youth rally in The Bahamas - hours after landing in the country to start a tour of the Caribbean (Image: Victoria Jones/Shutterstock)

"That's never his intention at all, but obviously for him to be able to mitigate against that he does need to have decent foresight of what's coming up."

‌



The insider claimed that the Sussexes aren’t always informed in advance of events and are unable to withdraw from commitments so they do not disappoint charities.

They added: “He can only mitigate against clashes if information is shared with him in advance. Some information is shared, but not all information is and that's fine."

‌



It comes weeks after the King made it clear the Sussexes will remain private citizens and are "on their own" despite their bombshell move back to the UK in the summer. In a firm letter issued on behalf of Charles, it stated that the Sussexes' should not use their HRH styles, which are still in abeyance, and that they "do not represent the sovereign" while out making public appearances.

View 3 Images Sources say Harry does not set out to overshadow his father or brother (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The guidance was sent under the King's instruction by his most senior official, the Lord Chamberlain, to offer clarity over Harry and Meghan's royal status after requests for guidance. It was issued to those in government, the military and lord lieutenants up and down the country.

The duke and duchess were said to be “surprised” by the formal letter and the couple, who are waiting to hear whether they will be given taxpayer-funded security, were said to prefer the term “public figures” instead.

‌



Meanwhile, today in the Bahamas, the King will sit down for talks with the prime minister and governor general during a busy second day of his royal tour.

Charles will hold an audience with the Caribbean nation’s premier Philip Davis and meet separately with Dame Cynthia Pratt, his official representative in the country.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

His visit comes in the wake of renewed calls from Caribbean nations for Britain to apologise for its role in selling enslaved people for profit and for reparations.

‌



During his day in the capital Nassau, the King will meet the families of four Royal Bahamas Defence Force (RBDF) Marines killed when Cuban MiG fighter aircraft sunk HMBS Flamingo in May 1980, after a dispute over illegal fishing. He will lay a wreath at the Flamingo monument erected at the RBDF headquarters.

Charles will end his day at a garden reception at Government House, where he will meet Bahamians who have made significant contributions to

News.title: All the key things in John Healey's Budget - from £100 payment to gas bills and bank tax
News.content:
All the key things in John Healey's Budget - from £100 payment to gas bills and bank tax

John Healey told MPs he was delivering a 'budget for the working people of Britain' - with a raft of measures including council tax relief, scrapping standing charges on gas bills and new charges for banks

The Budget: John Healey promises "budget for the working people of Britain"

John Healey has unveiled a raft of measures in his first Budget - including £100 payments for millions of Brits to help with energy bills.

‌



‌



The Chancellor also confirmed standing charges on gas bills will be abolished, and announced banks would be hit with higher taxes to help tackle the cost-of-living crisis.

‌



He also scrapped Rachel Reeves' proposed change to cash ISAs and announced fuel duty would not be going up.

‌



The Chancellor told MPs: "This is a budget for the working people of Britain. For British businesses, big and small, delivered at a time when global uncertainties and pressures are swirling worldwide and hitting people here at home."

Stay up to date with everything announced in our Budget 2026 live coverage.

Liz Truss schooled on live TV as she denies blame for mini-Budget catastrophe READ MORE :

View 4 Images Chancellor John Healey with his Treasury team ahead of the crucial Budget speech (Image: Simon Walker / HM Treasury)

‌



£100 Household Energy Payment relief

The Chancellor announced millions of households will get £100 to help with their energy bills - paid directly into their bank accounts.

Mr Healey said the payment would affect people in council tax bands A to D. The payments will be delivered through the council tax system, the Treasury said.

‌



He told the Commons: "Let me say this to families at home: I know that with the conflict in the Middle East, rising energy bills are a real worry.

"I know that people look to government at times like this, not to solve all their problems, but to give them a bit of breathing space. So today, I'm taking one further step.

‌



"This winter, for 20 million households in council tax bands A to D, I'm announcing a £100 energy payment for households, paid directly into people's bank accounts to deal with rising energy bills.

"That's a £2.6 billion scheme to take the pressure off in the coldest months and see people through to the spring."

‌



He confirmed that the Scottish, Welsh, and Northern Ireland governments would receive their share to give all nations "breathing space on their energy bills this winter".

‌



Standing charges on gas bills

"Unfair" standing charges have been removed from gas bills in today's Budget - in a move set to save millions of British families money.

Mr Healey unveiled the measure in his first economic statement to the country this afternoon, branding the charge outdated and unfair. Mr Healey will order Ofgem to ensure the charges are removed next year - or as soon as possible after. It is expected to save the average family around £45 a year.

‌



Mr Burnham said: "Abolishing gas standing charges is about basic fairness and giving people more control over their bills. I am determined to reform our broken energy market, so it better serves the public interest.”

VAT cut on electricity bills extended

Mr Healey confirmed that the VAT cut on electricity bills, announced in the first weeks of Andy Burnham's premiership, will be extended.

‌



It will now be in place through the winter and until July next year. He told the Commons: "In the first week of this new government, we took VAT off electricity for 29 million households. Today, I am extending that VAT cut through the winter and spring to July, taking £50 off the annual price cap."

Minimum wage

A key step announced in the Budget will be an increase in the national minimum wage and national living wage.

‌



These are going up by 3.9%, the Chancellor said. He told the Commons: "For 2.3 million of our lowest-paid workers, I'm increasing both the National Minimum Wage and the National Living Wage by 3.9%."

On April 1 next year, the National Living Wage will increase by 3.9% to £13.21 per hour - equivalent to an increase of £910 for a full-time worker. The National Minimum Wage for 18- to 20-year-olds will also increase by 3.9% to £11.27 per hour.

‌



Gambling tax hike to pay for high street boost

Chancellor John Healey said he will hike gambling taxes to pay for a high street support package.

This will include increasing machine games duty from 20% to 25% for higher stakes machines. But he confirmed there will be carve-outs for pubs and seaside arcades.

‌



He said it would support growth on high streets across the UK - more on that below. He said: "To pay for this support for our high streets, I'm raising taxes on gambling, by increasing Machine Games Duty from 20% to 25% for higher-stakes machines, whilst protecting pubs and seaside arcades."

Cash free ISA change scrapped

Mr Healey announced he will reverse Rachel Reeves's planned cut to the cash ISA allowance.

‌



The cash ISA allowance is currently set at £20,000 a year but had been due to be slashed to £12,000 from next April for under-65s.

The cutting of the cash ISA allowance was announced in the 2025 Budget - with the government hoping that it will encourage younger savers to invest in the stock market instead.

‌



He continued: "88% of people will pay no more tax on their savings, and I am taking a new approach today to encourage people on ordinary incomes to save and to invest. I will not go ahead with the cut to the tax-free amount that people can put into a cash ISA. The limit will stay at £20,000 per year, tax-free, for people of all ages and to make investment accessible.

"I will work with the sector to create a new `Starter ISA' to reward first-time investors."

‌



View 4 Images Rachel Reeves' cash ISA shake-up has been scrapped (Image: House of Commons/AFP via Getty I)

New bank tax to give families 'breathing space'

The Chancellor announced the surcharge on bank profits will rise.

‌



This will go up from 3% to 6% for 15 months. Mr Healey said the money would be used to boost Britain's high street.

Mr Healey told the Commons: "I want to say directly to our banks: I celebrate and I am grateful for the role that you play. And amid the global economic storms, I am looking to our banks to help fund breathing space for British families. And so banks will pay an extra 3% on the bank surcharge. This will be time-limited to pay for immediate support on energy bills, starting in January, ending 15 months later.

‌



"I've made my choice at this budget: asking a bit more of our banks to support ordinary people, raising taxes on gambling to support good growth on every high street."

End of Lifetime ISA penalty for home buyers

Mr Healey has promised to end the Lifetime ISA penalty for those buying houses that cost more than £450,000.

‌



He said: "I'm announcing that a new First Time Buyer ISA will replace the Lifetime ISA, and from today, I am dealing with the LIsa penalty. So if the home you want costs more than the limit, you will get back at least what you put in.

"And I'm going further: from next Spring, a new scheme for first time buyers who don't have the bank of mum and dad behind them.

‌



"Your First Home - an equity loan scheme, which I'm funding today with £4.7billion of government-backed lending."

Fuel duty increase scrapped

The planned increase in fuel duty has been scrapped to help motorists with the cost of living.

‌



Mr Healey said the 5p cut to fuel duty, which was due to end on December 31, would be extended until July 2027. The cut was introduced by the Tories in spring 2022 to freeze fuel duty at 52.95p per litre for both petrol and diesel.

The Chancellor told MPs: "With the war in the Middle East still driving high fuel prices, I am extending these tax cuts for motorists through the winter and spring to July, supporting households, hauliers, and farmers.

‌



"And for anyone who relies on their car for their work, from care workers to engineers, I am increasing the higher mileage rate from 25p to 35p per mile, and making permanent the increase to the standard mileage rate introduced earlier this year."

View 4 Images There was good news for motorists in John Healey's Budget (Image: ANP/Shutterstock)

‌



Hydrogen levy to be removed from household bills

The Government will directly fund hydrogen projects - with the controversial Gas Shipper Obligation scrapped.

Mr Healey told the Commons: "For many years, under Conservative governments, policy costs were loaded on to household bills through levies.

‌



"Today, I am putting an end to that, we will introduce a new cost control framework to drive down all aspects of energy bills and I will scrap the upcoming Gas Shipper Obligation - a levy to fund hydrogen projects - and instead back those projects directly from government."

Thousands of firms taken out of business rates

Some 70,000 more businesses will be taken out of business rates altogether - in a huge boost to small businesses.

‌



Mr Healey said: "In the first week of this government, we cut 20% off business rates for pubs, clubs, and music venues from April next year.

"But I've heard calls from members across this House, and a call from one member in particular, the Right Honourable member for Macclesfield (Andy Burnham), and so I'm increasing the threshold for small business rate relief for retail, hospitality, and leisure businesses from £12,000 to £18,000. That means 70,000 more businesses, I'm not just cutting their rates, I'm taking them out of paying business rates altogether.

‌



"That means half of our shops, restaurants, and gyms pay no business rates at all. And for all other businesses in these sectors, I will freeze their rates in real terms, so that none face an above-inflation rise for the next two years."

View 4 Images The government has announced a raft of cost-of-living measures (Image: Getty )

‌



Measures to tackle homelessness

At the weekend Mr Burnham announced funding behind his pledge to offer every rough sleeper a bed this Christmas will be doubled at the Budget.

No10 said cash to be unveiled at Wednesday's Budget will commit a further £432million to tackle rough sleeping - boosting total funding to £874m. It said the funding would help deliver the ambition to offer people a route off the street before Christmas while sustaining support for years to come.

‌



Mr Burnham, who outlined his mission to end rough sleeping during his first speech as PM outside No10, said: "Rough sleeping isn't a fact of life. It's a thing governments either choose to accept or don't. Well I don't accept it. That's why we're doubling funding so that people aren't just offered a safe route off the streets this winter but have that same support right through the rest of this Parliament too."

Cliff-edge rule for carers scrapped

Mr Healey has announced he is getting rid of a controversial rule that led to unpaid carers being punished with penalties.

‌



The Chancellor said he is scrapping a cliff-edge rule meaning that if a carer earns more than £204 a week, they forfeit their entire week’s carer’s allowance payment. This currently stands at £86.45 a week.

Boost for council housing

The Chancellor confirmed an extra £1.5 billion for the government's Social and Affordable Housing Programme to build more council housing.

‌



The government also plans to help more councils borrow for ­housebuilding by extending preferential rates.

Mr Healey said: "The Conservatives sold off our council houses - Labour is now building them back."

‌



More support for Ukraine

Britain will commit £10billion of additional economic and military support to Ukraine, and half a billion in urgent military funding this winter, Mr Healey announced.

The Chancellor told the Commons: "The week in Kyiv started with Russia launching another brutal ballistic missile attack on the city. And this morning, the Prime Minister and I called President Zelensky to tell him about our commitments in the Budget today.

‌



"He told us `you've made my day', £10 billion of additional economic and military support - based on loans, export finance guarantees, and half a billion in urgent military funding for this winter."

New rules for data centres

Mr Healey announced a new set of rules for data centres.

‌



He said: "It is based on sovereignty - with our first-of-its-kind sovereign AI unit protecting UK interests by channelling Government investment into strategic British AI firms, backed with another £140 million today.

"To ensure our most sensitive data stays under British control, I am setting out a new deal for datacentres in the UK. When the NHS uses AI to treat patients, we want that data here. When our armed forces use AI to keep us safe, we want that data here. So here's the deal.

Article continues below

"I am today launching a new British data centre covenant with strict tests that data centres must meet - to invest in local communities, create local jobs and protect local water supplies. In return, critical data centres will get the grid connections they need, and, where necessary, be allowed to build onsite generation while they wait."

News.title: Key points at a glance
News.content:
Chancellor John Healey has set out the government's tax and spending plans in his Budget â the first since Andy Burnham became prime minister.

Here is a summary of the main points.

LIVE: Follow all the Budget coverage

News.title: How the Budget affects you
News.content:
If you are living in a home in council tax bands A to D in England, you will receive a one-off Â£100 "Household Energy Payment" from January, funded by extra tax on banks.

It will be paid directly into your bank account.

You can find your council tax band by looking on your annual bill, or by looking on the government's website, external - although that was struggling to cope with traffic after the announcement.

Administrations in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive the equivalent funding, and they will decide whether to introduce the same payment.

This is designed to help with soaring energy bills, with a typical annual bill expected to be Â£2,000 or more in January, although you can spend the money on anything you wish.

News.title: Chancellor takes to the despatch box for his first Budget
News.content:
Chancellor John Healey began his speech by calling his first Budget one for the "working people of Britain, for British businesses big and small".

The Budget is built on "fiscal discipline" and will give Britain some "breathing space", the chancellor said in Parliament on Wednesday.

Follow the delivery of the Budget live.

News.title: Overturned carriages and makeshift medical tents at crash site
News.content:
Dozens of people are feared dead after a Spanish high-speed train collided with another train south of capital Madrid.

More than 500 passengers were travelling on the trains involved, and an initial death toll of 10 "will almost certainly rise", a spokesperson for the regional government said.

Spain's Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez says he is "shocked by the serious train accident" and is in constant contact with the transport minister

Rail operator Adif says the incident occurred between a Renfe train and another of the Iryo company, which covers the Madrid to Seville route.

Follow this story live.

News.title: What we know about the crash so far
News.content:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez said he was "shocked by the serious train accident in Toledo".

"I remain in constant contact with the Minister of Transport, and with the president of Castilla-La Mancha," SÃ¡nchez said on X, adding that emergency services were working on the ground "to assist those affected and ensure their safety, in coordination with all the involved administrations".

"My affection, solidarity, and support to all the victims and their families."

SÃ¡nchez and other Spanish politicians have cancelled all public engagements on Wednesday, including campaigning for next month's parliamentary elections.

Spain's royal family posted on X that it was "shocked and concerned" by the accident and expressed condolences for the relatives of the deceased and those affected by the crash.

A spokesperson for the EU said the bloc was ready to help Spain if needed.

A huge emergency response is under way with fire crews and helicopters at the scene.

Spanish news agency have reported that hospitals in the area have suspended planned surgeries as they deal with an influx of patients from the crash.

A blood transfusion centre in Madrid has also appealed for "urgent" donations. In a post on X, Centro de TransfusiÃ³n said it made the request "in the face of a possible sudden increase in care needs".

It reported that facilities in Toledo, Ciudad Real and AlcÃ¡zar de San Juan have cancelled procedures as casualties from the crash begin to arrive.

This is the second high-speed rail tragedy in Spain this year.

In January a high-speed train derailed in southern Spain, its rear carriages going into the path of a state-run Renfe train, claiming the lives of 46 people.

News.title: Russell Brand tells court allegations made friends and colleagues turn against him
News.content:
The actor and comedian was standing tall in the witness box with his hands clasped behind his back. He was wearing a dark navy suit with his curly hair resting on his shoulders.

Brand also claimed in court that he was told he could not stay with his son at Great Ormond Street hospital in London when the child was having open heart surgery, following the documentary and a newspaper investigation.

He told the court: "Due to material that had been published in the public eye they had to bar my attendance and presence.

"They were unclear about what legal reason there was but that was the reason they gave to my wife Laura and I."

Brand told the court: "My entire life has been consumed by these allegations," adding that he had "devoted myself to these matters".

Winter asked Brand if he recalled meeting the first complainant, who alleges he raped her at the Labour Party conference in Bournemouth in 1999.

Brand said yes, explaining that he found her "loquacious" and "interesting".

When asked if there was any truth in the allegations that he raped her, he said: "No."

Under cross examination, the prosecution suggested Brand "just didn't care whether she was interested in having sex with you or not". Brand rejected that, saying he did care "very much".

Asked whether he was sure he "didn't think no means yes", he replied: "I know what no means."

Brand was then asked about another woman, who alleges that the entertainer grabbed her breasts before dragging her into a toilet and raping her.

Brand said he recalled been invited to a party in London at a bar in 2004, and said a friend had introduced him to the complainant by saying "something like 'there's a bird here who really wants to meet you mate'."

When asked if he remembered what he said to her upon meeting, he told the court: "I would have said something like, 'You're really, really beautiful'."

The barrister asked whether he had grabbed her breasts. "Absolutely not," Brand replied.

When questioned if he would have behaved in the way that had been alleged, he said it would have amounted to "disgusting behaviour".

"I was increasingly focused on my promiscuity," he said. "That's not the way I would have behaved because it's not only criminal but vulgar."

Brand said he remembered going into the toilet with her but said "no" when asked if he had dragged or forced her there.

"Did your penis enter her mouth at all whilst in the cubicle?" Winter asked. "No," said Brand.

News.title: Tommy Robinson guilty of harassing two Daily Mail journalists
News.content:
Political activist Tommy Robinson has been convicted of harassing two Daily Mail journalists.

A jury at Southwark Crown Court found the 43-year-old, real name Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, guilty of two counts of harassment causing fear of violence.

The case concerned Robinson's response to Daily Mail and Mail Online articles from August 2024, showing him on holiday in Cyprus while riots took place in England following the Southport murders.

The court had heard how Robinson, from Bedfordshire, used "bully-boy, intimidatory tactics" to frighten reporters Andrew Young and Jacob Dirnhuber, forcing them to employ security or leave home.

Robinson had denied the charges, saying he had "panicked" and had been "scared" when the Daily Mail published a story accusing him of "stoking race riots from his sunbed".

He told the jury he felt the article had "endangered" his family by revealing they were staying in a hotel near Ayia Napa in Cyprus.

After the guilty verdicts, Frank Ferguson, the head of the Crown Prosecution Service's Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division, said Robinson had "weaponised social media and subjected two journalists to a campaign of harassment which caused them serious fear of violence".â

Robinson was granted bail ahead of his sentencing, scheduled for 16 Decemberâ.

Harassment causing fear of violence can carry a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison, or up to 14 years if the offence is racially or religiously aggravated.

News.title: Trump says US voter fraud is 'rampant' - evidence suggests it is extremely rare
News.content:
For years, Trump has made repeated unsubstantiated claims that postal voting leads to widespread fraud.

He has also encouraged Republicans to vote by mail in the midterms and has said he has cast his ballot by post in the past.

The president has been unsuccessful in his push for Congress to pass an act which would only allow people to vote by mail if they are disabled, ill, serving in the military, or travelling.

The majority of states allow, external people to vote by mail without having to provide a reason, and in the 2024 presidential election about 48 million people cast postal ballots.

Trump signed an executive order last year which directed the US Postal Service to only deliver ballots to voters on lists of citizens compiled by government agencies. It also sought to require states to use the same envelope style for postal votes.

However, the order was rejected by the US Supreme Court which called such changes so close to the midterm elections "arbitrary and capricious" - but said it could revisit the issue afterwards.

US states have different rules for verifying postal ballots, but every state matches certain voter information on the ballots against what they have on file to check they are eligible and most also conduct signature checks, external.

News.title: Legal bid to overturn Drumcree march ban fails
News.content:
An attempt to overturn the Northern Ireland secretary's decision to ban the Drumcree parade has failed.

The High Court in Belfast has ruled that Sir Chris Bryant's decision made on 9 October was lawful.

The judicial review was brought by a Portadown Orangeman against Sir Chris and the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) Chief Constable Jon Boutcher.

The secretary of state's intervention to stop the parade came after he received security advice from Boutcher.

A lawyer for the Orangeman told the court that an appeal of the judgment is "likely".

The Drumcree dispute led to a stand-off between Orangemen and nationalist residents of the Garvaghy Road in Portadown lasting almost two weeks.

Mr Justice Scoffield said: "The secretary of state's decision was lawful and within the margin of discretion properly afforded him, although it is highly regrettable that it was required in the circumstances which arose."

He said those who opposed the march should "take no particular joy in the outcome of this case".

The judge added that "the position which has now been reached has been brought about at very significant cost to the people of Northern Ireland - financially, through the diversion of police resources, and in terms of community relations".

"Depressingly, the threat of serious and widespread disorder has loomed large," he said.

He went on: "Significant concerns have now been expressed about respect for the rule of law in this jurisdiction.

"That includes among some elected representatives, by reason of their participation in the unnotified protest."

News.title: Terminally ill mum who can't talk, walk or dress herself refused Pip payment
News.content:
A terminally ill mum who has been given three years to live has been denied disability benefit despite being unable to eat, talk, dress or use the toilet independently.

Rachael Field, 56, from Rhondda Cynon Taf, who has tongue cancer, was first diagnosed six years ago.

She uses a feeding tube, has had her tongue and voice box removed, and had her windpipe reconstructed using chest tissue. Field also has mobility issues.

Earlier this year, she was denied Personal Independence Payment (Pip), to support people with disability-related extra costs.

The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) said it needed further evidence to complete the claim and was sorry for "any distress" to the family.

Field said she has had cancer four times in six years, and now cannot do anything for herself.

"I need help to wash, dress and use the bathroom. I can only walk a few steps with help. I cannot eat or drink, everything has to go through my feeding tube," she added.

News.title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position
News.content:
Andy Burnham has insisted there is "no confusion" over his position on the European Union, as he criticised the UK's current deal with the bloc.

The prime minister said it was his "responsibility" to improve the deal, which was ratified in 2020, at a summit in Brussels next month.

He denied he had shifted his stance since the Makerfield by-election when he promised not to "re-run" the Brexit debate. Earlier this week, he suggested he could call a referendum on the UK returning to EU freedom of movement, before No10 appeared to backtrack.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused him during Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday of failing to "respect" the 2016 Brexit vote.

Badenoch said Burnham had created confusion and asked if he wanted a referendum on rejoining the EU.

"There is no confusion at all," Burnham told MPs.

"The government has a collectively agreed position, which I have set out today.

"It is entirely consistent with everything that I've said, including in the by-election.

"The red lines in our manifesto, including on freedom of movement, will stay in place firmly for the whole of this Parliament."

Labour's 2024 election manifesto ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.

Freedom of movement allows EU citizens to travel, live, study and work in any member country.

It is a precondition of membership of the EU's single market, which enables goods, services and people to move freely between EU member states.

Badenoch accused Burnham of having "opened his mouth without engaging his brain" over freedom of movement during "the chancellor's big week" as the Budget is unveiled.

News.title: Bonfire Night policing in Scotland will be 'largest operation since Trump visit'
News.content:
Scotland's biggest police operation since the visit of President Donald Trump last year is to take place on Bonfire Night, in the face of a "unique" combination of safety concerns.

As many as 1,700 officers could be deployed on and around 5 November to deal with fireworks-related disorder, a European football match involving Celtic and potential protests in Glasgow.

Additional public order vehicles and drivers are being brought in from 18 English and Welsh police forces under mutual aid arrangements.

Police Scotland says the plan, titled Operation Amberlight, is intended to ensure the safety of the public and emergency services.

The force has already vowed that anyone caught up in disorder around Halloween and Bonfire Night will face "very real consequences".

This will be enforced through Fireworks Control Zones (FCZs), which ban the use of pyrotechnics in certain areas of Edinburgh and Glasgow from 30 October.

In recent years, emergency crews have been pelted with petrol bombs and missiles - though police said there were fewer instances of this last year.

News.title: Landline switchover could cut people off in emergency, minister warned
News.content:
Plans to switch off the UK's traditional landline phone network could leave people in remote areas unable to contact help in an emergency, MPs have warned.

Landline operators aim to complete the switch to an internet-based network instead of copper-wire cables by the end of January next year.

The government and operators say the move to digital landlines will offer a more reliable service.

But MPs representing remote areas of the UK urged security minister Dan Jarvis to ensure that scrapping the copper-wire network did not make their communities more vulnerable in a storm or other emergency.

Unlike digital services, the traditional landline network does not rely on mains electricity and continues to work in a power cut.

Labour MP Torcuil Crichton, who represents the Western Isles constituency of Na h-Eileanan an Iar, said: "Resilience is inbuilt in the islands but we have major problems with connectivity because of this move from analogue to digital phone lines."

He said that "when the power goes out people don't have the phone, they don't have the internet and often they don't have a mobile signal either".

Retail service providers have been giving back-up battery packs to vulnerable customers, which can keep landline phones operating for an hour or more.

But Crichton said this was "simply not adequate" and that mobile phone providers "simply don't have the means to maintain or keep their signal going during storms".

He urged the minister to get telecoms firms to "up their digital game" to protect places "on the edge where people are vulnerable, isolated from their neighbours, where the ambulance is an hour away and the storm is 70 miles an hour".

Similar concerns were raised by MPs from the West Country and the Lake District.

Markus Campbell-Savours, Labour MP for Penrith and Solway, said: "I ask the minister to imagine an elderly constituent living alone in an isolated Lake District valley where copper phone lines have been replaced by fibre.

"A storm takes out the power to their router in the night and by the time they wake, the modest battery back up has failed, as has the mobile mast, does the minister share my concerns that they would have no way to raise an alarm in an emergency and agree that we need a new technological solution to protect the elderly?"

News.title: Gas is cut over unpaid bills despite payments made
News.content:
Residents at a block of flats in north-west London have been left without heating or hot water due to historic unpaid bills of Â£600,000, despite monthly payments being made over several years.

About 126 homes have been affected since 23 October. In a letter to residents, the developer and buildings management said about Â£300,000 is owed to the gas provider and Â£300,000 to the electricity provider.

The building's management company, Rendall & Rittner, said: "We fully recognise the seriousness of the situation and the impact it is having on residents, particularly families and those who may be vulnerable."

The freeholder did not respond to a request for comment from BBC London.

Rendell & Ritter added: "Our immediate priority is to support residents and to work with the freeholder and energy supplier to have the gas supply reinstated as quickly as possible."

Rendall & Rittner took over management of the building in Dollis Hill in May this year.

Lucy Baxter, who moved in four years ago when the building was new, said: "I have a one-year-old, so it's very difficult.

"I haven't been able to give her a bath and our flat is on a lower ground floor, so it's much colder and we're really struggling.

"There are other disabled residents here, disabled children, elderly residents and lots of families. I'm very concerned."

She said tenants had received a warning letter from a debt collection agency about three weeks earlier but had since been "left in the dark" about the situation.

But management claimed residents had been kept informed since the outage began and that it intended to hold a residents' meeting in the near future.

News.title: Patient living in 'horrific pain' due to UK-wide drugs shortage
News.content:
A woman with multiple sclerosis (MS) has said she is living with "horrific pain" after being unable to get a drug she uses to manage her condition.

Jill Kenning has used Nabilone for 17 of the 18 years since she was diagnosed with MS and said the drug had been vital for managing her pain and helping her live a normal life.

She said she had spent most of her time in bed since running out of the drug last Tuesday.

Northern Ireland's devolved health department said there was disruption to supplies of the drug across the UK, meaning Nabilone was out of stock with wholesalers and not expected to be available again until December.

Pharmaceutical manufacturing company Brown & Burk UK Ltd, which supplies the drug to the UK, said they are doing "all that [they] can at this point in time" amid "technical issues".

According to a tracker published by the industry reference guide MIMS, the average number of drugs in short supply in the UK has trended upward this year, external.

The number of drugs in short supply reached 157 this week, up from a low of 107 in January.

News.title: 'Dissident republicans may be responsible' for hotel explosive device - PSNI
News.content:
Ulster Unionist councillor Darren Guy, who chairs the local policing and community safety partnership believes the incident was timed to cause maximum disruption.

He also said it may have been linked to the MoD being represented at a careers event at the hotel in September.

"Recently, there was a careers event held in that hotel where I believe an RAF [Royal Air Force] stall was there for the careers event at that time.

"I think this was specifically done this week to cause as much disruption as possible during the 40th Halloween celebrations with thousands of international visitors visiting the city and the amount of families, especially young families going out to enjoy the many things on offer.

"It is totally reckless and these people don't think about anyone else but themselves."

Sinn FÃ©in councillor Christopher Jackson said it was too early to "speculate" about any link between the alert and the jobs fair.

"We need clarification from those responsible," Jackson said.

He said this was "a disgusting attack on the city and the people of Derry".

"There is no justification whatsoever for carrying this out and putting people in danger, especially when the city is gearing up for the 40th anniversary of the Halloween festival.

"Derry is a warm and welcoming place and it's disgusting why someone or some organisation did this."

Foyle SDLP MP Colum Eastwood told BBC Radio Foyle's North West Today programme the incident must have been terrifying for those members of the public in the vicinity of the hotel .

"This was clearly a viable device which is really frightening for the staff and the visitors to the hotel and to the hundreds, probably thousands of kids who were at that funfair yesterday and have been over the past number of days," Eastwood said.

"I don't know what entered someone's head to think this was a good idea.

"It is appalling, reckless and achieves absolutely nothing."

Julie Middleton, Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) assembly member for Foyle, told BBC Radio Ulster's Good Morning Ulster programme on Wednesday that she was "deeply disturbed and disgusted".

"There is no excuse to leave a viable device anywhere at all, but in the middle of Ebrington Square, where you have people at their work, families out enjoying some half-term fun and tourists visiting and unfortunately this was designed to cause disruption and with any viable device, it was obviously designed to cause harm."

Middleton said many children would also be in the vicinity enjoying the fun fair.

"To think anyone would place something like this near our children, or anyone for that matter, is just deeply wrong."

News.title: Spanish FA postpones 24 Copa del Rey ties after fatal Toledo train crash
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Spanish football federation (Rfef) has postponed all 24 Copa del Rey ties scheduled for Wednesday following the fatal train crash near Madrid.

At least 64 people are dead after two high-speed trains collided in Spain. A government spokesperson for the Castilla La Mancha region said the two trains crashed just after 9am, causing two carriages to derail, with local authorities warning the death toll could rise.

A total of 544 people were travelling on the two trains impacted by the incident, which occurred between the towns of Mora and Orgaz, and involved a Renfe and an Iryo high speed train travelling from Madrid to Seville.

A statement from Rfef read: “As a sign of respect and solidarity with all the victims of the tragic train accident that occurred early Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo, the Rfef (Royal Spanish Football Federation) has suspended all 24 matches of the first round of the Spanish Championship-Copa del Rey (King's Cup) originally scheduled for this afternoon and evening.

“The Rfef will announce the revised tournament schedule and the final times for the postponed matches in the coming days.

“The great Spanish football family remains united in grief at the tragedy, offering their support to the authorities to help the victims of this devastating accident.”

Top-flight teams including Valencia, Celta Viga and Real Betis - who currently sit fourth in LaLiga - were all due to begin their Copa del Rey campaigns this evening.

The likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona enter the tournament during the round of 32 in December due to their involvement in the Spanish Super Cup,

Real Madrid are among the clubs to express its condolences following the crash.

At least 46 people are feared to be dead after two high-speed trains collided in the Spanish capital ( AFP/Getty )

“Real Madrid C.F. wishes to express its deepest sorrow over the tragic railway accident that occurred in the province of Toledo,” a statement read.

“The club extends its condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives, as well as its affection and solidarity to the injured and all those affected by this terrible accident.

“Real Madrid would like to express its full support to the emergency services and all those working in the rescue efforts, and shares in the grief of everyone impacted during these moments of profound sadness.”

Atletico Madrid also put out a statement, reading: “We join in the grief for the victims of the terrible railway accident that occurred this morning in the province of Toledo.

“We extend our deepest condolences to the family and friends of those who have passed away and wish a speedy recovery to all those injured.”
