After the huge success of The Celebrity Traitors’ smash-hit inaugural series last year, host Claudia Winkleman is back with a fresh crop of famous faces in the Scottish castle.

And once again, the BBC has booked an all-star line-up, with award-winning actors, chart-topping musicians and no less than five (five!) comedians among the celebrities playing as either Faithfuls or Traitors.

There’s a huge prize up for grabs too, as those who are victorious will win up to £100,000 for a charity of their choice.

Get to know the celebrities taking part in the ultimate game of deception below...

Michael Sheen – Faithful

open image in gallery Michael Sheen on ‘Celebrity Traitors’ ( BBC )

Stage and screen star Michael Sheen began his career with increasingly prominent theatre roles in the 1990s, culminating in Laurence Olivier Award nominations in 1998 and 1999, for his performances in Amadeus and Look Back In Anger, respectively. The Welsh star expanded his on-screen career in the Noughties, notably playing Tony Blair in three films penned by Peter Morgan (The Crown). His other film credits include the Oscar-nominated Frost/Nixon, British hit The Damned United and Woody Allen’s Midnight In Paris.

In recent years, Sheen has appeared in TV shows including of Good Omens, Quiz (in which he played Chris Tarrant), and A Very Royal Scandal. He has also become known for his activism, thanks to documentaries including Michael Sheen's Secret Million Pound Giveaway and Buried with Michael Sheen. He was announced as the new host of House of Games earlier this year, taking over from Richard Osman.

Maya Jama – Traitor

open image in gallery ‘Love Island’ host Maya Jama ( ITV )

Love Island host Maya Jama is swapping cameo appearances in the ITV villa for a stint in the BBC Traitors castle.

She’s hosted Love Island and its various spin-offs since 2023. Bristol-born Jama moved to London to pursue an acting career in 2012, but soon realised she’d be better suited to presenting. After joining MTV as a presenter in 2014, she went on to front a series of Channel 4’s The Circle, ITV’s Saturday night gameshow Cannonball and BBC Three’s competition series Glow Up: Britain’s Next Make-Up Star.

Jama’s other hosting jobs include the Mobo Awards and the Brit Awards, and she also previously enjoyed a stint in the Radio 1 studios, fronting her one twice-weekly show between 2018 and 2020. Her love life – including past high-profile relationships with rapper Stormzy, NBA player Ben Simmons and Portuguese footballer Rúben Dias – has also made headlines over the years.

Ross Kemp – Faithful

open image in gallery Ross Kemp is best known for playing Grant Mitchell ( BBC )

Ross Kemp is best known for playing EastEnders hardman Grant Mitchell from 1990 to 1999, and he has reprised the role multiple times since first leaving Walford. Most recently, Grant was back in E20 in April to say farewell to his longtime friend Nigel Bates. Kemp’s other acting credits include a mid-Eighties stint in Emmerdale and a phenomenal guest appearance in Ricky Gervais’s Extras.

He has also made a name for himself as a presenter and journalist, fronting documentaries such as the Bafta-winning Ross Kemp on Gangs, Ross Kemp in Afghanistan and Sky’s Extreme World, which ran for six series. Kemp has presented daytime quiz show Bridge of Lies on BBC One since 2022 and went viral online over the summer after he shared increasingly passionate Instagram videos to cheer England on during the World Cup.

Julie Hesmondhalgh – Banished Faithful

open image in gallery Julie Hesmondhalgh won an Olivier in 2025 ( Getty )

Coronation Street legend Julie Hesmondhalgh played Weatherfield’s Hayley Cropper for 14 years. The much-loved Hayley arrived on the cobbles in 1998 and was the first regular transgender character to appear in a British soap. Viewers were left devastated when Hesmondhalgh decided to leave the ITV programme in 2014. The emotional exit storyline saw Hayley take her own life after receiving a cancer diagnosis; the actor had asked bosses to kill her character off so she wouldn’t be tempted to return to the soap.

Hesmondhalgh has since landed TV roles in the likes of Russell T Davies’ Cucumber, Happy Valley and Broadchurch, as well as branching out into theatre, winning an Olivier Award for her performance in James Graham’s 2025 play Punch. In January last year, she played subpostmaster Alan Bates’s wife Suzanne Sercombe in ITV’s groundbreaking drama Mr Bates vs The Post Office.

Rob Beckett – Murdered

open image in gallery Comedian Rob Beckett ( Getty )

Rob Beckett was cast as one of five comedians in the Traitors castle. With his cheeky chappy persona, the south-east London born star soon won over fans when he started out on the stand-up circuit in 2009, and went on to appear on panel shows Mock the Week, 8 out of 10 Cats and the latter’s Countdown spin-off. In 2017, he won the third series of Taskmaster.

Beckett has also dipped his toe into the world of reality television on more than a few occasions, hosting three seasons of ITV’s I'm a Celebrity spin-off show, providing the voiceover for Celebs Go Dating and taking part in Celebrity Bake Off.

Together with Strictly Come Dancing host Josh Widdicombe, he fronts the podcast Parenting Hell. And Beckett is also part of a hugely popular double act with another of this year’s Celebrity Traitors contestants…

Romesh Ranganathan – Faithful

open image in gallery Comic Romesh Ranganathan ( PA )

Former maths teacher Romesh Ranganathan began his comedy career while he was still working full-time in the classroom. After a brief flirtation with freestyle rap, Ranganathan found his footing on the comedy circuit and enjoyed a huge boost in popularity when he appeared on the BBC’s Live at the Apollo in 2013.

Since then, he’s appeared on the likes of Taskmaster, Would I Lie To You?, Have I Got News For You and QI. Ranganathan has also fronted quiz shows including Sky’s A League of Their Own and the BBC’s The Weakest Link revival. He’s channelled his love of music into a weekly Radio 2 show, For The Love of Hip-Hop, and took over the station’s Saturday lunchtime slot from Claudia Winkleman in April 2024.

Beckett and Ranganathan have landed a number of joint gigs, with the former’s chirpy attitude being balanced out by the latter’s often sarcastic and deadpan musings. The pair have a popular Sky series, Rob and Romesh Vs…, and co-hosted the TV Baftas in 2023 and 2024.

Jerry Hall – Faithful

open image in gallery Wildcard booking Jerry Hall ( AFP/Getty )

One of this year’s truly wildcard bookings, supermodel Jerry Hall is bringing old-school glamour to the castle.

Hall’s modelling career began in the 1970s, when she appeared as a mermaid on the cover of Roxy Music’s album Siren. She became synonymous with the glamour of the Seventies disco era, appearing on magazine covers for the likes of Vogue UK, Cosmopolitan and Interview, and often being photographed at Studio 54 with close friend Andy Warhol, who counted Hall as a muse, and then-boyfriend Mick Jagger.

Hall and the Rolling Stones frontman remained together until 1999, with the pair welcoming four children during that time. Throughout their relationship, Hall continued to expand her career and moved into acting, landing roles in Tim Burton’s Batman, TV series Cluedo and a Broadway production of The Graduate.

Hall married media mogul Rupert Murdoch in a low-key London ceremony in 2016. The couple remained together until 2022, when Hall filed for divorce citing irreconcilable differences.

Joe Lycett – Banished Faithful

open image in gallery Comedian Joe Lycett ( Getty )

Birmingham-based funnyman Joe Lycett’s comedy has become increasingly surrealist and absurd over the years – with a touch of Martin Lewis thrown in for good measure. He’s appeared on all of the major comedy and panel shows on British television (think Taskmaster, 8 out of 10 Cats, Last One Laughing UK) and fronted his own consumer rights show Joe Lycett's Got Your Back, Channel 4’s Travel Man and The Great British Sewing Bee.

In 2023, he began hosting his very own live variety show, Late Night Lycett. The star has also leaned in to comedic stunts in recent years, legally changing his name to Hugo Boss to draw attention to the fashion brand’s use of cease and desist letters against small businesses.

James Blunt – Faithful

open image in gallery Singer James Blunt ( Getty )

James Blunt made the unlikely journey from British Army captain to chart-topper when he released “You’re Beautiful” in 2005, three years after leaving the forces. The single went straight to the top of the UK charts, and boosted the popularity of his debut album Back to Bedlam, which had actually been released a year before. With the record top of the charts, Blunt also also released “Goodbye My Lover” as a single.

At the 2006 Brit Awards, he was named best british pop act and best british male solo act, and a follow-up album, All the Lost Souls, followed in 2007. He has since released five more albums, with another – titled Airplane Mode – coming out in November this year. When he’s not in the studio, Blunt is a keen user of X and has frequently gone viral thanks to self-deprecating, sarcastic and pithy comebacks.

Bella Ramsey – Murdered

open image in gallery Bella Ramsey in ‘The Last of Us’ ( HBO )

Bella Ramsey was just 11 years old when they began filming Game of Thrones. The child star played Lyanna Mormont, the young ruler who found herself at the head of her family following her mother’s death. After appearances in CBBC’s The Worst Witch, Phillip Pullman adaptation His Dark Materials and anthology series Time, Ramsey landed a leading role in HBO’s The Last Of Us.

Adapted from the hugely popular PlayStation game of the same name, The Last Of Us sees Ramsay’s Ellie attempting to survive alongside unlikely guardian Joel (Pedro Pascal). The show and its leading stars both received awards nods for the first two seasons, with Ramsey nominated for an Emmy, a Critics’ Choice award and a Golden Globe. Two series of The Last Of Us have so far aired, with a third set to arrive in 2027.

Richard E Grant – Banished Traitor

open image in gallery Actor Richard E Grant ( AFP/Getty )

Legendary actor Richard E Grant has one of the most impressive CVs in the business. The Swazi-English actor made his debut as the titular character in 1987’s Withnail and I, and is also known for films including The Portrait of a Lady, Gosford Park, The Iron Lady, Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker and Emerald Fennell’s controversial Saltburn. He received an Academy Award nomination for 2018’s Can You Forgive Me?, a biographical drama about American author Lee Israel.

On the small screen, his credits include Doctor Who, Frasier, A Series of Unfortunate Events and Game of Thrones. In 2022, he released a best-selling memoir, A Pocketful of Happiness, which chronicled his 40-year marriage to dialect coach Joan Washington, and her death from cancer in 2021.

Leigh-Anne Pinnock – Faithful

open image in gallery Singer Leigh-Anne Pinnock ( Getty )

Singer Leigh-Anne Pinnock rocketed to fame as one fourth of Little Mix, the first group to ever win The X Factor. Pinnock triumphed with bandmates Jade Thirlwall, Perrie Edwards and Jesy Nelson in 2011 and Little Mix went on to become the UK’s most successful girlband since the Spice Girls, with hit singles including “D.N.A”, “Shout out to my Ex”, “Black Magic” and “Power”.

Nelson departed the group in 2020 and Little Mix continued as a trio until 2022, when they announced an indefinite hiatus. Pinnock has since pursued a solo career and initially signed with Warner Records, before leaving after the label decided against releasing her debut album. Pinnock then moved to Virgin and My Ego Told Me To came out in February this year. The singer and her husband Andre Gray are parents to twin daughters, and announced in May this year that a third child is on the way.

James Acaster – Traitor

open image in gallery James Acaster thinks comedians have a disadvantage on ‘Celebrity Traitors’ ( BBC )

James Acaster has said he’s worried previous winner Alan Carr’s success in the Traitors castle has “tainted” this year’s comedians. “I think we’re going to be the first ones under the magnifying glass being looked at – particularly at the beginning when you have absolutely nothing to go on,” he told the BBC.

The comedian is another of this year’s recruits who cut their teeth in stand-up, and has taken multiple shows to the Edinburgh Fringe Festival, with Repertoire also being released on Netflix. He hosts the popular foodie podcast Off Menu with Traitors Uncloaked host Ed Gamble and has written two books about music, James Acaster’s Classic Scrapes and Perfect Sound Whatever.

Miranda Hart – Faithful

open image in gallery Miranda Hart in her mega-hit BBC sitcom ( BBC )

Actor, comedian and writer Miranda Hart is best-known for her self-titled BBC sitcom, which landed multiple TV Bafta nominations and British Comedy Award wins across its three seasons. She also appeared as midwife Camilla “Chummy” Fortescue-Cholmondeley-Browne in Call the Midwife and made her Hollywood debut opposite Mellisa McCarthy in the action comedy Spy.

She’s release numerous books, including 2012’s Is it Just Me?, which merged anecdotes from her life with advice, and The Girl With The Lost Smile. In 2024, she released the memoir I Haven't Been Entirely Honest with You, revealing on the book’s promotional tour that she had secretly married at the age of 51. The book also recounted how she’d been experiencing a decades-long struggle with Lyme disease, which turned into ME (Myalgic encephalomyelitis), also known as chronic fatigue syndrome.

Amol Rajan – Murdered

open image in gallery Amol Rajan recently left the ‘Today’ programme ( PA )

Broadcaster Amol Rajan got his start in journalism at this very publication in 2007, and moved up the ranks before serving as editor between 2013 and 2016. After leaving, he became the BBC’s first media editor, before joining the Today programme’s presenting team in 2021 – a role he recently left.

On the small screen, Rajan has hosted University Challenge since 2023, and appeared on the likes of The One Show, Have I Got News For You and House of Games.

Joanne McNally – Faithful

open image in gallery Comedian Joanne McNally ( Getty )

Completing the series’ quintet of comedians, it’s Irish star Joanne McNally.

After years on the comedy circuit, McNally took her her dark one-woman show Bite Me, about her bulimia, to Edinburgh Fringe Festival in 2017. She hit the road with her Prosecco Express show in 2022 and the tour was extended multiple times. By the time it was done and dusted, McNally had performed a record-breaking 78 sold-out shows at Dublin’s Vicar Street venue, while her crowd at the London Palladium broke the 118-year old venue’s record for most alcohol sold.

McNally followed it up with the Pinotphile tour, which began in 2025, squeezing in appearances on Taskmaster and Channel 4's The Big Fat Quiz of Everything in between. She co-hosts the popular My Therapist Ghosted Me podcast with close pal Vogue Williams.

Sharon Rooney – Faithful

open image in gallery Sharon Rooney in ‘My Mad Fat Diary’ ( Channel 4 )

Scottish actor Sharon Rooney landed her breakthrough role in Channel 4’s acclaimed comedy My Mad Fat Diary back in 2013. Subsequent television roles have included parts in Sherlock, The Capture and Finding Alice, as well as appearing as series regular Sophie in Two Doors Down.

On the big screen, Rooney popped up in Greta Gerwig’s Barbie film, as a lawyer version of the famous doll, and played Miss Atlantic in Disney’s live-action remake of Dumbo, performing the track “Baby Mine”.

King Kenny – Traitor

open image in gallery King Kenny in the ring ( Getty )

While he’s not technically a comedian, social media star King Kenny loves to bring the laughs with pranks and stunts. Kenny, full name Kenny Oghenovo Ojuederie, is a former boxer who primarily fought other influencers, before quitting the sport earlier this year due to injury.

He’s built a huge audience on TikTok and YouTube, with almost three million followers across the two platforms. Kenny’s most popular videos include pranks – often involving his younger brother – and gaming-related videos. He was previously part of the Beta Squad collective with fellow pranksters including Niko Omilana, who appeared in the first series of Celebrity Traitors but went out early.

Professor Hannah Fry – Banished Traitor

open image in gallery Professor Hannah Fry ( PA )

Broadcaster and mathematician Professor Hannah Fry has been making television and radio appearances for more than 10 years. Some of her most notable cameos include the BBC Two series The Secret Genius Of Modern Life, the post-pandemic documentary Unvaccinated and number-crunching for Channel 4 during their general election coverage in 2024.

Fry also hosts The Rest Science podcast alongside Michael Stevens and has a huge following online, with more than 100 million views on her YouTube channel.

Sebastian Croft – Faithful

open image in gallery Actor and musician Sebastian Croft ( Getty )

Actor and musician Sebastian Croft is another Traitors star who has had a brush with Westeros – as a child star, he played a young Ned Stark in two episodes of Game of Thrones. Croft’s more recent credits include Netflix’s Heartstopper and Amazon Video romcom How to Date Billy Walsh.

On the music front, Croft has independently released two singles, “Toyko” and “Better than ever”. The star identifies as queer and in 2022, he designed a t-shirt featuring “two gay dinosaurs kissing, reminding everyone that Queer has always been here”, with profits from sales going to two charities that support LGBT+ refugees.

Myha’la – Banished Faithful

open image in gallery Myha’la ( Getty )

American actor Myha’la Herrold, known just by her first name, is best known for playing chaotic antihero Harper Stern in Industry.

Born and raised in California, the star began her acting career with a string of theatre roles, including parts in Shrek the Musical and a touring production of Book of Mormon. Myha’la has also appeared in the Loch Henry episode in series six of Charlie Brooker’s Black Mirror, the New York Times-inspired series Modern Love, and films Dumb Money and Leave the World Behind.

News.title: 'Dixie' map that divided US goes up for auction after Library of Congress was forced to turn it down
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A hand-drawn chart of the Mason-Dixon Line, the boundary that came to divide the free states from the slave states, goes under the hammer on Thursday.

The sale of the document, which has been remounted on backing made of Japanese rice paper, will be livestreamed. Lauren Brunk, vice president of Brunk Auctions in Asheville, North Carolina, expects it to fetch anywhere between $800,000 and $1.2 million.

“It’s not that often that you can really get this close to something that is so historically important," said Brunk. “And it was awe-inspiring, really.”

The map is a strip of linen-backed paper measuring 76 inches (193 centimeters) long and 6.5 inches (16.5 centimeters) tall. Soon after it was drawn, it was given to the family of attorney Benjamin Chew, who represented the descendants of Pennsylvania founder William Penn.

open image in gallery The original, hand-drawn survey of the Mason-Dixon Line at Brunk Auctions in Asheville, N.C. ( Brunk Auctions via AP )

The Chew family kept the map until 1982, when the late publisher Malcolm S. Forbes bought it for $360,000, outbidding the Library of Congress, Brunk said. At the time, it was said to have been the highest price ever paid at auction for an American map.

The map changed hands again in 2002. A vertical section showing the Delaware-Maryland border is housed at Princeton University.

The survey behind the document was carried out by Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon. Their work was originally meant to settle a border dispute between the then-colonies of Maryland and Pennsylvania.

Its place in history was secured later, when the 1820 Missouri Compromise used the line to establish the limits of human bondage in the still adolescent United States. From there, it became synonymous with the fundamental divisions that exploded into civil war four decades later.

open image in gallery A post marking the base point in the survey of Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon ( AP Photo/Matt Rourke )

“The Mason-Dixon Line that most Americans know is this dividing line between the northern free states and the southern slaveholding states,” Brunk said. “But the line was not drawn for that reason.”

A popular theory holds that the term "Dixie" derives from Jeremiah Dixon, though the true origin is disputed.

Brunk said she reached out to officials at the Library of Congress to see if they wanted to bid on it again.

“I wanted them to be aware that this was coming back to the market,” she said. “And they said, at this point, budgets being what they are, they were just not in a position to buy it.”

But if some patriot out there wants to purchase it on the library's behalf, Brunk said, “they’d be happy to have it.”

News.title: Man accused of murdering headteacher had ‘no consideration’ for road users, jury told
News.content:

A motorist accused of murdering a grammar school headteacher sped off from police looking to arrest him the following day, a court has heard.

Headteacher Michael Mullins, 56, was struck by a black Volvo XC90 as he cycled home from Stretford Grammar School in Manchester during the early evening of 20 April.

Simon Richardson, 35, is said to have driven at speed through give way markers at a junction in Warburton, Altrincham, and into the path of Mr Mullins.

Prosecutors accuse Richardson of murder because they say he knew Mr Mullins was beneath the wheels of his vehicle but drove on anyway.

It is alleged Richardson later travelled to a country lane in Lymm, Cheshire, and “veered sharply and deliberately from side to side” before he mounted a grass verge and drove over Mr Mullins who was finally dislodged.

Mr Mullins, from Northwich, Cheshire, was found still breathing in Wet Gate Lane – 2.2 kilometres from the collision in Paddock Lane – but was pronounced dead at the scene at 6.50pm, about 40 minutes after he was knocked off his bike.

On Tuesday, jurors at Manchester Minshull Crown Street watched dashcam footage of a police pursuit of the defendant driving a silver Ford Transit van in Failsworth, Greater Manchester, on 21 April.

open image in gallery Michael Mullins, who was mowed down and dragged for more than a mile to his death as he became trapped underneath a car ( Greater Manchester Police )

The van was followed to William Street where it briefly stopped and then sped off as officers approached.

In a statement read to the court, Pc Gerard Elliott, said he heard “tyres squealing” as the van took off and turned left into an alleyway and on to Oldham Road.

A pursuit followed in densely populated residential streets as Pc Elliott said he reached speeds of 50mph but was “not gaining on the Transit van”.

The van came to a stop in nearby Co-operation Street due to another vehicle blocking its path, said the officer, as the suspect ran off before he was apprehended shorty after, the court heard.

Another officer involved in the pursuit, Insp Tom Abbott, told the court: “The (van) driver showed no consideration for the safety of other drivers and pedestrians.”

Last week jurors saw CCTV footage of Richardson allegedly driving “erratically” in the moments before the fatal collision.

open image in gallery Jurors at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court were told that visible damage to Richardson’s Volvo was captured on an ANPR camera as he drove away from the collision – both to the bonnet and to the windscreen almost directly in front of the driver ( AFP/Getty )

His Volvo was said to be “absolutely tanking it” by a witness before he overtook cars on the approach to the junction of Dunham Road and Paddock Lane, the court heard.

Richardson denies murder and an alternative count of manslaughter.

He has also pleaded not guilty to an offence of dangerous driving.

The trial continues on Wednesday.

News.title: I stayed at Andy Murray’s five-star country house hotel – here’s what I thought
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

At this Victorian mansion turned country hotel, Andy and Kim Murray have successfully brought to life their vision for a five-star stay in the Wimbledon champion’s hometown

Location

Cromlix hotel is tucked away in Stirlingshire countryside on a 34-acre estate near the bucolic town of Dunblane, which is filled with traditional stone-built houses, country pubs and quaint cafes. It’s also the area where Cromlix owner and tennis legend Andy Murray grew up.

Glasgow and Edinburgh airports are both less than an hour's taxi ride away. Or travel to Dunblane by train from major stations such as Edinburgh Waverley, Glasgow Queen Street and Stirling for sweeping views of central Scotland’s hillscapes from the carriage windows. Call reception ahead of time to arrange private transfers to and from the station. There are parking spaces if you arrive by car.



The vibe

With just 20 rooms on the estate, Cromlix feels less like a hotel and more like a wealthy friend’s countryside manor. Thanks to the residential-style layout, which has been retained from the hotel’s past life as a laird’s private home, nothing about a stay here feels sterile.

open image in gallery The tennis court at Andy Murray’s Cromlix hotel is Wimbledon green and purple ( Cromlix )

Cromlix was given a full makeover in 2023 after Kim and Andy Murray took the hotel back into self-management 10 years after purchasing the property. It also closed earlier this year so that a new glass-fronted restaurant and a spa outhouse, the Woodland Retreat, could be added.



Service

Staff at Cromlix were on hand to help when we needed it, providing a map of the grounds and recommending local and popular whiskies in the restaurant, but were never overbearing and let us enjoy the hotel in our own time. Bonus points for providing jobs to the friendliest young people in the local area.

Bed and bath

There are six room categories to choose from, ranging from the generously large Turret Suites to smaller suites, cosy rooms and a ground floor apartment with a wet room. The Gatehouse at the entrance of the estate has been turned into a one-bedroom, self-catering lodge with a substantial kitchen.

open image in gallery Bathrooms at Andy Murray’s Cromlix hotel are spacious and some feature roll-top baths ( Cromlix )

I stayed in one of the Turret Suites, which comes with a large bathroom with a walk-in shower and a brass roll-top bath, a living room with a flat-screen TV and a separate bedroom, all connected by a private corridor. The complimentary minibar and hot drinks cabinet were accompanied by slabs of shortbread baked according to Andy’s Granny Erskine’s recipe.

As I arrived in a heatwave, and the historic suites don’t have air conditioning, a Dyson fan was set up in the bedroom to keep things cool.

open image in gallery Bedrooms at Cromlix hotel combine bold patterns with vintage furniture ( Cromlix )

Kim Murray was central to the interior design decisions, managing to echo the best of Cromlix’s surroundings without feeling obligated to throw in the stereotypical Scottish tartans and tweeds. Walls are papered in floral patterns, overlaid with chunky picture frames displaying horticultural motifs. More patterns and colours are injected into the space with pastel sofas, heavy drapes and upholstered headboards or bed canopies.

Vintage dressers, wooden vanities and twin basins add vintage charm; while original features such as the bay windows and high ceilings add to Cromlix’s homely vibe.



Food and drink

Come the evening, the bar, outside terrace and Cromlix’s new restaurant, the Garden Room, have a buzzy atmosphere, and are as popular with locals as guests. The sophisticated, locally-sourced menu at the Garden Room serves dishes such as goat's cheese soufflé, crab crumpets, wild turbot and local poultry dishes; with cheese plates and Scottish strawberry pavlovas to follow. The menu uses vegetables, fruit and herbs grown on the estate. All allergies and dietary requirements can be discussed with your server, who can recommend the best dishes for you.

open image in gallery The new Garden Room restaurant at Andy Murray’s Cromlix hotel in Scotland ( Cromlix )

Breakfast is served in the new glass-fronted Garden Room, consisting of a small continental spread and a la carte hot dishes, such as a full Scottish breakfast with haggis.

The 16-cover Cradle is Cromlix’s fine dining restaurant, offering a Scottish produce-focused tasting menu. It’s open Thursday to Sunday. An afternoon tea is also laid out in the light-filled Glasshouse every afternoon.

Facilities

The intimate one-room Woodland Retreat is where massages and facials take place. It felt particularly tranquil during my 80-minute full-body massage. The same goes for the nearby cold plunge and sauna, which look out over a small loch, and can be booked for private slots. Crocs and Dryrobes are provided. Booking ahead for all wellness offerings is advised.

open image in gallery The sauna and cold plunge at Andy Murray’s Cromlix hotel can be booked for private slots ( Cromlix )

Would this be a hotel owned by Andy Murray without a tennis court? It's hard to miss the netted court (which is beside a pickleball court) in the distinct Wimbledon shades of green and purple, ready for guests to serve up some aces.



Accessibility

There are three accessible ground floor rooms, two with walk-in showers and one with an adapted wet room. A new turning circle allows for drop-offs directly outside the reception. Due to Cromlix being a listed building, there are no lifts in the main building. The path leading to the tennis court is gravel, and access to the spa may currently be trickier due to pathways still being laid.

Pet policy

The hotel offers a “very important pup package”, where dog beds, bowls and a hamper are laid out in rooms before the guest of honour arrives with their owners. There's also a doggie breakfast menu available for room service and treats are left at turndown.

Check-in/check-out

Check-in is at 3pm; check out is 11am.

Family-friendly

The hotel welcomes children of all ages, and can arrange connected rooms, cots, sofa beds and extra beds in certain rooms. Children under five visiting with an adult can stay free of charge. Those aged between five and 15 will be charged a bed and breakfast rate of £65 per day.

There is no kids’ club at Cromlix, with stays at the hotel more suited to families who want to explore the local area. Kids' menus are available in the Garden room. A kids' package is also available, which includes a teepee set up in your room, toiletries, a bathrobe, milk, cookies and a storybook at bedtime. An external babysitting service can be arranged ahead of your stay.

open image in gallery A Turret Suite living room at Andy Murray’s Cromlix hotel in Scotland ( Cromlix )

At a glance

Best thing: Sauna time overlooking the loch.

Perfect for: A relaxed retreat to the countryside.

Not right for: People who want action-packed days.

Instagram from: The front lawn. Make sure to put on the Halley Stevensons wax jacket and Barbour wellies that can be grabbed from the porch.

Address: Cromlix, Kinbuck, Stirling FK15 9JT

Phone: 01786 820310

Website: cromlix.com



Amelia was a guest of Cromlix

News.title: Jennifer Lawrence addresses return to Hunger Games franchise
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Jennifer Lawrence is speaking out for the first time about reprising her role of Katniss Everdeen in the upcoming Hunger Games prequel.

After months of speculation about the cast of the original film franchise making an appearance in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, the 36-year-old Oscar-winning actor confirmed she will wear her iconic braid again in the new film, which hits theaters November 20.

“It was unbelievable,” Lawrence told Call Her Daddy host Alex Cooper about reprising the role during Wednesday’s podcast episode. “It was so crazy. It was the same crew. It was the same AD, who I’ve worked with a million times because I love him.”

She went on to say that working with co-stars Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson — who played Peeta Mellark and Haymitch Abernathy, respectively — again was “so emotional.”

“Josh and I didn’t walk to the bathroom without our arms around each other,” she said. “It was so beautiful.”

open image in gallery Jennifer Lawrence is returning as Katniss Everdeen in the new 'Hunger Games' movie ( Getty )

She joked: “And Woody, obviously, came through the window of my hotel room uninvited. It wouldn’t be the same if he listened to boundaries or used a door.”

Speculation about Lawrence, Hutcherson and Harrelson reprising their roles began to swirl after Suzanne Collins’ Sunrise on the Reaping novel ended with an epilogue featuring Katniss, Peeta and Haymitch.

The original four movies, adapted from Collins’ three dystopian books, grew into a multi billion-dollar global franchise, becoming one of the most commercially and culturally successful young adult adaptations of the 2010s. The films ran from 2012 to 2015, grossing over $3.3 billion worldwide.

open image in gallery Josh Hutcherson, Jennifer Lawrence, Liam Hemsworth and Donald Sutherland starred in the original Hunger Games franchise ( Getty )

Collins then continued the series with the prequel book The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, released in 2020, which centered around a young Coriolanus Snow, who is the main antagonist of the series as the evil president of its fictitious post-apocalyptic nation Panem.

The prequel was later adapted into a film starring Rachel Zegler as District 12 tribute Lucy Gray Baird and Tom Blyth as Snow, who was later played by the late Donald Sutherland, and will be portrayed in the new film by Ralph Fiennes. The film grossed more than $300 million in theaters.

Sunrise on the Reaping is set 40 years after The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, and centers on a young Haymitch, who is played by East of Eden star Joseph Zada, during the 50th Hunger Games. The movie features a star-studded cast including McKenna Grace, Whitney Peak, Fiennes, Glenn Close, Jesse Plemons, Maya Hawke, Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning and Billy Porter.

News.title: What caused the latest high-speed Spanish train crash as transport minister blames broken protocol
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Rescue workers in Spain on ⁠Wednesday were scouring the wreckage for more bodies at the crash scene where at least 64 people were killed when two high-speed trains collided, in the second deadly railway accident in the country this year.

Evacuated passengers streamed along a road near the scene, some splattered with ⁠blood or with their wounds bandaged, ​others wheeling ⁠suitcases and being given water by volunteers who said it had been donated from neighbouring towns.

Hundreds of ambulances, funeral home vans and helicopters were ⁠parked next to a train with several carriages sitting on an elevated section ​of ⁠track while twisted metal, broken panels ‌and wreckage could be seen strewn across an embankment beneath the line where at least three carriages had plunged.

What caused Spain’s deadly train crash?

One of the train’s ran into the tail of the other which had stopped, knocking two of its cars off the track.

The crash, which occurred in a flat stretch surrounded by fields in between the towns of Urda and Los Yébenes, left one car shredded into bits of metal and other material, scattering debris down a gravel slope.

open image in gallery The train crash follows a similar incident on the same line back in January ( AP )

A person briefed on the disaster said an express operated by Spanish train operator Iryo stopped near Toledo due to a signal fault, on orders from infrastructure manager ADIF, when it was struck by another high-speed train on.

A train operated by Renfe then struck the ⁠stationary train at high speed, causing several carriages of both trains to derail, the person said. There was no immediate response to a request for comment from Iryo or Renfe.

Spain's transport ⁠minister said the fatal train crash occurred after a Renfe high-speed ⁠train ​was ⁠authorised to continue its ⁠journey despite an active ​red ⁠signal because ‌of a stationary train on the ‌tracks ahead, breaking protocol.

Addressing reporters in Madrid, Transport Minister Oscar Puente said the red signal was issued due to a computer communications failure which automatically stopped traffic and an erroneous decision was made to restart the Renfe train.

open image in gallery Traffic on the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed rail line has been suspended ( Reuters )

The crash follows a collision nine months ago, where high-speed trains belonging to the same operators on the same line killed 46 people.

Experts on site identified wear on the joint between sections of the rail, known as a fishplate, which they said showed the fault had been there for some time, a source briefed on the preliminary probe told Reuters. They found that the faulty joint created a gap between the rail sections that widened as trains continued to travel on the track.

The crash, which occurred in January, triggered a debate about the level of investment in railway maintenance in recent years.

Accidents, including derailments and collisions, increased from 45 in 2016 to 57 in 2024 and 69 last year, according to Spain's railway safety authority. ‌In the same period, problems such as deterioration and breaks in the rails went from 494 and 667, a level below the 716 registered in 2024.

News.title: The hypocrisy of Mikel Arteta’s scathing reaction towards ‘kid’ Max Dowman
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

They don’t call them the troubled teens for no reason.

Max Dowman is 16 years of age (not sure anybody’s mentioned that before). Arsenal’s child prodigy is one of football’s most exciting talents, though as someone who cannot yet legally drive, he is still some way off reaching full maturity. His straight red card against Fleetwood, born from the short fuse not uncommon in those his age, was a clear indication of that.

His outburst was hardly unprovoked; Fleetwood midfielder Harrison Neal had just lunged in with a scissoring challenge, the type that has broken legs before. But that isn’t an excuse to lose your head, not at this level. Neither is his age, which on the pitch is a non-factor; he has been entrusted to play senior football so is expected to carry himself like a senior footballer.

open image in gallery Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct against Fleetwood ( Reuters )

Dowman’s kick-out, even if soft, was a major blunder on his end. He is now suspended for three games – barring a successful appeal – and will not get an opportunity for redemption until the visit of Manchester City on 29 November. That’s over a month of unavailability.

He should receive a dressing down from his manager to drive home the lesson that needs to be learned, especially in the context of his sending off for the England U19s at the beginning of the month. There is a pattern emerging of indiscipline that Arsenal need to nip in the bud.

However, there’s a good way of dealing with these things and a bad way, especially when the player in question is not yet an adult. Mikel Arteta went for the latter when he appeared to direct a furious reaction towards Dowman from the touchline as he walked down the tunnel, for all the world to see. This has now become the story, arguably more than his red card.

To reiterate, Arteta had every right to be angry at his player. The sending off was stupid, petulant and completely avoidable, putting Arsenal at a man disadvantage for the final five minutes, during which they could have found a late winner and avoided the perils of penalties. It lit the blue-touch paper for Arsenal’s humiliating Carabao Cup exit that would be sealed 21 minutes later.

But to put him on blast so publicly rather than wait until they’ve got the privacy of the dressing room felt irresponsible. Dowman is in an especially unique position as a player who burst onto the scene at the very top level aged just 15. Arteta himself has repeatedly stated how careful the club have to be in nurturing him to his full potential.

After becoming the Premier League’s youngest ever scorer with his goal against Everton in March, Arteta was keen to ensure the noise surrounding Dowman didn’t become overwhelming, even telling the media: “I need your help with that, guys.” You haven’t helped yourself here, Mikel.

open image in gallery Mikel Arteta had stern words for Dowman as he walked off the pitch ( Getty )

He’s poured fuel on the fire with his reaction, which now has a hypocrisy attached to it since he explained what compelled him to act the way he did.

“We knew when we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to expect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate,” Arteta said. Yet the 44-year-old Arsenal manager has also proven infallible on the emotional front. Arteta should have restrained himself and saved his telling off for the dressing room. Instead, he boiled over.

It’s rare to see a manager direct this sort of anger at a player who’s been sent off in the public eye. The trudge between touchline and tunnel is usually an awkward affair; sometimes there’s a consoling pat on the back, other times there’s a disapproving look, a roll of the eyes or no acknowledgement at all. So why did Dowman get the explosive treatment?

open image in gallery Arteta’s scathing reaction towards Dowman has become the story ( Getty )

Former Arsenal midfielder Paul Merson questioned whether a more senior Arsenal player would have been subjected to the same rage. “You have to remember he is 16 years of age – he's a kid,” he said.

“If that’s Viktor Gyokeres, he [Arteta] isn’t doing that. That’s what I don’t like. If it’s an experienced international, I don’t think he does that. He’s a human being. He’s not the last person to get sent off for Arsenal, nor the first.”

What goes on behind closed doors in London Colney to address Dowman’s dismissal is Arsenal’s business. But there is now a swirl surrounding the 16-year-old’s relationship with his manager that has been self-inflicted by Arteta. It is the last thing this situation needs. Both parties should have known better on a dismal night in the North West; it’s just one was a boy and the other was a man.

News.title: Fleetwood knock out Arsenal in one of the biggest shocks in League Cup history
News.content:
An unfamiliar opponent at a very familiar sounding venue, Arsenal play Fleetwood Town for the first time this evening at the Lancashire club’s Highbury Stadium.

Fleetwood, 18th in League Two, are the lowest-ranked team remaining in this season’s League Cup, having booked their place in the fourth round thanks to a victory at Sheffield United.

They were playing in English football’s sixth tier in 2009, and so while their stadium may share its name with Arsenal’s former home, the two clubs are worlds apart.

The League Cup is fourth of four competitions on Arsenal’s list of priorities, but Mikel Arteta should be able to rotate extensively while progressing to the quarter-finals. With a trip to Anfield on Sunday, that is a welcome luxury.

Kepa Arrizabalaga, Piero Hincapie, Cristhian Mosquera, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres are seasoned internationals in need of minutes and in line to start.

Max Dowman lit up Arsenal’s third-round victory at Ipswich Town, and 17-year-old centre-back Marli Salmon was not far behind him. Young striker and Northern Ireland international Ceadach O’Neill is also expected to be involved, and he may be joined by other academy players.

While attention is fixed on Premier League and Champions League success, Arsenal’s stinging defeat by Manchester City in last season’s final of this competition will not have been forgotten by Arteta or his players.

Matt Lawlor, Fleetwood’s manager, was full of praise for Arsenal in his pre-match press conference: “The champions are coming to town and they’re coming to our patch. The players need to be excited by it, not overawed by it. The respect is through the roof, but the fear can’t be through the roof.

“We’ve earned a game like this. We’ve had to go through round upon round of tough games, and none of them were easy. To get to where we are, we deserve that.”

Arteta has told his players that they must keep their standards high, with a lack of concentration or professionalism potentially their worst enemy against fourth-tier opposition.

Arteta said: “Our reputation, our pride, everything is in play. So every time you play a football match, and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve that, and then try to win and try to play a bit better than them.



“We know the risk, and in football, things can get very equal the moment you are able to match certain things, and that’s why our basics and habits have to be through the roof to be able to win the game.”

News.title: High temperatures linked to more than 700,000 deaths in 2023, study estimates
News.content:
Record-breaking temperatures killed an estimated 710,00 people globally in 2023, an increase of more than 36 per cent since 2015, according to new research.

A report on climate change and health by the Lancet medical journal shows that since the Paris climate agreement was introduced in 2016 the number of deaths linked to heat has rocketed.

Between 2006 and 2015 the average annual number of deaths attributed to heat stood at around 398,400 but between 2016 and 2023 the number increased to an annual average of 540,800, hitting a high of 710,000 in 2023.

The authors of the Lancet study say that extreme heat, which is linked to cardiovascular problems and is particularly dangerous for older people, pregnant women and those with other health conditions, must be considered a global health emergency. And they warn that the risks from high temperatures have accelerated in recent years.

News.title: Nigeria’s women and girls impacted the most by British and US funding cuts, committee is told
News.content:
UK and US aid funding cuts in Nigeria have impacted the country’s women and girls more than other groups, MPs were told on Tuesday.

Nigeria has been among the hardest-hit countries as many Western governments have slashed overseas development budgets to increase defence spending.

At the International Development Committee’s first hearing on the impact of aid cuts on global health in Africa, MPs were told that UK government cuts had impacted water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) programmes in Nigeria significantly, putting women and girls at risk.

“WASH is one of the lowest-funded areas in UK government support to Nigeria. WASH enables girls to stay in school, enables them to manage their menstruation effectively, enables women to give birth safely, and protects the lives of children under 5,” Evelyn Mere country director of Water Aid Nigeria said.

“The UK government says one of its priorities is that it will educate girls, empower women and make sure their voices are heard. It means that the UK says one thing, but with the aid cuts does another,” she added.

The British Foreign, Commonwealth, and Development Office (FCDO) announced earlier this year it would reduce its aid spending in Nigeria by 50.2 per cent over the next three years, from £136 million in 2025 to £68 million by 2029.

Nigeria has also faced substantial funding reductions from the US after the Trump administration shuttered USAID, the government’s foreign assistance arm. This included more than $600 million (£450 million) in health funding.

An FCDO internal impact assessment, published in July 2025, acknowledged that the biggest casualties of African funding cuts would be frontline WASH and women’s health programmes.

“Overall, any reductions to health spending risk an increase in disease burden and ultimately in deaths, impacting in particular those living in poverty, women, children and people with disabilities,” the assessment concluded.

News.title: Taliban forbids ‘un-Islamic’ sight-saving operations
News.content:
Hundreds of people each year will be denied sight-saving operations in Afghanistan after the Taliban forbade corneal transplants, doctors have told the Telegraph.

Officials have ruled that the transplant procedure is not permitted under Islamic teachings and have ordered surgeons to halt operations.

It is the latest in a stream of edicts limiting access to health care issued by the regime since it swept to power in 2021.

The edict came just months after a medical charity had helped train up local doctors to conduct operations in the Afghan capital, Kabul, and the eastern city of Jalalabad.

Doctors say there is a severe need for corneal transplants in Afghanistan to restore sight in patients injured in explosions and accidents.

Dr Noor Zaman Hashim of Noor Eye Hospital in Kabul said his staff had conducted 90 transplants in recent months, before the programme had been halted by the Taliban order.

He said the hospital had a growing waiting list, comprising mostly young people who had lost their eyesight because of trauma, injuries, explosions and welding-related accidents.

“Decades of violence have devastated Afghanistan’s healthcare infrastructure. We neither have sufficient ophthalmologists nor locally available corneas to meet the demand for transplants,” he said.

“The Taliban have verbally instructed us to stop the transplants. Nobody has the courage to defy their orders because of the risk of severe punishment,” he said.

News.title: The silent war: As Israel chooses a new leader Gazans wait for life to begin again
News.content:
One year after the ceasefire, Gaza’s health system is still on its knees. Of Gaza’s 228 primary care facilities, only just over half are functioning, according to the WHO.

Medicines are getting in, with almost 87 per cent of requests granted, says the WHO.

It means that someone with a fever or a minor injury can be treated but if it’s anything more complicated there are few options.

None of Gaza’s 36 hospitals are fully functioning, with just 19 partially working, according to the WHO.

There is no MRI scanner anywhere in the Strip, only about 30 per cent of facilities have basic X-rays, and only 12 to 17 per cent have dialysis capability, according to Physicians for Human Rights-Israel (PHRI), a medical NGO founded by Israeli doctors

Chronic illnesses are getting worse. Sally Saleh, head of health and emergency response at Medical Aid for Palestinians (MAP), says there is no capacity to monitor patients or guarantee consistent medical access, so preventable complications from cancer, kidney disease and diabetes will accumulate.

“We need to move beyond simply keeping services alive from one week to the next,” she told The Telegraph.

Power is the biggest hurdle, doctors say. Gaza’s electricity grid has been dead since Israel turned off the supply in October 2023, so hospitals rely on expensive and unreliable generators.

Dr Ahmed Muhanna of Al-Awda Hospital in central Gaza said that when his generators broke down, the hospital rented one for $1,200 a day, but it may only run for 10 hours.

Fuel and spare generator parts are in short supply – but Cogat blames Hamas for stealing fuel and it says that because “Hamas operates inside hospitals” it has to monitor where spare parts end up.

One major problem for those trying to get supplies into the Strip is Israel’s ban on “dual use” items, material it deems serves both a civilian and military purpose. Items that have been blacklisted include generators and metal tent poles.

Cogat says generators, X-ray machines and oxygen concentrators are allowed in under monitoring arrangement with aid groups. But aid agencies told The Telegraph that the rules on what is permitted change from day to day.

Israel allows 15 trucks of dual-use items to enter every week. But the WHO says repeated delays in bringing medical equipment, prosthetics and diagnostic tools into Gaza are delaying patients’ recovery.

In the last six months alone, a single shipment of prosthetics and assistive devices for amputees was rejected four times, the WHO added. It is particularly concerning as Gaza is now home to “the largest cohort of child amputees in modern history”, according to the UN.

“Every rejection means another delay for someone who has already lost a limb and is simply waiting for the chance to walk again,” said Dr Reinhilde Van De Weerdt, WHO Representative in the Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT).

In July Cogat said over 10,300 pallets of health products had been approved since the start of the year, but only 3,238 had reached the crossing. It blamed “a delivery bottleneck” among the organisations that requested them rather than a “Cogat controlled supply bottleneck”.

Crumbling hospitals mean that around 20,000 patients, including 4,000 patients, need urgent medical evacuation. The WHO says about 5,700 patients have been evacuated since the ceasefire. Save the Children estimates that at the current rate the backlog would take four and a half years to clear.

Cogat disputes WHO and UN figures, and says that it has approved the majority of evacuation requests.

Sports.title: Viral Sunday League team with Heskey, Cisse and Drinkwater has brutal forfeits system including shaved heads and fines
Sports.content:
Next

WYTHENSHAWE VETS have a stunning star-studded squad featuring Premier League legends – and they arrange brutal forfeits before heading onto the pitch.

Emile Heskey, Danny Drinkwater and Papiss Cisse are just some of the famous names to have featured for the Sunday league side since hanging up their boots.



And David Norris, who landed a knockout blow when he got in the boxing ring with Simon Cox earlier this month, was recruited by Wythenshawe Vets when he retired from professional football.

The EFL icon, 45, featured for the likes of Ipswich, Portsmouth and Leeds during his career.



But Norris has revealed the banter is still alive and kicking in the Wythenshawe Vets dressing room.

Forfeits and bets are arranged before kick-off, leading to some hilarious moments behind the scenes.



Norris, who reckons the rivalry between Portsmouth and south coast foes Southampton is underrated, told SunSport: “Being back in the dressing room is the best bit.

“The banter is flying because footballers just sink back into those immature roles.

“We had a bet involving one of the lads. He had to score in that game otherwise his head was getting shaved.

“He had a one-on-one and missed it so, after the game, they called for the clippers. He stood there in the changing room and we shaved his hair off.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Huge names to have featured for Wythenshawe Vets Stephen Ireland Emile Heskey Papiss Cisse Antonio Valencia Joleon Lescott Danny Drinkwater Marc Albrighton Oumar Niasse Nedum Onuoha Maynor Figueroa Jefferson Montero David Norris George Boyd Keiren Westwood

“Even on the pitch, the banter is still there if something funny happens or something good comes off.

“We’re starting to bring in fines if anyone turns up in the wrong gear, for example.

“We go for a beer after games and it’s more relaxed than we were used to, so we can enjoy it a bit more.

“There will probably have a Christmas do as well. We try to replicate what we used to do when we were in the Premier League or EFL.

“The group chat’s always going off with something and people are putting memes up of players. It’s good fun.”



Stephen Ireland took over as the viral Wythenshawe Vets’ chief after suffering a gruesome double leg break at the end of last season.

And the former Manchester City midfielder, 40, asked Norris to get involved.

The one-time EFL promotion winner added: “I was doing bits with Stephen Ireland, strength and conditioning wise.



“One day he said he’s involved with this football team. I’d seen that they had managed to rope in a few ex-pros.

“Stephen knows his stuff but he is not the manager out of choice. He broke his leg in one of our games.

“I don’t know too many people who love football more than him, so he’d definitely love to be playing still. I’m sure he’ll come back and start playing again.

“But, for now, he’s taken up the managerial role. With the quality and calibre of players we have, you don’t really need to say too much.”

Norris has been shocked by the quality and fitness levels displayed by some of his team-mates.



He admitted: “Just how good Stephen Ireland is has been an eye-opener for me.

“I played against George Boyd a few times so I knew how good he was and still is.

“When it comes to Papiss Cisse, Marc Albrighton and Danny Drinkwater, you can see they’ve got that next level of thinking that takes them one step ahead.



“I didn’t quite make it to becoming a Premier League regular or featuring in Europe, so now I’m seeing what these lads are doing and what the difference was.

“They’re so fit as well. Normally, the legs go. I’ve played in charity games where you can see some ex-pros have still got the ability but they can’t move.

“We have a really strong team and we don’t really ease off once we go ahead.

“We don’t train and we can pick and choose when we’re available. But you can’t get rid of that competitive edge.”

Sports.title: Max Dowman made unwanted history with red card against Fleetwood – but why Arsenal wonderkid is in good company
Sports.content:
Next

MAX DOWMAN’s sending off against Fleetwood on Tuesday marked a historic occasion.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player in the history of the Carabao Cup – and professional English football – to be sent off.



It is a record no player would hope to set, but one that Arsenal have come close to on a number of occasions.

In fact, of the 8 youngest players to receive a straight red card in a major English competition, four of them did so for Arsenal.



Myles Lewis-Skelly was the most recent of the group before Dowman, and came the closest to breaking the record when he was sent off against Wolves in January 2025.

The versatile star was just 18 years and 121 days old when he was controversially sent off by Michael Oliver for a cynical foul on Matt Doherty.



Only Wayne Rooney – who was sent off for Everton against Birmingham at 17 years and 63 days old in 2002 – was handed a straight red card at a younger age.

Lewis-Skelly then bizarrely contested the dubious honour again less than a month later, when he was sent off against West Ham for hauling down Mohammed Kudus.

Cesc Fabregas may be a keen mind in his role as Como boss, but in 2006 he was a teenager making a splash under Arsene Wenger after breaking into the Gunners first team.

But he got a bit carried away during a clash with Everton and ended up shoving Tim Cahill in the face in injury time, earning himself a red card at the age of 18 years and 262 days old, making him the seventh youngest player to be sent packing.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

There must be something about creative Arsenal midfielders, with the eighth-placed troublemaker being Jack Wilshere.

He was just 26 days older than Fabregas when he saw red for clattering Birmingham star Nikola Zigic in the final moments of their 2010/11 Premier League battle.

But Dowman should not feel too bad about carrying the torch for Arsenal’s pattern of young stars being sent off.



He is in great company on the list of superstars to be sent off early in their career.

The aforementioned Rooney held the title before Dowman, while Liverpool’s future Ballon d’Or winner Michael Owen is the third youngest player overall to be sent off in English football – though his came in the form of two yellows rather than a straight red.

The 18-year-and-117-day-old was handed a second caution not long after levelling a tie against Manchester United in 1998.

United star Shea Lacey’s two yellow cards in quick succession in the 2025/26 season made him the youngest player ever to be sent off in the FA Cup at 18 years and 272 days.



The list of future prospects to once let their discipline slip is even more impressive overseas.

Lionel Messi famously received a red card moments into his Argentina debut against Hungary as an 18-year-old.

The phenom struck a defender in the face with his elbow while escaping a challenge and was briskly sent down the tunnel – but few could argue with the messianic status he would go on to secure with his national side.



Even this year’s favourite for the golden boy award, Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi, got in on the act when he was sent off against Benfica in March 2025 at the age of 18 years and 42 days.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cristiano Ronaldo couldn’t even wait to get on the pitch before receiving his first major telling off, after he was banned for a game at the age of 15 during his Sporting Lisbon days over a row with his coach.

It is a good thing then that Dowman did not react to Arteta’s public chastising of him as he left the field on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Liverpool vs Arsenal gets surprise referee appointment as Chelsea vs Man Utd official also revealed
Sports.content:
Next

REF Andy Madley has been handed his first “Big Six” Prem showdown in two-and-a-half YEARS when he takes charge of Arsenal’s visit to Anfield on Sunday.

Yorkshireman Madley, 43, is in his eighth year on the Prem reffing roster.



But while he has been the man in the middle for five previous games between the Prem’s traditional powerhouses, the last was Manchester City’s March 2024 3-1 derby win over United.

Madley has since taken charge of the 2024 FA Cup Final between the two Manchester giants but his appointment by ProRef boss Howard Webb is a slight surprise.



Michael Oliver, widely recognised as the Prem’s top official and who whistled last week’s game between PSG and Barcelona, is instead reffing Spurs’ home game with Crystal Palace on Saturday.

That appointment suggests he is involved on Champions League duty on Tuesday.



Sunday’s match will be only the sixth time Madley has taken charge of an Arsenal match in the top flight.

The Gunners have won two and lost one of the previous five, the last being the 2-0 home win over Everton in March.

By contrast, he has previously taken charge of 17 Liverpool games.

The Anfield outfit have won nine of those – including the 7-0 humiliation of Manchester United in 2023 – and have lost three times.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The weekend’s other crunch game, Chelsea’s home match with struggling Manchester United, has been handed to Peter Bankes, excellent in Aston Villa’s win over Manchester City on Saturday.

The game between Liverpool and Arsenal will be a crucial one early in the season as the Gunners look to keep pace with Man City at the top of the table.

Liverpool, meanwhile, are just six points off the Gunners in the build up to the showdown.



Andoni Iraola‘s side have an impressive record against Arsenal at home and haven’t lost to the north Londoners since September 2012.

As for Chelsea and United, the game comes after both sides suffered a dismal defeat last time out.

Chelsea were beaten 2-0 at home to rivals Tottenham, while United were on the end of a 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth.

That dreadful result extended Michael Carrick‘s run without a win to EIGHT games.

The former United star has been given more time in the role despite coming under fire and falling out with captain Bruno Fernandes.



But a bad result at Stamford Bridge could see him axed amid speculation Eddie Howe or Antonio Conte could take over.

Sports.title: Max Dowman was unlucky to be sent off against Fleetwood – Cole Palmer incident was worse than Arsenal star
Sports.content:
Next

MAX DOWMAN became the youngest player in English football history to be shown a straight red card – but was he hard done by?

The Arsenal wonderkid, 16, was given his marching orders in the 85th minute in the shock Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood.



Midfielder Dowman reacted to a heavy challenge by Harrison Neal with ref Michael Salisbury deciding he had kicked out.

Mikel Arteta angrily stared at Dowman as he trudged off, and it proved costly as the Gunners lost on penalties to the League Two side.



Dowman faces a three-match ban – starting with the visit to Liverpool in the Prem on Sunday – but the Gunners have appealed.

And former Premier League referee Mark Halsey reckons the decision could be overturned.

Halsey said: “Max Dowman was unlucky to be sent off for his retaliation towards at Harrison Neal during Arsenal’s disaster Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood on Tuesday night.

“The teenager was petulant and aggressive towards his opponent, but he did not commit the offence of violent conduct.

“Dowman’s incident has been compared to Cole Palmer’s first yellow card for his sending off against Tottenham on Saturday evening.

“I said at the time that a yellow card for Palmer’s bump into Mateus Fernandes was the correct decision, and I think Dowman’s frustrated “kick” was the same.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“There’s not a lot of difference between the two challenges, if anything Palmer’s was a little more aggressive than Dowman’s.

“For me, Dowman has not committed violent conduct, but rather has adopted an aggressive attitude towards an opponent.

“That is exactly what happened with Palmer.

“Dowman was frustrated by being on the end of a hefty challenge from Fleetwood’s Neal, but the defender clearly got the ball.

“The follow through was obviously heavy, but we have to allow those kinds of challenges in the game.



“If we take those out, we might as well not have a football game.

“The 16-year-old retaliated, and he was wrong to do so, but there is not enough for violent conduct and a red card.

“Arsenal are appealing the decision, which was a difficult one for referee Michael Salisbury, who didn’t have the aid of VAR the same way that Chris Kavanagh did for Palmer’s yellow card.

“I thought Dowman was unfortunate to be sent off, which could mean the decision is overturned if the panel takes the same view.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“If not, he will still face a three-match ban for his actions.



“That ban will carry into the Premier League, meaning Dowman will miss Arsenal’s trip to Anfield to face Liverpool this Sunday as well as their games at home to Hull City and away against Newcastle.”

Sports.title: Liverpool contact Lamine Camara’s camp with January transfer not ruled out as Chelsea turn attention to Alex Scott
Sports.content:
Next

LIVERPOOL have made contact with Lamine Camara’s camp again as they step up their interest in the Monaco midfielder ahead of the January transfer window.

SunSport understands the Reds have asked to be kept informed of developments surrounding the Senegal international, who came agonisingly close to joining Chelsea in the summer.



Talks are continuing behind the scenes, with Liverpool keen to explore the possibility of bringing the highly-rated midfielder to Anfield.

A January move has not been ruled out, although any deal would require compromises from Liverpool, Monaco and the player himself.



Liverpool are looking to strengthen their midfield with a player of Camara’s profile, and the 22-year-old has emerged as an attractive option.

The Senegalese star was left disappointed after his proposed switch to Chelsea collapsed in the summer but he has refused to let that setback derail his progress.

Instead, Camara has knuckled down at Monaco and continued to establish himself as one of the most exciting young midfielders in French football.

He has started ten of Monaco’s 12 matches this season, scoring twice and providing an assist as the French side sit fourth in Ligue 1.

But it is not just his performances on the pitch that have caught the eye, with his maturity and attitude following the Chelsea disappointment earning admiration.

Camara has shown remarkable resilience for a player of his age, while his energy, athleticism and ability to influence games have made him a standout performer.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

His manager has been particularly impressed by the youngster’s response and believes he possesses qualities that could make him a special player for years to come.

Filipe Luis recently told L’Equipe: “In twenty years’ time, we may well see plenty of players like him.

“He can run a marathon, play for ninety minutes without ever letting up, whilst playing football. He embodies the future of the game.”

Those qualities have only strengthened Liverpool’s interest, with the Reds believing Camara has the attributes to thrive in the intensity of the Premier League.



Liverpool are currently understood to be leading the race for his signature, with Chelsea now turning their attention towards Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott.

And while a move to England is not guaranteed in January, there is a growing feeling that Camara’s future could eventually lie in the Premier League.

The midfielder has also been keeping a close eye on the progress of his Senegalese compatriots in England, particularly close friend Nicolas Jackson and rising youngster Ibrahim Mbaye.

Both made their mark as Aston Villa ended Manchester City‘s perfect start to the Premier League season, with Jackson scoring twice and Mbaye providing an assist.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fellow Senegal international Iliman Ndiaye was also involved in the action, setting up City’s goal in a match that showcased the growing influence of Senegalese players in English football.

The trio later celebrated their contributions by sharing a picture in their Senegal WhatsApp group, and Camara will be hoping he gets the chance to join his international pals in the Premier League before too long.

Sports.title: Differential options for Gameweek 9: Brian Brobbey among bold selections due to favourable double header
Sports.content:
Next

WE know there are plenty of Dream Team managers who like to play the game their own way.

Sometimes it’s sensible to follow the crowd but other times it pays to go against the grain by recruiting a player overlooked by over 95% of gaffers.

With that in mind, allow us to present some differential options for Gameweek 9.



Brian Brobbey (£3m)

It takes a lot of courage to use a transfer on a player who represents the team currently bottom of the league.



But there’s method to this madness as Sunderland’s Gameweek 9 double header is a very favourable one on paper.

The Black Cats travel to struggling Coventry on Saturday and will then host Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League on Thursday.

Brobbey averages 5.6 points-per-game this season and is his side’s primary goal threat — let’s not forget he bagged a hat-trick at the Etihad before his recent hamstring injury.

The Dutchman features in 4.2% of teams right now and this minority of Dream Team bosses will be hopeful of healthy returns this coming Gameweek.

Granit Xhaka (£3.5m), Enzo Le Fee (£3.3m) and Nilson Angulo (£3.3m) are the viable midfield options.

Bear in mind, Sunderland are due to host Brentford later today — watch out for availability problems.

James Hill (£3.4m)



This is a perfectly logical recommendation.

Bournemouth’s No5 is statistically the most in-form defender in the game at the time of writing having notched 32 points across his last three outings.

He produced a heroic performance at Old Trafford, making seven tackles and earning three bonus points via four blocks and four interceptions on top of the Cherries’ clean sheet for a 13-point return.

Marco Rose’s side have kept four consecutive clean sheets and suddenly Hill’s ownership of 0.8% looks ridiculously low.

Bournemouth are scheduled to host Aston Villa in the Carabao Cup this evening but their following fixtures are nothing to fear: Leeds (h), Sparta Prague (a), Ipswich (a), Nottingham Forest (h), Celta Vigo (a), Fulham (a), Brighton (h), Hull (h), Viktoria Plzen (h).



That friendly run takes Hill and company to mid-December.

Tottenham Punts

Spurs don’t have a second fixture in Gameweek 9 which puts them at a disadvantage as nine teams will double up but allow us to explain our reasoning.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side will host Crystal Palace on Saturday, which is one of the most appealing match-ups the Premier League has to offer at this moment in time.

The Eagles have the worst defensive record in the top flight this season having conceded 19 goals in their first eight games.



Tottenham’s attackers will be licking their lips, Mathys Tel (£2.9m), Mohammed Kudus (£4.2m) and Omar Marmoush (£4.4m) in particular — the latter is the most popular of the three with an ownership of 1.5%.

1.2%-owned Mateus Fernandes (£3.3m) is a decent option too off the back of his impressive all-round display against Chelsea.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Alternatively, Jan Paul van Hecke (£4.2m) quietly boasts an impressive average of 5.8 points-per-game, matching Josko Gvardiol (£5.3m).

With Leeds and Ipswich to come after Palace, Spurs will be hopeful of clean sheets in the coming weeks.

Sports.title: The strict anti-booze diet, secret guilty treats, and fitness regime behind England captain Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or win
Sports.content:
Next

FOOTBALL legends of the past may have fuelled their career on pints and fry-ups, but today’s heroes are much more conscious of their diets.

Many of the world’s top footballers have private chefs, follow concise diet plans and intense fitness routines to give themselves the longevity to stay in the game well into their 30s.



In the form of his life at 33, Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane is the poster boy for the modern elite athlete.

Powered by a strict regime, zero alcohol and a secret sweet tooth, the England skipper is rewriting the rulebook on physical endurance.



Like a vintage wine, Kane is getting better with age.

SunSport looks how the Three Lions superstar maintains his peak condition…

Anti-party stance

It was a little unusual to see Kane enjoying his Ballon d’Or success into the early hours at exclusive London nightclub Cirque Le Soir on Monday night.

It was even more out of a character to see him lifting a shot glass in the air, because Kane is teetotal during the season. He does allow himself a cocktail on holiday when he has a rare summer off.

Kane is the anti-party pioneer, preferring to spend his spare time at home with his wife, Katie Goodland and their kids.

To unwind, he regularly plays golf and walks his dogs, Brady and Wilson.



He told Football365: “I like to keep things private and I think that’s all down to the type of person I am. I’m a pretty normal guy and do normal things. I’ve never been someone who goes out to nightclubs.

“When I have spare time, I like to spend it with my wife and kids, I like to play some golf.

“Unfortunately, there are some things that are a bit more difficult to do when you are going to a busy place and people recognise you. In general, I’m just a pretty normal guy.”



The Kate factor

One of the biggest factors of Kane’s incredible durability and lack of major muscular injuries isn’t just through the excellent club facilities at Bayern.

It starts at home with wife Katie, a qualified sports science graduate and fitness instructor, and his personal chef Dan Sergeant.

Kane’s diet isn’t about carb-loading. He routinely treats food as an adaptive performance tool that can change based on his daily physical load.

To combat joint strain and muscle soreness, the forward will drink tumeric and ginger shots, which targets post-match muscle inflammation.



His go-to breakfasts are eggs and avocado on brown bread, or a spinach omelette to provide healthy fats and proteins that aid cellular repair.

Slow-cooked bone broth dishes, naturally rich in collagen, glycine, and glucosamine, which directly reinforce tendon elasticity and joint recovery, also figure in Kane’s diet.

On low-intensity days, he will pivot to lighter proteins, including white fish, salmon and chicken, often paired with vegetables or salad.



But even Kane has a cheat meal

To match the longevity of the likes of Critiano Ronaldo, 42, and Robert Lewandowski, 38, staying fit and not being tempted by too many cheat meals is key.

According to reports, Kane does enjoy a crispy chicken burger loaded with coleslaw and spicy mayo, classic cheeseburgers, steak and ribs.

He has a sweet tooth and weakness for a traditional British dessert.

When asked what his guilty pleasure was in an interview with The Telegraph in 2017, he quickly revealed: “Apple crumble!”



He has it with custard, bringing a slice of home to Bavaria.

Kane has also been partial to a Five Guys chocolate milkshake, but those occasions are few and far between.

Recovery tech and home gym

Living in the ultra-exclusive Grünwald area, Bavaria’s answer to Hollywood, Kane lives a peaceful and quiet life.

He has a home gym, a sauna and all the best recovery and wellness tools money can buy.

One of the most recent things Kane has said has benefited him is electro-acupuncture.

The science says it targets peripheral nerves, relieves tension and restores optimal muscle firing patterns.

A staple of his post-match and post-training routine is targeted cryotherapy and ice baths.



By submerging his body in sub-zero water, he is able to flush away metabolic waste, combat acute inflammation and drastically cut down on delayed onset muscle soreness.

Kane’s wellness centre in his Bavarian home features an infrared sauna.



They are better than traditional dry saunas because infrared heat penetrates deeper into muscle tissue.

It increases localised blood flow, promotes cellular repair, and aids detoxification without putting unnecessary cardiovascular strain on the body.

Kane’s home gym includes dedicated equipment for Nordic hamstring curls, incline treadmill running, and eccentric strength training to protect his lower limbs during long grueling seasons.

But, away from the fancy equipment, Kane’s biggest weapon in his arsenal is sleep.
