Kane even has a specialised sleep setup, from bespoke foam mattress toppers to gel cooling pillows that regulate core body temperature, reduce late-night match adrenaline, and maximise athletic recovery.

Sports.title: Spanish Football Federation postpone all 24 Copa Del Rey fixtures today after fatal train crash
Sports.content:
Next

SPAIN’S FA has suspended Wednesday’s Copa del Rey schedule following the tragic railway crash in Toledo.

At least 50 people were killed and 179 injured after two high-speed trains collided between the towns of Los Yebenes and Urda.



Horror footage has shown smoke coming from the scene as two carriages were derailed off the line connecting Madrid to the southern Andalusia region.

And the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) has now announced that all 24 games in their domestic cup competition will be postponed after the country was plunged into mourning.



An RFEF statement read: “OFFICIAL. Today’s Copa del Rey matches have been suspended.

“As a sign of respect and solidarity with all the victims of the tragic train accident that occurred early Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo, the RFEF (Royal Spanish Football Federation) has suspended all 24 matches of the first round of the Spanish Championship-Copa del Rey (King’s Cup) originally scheduled for this afternoon and evening.



“The RFEF will announce the revised tournament schedule and the final times for the postponed matches in the coming days.

“The great Spanish football family remains united in grief over this tragedy, offering its support to the authorities to help the victims of this devastating accident.”

Wednesday’s matches involved five Spanish top flight teams, including Levante, Alaves, Valencia, Celta Vigo and Real Betis.

It is not known what will happen with the 14 matches set to be played on Thursday.

Thursday’s schedule will see more high profile teams such as Sevilla, Athletic Bilbao and Getafe feature in the cup competition.



Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atletico Madrid and Real Sociedad do not enter the competition until the Round of 32 in December.

The Copa Del Rey is Spain’s oldest football cup competition after being founded in 1903.

Spain has been rocked by the shocking derailment following the crash involving the Iryo and AVE trains, with the death toll likely to rise.



There were 146 passengers onboard the Iryo train, including one baby, at the time of the accident.

Some 397 passengers were onboard the AVE service.

Emergency services rushed to the scenes to help victims trapped in the carriages as one told Capital Radio he was “blown into the air”.

Another witness told Onda Cero that the Iryo train was stationary on the tracks for about five minutes before the “incredible impact”.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on X: “Shocked by the serious train accident in Toledo. I remain in constant contact with the transport minister, Oscar Puente, and the president of Castilla-La Mancha, Emiliano Garcia-Page.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Emergency services are working on the ground to assist those affected and ensure their safety, in coordination with all the involved administrations.

“My affection, solidarity, and support to all the victims and their families.”

Sports.title: Lewis: I've earned my England RL World Cup spot
Sports.content:
Mikey Lewis insists he has ‘earned’ his place in England’s Rugby League World Cup squad despite limited game time so far.

The 2024 Man of Steel winner with Hull KR, Lewis struggled for form during the course of the 2026 Super League season, but was included in Brian McDermott's England squad for the World Cup.

Yet the 25-year-old was left out of the matchday squad for England's opening 30-12 defeat to Tonga and was initially overlooked again for their second clash with France, before a late reshuffle saw him named on the bench.

Lewis emerged for the final 20 minutes against the French, scoring two tries as part of a crushing 82-0 victory.

For Friday's must-win contest against Papua New Guinea in Wollongong, Lewis has been named in the squad on the bench.

"The way my year went wasn't really the best, I don't need anyone else to tell me," Lewis said. "I just had to put myself in the shop window. I have earned my spot.

Image: Lewis was left out of the squad to face Tonga, and was initially out of the squad to face France before being drafted in

"I'll always represent my country to the best of my ability. I was told to run with the ball, and I wanted to play with a smile on my face.

"Last week the hard work was done, my job was to go and cause havoc - that was my instruction, and I did that.

"I might get different instructions this week, but I'll do it, because I am proud to play for my country - 20 minutes is 20 minutes for England, I don't really care it's only 20 minutes."

Image: Lewis emerged off the bench for the final 20 minutes against France, scoring two tries

'We still have a fighting chance of making semi-finals'

Speaking to media last week, head coach McDermott said Lewis had shown "humility" in camp, adding he had endured "a frustrating end to the season."

For McDermott, Lewis and England, attentions now turn to the task of qualifying for the semi-finals.

A potential first-ever group-stage exit at the Rugby League World Cup loomed after England's heavy opening defeat to Tonga, and despite thrashing France, their semi-final hopes remain out of their hands.

The tournament's unusual format sees Groups B and C merge into a six-team table, with only the top two sides advancing to the semi-finals.

England have two points heading into Friday's final pool clash with Papua New Guinea and need a convincing victory, alongside favourable results elsewhere, to stand any chance of progressing.

Image: England coach Brian McDermott has branded the Rugby League World Cup format 'harsh,' with his side up against it to progress

Quite simply, before Tonga face Samoa, England must beat Papua New Guinea and do it by a considerable margin.

Samoa's thumping 78-4 win over France in their tournament opener and a 64-6 victory over Papua New Guinea on Saturday leaves them with an impressive +132 point difference.

England beating France takes them to a +64 points difference, 68 points behind Samoa heading into the final round of fixtures. Another win Friday would lift them to four points and level with both Samoa and Tonga.

McDermott's side would then be left to wait 48 hours for the outcome of Tonga vs Samoa in Sydney. A Samoa win would guarantee England's elimination, while a Tonga victory would see the points difference decide second spot.

Image: Lewis says England still have 'fighting chance' of making semi-finals

England don't necessarily need to beat Papua New Guinea by 68 points or more, but a victory by that margin would mean any loss for Samoa would be enough to progress.

A smaller England win would see them need Samoa losing by a bigger score, depending on England's final points difference.

"We just have to go out and do what we have planned," Lewis said.

"It will be a tough game, but we have the strike and desire.

"We have a fighting chance, we believe in that. So, we just have to put the hard work in. It is a unique position, so just enjoy that."

Sports.title: Ref Watch: Arsenal's red card appeal will fail - Dowman was aggressive
Sports.content:
Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher believes Arsenal's appeal against Max Dowman's red card in their shock Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town will fail.

Dowman was sent off for violent conduct after kicking out at Harrison Neal following the defender's strong challenge on the teenager late in the fourth-round tie, which Arsenal lost on penalties.

Arsenal must submit appeal documents by 1pm on Thursday and are hopeful a decision will be made before their match at Liverpool, live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

However, when asked if he thought Arsenal's appeal would be successful, Gallagher told Sky Sports News: "I don't, because of the aggressiveness of Dowman, and you can see the intent. I think it will fail."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Dowman SENT-OFF as Gunners go down to 10-men.

He added: "I think it is [a red card]. People are comparing it to Cole Palmer on Saturday (with Mateus Fernandes), I think Dowman is a little bit more aggressive.

"He knows what he's doing. He almost brings his knee up in a kicking action."

Gallagher believes Arsenal should also have been awarded a free-kick, and Neal a yellow card, for his tackle on Dowman.

"Although Neal gets the ball, he's too aggressive," said Gallagher. "It's a reckless challenge and he's had little regard to the safety of Dowman.

"Neal is not bothered whether he catches him afterwards. He was always going to get Dowman. He knows when he makes that tackle what he's going to do. That's enough for a free-kick and a yellow card."

'Dowman will get kicked all his career'

Sky Sports' Paul Merson felt the red card was harsh, but that Dowman must be prepared to face strong challenges throughout his career.

"The tackle from the lad is an old-fashioned tackle. He gets the ball, follows through at the same time. In a way, I would say, it's a great tackle," he said.

"And then Dowman's retaliating. His foot's got caught. I don't think it's as bad as what everybody says. I think the reaction of the players has sort of made his decision.

"It's not that bad. In my opinion, it wasn't a red card. I don't think it should have been given.

"The kid's 16 years of age. Let's not get away from it. My worry is that at Arsenal, and when you play for one of the big clubs, which I found out later in my career, you get told once or twice, and that is it.

"And he's been told again. Obviously, Arteta's told him. He got sent off the other week for England against the USA. He's going to get that for the whole of his career. He's going to be kicked.

"People are going to look at the game now, and they're going to go, 'Right, we've got to upset him. Try and get inside him. Try and upset him'. And he's got to be better than that."

Merson and McAnuff question Arteta reaction

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul Merson has shared his concerns for Max Dowman following the red card the teenager picked up in the League Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town.

As Dowman headed towards the tunnel and past the dugouts, Mikel Arteta leaned in and said something to the teenager, which Merson criticised, saying the Arsenal manager should have put an arm around him.

Asked what he said to Dowman, Arteta told reporters: "It was something that we discussed before the game." Arteta refused to go into any more detail when pressed.

Asked whether Dowman has something to learn from the incident, Arteta replied: "We knew when we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to expect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate."

Reacting to the incident, Merson said: "If that's [Viktor] Gyokeres, who's an experienced international, he [Arteta] isn't doing that - but he does that to a 16-year-old kid?

"He's not the last person to get sent off for Arsenal, nor the first. If it was me, I'd have put my arm around him. It's still 1-1, they're still in the game.

"We all say things in life we wish we hadn't and if he [Arteta] could have that back, he'd do it differently."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former MK Dons manager Karl Robinson is clearly impressed with Arsenal's decision to appeal Max Dowman's red card against Fleetwood, describing it, on Sky Sports FC, as 'genius leadership'.

Fellow Sky Sports pundit Jobi McAnuff said: "I can't understand the reaction. Arteta probably feels it was petulant, naive which I think it is.

"It is frustration from Dowman, but when you see the reaction from Arteta... we have to remember he's 16.

"Yes, he's a fantastic talent, but he will make mistakes along the way. I didn't like the reaction at all."

He added: "Dowman is potentially the future of Arsenal. Arteta didn't get that quite right."

Sports.title: McLaren plan further upgrades after Austin struggles
Sports.content:
McLaren plan to bring more upgrades to the car in the remaining rounds of the 2026 Formula 1 season after struggling to compete at the front in recent races.

Since Lando Norris missed out on victory in Madrid last month, McLaren have failed to finish on the podium in the last four races, despite bringing new parts to the car in that period.

After qualifying eighth at last weekend's United States Grand Prix, Norris described the MCL40 as "easily the hardest car I've ever driven in my life".

Norris ran in second place late on in the race by adopting an alternative one-stop strategy but was overtaken late on by Charles Leclerc, Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton as he dropped to fifth, while Oscar Piastri finished seventh.

"There will be some more stuff coming," said team principal Andrea Stella on McLaren's upgrade plans, given most teams are now focusing on designing their 2027 cars.

"I think ultimately we will only be able to do so across Brazil and Vegas. So, Mexico there won't be very much, but Brazil and Vegas there will be some upgrades.

"Hopefully this will help us to be consistently in the fight for podiums and hopefully start to lean on the level of competitiveness that is required to fight for the victory. So, there's a few upgrades that are still in the pipeline."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc makes two great overtakes on Lando Norris and Max Verstappen in Austin

McLaren confirmed in their press release ahead of this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix that the team "remains committed to learning, developing and extracting the maximum from the MCL40 at every opportunity".

"After the successful introduction of changes to the front and rear corners of the MCL40 in Austin, the car will remain essentially unchanged going into this weekend's race," they added.

"This will therefore only see a small selection of parts delivered to track in Mexico City through the team's development pathway with further developments in the pipeline for the remaining rounds of the 2026 season, starting from the race in Sao Paulo."

Formula 1 2026 remaining races Mexico This weekend Qatar November 27-29 Brazil November 6-8 Abu Dhabi December 4-6 Las Vegas November 20-22

Norris points to qualifying as a weakness

Norris has claimed three pole positions this year in Budapest, Zandvoort and Madrid, but his biggest margin to second place in those qualifying sessions was 0.102s.

The car appears to have been on a knife edge throughout the season, which Piastri has struggled more with, and Norris says the slow-speed corners have also been an issue for the team.

"There's been a lot of races we have shone and done a very good job. Qualifyings we have struggled," Norris told Sky Sports F1.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris admits he did a 'terrible job' during Austin qualifying and that the McLaren is the 'hardest car' he has ever driven

"We roughly know where we need to improve the car. I think in Austin it was clear the slow-speed corners we lost almost three tenths a lap, every single lap. That's a chunky bit of lap time to lose so consistently.

"We need to improve in certain areas. If we can do that, I'm very confident we can have some good results but it seems to be a challenging area for us to improve as much as we like.

"We will keep working hard. The team are doing a very good job and we will keep trying to pick away."

Davidson: McLaren car suits high grip tracks Sky Sports F1's Anthony Davidson



“McLaren seem to suit a high grip surface and that’s not what we had in Austin or Malaysia. They are better on medium to high-speed corners like Budapest, Zandvoort, Madrid.



“Mexico is a track Lando likes. It’s not a bumpy track, so let’s see how Lando can go there this year. It’s one of his best tracks and he dominated last year’s race there.”

Sports.title: Nations Championship: Schedule as inaugural tournament gears up for finals
Sports.content:
It has been labelled a "tectonic shift", set to shake up the world of rugby union, but what is the Nations Championship, what have been the results so far, and what is the schedule this November?

What is it?

The Nations Championship is World Rugby's new 12-team tournament that pits the giants of northern and southern hemisphere rugby against each other on a more consistent basis.

The tournament is designed to align northern and southern hemisphere rugby calendars, guaranteeing high-profile fixtures to add more structure and meaning to the existing international windows between World Cups.

Who's involved?

The Six Nations teams - England, France, Ireland, Scotland, Wales and Italy - will take on the four Rugby Championship sides - South Africa, New Zealand, Australia, Argentina (SANZAAR) - with Fiji and Japan also representing the southern hemisphere.

Image: Twickenham will host the inaugural Nations Championship Finals Weekend at Allianz Stadium

How does it work?

Each team will play six matches: three in July in the southern hemisphere and three in November in the northern hemisphere.

Twickenham's Allianz Stadium will then host Finals Weekend from November 27 to 29, where the inaugural champions will be crowned.

Rankings for Finals Weekend will be determined by results from the opening six matches, with each northern hemisphere team playing an additional fixture against the correspondingly ranked southern side.

Sports.title: Carrick and Fernandes hold clear-the-air talks ahead of Chelsea fixture
Sports.content:
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick and captain Bruno Fernandes have met face to face to clear the air, with both vowing to refocus on turning the club's season around.

Fernandes was an unused substitute after being dropped for the 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth on Sunday after he criticised Carrick's tactics following the 4-1 thrashing at Como in the Champions League.

Carrick had described his reasons for dropping his captain as "pure football".

"Picking the team is always a difficult decision," Carrick told Sky Sports. "We've got to make what we feel is the right one for the team to try to get the performance we want."

However, Carrick and Fernandes met at United's training ground on Tuesday, Sky Sports News has been told, for an open and frank discussion, with the head coach satisfied the animosity between them is over, although it is not known if the midfielder apologised for his public criticism.

Fernandes is now expected to be in contention for United's Premier League game against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

The individual meeting between Carrick and Fernandes was in addition to an all-squad meeting, where there was a renewed determination from all the players and staff that performances have to improve immediately.

There was also a mutual admission, we are told, that there has been a squad-wide underperformance so far this season.

Carrick and the Man Utd players have been given the chance to turn their form around despite the under-pressure head coach thought to be on the brink after Sunday's defeat.
