Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes set for Man United return after fresh talks with Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes set for Man United return after fresh talks with Michael Carrick

Bruno Fernandes is expected to start for Manchester United against Chelsea on Saturday, talkSPORT understands.

The Red Devils captain is set to return to the side following clear-the-air talks with Michael Carrick.



3 Carrick is set to recall Fernandes after clear-the-air talks Manchester City Credit: Getty

Fernandes was an unused substitute for last weekend's home defeat to Bournemouth.

Carrick dropped his skipper after the Portugal midfielder criticised his tactics following their Champions League loss to Como.

The United boss later explained that his decision had been for 'pure football' reasons.



Fernandes return

However, Fernandes is now in line for an immediate return to the side in their next match.

It follows talks between the pair ahead of training at Carrington on Wednesday.



United travel to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, October 31.

The match is scheduled to kick-off at 12.30pm, live on talkSPORT.

Carrick will remain in charge for the fixture amid mounting pressure on the former Red Devils midfielder.



United have given their current manager more time to turn their fortunes around.

His side are winless in eight matches in all competitions following Sunday's 3-0 loss to Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

3 Fernandes was an unused substitute against Bournemouth Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

The result leaves the Red Devils 16th in the Premier League and only a point above the bottom three.



Their last win came at home to Azeri champions Sabah in the Champions League last month.

Meanwhile, they have not tasted victory in the Premier League since beating Ipswich Town on August 30.

Fernandes form this season

Fernandes scored a hat-trick in that fixture as well as providing an assist for Bryan Mbeumo.

However, those remain his only league goal contributions in seven appearances this season.



The 32-year-old's only other goal came against Sabah on September 10.

3 Fernandes has four goals for United this season but has failed to score in seven matches Credit: Getty

Fernandes has since failed to score or assist in seven matches across all competitions.

It follows his nine goals and 22 assists for United last season, which included a record 21 Premier League assists as they finished third.

Sports.title: Harry Kane’s ex-teacher reveals inside story behind picture of Ballon d’Or winner and his wife with David Beckham
Sports.content:
Harry Kane’s ex-teacher reveals inside story behind picture of Ballon d’Or winner and his wife with David Beckham

Harry Kane's former teacher has revealed the kids on the playground have swapped 'Bending it Like Beckham' for 'Hammering it like Harry.'

The Chingford Foundation School is the only school to produce two England captains in Golden Balls and the winner of the Golden Ball.

3 Harry Kane scooped the Ballon d'Or award in London on Monday night Credit: AFP

Kane beat out competition from Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or in 25 years.

And it was a full-circle moment for Mark Leadon, who sent the Bayern Munich star a touching message ahead of the 2-2 draw with Arsenal.

On how inspiring it was to see Kane claim the Ballon d'Or, the PE teacher told talkSPORT: "Oh, absolutely, and it was a bit like a full circle because when I first started the school, which was probably around 95, it was all talk about David Beckham in the playground.

"And of course, as Harry became famous and it was talked about, the boys and girls in the playground wanted to be like Harry.

"You never know, there might be a third one come along sometime.

"We've been told that we're the only school to produce two England captains, so it's again something that we're really, really proud about."

Part of Kane's legacy is 'his work ethic'

The 33-year-old, who is the first Englishman to lift the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001, scored an incredible 73 goals in 65 matches for Bayern and England during the 2025/26 season.

He broke endless records en route to lifting the Bundesliga, the German Cup and German Super Cup, while also captaining the Three Lions to their best World Cup finish since 1966.

Mr Leadon added: "I think part of his legacy is not just on the field, obviously; his stats and the numbers speak for themselves, but the way he carries himself, the work ethic, the leadership that he's shown.

3 Kane and his now-wife, Katie Goodland, started dating seven years after this picture with Beckham at the 2005 launch of his academy in Greenwich

"It really has shown through, and there are so many little narratives, and I remember his work ethic, not just in PE and sport but throughout the curriculum in all the subjects that he did.

"He worked hard; students liked him, teachers liked him.

"They had nothing but respect for him, and that was part of his work the work ethic that he put in dedication."

Young Kane and his wife with Beckham

Kane is married to his childhood sweetheart, Kate, with the couple sharing four children together.

The former classmates were famously pictured alongside Beckham at the opening of his academy in Greenwich, in 2005.

3 England captain Kane shares four children with wife Katie Goodland Credit: Getty

Mr Leadon continued: "There's that famous photograph on social media with David Beckham flanked by Katie and Harry on the other side.

"We helped open the David Beckham Academy by taking our students in a minibus down there, and they asked us, 'Can we have a photo shoot?'

"And they wanted the best boy and the best girl footballer, and obviously we picked Harry and Katie.

"Who was to know that all those years later what came to pass - that alone is an amazing story, I think!"

Sports.title: Fleetwood goalkeeper reveals specific Arsenal plan that led to Max Dowman red
Sports.content:
Fleetwood Town planned to wind up the Arsenal players before Max Dowman was sent off during their Carabao Cup fourth round win.

The teenage forward was shown a straight red card as the Gunners were beaten on penalties by their League Two opponents.



4 Dowman's red card was part of Fleetwood's plan against Arsenal, says their goalkeeper Credit: Getty

Dowman was dismissed for violent conduct after kicking out at Fleetwood midfielder Harrison Neal.

It followed a strong tackle from Neal on the Arsenal teenager.

The Gunners have since appealed against the decision, which will see Dowman miss their next three Premier League matches.

Fleetwood's plan for Dowman

Fleetwood goalkeeper Jay Lynch has now revealed Matt Lawlor's side planned such tackles on the Arsenal players.



Their intention during the match was to get stuck in and wind up their rivals, the shot-stopper told the Sports Breakfast on Wednesday morning.

Lynch added that the Fleetwood players wanted the weather to be as bad as possible at Highbury Stadium during the match.



Speaking to Alan Brazil and Dean Saunders, he was asked if there was a plan to get a foot in and disrupt Arsenal.

The 33-year-old explained: "Yes, obviously you’ve seen it with the Max Dowman tackle, their sending off.



"That’s what we’re about, that’s what League Two is about. It’s about winning your duels fairly, I think it was a fair tackle.

"Obviously we’ve had a storm at the minute with the weather, we actually wanted it as bad as possible.

4 Lynch revealed Fleetwood intended to wind up their Arsenal rivals Credit: AFP

"As we drove into the stadium, the sun is shining, we’re thinking ‘oh no, this suits them,’ then the wind comes, we’re like, ‘alright, game on.’"



Lynch, who joined the club in 2022, went on to save Bruno Guimaraes' spot-kick as Fleetwood won 5-3 on penalties following a 1-1 draw.

The Fishermen are now into the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup for the first time in their history.

They are also the first League Two club to reach the last eight since Colchester United in 2019.

Should Dowman have been sent off?

Arsenal's appeal against Dowman's red card comes after referee Michael Salisbury's controversial decision to send off the 16-year-old.



It comes less than a month after he was dismissed whilst playing for England's Under-19s against the USA for violent conduct.

4 Arsenal are set to appeal against Dowman's red card Credit: Getty

Sam Matterface, Danny Murphy and Brad Friedel discussed the incident live on talkSPORT on Wednesday morning.

Reacting to the referee's call, Murphy explained: "It’s a ridiculous decision. The referee losing it a little bit really, a competent referee would have just nipped it in the bud.



"He didn’t lash out, it wasn’t violent, he just nudged into him because he took a hefty whack.

"The tackle was fine. It’s not a sending off either. He got the ball and then left a little bit on him."

Meanwhile, Friedel believes a different referee may have handled the situation better.

He added: "A referee in control possibly could have booked the first tackle, but what he would have done is he would have had a word with that player, pulled Dowman to one side, had a word with him.



4 Referee Salisbury has been criticised for his handling of the red card incident Credit: Getty

"Maybe give the booking out to the first tackle, tell everyone else, ‘get out of my face’, and if someone got in his face, maybe book them for dissent or something like that and then it’s done.

"It’s not a problem for the manager to basically tell Dowman, you need to control your emotions, because this could happen, it could be a Champions League final coming up."

As for how the incident could affect Dowman, Murphy added that it could prove to be a learning experience for the youngster.



The former England midfielder admitted: "I think it’s great because Arsenal are looking at bigger fish than League Cups this year. They want the Champions League, they want the league again.

"So if he’d have done that in a Champions League knockout game, a head-to-head game where he’s come on against Manchester City or Liverpool on Sunday at Anfield.

"Because if he comes off the bench or starts at Anfield and it’s lively, he’s not going to do that again now, is he? I think he’ll learn a hell of a lot."

If Arsenal's appeal against Dowman's red card is successful, he will be cleared to face Liverpool on Sunday.



At present, the winger will miss the match along with upcoming fixtures against Hull City and Newcastle United through suspension.

Sports.title: Ashley Cole interviewed for first EFL job but faces competition from Championship coach
Sports.content:
Ashley Cole interviewed for first EFL job but faces competition from Championship coach

Ashley Cole has been interviewed by League One Bromley over their vacant manager role.

Bromley sacked Andy Woodman with the club 22nd in the third tier of English football.

3 Ashley Cole spent eight games in Serie B last season - before leaving in the summer Credit: Getty

The Ravens have enjoyed a meteoric rise up the pyramid over the last three seasons.

Following promotion from the National League in 2024, they finished top of League Two last season.

Ashley Cole to Bromley?

talkSPORT understands Chelsea and England legend Cole was interviewed by Bromley on Tuesday.

He is believed to have competition from Blackburn assistant manager Mike Dodds.

This would represent Cole's first managerial role in England.

The 45-year-old had an eight-game spell in charge of Serie B Cesana last season.

Since retiring, Cole has held coaching roles at Derby, Chelsea, Everton and Birmingham.

He has also been part of the coaching staff with the England Under-21s and senior squad.

Speaking to The Guardian after being hired by Cesana, Cole said: “I really appreciate the opportunity I’ve been given.

“While it is true this is my first head coaching role, the body of work I’ve done over my seven years on the grass [as a coach] means there is nothing more I could do to prepare.

3 Cole won three Premier League titles as a player Credit: Getty

“The hours I’ve put in, the experiences I’ve had, and the managers and coaches I’ve worked under have guided me to a place where I feel ready and that I should be a head coach.

“I am definitely thankful to Cesena for the opportunity, but I have more than enough experience.”

Ashley Cole's career

Cole is widely considered as one of the best left-backs of his generation.

He won Premier League titles with Arsenal and Chelsea, before finishing his career with Roma, LA Galaxy and Derby.

Cole also won 107 caps for England.

He retired in 2019 and moved into coaching with then manager Frank Lampard.

Bromley sack Woodman

The Ravens have won just two of their opening fixtures, losing six straight in all competitions since beating Huddersfield on September 19.

Owner and Chairman Robin Stanton-Gleaves said: “I would firstly like to offer my sincere thanks to Andy for all he has achieved during his time with us.

3 Woodman had been in charge of Bromley since March 2021 Credit: Getty

“It’s no surprise that this club has reached new heights and Andy has been fundamental in helping us achieve that.

"I would like to reassure our supporters that we will be entering this new chapter with the same ambition and determination to keep moving this football club forward.

“On a personal note, Andy has been a pleasure to work with, and I wish him all the best for the future.”

Former player Byron Webster will be taking charge on an interim basis while the club appoint a permanent replacement.

Sports.title: Arsenal made double transfer mistake in the summer and Fleetwood embarrassment proved it
Sports.content:
Arsenal made double transfer mistake in the summer and Fleetwood embarrassment proved it

Arsenal have been warned they are 'missing something' after letting two key players leave the club in the summer.

It follows their shock Carabao Cup exit at the hands of League Two side Fleetwood Town.



3 Arsenal's loss to Fleetwood highlighted a transfer mistake, says Jamie O'Hara Credit: Getty

The Gunners were beaten on penalties at Highbury Stadium on Tuesday night after labouring to a 1-1 draw in the fourth round.

Their defeat was the first for the reigning champions of England to a fourth-tier side in the competition for 52 years.

Ex-Tottenham midfielder Jamie O'Hara believes Arsenal's struggles against Fleetwood stemmed from the sales of Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli.



The pair were allowed to leave the club for Besiktas and Al Hilal, respectively, in the summer.

It came despite the duo providing a combined 37 goals and assists across all competitions last term.



Arsenal's transfer mistake

Following Arsenal's penalty shootout defeat, O'Hara was joined on The Sports Bar by Gunners fan Francis.

During their discussion, the talkSPORT co-host explained: "I’ve been watching you this season and, look, you know how to win in Premier League games.



"I’m not convinced. I feel like you’re missing something. I feel like you’re missing Trossard a little bit, even Martinelli.

"I feel like you’re missing someone who can just come up with something special out of nothing."

Trossard departed for Besiktas in July for a £16.7million fee despite his 11 assists for Arsenal last season.

3 Arsenal have been warned they were wrong to sell Martinelli and Trossard Credit: Getty



The Belgium winger was tied with Declan Rice for the most of any Gunners player across all competitions.

Meanwhile, only Viktor Gyokeres scored more goals for the club than Martinelli, who ended the campaign with 11 to his name.

The 25-year-old joined Al Hilal for £55.2million at the end of the transfer window.

Arteta's selection headache

Despite signing Christos Tzolis following Trossard's exit, Mikel Arteta appears short of options out wide this term.



Both Tzolis and Bukayo Saka are currently sidelined through injury, leaving Noni Madueke and 16-year-old Max Dowman as the only first-team wingers.

However, Madueke was not included in the matchday squad against Fleetwood.

3 Arsenal opted to sell Trossard to Besiktas in July Credit: Getty

Instead, Dowman started on the right, with 18-year-old striker Ceadach O'Neill making his debut on the opposite flank.



O'Neill was ultimately replaced by Eberechi Eze after 66 minutes.

Meanwhile, Dowman was sent off with five minutes left of normal time.

As a result, the teenager will be suspended for Arsenal's upcoming Premier League matches against Liverpool, Hull City and Newcastle United.

It leaves Madueke as the only recognised wide player available to Arteta for those fixtures at present.

Dowman will not be cleared to return to the side domestically until the visit of Manchester City on Sunday, November 29, although the Gunners are expected to appeal.

Sports.title: Dirk Kuyt handed emergency manager role with imminent Liverpool fixture
Sports.content:
Liverpool legend Dirk Kuyt has been appointed interim manager of Fenerbahce.

It comes just seven days before the Turkish giants host Liverpool in the Champions League - live on talkSPORT.

2 Liverpool could come up against a very familiar face in the Champions League next week Credit: Getty

Kuyt steps up from his role as assistant manager following the resignation of Ismail Kartal.

The 65-year-old returned for a fourth spell as manager in June but experienced a tumultuous four months.

He offered his resignation in September after a 1-1 draw with Roma in the Champions League, but chairman Aziz Yildirim refused to accept it.

On Tuesday, however, his exit was agreed by mutual consent following a damaging 2-1 defeat to arch rivals Galatasaray on the weekend.

Fenerbahce, who have ex-Premier League stars N'Golo Kante, Romelu Lukaku, Mason Greenwood and Ederson in their ranks, are now six points adrift of league leaders Galatasaray in fifth.

It also came weeks after an embarrassing 6-0 hammering by Aston Villa in Europe earlier this month.

Kuyt has now been placed in temporary charge - with the Istanbul club set to host Goztepe in the Super Lig on Saturday before the visit of Liverpool on November 4.

A brief statement confirmed that Kuyt would be in charge 'until a new head coach is appointed'.

Ex-Turkey manager Vincenzo Montella has been linked with the vacancy, although there is no current timeline on when a new boss will be named.

Kuyt at Fenerbahce

While Kuyt is best remembered for his six-year spell at Liverpool, he is equally loved at Fenerbahce.

2 Kuyt scored 71 goals in 285 appearances for Liverpool in all competitions Credit: AFP

After leaving Anfield in 2012, the former Dutch forward went on to win the Super Lig, Turkish Cup and Super Cup during a three-year stint in Turkey.

Since transitioning into coaching, Kuyt served as a head coach at various clubs in the Netherlands, before returning to Fenerbahce as an assistant earlier this year.

This interim role represents the biggest challenge of his coaching career so far.

Sports.title: When is Cristiano Ronaldo playing next with star ready to return after interrupted schedule
Sports.content:
When is Cristiano Ronaldo playing next with star ready to return after interrupted schedule

Cristiano Ronaldo will return to action with Al Nassr this week following the postponement of Monday’s crunch AFC Champions League fixture.

The 41-year-old has endured an interrupted schedule of late with two Al Nassr matches having fallen foul to the ongoing tensions in neighbouring Yemen.



4 Cristiano Ronaldo and Al Nassr have seen two matches postponed as tensions remain high in the Middle East Credit: AFP

It comes after 13 people were killed when a missile launched by Houthi forces hit Riyadh airport on October 10.

The reigning Saudi Pro League champions saw their recent clash with Al Ahli moved to March 2027.

And that was followed by the postponement of Monday’s match against Al Wasl after the Emirati outfit claimed they were unable to travel to Saudi Arabia.



The five-time Ballon d’or winner last took to the pitch last Friday as he inspired Al Nassr to a 3-1 win at Al-Faisaly.

Ronaldo failed to get on the scoresheet but provided an assist to put his side two goals to the good.



The win left Al Nassr in second place, two points adrift of rivals Al Hilal in their quest to retain the Saudi Pro League title.

When is Ronaldo back in action?

Fear not Ronaldo fans, the Portuguese forward will be back on the pitch on Thursday, October 29.



The talismanic star will be in the squad to face ninth-placed Al Kholood in a Saudi Pro League fixture with kick off scheduled for 6pm GMT.

Ronaldo will pull on the yellow shirt a further two more times before the international break.

Al Nassr travel to Uzbekistan to take on Pakhtakor in the Champions League on November 2 before signing off with a league clash away at Al Hazem four days later.

4 Ronaldo's Al Nassr sit second in the Saudi Pro League table as they step up their efforts to claim back-to-back titles Credit: Getty



Then, all eyes will be on Ronaldo’s potential return to the Portugal squad following his recent 30-day suspension after leaving the international camp last month.

Ronaldo stormed out of the Portugal camp after a conflict with head coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

He later released a statement apologising to his teammates whilst admitting he deserved to be reprimanded for his actions.

Ronaldo was subsequently suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation and fined €255 (£214).



With the ban made effective from September 30, Ronaldo is cleared to feature for his country during next month’s internationals.

It is not a given that Ronaldo will be called up for the two Nations League fixtures against Denmark and Wales.

4 Ronaldo was left seething after claiming Portugal boss Jorge Jesus failed to keep promises over his game time Credit: AFP

4 All eyes will be on the Portugal head coach to see if he includes Ronaldo in his squad for November's Nations League fixtures Credit: Getty



Portugal have won all four of their Nations League matches with Ronaldo having featured in just one of those fixtures.

The legendary striker was tipped to call time on his international career following Portugal’s World Cup exit this summer.

But the forward, who turns 42 in February, appears to have no plans to hand over the baton just yet.

Ronaldo is closing in on an unprecedented 1,000 career goals with 146 of them coming for the Selecao.



He currently sits at 981 career strikes in 1340 matches – a ratio of 0.74 goals a game.

Sports.title: Hulk Hogan's daughter rages after the sale of his $5.9M Florida mansion: 'Enjoy your dirty money'
Sports.content:
Hulk Hogan's daughter rages after the sale of his $5.9M Florida mansion: 'Enjoy your dirty money'

The daughter of late wrestling icon Hulk Hogan expressed her anger over the sale of her father's mansion.

After being listed in January for nearly $11 million, the 5,400sq ft beachfront mansion the 'Hulkster' owned in Clearwater Beach, Florida was recently sold for $5.9 million.

A guest cottage located next door to the mansion was also sold for $2.8 million.

In a rant on Instagram, Brooke Hogan accused close friends and family of trying to make money off her father.

Brooke, 38, shared an image of the property to her Instagram story with a big 'SOLD' sticker across it.

'The sick feeling is indescribable,' Brooke captioned the post.

Brooke Hogan, the daughter of late WWE icon Hulk Hogan, called out family and friends after her dad's Clearwater Beach properties were sold off for millions of dollars

The 5,400sq ft beachfront mansion the 'Hulkster' owned in Clearwater Beach sold for $5.9m

She wrote in her Instagram story rant: 'Enjoy your dirty money. You took my dad.'

Brooke continued her posts by speaking about the years she lived at the home with her father and Hulk's ex-wife Jennifer McDaniel, who was married to him from 2010 to 2021.

'We cooked, we watched Jerry Springer, we played music, we cried,' she continued.

'I walked in that garage every visit and hugged him right when he'd open the garage door. I'd sit next to him for hours in the chair he died in.'

Brooke revealed that she and McDaniel cared for Hulk for years during multiple health battles, including back surgeries and knee and hip replacements.

From there, she called out people who she believes took advantage of her father, born Terry Gene Bollea, after his passing.

'First Jen-who no one but me treated with respect. Then I was gone...the truth teller...I'm sure to everyone's delight,' she posted.

'And now it's all gone. Sold for profit. Just like him...used for f***ing everyone else's gain. Saddest ending I've ever seen. You know who TF you are.'

Further posts included another photo of the house with a pointed caption: 'Enjoy your dirty money. You took my dad.'

Brooke says she asked to be written out of her father's will to avoid fights over his estate

Brooke added that many people only showed up when they wanted something out of Hulk Hogan, not when he needed help.

'Apparently EVERYONE will show up at the end if you're famous enough and they can profit off your demise,' she wrote.

In a follow-up post, Brooke clarified that she wasn't calling out any WWE Wrestlers, rather specific friends and family who used Hogan's fame for their own benefit.

She told US Magazine: 'There’s something deeply unsettling about watching a person’s life and memories reduced to transactions.

'Some people see a home filled with history and love. Others simply see what it’s worth. I’ve learned that the way people move when there’s nothing left to gain from someone anymore can tell you everything about how they valued them when they were alive.'

Back in 2023, Hulk wrote Brooke out of his will, making her brother, Nick, Hulk's sole beneficiary. Brooke previously revealed that she asked to be removed from the will as she didn't want to be involved in any fights over money.

'I've had to hear everyone say I'm the jerk for stepping away from the toxic behavior and brainwashing, fake, greedy people… 'I should have been there.' 'Everyone else' was there till the end. NO. They were there AT the end. To collect,' she wrote.

Sports.title: Shamed rugby star who was caught in sex act behind Greggs gets married just WEEKS after betrayed ex-wife tied the knot with her 'best friend'
Sports.content:
Shamed rugby star who was caught in sex act behind Greggs gets married just WEEKS after betrayed ex-wife tied the knot with her 'best friend'

Disgraced rugby league star Joe Westerman, who was caught performing a sex act on a woman behind a Greggs, has re-married just weeks after his betrayed ex-wife tied the knot with a new man.

England international Westerman was dumped by his first wife Lauren after being caught on camera performing a lewd sex act with a woman in an alleyway behind the popular bakery chain.

The woman involved was never identified but Lauren said she was a friend's wife.

The embarrassing headlines, sparked by the footage that went viral on social media, also landed the 36-year-old player in hot water with his Super League club Castleford Tigers.

As footage of his sex act went viral, the heartbroken mum-of-three went public with her disgust at Westerman's behaviour, threw him out of the family home and began divorce proceedings.

Six months on from the scandal, Westerman found happiness with local estate agent Alison Hopkinson, 37, and the pair wed on Monday in an intimate ceremony with family and friends.

Rugby league star Joe Westerman is remarried after being caught in a lurid sex act

Westerman tied the knot with estate agent Alison Hopkinson in an intimate ceremony

Rugby league star Westerman delivers his speech at Monday's wedding in Scarborough

Westerman shared photos of the big day on Instagram, captioned: 'A day we will never forget. Thank you to everyone who made it so special. Here's to our forever. The Westermans.'

He wore a beige suit for the ceremony in Scarborough, while Alison wore an A-line dress accompanied with a short train.

The pair's nuptials comes just weeks after Lauren got hitched to HGV mechanic Karl Holmes.

Lauren, who has now taken her new husband’s surname, wrote on Facebook: ‘Someone once told me that you’ll only ever be happy in life if you marry your best friend and I feel so lucky to be doing just that.’

Sharing photographs from the celebrations, she added: ‘Thank you again to everyone who came and celebrated with us. It really was the best day of our whole lives.’

A family friend told the Daily Mail the wedding felt like a particularly sweet ending after the very public collapse of Lauren’s marriage to former England international Westerman.

The friend said: ‘Something so good has come from something so bad.

‘Lauren was mortified by what Joe did to her. She is a very private person and for that footage to go viral was humiliating.

‘I especially felt for their eldest daughter, who was at senior school at the time.

‘It was awful for the family, but Lauren has come through it. Now she’s happy and that’s what matters.

HGV mechanic Karl, who has ‘been through some dark times as well’, is helping her ‘learn how to trust again’.

Karl, who bears more than a passing resemblance to Lauren’s 6ft 4in ex, proposed during a trip to Gran Canaria in April and has repeatedly gushed over his new wife on social media.

In one loving Facebook post, he wrote: ‘This woman is truly one in a million no matter what ideas I come up with, she goes with it.

‘Find yourself a women like this and nothing’s ever a worry or problem again.

‘No matter what, she has my back and nothing is too much. Love you darling, never stop being you.’

At the couple’s wedding reception, an emotional Karl told guests: ‘I would never, ever change anything of her. She’s the most amazing woman I’ve ever met and I will stick by her.’

Lauren and her new man went public with their romance in August 2023 – six months after her first husband was caught with his trousers down after a night out drinking.

The primary school teacher spoke of her anger and humiliation after her teenage daughter was shown the seven second clip by friends.

Westerman apologised for his actions and issued a grovelling apology blaming his 'decision-making around alcohol'. He was also fined by his Super League club and told to carry out community service as a punishment.

Their nuptials come weeks after Westerman's ex-wife Lauren tied the knot with fellow rugby player Karl Holmes

Joe Westerman and Lauren separated after his drunken infidelity went viral

Soon after his night of shame, Westerman struck up a romance with estate agent Alison Hopkinson, to whom he is now married

In a series of texts to Lauren he wrote: 'Words will never ever explain how sorry I am. I can't explain what happened cos I physically can't remember. It's disgusting and I now have to live with it forever. Losing you and the kids is heart-breaking Lauren, you deserve so much better.'

Adding: 'You always said alcohol would f*** me up. Story of my life. I miss you like crazy. U was perfect. I need you to know I can't remember anything about that night. I look like a zombie.'

But the words cut no ice with Lauren who ended their nine-year marriage and told her husband to leave the marital home.

Lauren said she would never take back her cheating husband 'one trillion per cent' and said she felt sorry for her children and those of the woman involved.

Lauren said: 'What kind of example would I be setting to my children - particularly my girls - if I were to give it another go?

'I want them to know that this is not all right, that it isn't acceptable behaviour in a relationship and that we all have self-worth.

'I now have to think about my children and begin rebuilding our future together. It's daunting, but he's got no one to blame but himself.'

She added: 'Truth is, he only told me because it was on social media. But I'm glad it was found because the thought of kissing him after that just makes me feel sick.'

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta taught Max Dowman an important lesson with his reaction to Fleetwood red card - forget the woke punditry gone mad, one day Arsenal wonderkid will look back and thank his manager
Sports.content:
The course of a few brief days last week told us much about the blizzard of hype that Max Dowman is up against and how brands grazing off football are seeking to monetise him.

Adidas are selling some new boots with Lionel Messi’s name on them and their promotional campaign included the Argentine’s list of his top ten footballers under the age of 21, with Dowman among them. There were no quotes from Messi saying why he liked the 16-year-old Arsenal player and certainly no spoken words.

But the PR story flew, Dowman's manager Mikel Arteta found himself asked about it at his press conference, and the name of the boots was sent around the world. It’s how football works.

This contributed to something of a Dowman onslaught when Arteta sat down last Friday to discuss Arsenal’s home match against Everton. The fixture was the one in which the teenager announced himself in March, becoming the youngest goalscorer in both Premier League and the club’s own history.

Arteta found himself fielding so many questions about Dowman, his potential, why he hadn’t played him so much, why hype brought dangers, that he had to draw a line under things. ‘Yes, very exciting! Enough! Enough, OK?’ he said.

The environment was rather less benign on the windswept Fylde coast at Fleetwood on Tuesday but the self-same hype revealed itself, albeit in a far less laudatory way.

Mikel Arteta has a word with Max Dowman as he trudges down the tunnel following his red card at Fleetwood Town

Dowman had fallen for the oldest trick in the book when he lashed out at Harrison Neal

Dowman was sent off, Arsenal were bundled out of the Carabao Cup by the League Two side and that turned out to be TV gold for Sky Sports, who unexpectedly found their C-listers contributing to a successful new flank in the Dowman narrative.

Arteta had given Dowman a look like thunder and uttered something to him as he trudged towards the dressing room. ‘You have to remember he is 16 years of age – he's a kid,’ opined Sky’s former Arsenal midfielder Paul Merson in the studio, declaring that he ‘didn’t like’ this.

Jobi McAnuff, an ex-Orient and Watford player sitting beside Merson, was of the same mind. ‘I didn't like the reaction at all,’ McAnuff said. ‘Dowman is potentially the future of Arsenal. Arteta didn't get that quite right.’

The idea of hiring a lip-reader to establish what an Arsenal manager said to a player after his dismissal at Fleetwood seems a tad hysterical, though the condemnation of Arteta and outpouring of national empathy for Dowman had made this a matter of debate.

It was the results of that specialist, Nicola Hickling, which finally provided some sense and perspective, when they were published.

Arteta’s actual words to Dowman? ‘Get to the dressing room Max.’ A little like that ‘get to your room’ which some of us have perhaps tried out, to no beneficial effect whatsoever, on our own children.

The manager's response was, of course, entirely proportionate, particularly since Arteta had warned Dowman in advance that he would be subjected to the kind of cynical act of incitement from Fleetwood’s Harrison Neal which saw him dismissed.

The Spaniard’s usual reaction when one of his players is sent off is to ignore them flatly as they leave, putting them in the kind of deep freeze that makes you shudder for the consequences in the sanctuary of the dressing room. This actually felt kinder.

The notion that Arteta was at fault for scowling at a young, dismissed player is woke punditry gone mad. If Dowman wants to play senior football, then he will be needing to grow up fast

The notion that Arteta was at fault for scowling at a young, dismissed player is, to coin an expression, woke punditry gone mad. If Dowman wants to play senior football, then he will be needing to grow up fast.

He was subjected to the oldest trick in the book – provocation – and fell for it hook, line and sinker, handing Fleetwood an opportunity they gleefully took. Why wouldn’t he be censured – if that dagger of a look of Arteta’s and six subsequent words of instruction really can be described as such?

It’s adulation which managers like Arteta most have to protect players like this against. David Moyes once stated that his job was a ‘one-man battle to protect Wayne Rooney from over-exposure’, when the future England captain was a young tyro at Goodison Park.

While Dowman has appeared in an adidas ad with Ian Wright, Moyes fought to keep Rooney away from early  campaigns and lucrative boot deals, believing that premature commercial exposure would distract him.

But only experience can insulate such prodigies from the harsh realities of the football field and the fact that they will be targeted by their inferiors wherever they go. It is Dowman’s second red card this month.

He was also sent off while representing England Under 19s against the United States in a behind-closed-doors friendly in Marbella, having appeared to kick out at an opponent. Some felt the punishment harsh. There are no conclusions to be drawn.

He is a steely, competitive player, confident with a ball at his feet and unafraid to hold his own against those much older than him, so there will be confrontations and altercations.

He was only 14 when he went face-to-face with a 19-year-old, Afonso Moreira, against Sporting Lisbon Under 19s in 2024, and after some shirt-pulling, the two of them squared up.

Dowman is already a figure of mass interest, and holds three world records as the youngest player to score for Arsenal and in the Premier League, and win the competition

If Dowman makes it to the top, he will look back at the way he was provoked and reacted and reflect that Mikel Arteta taught him something important in Fleetwood

Arsenal academy staff soon took him off because they sensed his aggression may spill over, though it told them he had the necessary fight. His ability to stay on the right side of the line will dictate where his future heads.

Arsenal are appealing Dowman's dismissal in wet, wild Fylde, which means Dowman may yet feature for Arsenal on Sunday at Liverpool.

But if he ever makes it to the proper international stage, perhaps to face the dark arts of Argentina or Italy in front of the world, he will look back at the way he was provoked and reacted and reflect that Mikel Arteta taught him something important on that night in Fleetwood.

Sports.title: Arsenal launch appeal against Max Dowman's red card: Gunners fight to overturn 16-year-old's ban before Liverpool clash following his furious reaction towards Fleetwood rival in League Cup exit
Sports.content:
Arsenal launch appeal against Max Dowman's red card: Gunners fight to overturn 16-year-old's ban before Liverpool clash following his furious reaction towards Fleetwood rival in League Cup exit

Arsenal are appealing Max Dowman's red card from their shock defeat against Fleetwood on penalties in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night.

The 16-year-old was given his marching orders after reacting aggressively to a heavy tackle by Harrison Neal.

Dowman was fortunate not to be injured by the challenge but then kicked out at the midfielder and was scolded by Mikel Arteta as he skulked off the pitch.

His ban applies for the next three games, meaning he is set to miss fixtures against Liverpool on Sunday and then Hull and Newcastle, all in the Premier League.

The Gunners have until 1pm on Thursday to submit their appeal documentation.

Dowman has played four times this season and Arsenal are keen to have him available, particularly after injuries to Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke.

Arsenal are appealing Max Dowman's sending-off against Fleetwood Town

The Gunners were beaten 5-3 on penalties in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup after a 1-1 draw with Fleetwood in regular time.

Aaron Loupalo-Bi opened the scoring for the League Two strugglers before Viktor Gyokeres got Arsenal level early in the second half. Dowman was sent off in the 86th minute.

The ferociousness of Neal's challenge irked many Arsenal supporters. Piers Morgan took to X to express his support for Dowman at full-time, while conceding his side were poor in general.

'No way is that a straight red,' his post began. 'Dowman was mown down in a thuggish way, and reacted like anyone would when someone nearly broke their leg.

'Blaming a 16-year-old kid for Arsenal's abject humiliation is also ridiculous. None of our players turned up.'

AFTV regular Tai echoed Morgan's sentiments, branding Fleetwood's tackles in general as 'disgusting' and that Dowman is right to react with the likes of former players such as Aaron Ramsey and Eduardo being on the receiving end of leg-breaking tackles in the past.

'You can criticise Max, but Max is 16. He's seen that. Is he going to wait for his leg to be broken? The challenges that they were doing were absolutely disgraceful. This is disgusting,' Tai told the AFTV YouTube channel.

'The ref was not doing his job so now what we have is a situation where players again endanger other players' career. Aaron [Ramsey] nearly had his leg amputated. Eduardo nearly had his leg amputated.

Max Dowman (far right) was sent off for his reaction to heavy challenge on him on Tuesday

The Arsenal star reacted furiously after being on the receiving end of this Harrison Neal tackle

Arsenal fans defended the 16-year-old for his reaction to Fleetwood midfielder Neal afterwards

Arsenal fan Piers Morgan took to X to defend 16-year-old Dowman's actions

AFTV regular Tai accused Fleetwood Town of several 'disgusting' challenges during the match

Meanwhile, AFTV's Julian claimed the pitch dimensions were a reason why the Gunners lost

'I expect players to not endanger other players' careers. Max is 16. He does not want to get his leg broken like happened to Aaron and Eduardo. Now, you can say Max is wrong but Max is trying to defend himself.

'The referee did not do his job, and it is scandalous. It's disgraceful. And I'm disgusted that we've come here to face this. Fleetwood Town should be ashamed of themselves because that's a tackle that endangers our players careers.'

While Tai was unhappy with the refereeing display, his fellow AFTV member Julian chose to blame the pitch dimensions for the visitors' defeat at Highbury Stadium, home of League Two Fleetwood.

'It's 102metres long, the Premier League is 105m long: it's just under three per cent difference,' Julian quipped.

'When you have a margin of that kind of level, it is only small but it can make a difference. And what that allowed Fleetwood to do was to make it easier for them to condense the play on a smaller pitch - which they're used to playing on.

'We're not talking about the main reason why they lost, we're talking about the small margins and the smaller margins tonight was three metres less in length in the pitch. It's one of the smaller reasons.'

Sports.title: Meet Fleetwood's giant-killers: Victory over Arsenal inspired by an ex-warehouse worker, 'the next Wayne Rooney' and the star romantically linked with tennis ace Heather Watson
Sports.content:
Meet Fleetwood's giant-killers: Victory over Arsenal inspired by an ex-warehouse worker, 'the next Wayne Rooney' and the star romantically linked with tennis ace Heather Watson

Fleetwood Town pulled off one of the biggest giant-killings in Carabao Cup history on Tuesday night as they knocked out Premier League champions Arsenal on penalties.

A team composed of a former warehouse worker and a player once dubbed 'the next Wayne Rooney' beat a side 83 places above them in the English football pecking order.

Among them are pizza lovers, padel players, and multiple former stars from Manchester United and Man City.

Without further ado, here are Fleetwood's heroes.

Fleetwood stunned Arsenal as they knocked them out of the Carabao Cup on penalties

Jay Lynch, goalkeeper, 33

A former warehouse worker who was once let go by Accrington Stanley for complaining about his lack of game time on Twitter.

His only complaint on Tuesday night was that he lost his voice organising Fleetwood's defence – before saving Bruno Guimaraes' penalty to set them on course for victory.

The father of two is friends with Jesse Lingard and Tommy Fury – they attended his wedding – and a big fan of Craig David.

Finley Potter, defender, 22

Potter played with a bandage above his eye after sustaining a cut in a 2-1 defeat by Exeter on Saturday.

Soldiering through injury is part of his story. The former England and Sheffield United youngster overcame an 18-month knee injury in his late teens before winning a contract with Barnet.

Shaun Rooney, defender, 30

Has history of cup glory after winning two domestic trophies with St Johnstone in Scotland. He scored the winning goal in the club's Scottish League Cup and Scottish Cup triumphs in 2021 – playing for 80 minutes in the latter with an injured ankle and painkillers.

The Scot comes from a footballing family – his great-uncle Benny and great-grandfather Bob also played. It is unclear whether he is still dating tennis star Heather Watson, but she went to watch him play in the Europa Conference League with St Mirren in 2024.

Goalkeeper Jay Lynch, who used to work in a warehouse, saved Bruno Guimaraes' penalty

Defender Shaun Rooney has history with cup heroics and has been romantically linked to tennis star Heather Watson

Conor Haughey, defender, 19

Academy graduate Haughey admitted he had not even practised penalties after scoring the winner against Arsenal.

The teenager got so carried away that he swore in his post-match interview, forcing Sky Sports to apologise. The Belfast-born defender is a Northern Ireland youth international and was the youngest-ever player to appear for Glentoran at 15 years, three months, and eight days old.

Rhys Bennett, wing-back, 22

A Manchester United youth academy graduate who received encouragement from Harry Maguire and Scott McTominay after leaving the club in January.

Played the full 90 minutes against Arsenal a year after revealing that his father, David, had died by suicide. He has done his dad proud.

Harrison Neal, midfielder, 25

Neal's main contribution was putting in the agricultural challenge which sparked Max Dowman's reaction and got the Arsenal prodigy sent off.

The Barnsley-born lad keeps a low profile. At Barrow he was nicknamed Casper after the teenage lead character in the film Kes.

Crispin McLean, midfielder, 20

The Scottish youngster, formerly of Celtic and Rangers, signed his first professional deal with Fleetwood in 2024.

A fashionable chap who also enjoys playing padel.

Rhys Bennett played in the clash a year after revealing that his dad had died by suicide

Mark Helm, midfielder, 25

Another former Manchester United kid who joined the giants aged seven and was once apparently dubbed 'the next Wayne Rooney'.

The midfielder recently told Fleetwood's media channel that he has a fear of snakes and would be an electrician if he wasn't playing football. His favourite food is pizza.

Jake Batty, wing-back, 21

Four years ago, Batty was playing Sunday league football in Liverpool.

Blackburn gave him his break in the game and he joined Fleetwood in the summer after spells with Accrington and Swindon. A travel nut who has previously been quad biking in the desert in Egypt.

Aaron Loupalo-Bi scored the biggest goal of his career when he put Fleetwood ahead

Ched Evans, striker, 37

A veteran EFL striker who played in the Premier League for Manchester City in their first year of Abu Dhabi ownership.

Spent four years out of football between 2012 and 2016 after being convicted and imprisoned for rape, but was released in 2014 and found not guilty via a retrial in 2016.

Aaron Loupalo-Bi, striker, 20

Scored the biggest goal of his career when he nutmegged Arsenal goalkeeper Illan Meslier 21 minutes into this clash at Highbury.

The London-born forward, who is on loan from Fulham, has featured for England's Under 18s.

Manager: Matt Lawlor, 38

Lawlor admitted he forgot the match was going to penalties and was preparing for extra-time with just minutes to go in his side's heroic triumph.

Only played as high as non-League and entered the Fleetwood dugout in January after two previous caretaker spells with the League Two outfit.

Sports.title: OLIVER HOLT: Why Fleetwood beating Arsenal is the biggest Cup upset I've ever been to - and the rest of my top 10
Sports.content:
OLIVER HOLT: Why Fleetwood beating Arsenal is the biggest Cup upset I've ever been to - and the rest of my top 10

Oliver Holt Chief Sports Writer

Arsenal were stunned by League Two Fleetwood on Tuesday night, the champions of English football dumped out of the Carabao Cup by a team 84 places below them in the football pyramid.

Our Chief Sports Writer OLIVER HOLT was at Highbury to witness the giant-killing first-hand – and it ranks as one of the finest cup upsets he has seen in his career.

But how do Fleetwood's heroics compare to Lionel Messi being suckerpunched at the World Cup, or the comeback to end all comebacks in the Champions League final?

Read on to find out Oliver's verdict...

10. Manchester United 1 Porto 1 (2-3 on aggregate)

March 9, 2004. Champions League last 16 second leg, Old Trafford

This was a 1-1 draw at Old Trafford but it was enough to knock United out of the Champions League.

It was the match that put Jose Mourinho on the map when he ran half the length of the touchline to celebrate the late equaliser that put his team through and finished his sprint with a knee slide.

Porto went on to win the competition that season and Mourinho’s career was launched like a rocket.

United players react in disbelief after Costinha (not pictured) equalised for Porto in the 90th minute

Jose Mourinho announced himself in English football with his sprint down the Old Trafford touchline as his upstart Porto side went on to win the Champions League

9. Manchester United 3 Barcelona 0 (3-2 on aggregate)

March 21, 1984. Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final second leg, Old Trafford

Maybe it should never be an upset when a club of Manchester United’s size win a match but this was the Barcelona of Diego Maradona and United were 2-0 down from the first leg in Catalonia.

Inspired by Bryan Robson, United played like a whirlwind and swept Barcelona aside to win 3-0.

I was standing in the Stretford Paddock and it’s still one of the best atmospheres I’ve ever experienced at a football match.

Manchester United captain Bryan Robson exchanges pennants with Barcelona's Diego Maradona ahead of the second leg

The inspirational Robson scored twice to draw United level on aggregate, before Frank Stapleton's winning goal

8. Clyde 2 Celtic 1

January 8, 2006. Scottish Cup third round, Broadwood Stadium

The English press flocked to Clyde’s Broadwood stadium to watch this game because it was Roy Keane’s debut in Scottish football following his move from Manchester United. It didn’t go well.

Clyde stunned their mighty visitors and won 2-1. It was a sign of things to come for Keane north of the border.

The English press flocked to Clyde’s Broadwood stadium to watch this game because it was Roy Keane’s debut in Scottish football

Clyde's players led by captain Michael McGowan (centre) celebrate their historic victory over their mighty visitors

7. Manchester City 0 Wigan Athletic 1

May 11, 2013. FA Cup final, Wembley Stadium

City were just entering their period of dominance in the English game when they were beaten by relegation-threatened Wigan Athletic in the FA Cup final.

It was the first major trophy in Wigan’s existence and it was laden with emotion for their owner, Dave Whelan, who broke his leg playing for Blackburn Rovers in the 1960 FA Cup final against Wolves.

Whelan led the team out and watched them win courtesy of Ben Watson’s last-minute goal.

Wigan's Ben Watson heads in a late winner in the 2013 FA Cup final, shocking Man City as they were about to enter a period of dominance in English football

Watson (right) celebrates sending Wigan towards the first major trophy in their history

6. Stockport County 5 Bolton Wanderers 3 (AET)

November 17, 2021. FA Cup first round replay, Edgeley Park

Stockport were in the National League when they were paired with one of the old giants of the English game in the FA Cup. They drew the first tie in Bolton and then went 2-0 down inside six minutes with some kamikaze defending in the replay at Edgeley Park.

But then Paddy Madden scored a penalty, the comeback began, the ground turned into a bear-pit and the big boys from Bolton crumbled to a 5-3 defeat.

Ashley Palmer (5) powers in a header to bring Stockport back from the dead and send the tie to extra time

Scott Quigley (centre) struck five minutes into extra time to put Stockport in front

5. AC Milan 3 Liverpool 3 (AET, 2-3 on penalties)

May 25, 2005. Champions League final, Ataturk Olympic Stadium

Can you have a giant-killing in a Champions League final? Well, it felt like it when Liverpool worked the Miracle of Istanbul on AC Milan.

Liverpool’s starting line-up included Steve Finnan, Djimi Traore and Harry Kewell. Milan had Cafu, Paolo Maldini, Andriy Shevchenko, Kaka, Hernan Crespo and Andrea Pirlo.

Liverpool were embarrassed in the first half but they had the life-force that was Steven Gerrard and they came back from 3-0 down to effect the most stunning comeback in Champions League history.

Liverpool overcame a 3-0 deficit and an AC Milan superteam including Kaka, Paolo Maldini and Andriy Shevchenko (pictured) to win the 2005 Champions League final on penalties

Captain fantastic Steven Gerrard lifts the trophy after Jerzy Dudek's heroics in the shootout

4. Plymouth Argyle 1 Liverpool 0

February 9, 2025. FA Cup fourth round, Home Park

This had a Fleetwood-Arsenal vibe about it. I love going to Home Park. It’s another ground that feels like one of the outposts of the English game but it has the fanatical home support of the Green Army and one of the most handsome stands in the country, the Mayflower Grandstand.

Liverpool were on their way to winning the title under Arne Slot but he made 10 changes for this game and the Championship’s bottom club made him pay the penalty.

Liverpool were on their way to becoming Premier League champions when they travelled to Home Park in February 2025 - but a penalty from Ryan Hardie (second right) stopped them in their tracks

Then Plymouth boss Miron Muslic (centre) celebrates his side's remarkable victory in the home dressing room

3. Argentina 1 Saudi Arabia 2

November 22, 2022. World Cup group stage, Lusail Stadium

This felt like the end for Lionel Messi. I’m hoping most people have forgotten now, but I also wrote that it was the end. A few weeks later, he was lifting the World Cup for the first time.

That felt like a distant prospect after this humbling at the Lusail Stadium in Argentina’s opening game of the tournament. Messi had scored a penalty to put Argentina ahead but Saudi Arabia recovered to take a deserved 2-1 lead and win the game.

Messi looked tired and shot. It turned out he was just getting ready to prove everyone wrong.

Salem Al Dawsari's stunning winning goal condemned Argentina to defeat in their opening match, before they recovered to win their third World Cup title

2. England 1 Iceland 2

June 27, 2016. Euro 2016 last 16, Stade de Nice

Lagging only behind the 1-0 defeat by the USA in Belo Horizonte in 1950, this was England’s biggest humiliation in tournament football.

I remember arriving at the stadium in Nice and hearing and seeing the Viking Clap for the first time and getting a bad feeling as the Iceland fans went through their choreographed routine.

Once England went behind and the enormity of what was unfolding began to dawn on them, they froze. It was an abject humiliation.

Iceland's players react after knocking out Roy Hodgson's England at Euro 2016 - one of the biggest humiliations in the national team's history

Conor Haughey (left), the 19-year-old Northern Irish left back, celebrates after scoring the winning penalty in Fleetwood's giantkilling of Arsenal

1. Fleetwood Town 1 Arsenal 1 (5-3 on penalties)

October 27, 2026. League Cup fourth round, Highbury Stadium

Straight in at the top of my list. Nothing against Arsenal, who took the game seriously and behaved with class and dignity, but there was something life-affirming about being at Highbury Stadium on Tuesday night to see a team near the foot of League Two knock out the champions of England.

Fleetwood’s win on penalties summed up so much of the magic and the eccentricity of cup competitions in England. A drone delaying play, a gale raging through the stadium, a remote outpost of our game, a team that had not practised penalties scoring all five of their kicks, a stadium with a 5,000 capacity, a club whose fans are known as the Cod Army. It had everything.

At a time when there is so much cynicism in the English game, when Manchester City have been found guilty of serial cheating, this felt like an antidote.

Sports.title: Thierry Henry hits back at Ballon d'Or hosting backlash after excruciatingly awkward Lamine Yamal 'joke' and the 'disrespectful' moment he corrected co-host Kate Scott
Sports.content:
Thierry Henry hits back at Ballon d'Or hosting backlash after excruciatingly awkward Lamine Yamal 'joke' and the 'disrespectful' moment he corrected co-host Kate Scott

Thierry Henry had no remorse as he responded to critics of his Ballon d'Or hosting performance after he received backlash for awkwardly joking with Lamine Yamal, and appearing to correct his co-presenter Kate Scott.

The Arsenal legend shared the stage with his fellow CBS Sports broadcaster on Monday evening and caught heat for questioning whether Yamal's award for Young Talent of the Year - the Kopa Trophy - was the one he really wanted.

Yamal, then considered a favourite for the Ballon d'Or, was politely bashful, brushing off the joke and suggesting that his Spain and Barcelona team-mate Pau Cubarsi would have been a more worthy winner.

Henry's performance came under further scrutiny when he informed Scott of the correct pronunciation of Brazilian icon Socrates - after she had announced the name in the style of the Greek philosopher.

But after a day of online criticism, Henry took to social media to give his side of the story and lambast those who didn't find his 'jokes' funny and who were 'getting really excited about nothing'.

'First and foremost, Lamine Yamal, I wasn’t checking his ego at all, I just thought as the third time he’s winning that trophy, I asked him if that was the one he really wanted, and I brought out a laugh from people,' Henry explained. 'We all know what he wanted, he didn’t get it.

Thierry Henry recorded a video for fans on social media who criticised his Ballon d'Or hosting

The Arsenal legend had appeared to correct his co-host and fellow CBS Sports star Kate Scott

Henry had also asked Lamine Yamal if he had won the trophy he really wanted when he was awarded the Kopa Trophy

'I’m a big fan of Lamine Yamal, I wasn’t checking his ego at all. That you didn’t like the joke, I can understand. But don’t do that, he’s one of the players I’d pay to watch, I love him.

'I was just asking him, if it’s the one he really wants as the real prize was coming after. Unfortunately he didn’t win it, because he’s a hell of a player I’d pay to watch.

'Now let’s move on to Kate, she was with me on the joke, and you can ask Kate, by the way. She did it on purpose, to say Socrates, and I had to say, Socrates.

Again, that you didn’t like the joke, I understand, but please stop saying I disrespected Kate, I will never do that, and you can ask her people, she was in on the joke with me, she did Socrates on purpose, and I said Socrates, so please stop inventing stories.'

Finally, Henry confronted his comments made to Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane after his acceptance speech, when he told the England captain that he was 'always going to back up' his rival for the top prize Kylian Mbappe.

The former World Cup winner explained that during a recent interview on CBS, Kane had teased him for supporting Mbappe for the Ballon d'Or, and that Henry was merely giving his remarks context.

'I just told him the other day, I’m French, and I was always going to back up and support my fellow countrymen,' Henry continued. 'I said to him, "you are a worthy winner, you deserve it, you are the example that work ethic is a talent, working hard is a talent".

'I said "you are a worthy winner, well done, Harry Kane", and I call him Sir Harry Kane since the World Cup.

'So please, people out there, relax, relax, I love Harry Kane, I love Lamine Yamal, and I didn’t disrespect Kate, she was on the joke with me, once again, have a good night.'

Kane at the time listened to Henry's remarks thoughtfully and accepted the compliment with thanks to widespread applause.

As he was asked a question directly, Yamal was unable to demur, and grinned as the audience laughed at Henry's implication that he was focused on a greater award.

After he had collected himself, the Barcelona teenager dodged the question in his native Spanish.

On the night, his comments to Scott were less well received as the joke failed to land.

In the wake of Scott's pronunciation of the award, which was given to Arsenal star Bukayo Saka, Henry had quipped: 'What do you mean Socrates?'

'We don't have any philosophers here. It's (correct pronunciation) Socrates. We're not going to debate it.'

Henry's comments were not the only incidents at Monday night's ceremony labelled by fans online as disrespectful, with the behaviour of Mbappe, Yamal and last year's winner Ousmane Dembele also coming in for heavy criticism.

A video captured moments after Kane was named the best footballer in the world show both French players failing to stand up to shake his hand.

Sports.title: Arsenal's defeat by Fleetwood is the greatest upset in the history of the Carabao Cup: Premier League champions sunk by League Two side on dismal night for Mikel Arteta, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
Arsenal's defeat by Fleetwood is the greatest upset in the history of the Carabao Cup: Premier League champions sunk by League Two side on dismal night for Mikel Arteta, writes OLIVER HOLT

Beside the tram tracks that run all the way down to Blackpool and the Pleasure Beach, just along from the hulking iron anchor embedded in the pavement at the start of Fisherman’s Walk, they were doing a brisk trade at The Eating Plaice as kick-off to one of the greatest occasions in this town’s history edged closer.

One of the ladies behind the counter upbraided an Arsenal fan taking his plate of fish and chips through to the restaurant.

‘You’ve done yourself there, love,’ she said. ‘If you’d ordered in there, you could have had fish and chips, mushy peas, a brew and bread and butter for £10.95.’

It was the start of a bad night for Arsenal and a beautiful evening for the wider glory of English football at one of its most remote outposts.

Arsenal had played Bayern Munich in their previous away game but not even the Allianz Arena could have prepared them for their return to a stadium called Highbury and a Carabao Cup fourth-round tie against a League Two side 85 places below them in the pyramid.

A drone, hovering ahead, stopped play early on. A gale blew off Morecambe Bay. Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman was sent off late in the second half. The tie went to a penalty shoot-out and Fleetwood did not miss a single one.

Bruno Guimaraes, a Brazilian World Cup star, blinked first and missed. Conor Haughey, a teenage centre back from Northern Ireland, took Fleetwood’s final kick and buried it high past Illan Meslier in the Arsenal goal, to send his team into the quarter-finals of the competition and seal the biggest upset in the history of the League Cup.

Arsenal have been knocked out of the Carabao Cup on penalties by League Two Fleetwood

After taking the lead in the 21st minute, Arsenal scored through Viktor Gyokeres in the second half - but Fleetwood Town managed to hang on

The loud speaker system played Depeche Mode singing ‘I just can’t get enough,’ over and over again as the Cod Army, Fleetwood’s loyal fans, invaded the pitch. Manager Matt Lawlor, a local man, whose young son was in the crowd, could not stop his tears flowing. His team is 18th in League Two, two points off the relegation zone, and they had just beaten the champions.

‘Football’s getting a little bit more clinical and removed,’ said Lawlor in the post-match mayhem. ‘And that to me tonight, there was that feeling we all get as football fans. That was what you kind of live for, isn’t it?

‘To be giving that to football fans, especially Fleetwood fans, is unbelievably special. Football’s a funny old game, isn’t it?’

There is a frontier feel about this town, a bit like Barrow-in-Furness on the other side of Morecambe Bay. Sea salt in the veins and a harbour once home to a flotilla of trawlers. The wind blows through it so hard it whisks away anything that is not nailed down. The Vintage Emporium and Odditorium advertises its wares near the seafront.

It feels like giant-killing country here. It is giant-killing country here. Especially last night, when a gale blew through the ground, bending the corner flags and threatening to sweep laptops off the press tables and dislodge red-and-blue hats from the heads of the Cod Army regulars who filed into the stands and leaned against the crush barriers on the terraces behind the goals.

This was Highbury, but not as Arsenal know it. There is nothing Art Deco about any of the stands at Fleetwood Town’s delightful ground. The capacity is 5,327. The trendy restaurants of Upper Street are not a short walk away down Holloway Road. This is a different kind of Highbury. A single-storey sports and social club sits behind the touchline opposite the main stand. A banner proclaiming ‘Up the Cods’ hung behind one of the goals.

It is more than 20 years since Arsenal — who brought 1,100 fans north with them — played the final game at their Highbury and Arteta respected the name and the competition by picking a strong side.

This was a million miles from Monday’s Ballon d’Or ceremony at the London Palladium, where Arteta had lost out to Luis de la Fuente in the Manager of the Year category, to this football outpost by the sea but the Arsenal boss gave every signal he and his team were approaching the task with relish. In his line-up here were Viktor Gyokeres, Kai Havertz and Myles Lewis-Skelly. They are not strangers to tricky trips like this. They negotiated a visit to Mansfield Town’s Field Mill ground in the FA Cup last year with aplomb.

Dowman was shown his marching orders for kicking Harrison Neal and a less-than-impressed Arteta appeared to say something to the youngster as he headed for the tunnel

Bruno Guimaraes hit an unconvincing fourth penalty for the Gunners which he saw saved

Join the discussion Is Arsenal's defeat to Fleetwood the greatest cup upset you've ever witnessed?

Teenagers Dowman and Marli Salmon started that game just as they started this one. Arteta also handed a debut to Ceadach O’Neill, 18.

Less than two minutes in, play was halted by the sight of a drone of unknown provenance hovering over the pitch. It is not the first time it has happened at a game, but it seemed to unnerve Arsenal. The teams came to the sidelines before play was resumed after seven minutes. The drone operator was apprehended by police in a nearby park. Stick the whole episode in the Odditorium.

Midway through the half, there was some football drama, too. Aaron Loupalo-Bi ran on to a through ball and held off Salmon before turning him and rifling the ball through the legs of Meslier.

Never has Highbury celebrated a goal against Arsenal with such unbridled joy. The theme to Captain Pugwash, the Fleetwood goal music, carried across the ground on the breeze.

But five minutes after the interval, with Martin Odegaard introduced to the fray, Arsenal were level. O’Neill swung a fine cross into the box and after a bit of pinball, Gyokeres forced it over the line. Five minutes later, Jay Lynch pulled off a last-ditch save to deny Havertz from close range.

Odegaard changed the game. Arsenal dominated midfield now and were turning the screw. Havertz prodded into the side-netting and Lewis-Skelly skied an effort over from the edge of the six-yard box. ‘Champions of England, you’re having a laugh,’ the Cod Army sang.

Five minutes from the end, Dowman reacted to a challenge by Harrison Neal and kicked him while on the floor. He was shown a straight red card. Dowman is still only 16. As he trudged off the pitch, Arteta muttered something in his ear. The kid was doing his GCSEs this summer. This will be a valuable part of his football education.

Lynch saved from Ben White in the dying seconds and the tie went to penalties. Arsenal blinked first. Guimaraes hit their fourth penalty to the keeper’s left and Lynch dived to push it out. Haughey stepped up to take Fleetwood’s fifth and smashed it into the roof of the net.

Haughey is 19 but when he spoke after the match, he was the personification of the wonder that had overtaken this town. ‘When I saw Guimaraes miss,’ he said, ‘I was buzzing. I thought “hit it and then run like mad”. If I seem confident, well I’m a Belfast lad and if you’re not confident in Belfast, you get eaten up.’

Arteta was keen to pay tribute to Fleetwood. ‘We didn’t want to go through this,’ he said, ‘but it is part of the history of football here.’ By then, Highbury was echoing to the sound of lawnmowers on the pitch. The gale still blew.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick future LIVE: Bruno Fernandes meeting, duo at risk, Ratcliffe jets in
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick could be on his way out the doors of Manchester United

Michael Carrick continues to face increased pressure at Manchester United following a poor start to the new season, with limited time available to reverse fortunes at Old Trafford

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's live Michael Carrick blog for Wednesday, October 28.

The Manchester United head coach finds himself under immense pressure at Old Trafford following a sub-par start to the season, which has left the Red Devils sitting 16th in the Premier League table, just one point from the drop zone after eight matches played.

Carrick was on the verge of being sacked this week but has been given a stay of execution. He will now take charge of Saturday's 12.30pm clash with Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, but that could serve as the straw that breaks the camel's back for the 45-year-old, unless United are able to clinch all three points in west London to buy him valuable breathing space.

The general consensus is that players and staff want to help keep Carrick in a job, with one player telling BBC Sport: "The feeling is that we all want to put it right. Players, staff, everyone."

However, it's not just Carrick who is feeling the heat at the Theatre of Dreams at present. Sources close to the club believe that Sir Jim Ratcliffe could be considering an overhaul of the hierarchy in the event that the Englishman fails to turn the tide.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

It is suggested that the sporting director, Jason Wilcox, and the CEO, Omar Barrada, could also be sent packing alongside Carrick.

Stay tuned as we bring you all of the latest news and updates on Carrick's future throughout the day.

Sports.title: Arsenal 'didn't take it well' as Fleetwood hero reveals post-match behaviour
Sports.content:
Arsenal 'didn't take it well' as Fleetwood hero reveals post-match behaviour

Fleetwood Town goalkeeper Jay Lynch says Arsenal's stars didn't take their Carabao Cup upset defeat well

View 2 Images Arsenal were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood Town. (Image: (Photo by Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Fleetwood Town goalkeeper Jay Lynch has revealed that Arsenal's dejected players did not take defeat well following the League Two side's stunning Carabao Cup upset on Tuesday night. The Cod Army knocked out the Gunners on penalties, converting all five of their spot-kicks while Bruno Guimaraes saw his effort kept out in the decisive moment for Mikel Arteta's men.

‌



‌



Lynch was the shootout hero, pushing away the Brazilian's penalty to hand Fleetwood the upper hand, before Conor Haughey stepped up to seal a remarkable 5-3 victory. Wild scenes followed the winning penalty, with supporters streaming onto the pitch to mark a historic triumph for the Lancashire club.

‌



Lynch has since revealed that Arsenal's players did not exchange any words with their Fleetwood counterparts after the loss. Speaking on talkSPORT, Lynch said: "It's obviously such a huge moment for us and all the fans ran on, no one actually got chance to speak to them.

‌



"I think the gaffer spoke to their gaffer briefly, but because of all the fans we didn't actually get a chance to ask for shirts or even speak to them or anything, to be honest. They didn't take it well, let's put it that way."

‌



Fleetwood, who currently sit 18th in League Two, caused an early stir when Fulham loanee Aaron Loupalo-Bi fired them in front after 21 minutes, against a heavily-rotated Arsenal outfit that struggled to find any rhythm on the Fylde coast.

The introduction of Martin Odegaard proved to be a pivotal moment in the tie, with the Gunners looking noticeably more threatening after the break, drawing level in the 50th minute when Viktor Gyokeres just managed to grab his first goal of the campaign.

‌



View 2 Images Jay Lynch was the hero as Fleetwood knocked Arsenal out (Image: Getty Images)

Yet, as Arsenal piled on the pressure without managing to find a winner, frustrations boiled over when teenage sensation Max Dowman was shown a red card with just five minutes left on the clock.

‌



The Gunners have since lodged an appeal against the dismissal, which came after Dowman lashed out at Harrison Neal following a robust challenge, with manager Mikel Arteta visibly rounding on the youngster as he trudged off the pitch.

Lynch still had time to produce crucial saves from Ben White and Odegaard before the match was settled by a penalty shootout, in which Fleetwood held their nerve from 12 yards to seal a stunning and memorable victory.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta's behaviour in Fleetwood tunnel shows he's not like mentor Pep Guardiola
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta's behaviour in Fleetwood tunnel shows he's not like mentor Pep Guardiola

Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor has revealed what Mikel Arteta did after Arsenal's shock defeat

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has been praised for his conduct after Arsenal's defeat to Fleetwood (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta took Arsenal's shock Carabao Cup loss with more grace than one of the worst defeats of Pep Guardiola's Manchester City career. League Two Fleetwood stunned Premier League champions, who had Max Dowman sent off late on, on penalties to advance to the quarter-finals after a 1-1 draw.

‌



‌



Bruno Guimaraes saw his spot-kick saved by Jay Lynch before Fleetwood's Conor Haughey lashed home to spark a pitch invasion as the Cod Army produced one of the greatest upsets in the competition's history.

‌



While Arteta isn't universally popular with rival clubs and fans, he showed his class in the aftermath of the defeat, with victorious Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor hailing the Spaniard's sportsmanship.

‌



He said: "He shook my hand two or three times and he was really, really gracious. I can imagine it's a really disappointing night for him.

Fleetwood manager says Mikel Arteta's tunnel behaviour after cup upset sums up Arsenal boss READ MORE :

Arsenal make fresh Max Dowman decision after Fleetwood red and Mikel Arteta anger READ MORE :

"But the way that he acted there, with class, is amazing. I would love to catch up with him and pick his brains, but he's been really busy with media and all the emotions that come with it.

"We've not managed to cross paths, but he said well done in the tunnel briefly and how well we did, which is obviously a show of class from him."

‌



It was a far cry from his mentor's conduct during City's FA Cup defeat to League One Wigan in 2018, when Arteta was part of Guardiola's coaching team. Following Fabian Delph's red card just before half-time, tensions boiled over, with Guardiola and Wigan boss Paul Cook clashing on the touchline.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The ruckus spilt into the tunnel area, where, helpfully, the BBC had placed a camera that showed the managers yelling at each other and needing to be restrained by staff. Wigan won 1-0 thanks to Will Grigg's early goal.

It's worth pointing out that this wasn't common behaviour from Guardiola following a defeat, which he generally accepted with good grace. But it was a notable difference from Arteta's magnanimous reaction to the Fleetwood loss.

‌



View 2 Images Pep Guardiola's spat with Paul Cook was caught on camera (Image: BBC)

The Gunners boss, who had named a strong team, said: "That is why football is entertainment, especially in this competition and in this country, things like that.

‌



"They believe in it and the people have it because of the history. We didn't want to go through this and we are extremely sad but we need to congratulate the opponent."
