Sports.title: Antonelli’s coronation, Mexico’s optional turn one and more Mexican GP talking points | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The world championship outcome may be a foregone conclusion but there are plenty of other talking points of note at this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix.

All over bar the shouting

There could hardly be less doubt over the destination of this year’s world drivers’ championship. Yes, theoretically there are still three drivers in the hunt, but the two who aren’t Andrea Kimi Antonelli realistically need him not to score in the next four consecutive races to still be in with a shot come the final round.

On top of that, consider that at least one of the remaining rounds might not go ahead anyway. In which case even this flimsy conjecture is moot, and the championship is already Antonelli’s.

But if, as seems almost certain, he does win the title this weekend, what a venue to do it at. If the remodelled Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez has one thing going for it, it’s the joyous theatre of F1 fever which greets drivers in the stadium at the end of the race.

Optional turn one

The opening trio of corners on the Mexico City track has been a trouble spot since Hermann Tilke’s designers reworked the layout for the race’s return in 2015. The tight corner configuration and generous run-off area make it easy for drivers to abuse track limits at this point on the track.

Last year’s start was a particularly egregious example as multiple drivers arguably benefitted from cutting the corner. Max Verstappen’s approach to it gave every indication he never intended to stay within the track’s boundaries.

Will race control take note and put stricter measures in place? There was little sign this was a priority in Austin last weekend, where track limits have long been a problem.

Debutants Slater and Mini join the rookies

At least two drivers will make their debuts in an F1 practice session this weekend. Audi’s promising rookie Freddie Slater, who finished second in Formula 3 this year, will take over Gabriel Bortoleto’s car for first practice. Alpine’s Gabriele Mini will be in Franco Colapinto’s car.

Several of the regular practice session drivers will also appear: Frederik Vesti at Mercedes, Luke Browning at Williams and Ryo Hirakawa at Haas. Some teams are yet to confirm their plans.

Mexico versus Lawson

Liam Lawson was at the centre of a bizarre incident last year when he had the misfortune to encounter two marshals on track. Incredibly, Mexico’s automobile club accused the blameless driver of being responsible for the oversight.

The FIA later made it clear Lawson had done nothing wrong. Hopefully there is no repeat of either administrative slip-up this year.

Perez hits 300

Last year’s Mexican Grand Prix was the first without a home driver since the event returned to the calendar. But Sergio Perez is back on the grid this year and will mark his 300th start in front of his home crowd.

Expect the usual huge cheers for the Guadalajaran. However the hope of a points finish looks as remote as ever. Indeed, the combination of high cooling demands and several heavy braking points could aggravate one of Cadillac’s most obvious weaknesses.

Sports.content:
With Andrea Kimi Antonelli poised to win the world championship this weekend, has Formula 1’s ruined season diminished his inevitable triumph? Rick disagrees:

I agree with the disappointing season but I don’t think it takes away from soon to be Antonelli’s championship season. In my almost 50 years of watching F1 there have been many unusual situations and this season will just be added to that list.

I find the biggest problem is that the current ownership knows that they can bring in more casual watchers by reducing true racing and making the spectacle more “entertaining” which in turn means more profit. Will that change? I doubt it because to the owners, it’s about the show and how much revenue it generates, not about racing.

I’ve lived in six countries, most of my life in the USA, and I can say with confidence that greed is the driving force in the country. I’m absolutely not against striving for something, working hard and making huge amounts of money. The problem is when you sacrifice the quality of your life for the desire to make more. In my opinion, that attitude is what drives F1 now and until it changes, I doubt we will see true racing.

Sports.title: Stats: Russell scored as many points as Hulkenberg in last three rounds | 2026 United States GP stats and facts
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli is on the verge of sealing a historic championship triumph following his victory in the United States Grand Prix.

George Russell was Mercedes’ most recent race-winner going into Austin, and this was Antonelli’s first win in over a month. But Russell’s fading championship challenge has collapsed entirely over the last three rounds.

The rot set in with his retirement in Malaysia, which not only left him point-less but prompted a grid penalty in Singapore. He compounded matters there by crashing out of the sprint race while leading.

The upshot is, with only an eighth and a ninth place to count from his last three grand prix weekends, Russell has added just six points to his tally in that time. He has been out-scored by eight of his rivals, including Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson, who picked up three times as many points as Russell over the period.

Underlining just how badly the last three rounds have gone for Russell, his haul of six points matches that of Nico Hulkenberg, who lies 14th in the championship standings.

Antonelli’s ninth career victory last weekend means he has now won more grands prix than his team mate. He has drawn level with rivals Charles Leclerc and Oscar Piastri – plus Piastri’s manager, Mark Webber.

Thanks to Antonelli’s success this year, and Piastri’s failure to win since last year’s Dutch Grand Prix, Italian drivers now have as many grand prix wins as Australians. Antonelli claimed the 52nd grand prix win for an Italian driver, putting the two nations level in seventh place on the all-time list.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Antonelli also scored his seventh pole position, giving him as many as Jacques Laffite. But he missed out on the fastest lap, which Leclerc scored for the second race in a row. It is Leclerc’s 15th fastest lap, matching his Ferrari predecessors Felipe Massa and Clay Regazzoni, plus three-times world champion Jackie Stewart.

Isack Hadjar equalled the best qualifying position of his career with third place. He previously achieved this in the Australian Grand Prix earlier this year.

Unusually, both Red Bull drivers finished lower than they started. However their recent upswing in form continued and they look increasingly likely to avoid finishing outside the top three in the championship for the first time since 2015. They out-scored McLaren for the fifth round in a row, have drawn level with them on 355 points, and are classified ahead of them in third place by dint of their higher finishing positions in races.

However third place for Max Verstappen means he is no longer a championship contender for the first time in almost six years. The last race Verstappen competed in which he could not take the title was the 2020 season finale at Yas Marina. He dropped out of contention for that year’s championship four rounds earlier at Imola.

Finally, Gabriel Bortoleto set a new record for the largest grid drop penalty ever issued to an F1 driver. He collected a total grid drop of 80 places after Audi replaced multiple parts of his power unit during the weekend. As he qualified 13th and started 21st, he only served 10% of the penalty. The record was previously held by Jenson Button, who had a 70-place grid penalty at the 2015 Mexican Grand Prix.

Sports.title: Amanda Serrano Deserves Farewell Despite Weak Skye Falzon Matchup
Sports.content:
Amanda Serrano’s sendoff against Skye Falzon relies on nostalgia rather than pure sporting drama. Falzon brings regional hardware and a top ranking, yet lacks proven elite credentials. What we get is a routine title defense tied to a historic milestone, an arrangement Serrano has fully earned.

Serrano wraps up her legendary run on January 9 in San Juan, Puerto Rico, streaming live on DAZN. Holding belts across seven divisions, ruling undisputed at featherweight, and enduring three grueling battles with Katie Taylor means she has nothing left to prove. Still, every fight card deserves an honest look for what it actually presents.

You can understand the business calculation from Serrano’s camp: after twenty years, seven divisions, and the physical toll of three wars with Taylor, the desire to cash a final check without risking a bad knockout or a tainted scorecard makes self-preservation sense. But for fans who actually value real drama over a victory lap, it feels empty. Ending on a layup preserves the record, but it rarely produces the kind of memorable final high note people talk about years down the road.

Falzon sports a 12-2 record with seven stoppages, holding the WBA Asia and Oceania featherweight belts. Ranked fourth by the WBA, her paperwork checks out, yet those regional honors offer very little reason to expect a competitive scrap.

Her most recent outing saw her cruise past Monika Singh on September 11 with three matching 99-91 cards. Her only losses came early, dropping bouts to Sarah Watt in December 2021 and Pam McClelland in July 2022. She brings decent momentum, but regional dominance leaves one massive question looming over the ring: what happens once Serrano starts connecting?

That gap exposes the promotion’s biggest flaw. Sanctioning bodies provide official stamps, not guaranteed entertainment. Falzon has the numbers, but nothing suggests she can truly trouble the champ.

Nobody can fault Falzon for taking the call. Any fighter chasing a world crown would be crazy to turn down a golden ticket just because critics consider them outgunned.

“One last fight. One last walk. One final chapter,” Serrano posted on X. “Boxing has given me everything. It’s taken me around the world, allowed me to chase dreams I once thought were impossible, and given me the opportunity to inspire the next generation of fighters.”

That said, nothing is completely guaranteed inside the ropes. Serrano had to grind out a close majority decision over Lucrecia Manzur during her last defense. That showing proves that any slight dip in sharpness matters, even against an opponent with a lighter record.

At its core, the main attraction remains untouched. Puerto Rico gets to salute its greatest warrior. That moment means something, so there is no reason to pretend Falzon is a monster test. Serrano gets her well-earned homecoming, while supporters get an honest look at the match in front of them.

Sports.title: Keyshawn Davis Ducks $6 Million Question After Richardson Hitchins Says Fight Is Off
Sports.content:
Keyshawn Davis fired back against claims that he priced himself out of facing Richardson Hitchins, yet his heated response sidestepped the actual financial dispute. Davis stated he signed a bout contract back in August and insists Hitchins is the opponent he targets next. He never touched the alleged $6 million purse demand that Hitchins claimed blew up the deal.

Hitchins ignited the dispute on October 23, declaring the contest dead across social media while revealing the financial rift:

“Keyshawn Out Priced himself to fight me Like i said i been agreed to the fight going on 2 months i was wondering what was the hold up but He was asking for 6ms to fight me And mind you boy never even made more than a M in boxing #FIGHTOFF son a clown.”

Taking to social media, Davis focused heavily on personal bravery, flashing his Olympic pedigree to shut down talk that he backs down from rivals. That approach silences people questioning his heart. It does nothing to explain how two fighters calling each other out still managed to stall negotiations.

“Back in August, before he even started doing the interviews, I DM’d him saying, ‘The ink is dry. Did you sign your contract?’ He said, ‘Business will get handled soon.’ … Now he’s saying I overpriced myself. So he never got back with me that he signed,” Davis stated.

That reported interaction gives Davis his firmest talking point. If accurate, he told Hitchins his paperwork was locked down well before this public spat erupted, establishing a distinct timeline that challenges the opposing narrative.

The mystery sits inside whatever document he inked. Davis omitted the purse figures, skipped any special clauses, and avoided confirming if Hitchins held matching conditions. Putting ink to paper does not prove the final terms worked for both camps.

Davis shifted quickly from quoting direct messages to guessing at his rival status. He assumed Hitchins probably avoided signing altogether, claiming that explained sudden talk about Brian Norman. The gap in knowledge counts. Davis can vouch for his own side of the table; he cannot verify the paperwork across the divide.

Hitchins brought up an exorbitant asking price, highlighting that Davis never collected a $ 1 million purse in his career. Davis countered with his readiness to trade punches. Both boxers can crave the contest while remaining completely split on compensation. Neither has established the pay-per-view drawing power required to justify an eight-figure event budget.

Davis has every right to secure his worth. Silencing accusations that excessive demands derailed the bout requires clear numbers: his requested purse, the promoter counteroffer, and the actual status of that proposal. A medal collection cannot clarify a balance sheet.

The talk surrounding Devin Haney clearly touched a nerve. Davis brought up Haney multiple times, batting away claims of fear while refusing to detail the actual business negotiations. Running into another collapsed deal gives detractors more ammunition, and repeating how fearless he feels will not convince skeptics.

“I want my next fight to be you. I don’t want nobody else,” Davis told Hitchins directly.

He told fans to flood the comment sections and prod his rival into accepting the contest. Shifting the heat onto an opponent plays well to an audience, yet it expects spectators to assign blame without seeing a single page of the paperwork.

Davis gave the boxing world a specific claim to chase by pointing to an August signature. The real challenge comes down to whether those terms back up his stance on the purse. Until he addresses the numbers behind that signature, he delivers pure theatrical heat without resolving the financial facts.

Sports.title: Andy Cruz Loses His Zero, Keeps His Problem
Sports.content:
Andy Cruz’s first professional defeat did little to boost his appeal to lightweight’s marquee names. Raymond Muratalla edged him in a grueling encounter that reinforced how dangerous Cruz remains. He surrendered his spotless record, yet none of the elite skill that makes him a nightmare opponent disappeared.

Cruz still demands top-tier competition. “William Zepeda. I’m coming for you,” he told reporters, singling out the WBC champion. Calling out the division’s best is simple enough. Persuading a champion to share a ring with him when safer, lucrative options exist is the real hurdle.

Muratalla earned respect for meeting Cruz head-on to retain his IBF belt. He brought steady pressure, landed big shots, and took home a majority decision. The scorecards of 114–114, 116–112, and 118–110 painted wildly divergent pictures of the bout. The Ring’s post-fight analysis favored Muratalla’s aggression while raising eyebrows at the wide 118–110 total.

The outcome proved Cruz could be outpointed at championship level. It offered zero comfort to rivals expecting an easy night. Muratalla worked relentlessly for all 12 rounds against a challenger who kept landing sharp counters. The loss revealed technical adjustments Cruz must make, yet his durability and ring IQ stayed intact.

Cruz answered in July by halting Abraham Montoya inside three rounds. That stoppage lifted his record to 7–1 with four knockouts, keeping his name in the mix. Steamrolling Montoya could not erase the tactical questions from the Muratalla clash. Facing another elite technician will reveal much more.

Landing that test remains the obstacle. Muratalla vacated his 135-pound strap to chase opportunities above, joined by Shakur Stevenson, who also left the division behind. Their exits put Zepeda and Abdullah Mason atop The Ring’s lightweight rankings, keeping Cruz hovering in the contender pack.

Mason recently floated Zepeda and Joe Cordina as potential targets. A clash with Zepeda brings a unification, while Cordina offers a credible defense. Cruz sat completely outside those discussions, despite loudly hunting Zepeda himself. That reality highlights his dilemma. Rival champions are not necessarily running scared, but they are looking elsewhere.

Cruz risks watching this cycle repeat. Elite fighters can chase unification paydays or fan-friendly matchups while he bides his time. Technical wizardry gives him an edge in any ring, but skill alone provides little financial incentive for rivals to take the risk.

The IBF’s mandate ordering Cruz to fight Artur Subkhankulov for the vacant lightweight crown provides an answer. Grabbing that strap would hand Cruz real leverage, giving unifications a genuine prize to dangle.

Even then, deals require willing partners. Cruz understands the gap between deserving a shot and securing one. His immediate test is capturing the title. Finding out if holding gold finally forces the division’s biggest stars to answer his call comes next.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Shows His Brilliance Against Emanuel Navarrete
Sports.content:
San Antonio, Texas – O’Shaquie “Ice Water” Foster demonstrated his technical boxing skills Saturday night by boxing brilliantly to defeat Emanuel “Vaquero” Navarrete by unanimous decision (115-111, 118-108×2). He outpointed him by putting on a masterclass. He was offensively sharp and defensively elusive.

Scoring a pair of knockdowns in the twelfth round and holding him to career lows in both total punches landed (99) and connect rate (18.8 %), Vaquero struggled offensively, not being able to land anything of significance, finding it difficult to find the target all night. His connect rate was anemic, landing in the single digits for 8 of the 12 rounds (Compubox).

With the win Foster (26-3, 12 KOs) captured the vacant Ring Magazine super featherweight championship and unified the WBO, IBF, and WBC titles. He now becomes the frontrunner for the fighter of the year award, having earned victories over Raymond Ford and Navarrete (40-3- 1, 33 KOs).

After the win, Foster told the media at the post-fight scrum, “I feel like it was a great performance. I finished strong man. I put him down twice at the end. I feel like there was a lot of people raving saying that I didn’t have no power and that I wasn’t going to be able to keep him off of me. I feel like I showed them tonight that I’m an all-around fighter.”

Many boxing experts believed this fight to be a 50-50 fight where either fighter could have come out victorious. O’Shaquie proved Saturday he is an elite fighter, having defeated another top fighter.

Since having lost controversially to Robson Conceicao in July of 2024, he’s showed significant improvement since then. Earning his revenge in the rematch against Conceicao, then defeating Stephen Fulton convincingly, followed by his most recent performances against Ford and Navarrete.

Vasiliy Lomachenko seems poised to come out of retirement and make an undisputed run in the 130-pound division, stating this is his normal weight and that he wants to become undisputed again.

Foster has his eyes set on becoming undisputed champion and made it known to the media that this is his immediate goal and does not want to deviate from this by entertaining a fight with Shakur Stevenson or Lomachenko; for now, he wants to become undisputed.

The other divisional titleholder is WBA super featherweight champion Anthony Cacace, who is set to defend his title next against Nick Ball on December 19. O’Shaquie has every intent of pursuing a fight against the winner.

He did say he would be willing to fight Lomachenko afterwards, “I want Loma to get a tune-up fight or something cuz when I beat him I don’t want any excuses, man. He been retired.” With the return of Loma and Foster on the verge of becoming undisputed, it’s becoming one of the must-watch divisions.

Sports.title: Keith Thurman Can’t Talk Away The Fundora Loss
Sports.content:
Keith Thurman’s dismissal of Sebastian Fundora’s power makes his own performance harder to explain. If the punches were only “medium,” as Thurman insists, the unanswered question is why he couldn’t produce enough offense to keep the referee out of their fight.

“Medium. Medium, bro,” Thurman said to Brian Custer. “Like, I mean, come on. He never knocked me down.” Thurman’s defense of his performance rests heavily on that distinction: Fundora stopped him, but never put him on the floor.

Thurman rejected Fundora’s comment, relayed by Brian, that the referee had saved him from further punishment. He said a second-round counter pushed him downward because of Fundora’s height, rather than buckling his legs, and maintained that he could handle the punches.

“I’ve been in the ring with a lot of punchers, you know? I mean, at welterweight, Manny Pacquiao, Danny Garcia,” Thurman said. “It was medium. I could take that all day.”

That comparison draws on Thurman’s championship past, but his experience against established punchers cannot settle whether he was defending himself effectively against Fundora. His own description of the fight supplies a more revealing explanation than the power rating.

Thurman said Fundora’s height and reach were more difficult to deal with than he expected. Tall sparring partners had not fully prepared him for the distance he encountered, and he was still adjusting when the referee intervened.

Fundora did not need every punch to hurt Thurman badly if his reach and output kept Thurman occupied with protecting himself.

Thurman wanted more time, saying he had moved toward the middle of the ring and was beginning to feel comfortable defensively. He believed the decision should have remained with him and his corner.

“I just wish the ref would have used his eyes a little bit more and let me and my team make the decision, man,” Thurman said. “Like, if we get into the eighth round and it’s not getting any better, so be it. But I was determined to take the young man’s punches. It wasn’t really my night. My hands were not going.”

Thurman weakens his own argument by admitting he wasn’t throwing back. Being able to take Fundora’s punches wasn’t enough. He needed to answer them, and the referee didn’t have to wait for a knockdown to intervene.

Thurman also blamed an awkward weight cut and acknowledged a poor performance. Those explanations might account for his struggles, but they don’t explain why he believes more rounds would have changed anything.

Thurman had more to say when he discussed Fundora’s height, reach, and punch output. He admitted he couldn’t get comfortable against them. Calling Fundora’s power “medium” does nothing to explain why he couldn’t get past those advantages and land his own shots.

That version of the Fundora loss gives Golden Boy and DAZN something to sell: Thurman was still adjusting, his chin held up, and the referee denied him a chance to turn things around. It makes Ortiz sound like he’s facing a dangerous veteran whose right hand could punish a mistake. The harder sell is explaining how Thurman will land that punch after admitting he couldn’t get his offense going against Fundora.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Buys Time, But Bektemir Melikuziev Isn’t Going Away
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia secured room to maneuver around an overdue mandatory defense, clearing a route to meet Nikita Zon on October 31 with his WBA super middleweight belt intact. Bektemir Melikuziev receives a firmer pledge for what follows, though Munguia reaps the instant reward.

This reported step aside setup introduces clear barriers against future stalls. Guardrails like these are important given that the WBA had already formally mandated the title bout. Melikuziev is asked to sit and wait on a fight the WBA deemed past due.

The sanctioning body ordered Munguia against Melikuziev back on September 21, granting both corners until October 21 to finalize terms. Official notices indicated the champion’s mandatory window actually lapsed on August 30. The champion stood obligated to face his top challenger right then.

According to a Team Munguia dispatch circulated by Cesar Seda, this new deal triggers an additional 30-day negotiating window right after October 31.

Such an extension merely sets up another round of talks instead of placing Melikuziev directly under the arena lights. No date or site was attached to that mandatory meeting. Munguia’s chosen bout holds a firm calendar spot; the actual title challenger must still wait on one.

Zanfer operations head Guillermo Brito confirmed a mutual pact exists, while leaving ultimate ratification in sanctioning hands.

“We have an arrangement, but the WBA still has to determine it,” Brito explained via Izquierdazo.

That boundary stops Munguia’s side from claiming a private deal equals formal sanctioning consent. The missing piece remains legitimate organizational approval.

The sharpest terms target what Munguia cannot pursue going forward. His camp pledges he will steer clear of any intervening bouts, including unifications, prior to squaring off with Melikuziev. The terms also rule out procedural challenges that could stall the defense, alongside a promise not to petition for WBA super champion standing.

These limits aim to shut down bypass options. A unification clash often provides an appealing detour. Seeking an elevated title tier might spark fresh bureaucratic wrangling. The paperwork aims to settle these hurdles before they fuel further delays.

Melikuziev’s camp earns points for locking down explicit pledges. Still, their worth comes down entirely to accountability. Ink on paper means little to a top contender if the next detour merely sparks another cycle of waiting.

With no money figures made public, there is zero evidence Melikuziev took a payout or parted with his title opportunity for cash.

Munguia collects his bout with Zon; Melikuziev collects signed guarantees for the future. The WBA faces the challenge of transforming those guarantees into an actual title fight with a fixed date once October 31 wraps up.

Kicking the can down the road to take on Zon buys Munguia a brief reprieve, but it does not erase the problem waiting in the wings. Melikuziev is not going to politely fade into the background, and the WBA is eventually going to run out of patience for stall tactics. Melikuziev is a legitimate puncher who brings real risk to anyone trying to play it safe at 168 pounds.

Holding a belt means taking on the top contenders when their turn arrives. If Munguia wants the prestige, the marketing power, and the leverage of being a recognized champion, he has to earn it in the ring against the rightful mandatory. If he prefers softer touches and exhibition-style tune-ups, the honorable move is to vacate the strap and let the hungry contenders fight for it. Sitting on a title while dodging a live wire like Bektemir just holds up the division.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Arrest Complicates Zuffa’s Rebuilding Job
Sports.content:
Edgar Berlanga’s reported arrest puts Zuffa Boxing in a difficult spot with a headliner whose competitive standing was already under scrutiny.

Stopping Steven Butler in seven rounds on July 26 at Madison Square Garden’s Theater gave Dana White’s outfit a clean knockout for the highlight reel, but surviving an early knockdown against a fringe operator did little to prove Berlanga belongs near the elite bracket at 168 pounds.

That sporting reality turns this legal situation into a genuine commercial problem. Berlanga needed his next fight announcement to drive the narrative and validate his position as a marquee attraction following his 2024 points loss to Saul Canelo Alvarez. Instead, public focus has abruptly shifted to serious criminal allegations while the competitive value of the Butler victory remains thin.

Lakeland Police arrested Berlanga on October 26 in Polk County, Florida, regarding an incident alleged to have occurred October 18, according to an Uncrowned report published by Yahoo Sports. Court records cite first-degree misdemeanor battery alongside a second-degree felony count of aggravated battery.

A judge set combined bail at $16,000 during an October 27 court appearance at Bartow Courthouse. His formal arraignment is set for November 17 at 8:45 a.m., where he will enter a plea. These charges remain strictly allegations, and Berlanga retains the presumption of innocence under the law.

Zuffa invested heavily in Berlanga to anchor its boxing venture, banking on his recognizable name to draw viewers. Yet his competitive trajectory required careful handling even before police became involved. Butler offered a recognizable target Berlanga could eventually wear down, but trading knockdowns with a fragile contender exposed defensive flaws that better super middleweights would punish. A win of that level cannot carry an entire promotional campaign.

Matchmakers now face frozen options. Staging another contest against lower-tier opposition might produce another finish, but it will do nothing to answer doubts about Berlanga’s ceiling against genuine contenders. Booking a significant step up in class would give his rebuilding phase real credibility, yet it carries the immediate danger of another defeat.

The legal process clouds the entire calendar. With arraignment running into late November, assembling a meaningful training camp or booking a major date becomes an expensive risk. While no upcoming bout has been formally scrapped and Zuffa has announced no disciplinary action, sponsors and broadcasters inevitably pull back when headline talent faces felony assault claims.

The real issue involves promotional credibility. Zuffa must prove that Berlanga’s performances inside the ropes warrant the attention he receives. The Butler stoppage offered a modest rebound, but it never answered the larger questions about his true ability. Now, with serious legal dates taking precedence over fight negotiations, convincing the public to take Berlanga seriously as a top contender just became far more difficult.

Promoters tolerate outside chaos for fighters who deliver elite pay-per-view numbers or dominant championship runs, but Berlanga brings neither of those things to the table.

Zuffa signed him expecting a turnkey attraction who could headline cards on name recognition alone. Instead, they inherited an expensive puzzle. His early sixteen-fight knockout streak built an inflated reputation, yet the moment Top Rank put him in with actual durable pros, the power vanished, and the technical limitations showed.

Surviving a knockdown against Steven Butler just to score a mid-tier stoppage did not convince anyone that Berlanga could hang with the monsters at super middleweight. Taking on punchers like Christian Mbilli, Osleys Iglesias, or Diego Pacheco would likely end his run as a viable headliner overnight.

That leaves Zuffa holding a contract on an expensive fighter they have to baby through soft touches, all while paying him marquee money. If Dana White and his team were already realizing that Berlanga’s ceiling is strictly as a domestic-level gatekeeper rather than an elite world champion, an aggravated battery felony arrest gives them the ultimate clean exit.

Contracts at this level always carry standard morals and conduct clauses. Invoking that language allows a promotion to walk away without paying out a severance or having to fulfill dates for a fighter who became more trouble than he is worth. If Zuffa wanted an off-ramp from the Berlanga business, the legal system just handed them one on a silver platter.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol Has Zero Reason To Grant Anthony Yarde An Unearned Shot
Sports.content:
Anthony Yarde is eyeing Dmitry Bivol before hanging up the gloves, but calling out the division elite after almost a year out of action leaves him in a tough spot. To turn that target into reality, the British light heavyweight must snap his inactivity, build momentum, and take down legitimate contenders.

Yarde has been sidelined for 11 months following his seventh-round stoppage loss to David Benavidez in November 2025. Coming off an extended break plus a stoppage defeat, there is little incentive for Bivol to grant him an unearned shot.

Still, the 35-year-old insists Bivol is the missing name on his resume. Having shared the squared circle with Sergey Kovalev, Artur Beterbiev, and Benavidez, he is eager to complete his personal sweep of the era’s best.

“A fight for me that I would have to make in my career would be Bivol, just for my own personal thing, because I fought all the best people and he’s definitely one of the best people,” Yarde told Sky Sports News. “Partly my character, partly you can call it a screw loose, I want to fight the best people in my generation.”

Nobody questions Yarde courage. He proved his grit by traveling to Russia against Kovalev, and pushed Beterbiev to the brink before being halted. The problem is that none of those valiant attempts brought home a world championship, and falling to Benavidez set him back considerably.

That leaves Bivol with virtually no motive to pick Yarde. Without a headline victory to his name recently, the Londoner cannot offer the kind of leverage or massive payday that would lure the champion into a voluntary defense. Short of capturing a mandatory slot, he has no way to force Bivol’s hand.

Father Time is ticking as well. At 35, Yarde cannot afford to sit idle waiting around for a lottery ticket. He needs activity, consistency, and meaningful wins against top 175-pound contenders to build real leverage.

Fortunately, he sees an alternate avenue. Yarde is keeping a close watch on the vacant WBC light heavyweight title rematch between Joshua Buatsi and Willy Hutchinson. Backing Buatsi to win, Yarde recognizes that an all-British grudge match would generate serious domestic buzz, while snagging that green belt would give him the exact negotiating chip he needs to tempt Bivol.

Meanwhile, Bivol is scheduled to meet Callum Smith on December 12 in Russia. Yarde believes Smith has a strong shot at an upset given his championship pedigree at 168 pounds.

Should Bivol handle business as expected, his masterclass footwork, sharp hand speed, and distance control would give Yarde fits. Before worrying about that stylistic nightmare, however, Yarde must get back to work and give the division king a real reason to pick up the phone.

Ghana News.title: Benjamin Joe Danso: Waving the banner of neutrality when convenient
Ghana News.content:
Before I begin this foray into the murky waters of public controversy, let me issue this disclaimer: this is not in any way a value judgment on any public appointment, now or at any time in the past. It is, rather, a contribution to the larger discussion of how suspicious we are of each other as a people.

Now, with that out of the way, I shall proceed to the substantive issue and the core message of this epistle.

A few weeks ago, the President swore in two new Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission (EC). As with almost every appointment to a ‘sensitive’ state institution, the news was greeted with jubilation or lamentation, depending on which side of the divide you stand. Those of us who feel no need to pick a side watched from the fence, weighing whose argument held up.

Amid the accusations and counter-accusations, one word was waved at us again and again: ‘neutrality’. One camp insisted the EC needed a neutral umpire while the other insisted the appointees were as neutral as anyone could be. My take, and here comes the shocker, is that no one above the age of five can truly be described as neutral.

To call a grown adult neutral is to discount everything that nature, nurture and socialisation have made of them. What we can and must demand of those we place in sensitive state institutions is objectivity, the discipline of being fair-minded in the face of the facts.

Think about it for a moment. A child is born into a particular home, in a particular town, speaking a particular language. Before she can spell her own name, she has absorbed which radio station plays in the kitchen every morning, which politician makes her father raise his voice, and whose posters her grandmother tears down at election time. By the time she starts school, the dust of opinion has already begun to settle on her. Add to that the church or mosque, the secondary school, the university hall, the workplace, the WhatsApp groups, the funerals where politics is argued over jollof, and you have an adult who is a walking archive of preferences, loyalties and convictions.

Now fast-forward to the moment such a person, at forty-five or fifty-five, is nominated to a high public office. By then, they have voted in several elections. They have opinions on the economy, on ‘galamsey’, on which government built which road. To demand that this person be ‘neutral’ is to demand that they be a blank slate, and that is simply not how human beings work.

Let me go further. If we ever found a fifty-year-old citizen with no opinion whatsoever on the affairs of this nation, should we really trust them to manage its elections? Such a person is either not being truthful with us or has been so disengaged from national life that they hardly qualify for the job. Neither option inspires confidence.

This is why the distinction between neutrality and objectivity matters. Neutrality is a state of being; objectivity is a discipline of doing. Neutrality concerns what is in your head and heart, which no one can audit. Objectivity concerns what you do with the evidence placed before you, which everyone can scrutinise. One is an impossible claim about a person’s inner life; the other is a measurable standard of public conduct.

Consider the football referee. Many referees grew up supporting a club. Some may still quietly celebrate when their team wins on a Sunday. We do not, and cannot, demand that they erase that boyhood love. What we demand is that when a defender clips an attacker in the box, the whistle goes, no matter whose shirt either player is wearing. The referee is not judged by the club he supported as a boy; he is judged by the penalties he awards and refuses on the day.

Or consider our judges. The judicial oath, in many Commonwealth traditions including ours, requires a judge to do right ‘without fear or favour, affection or ill-will’. Read those words carefully. The oath does not pretend that judges have no affections or ill-will. It assumes they do. It simply demands that, in the discharge of their duties, those affections be set aside. That is objectivity in a sentence, and it is a far more honest standard than the fiction of neutrality.



Which brings me to the title of this piece. If you have watched our politics long enough, you will notice something curious about the banner of neutrality: it is raised and lowered depending on who holds the flagpole. When an appointee appears to lean towards the other side, neutrality becomes a sacred principle, invoked with the passion of a Sunday sermon.

When the appointee appears to lean towards our side, the same principle suddenly becomes ‘unrealistic’, and we are reminded that ‘everyone has a background’. The party in opposition discovers neutrality; the party in power forgets it.

Then the roles switch, and the script is read again with the actors swapping costumes. A standard that applies only to your opponents is not a standard at all. It is a tactic.

The cost of this selective outrage is not small. It feeds the deep suspicion we hold of one another as a people. We have come to assume that every Ghanaian carries a party card stitched into the lining of their soul, and that no professional can ever rise above where they come from. When that assumption takes hold, no decision of any institution can ever be accepted on its merits. Every ruling is pre-judged by the perceived colours of the person who made it. The loser always cries foul, the winner always cries vindication, and the institution in the middle slowly bleeds credibility, whatever the actual quality of its work.

So what should we demand instead? We should judge appointees by their conduct rather than their pedigree. Are their decisions transparent? Do they give reasons for what they do? Are they consistent, applying the same rule to the powerful and the powerless, to friend and foe? Are they willing to rule against the side they are presumed to favour when the facts demand it? Are they open to scrutiny and correction? These are questions we can actually answer, with evidence, over time.

We must also strive build institutions that do not depend on saints. The genius of good institutional design is that it assumes people have leanings and builds guard-rails accordingly: party agents at every polling station, public collation of results, independent audits, clear rules on recusal, and courts that can review contested decisions. A well-designed system makes it difficult for any single official, however partisan their private heart, to tilt the outcome. That is a far safer bet than hoping we have found the one adult in the country without an opinion.

And for those who accept these appointments, the burden of proof is heavier on you, and rightly so. In a society as suspicious as ours, it is not enough to be objective; you must be seen to be objective, every single day. That means explaining your decisions, stepping aside where your interests are genuinely conflicted, and resisting the temptation to reward those who cheered your appointment or punish those who opposed it.

Let us, then, retire the word ‘neutral’ from our appointment debates. It promises something no human being can deliver and gives every side a convenient stick with which to beat the other. The better question to ask of anyone placed in a sensitive state institution is not ‘Where does this person come from?’ but ‘What does this person do with the facts before them?’ The first question will always divide us, because we all come from somewhere. The second can unite us, because the facts, when fairly weighed, belong to all of us.

We will never find a referee who has never loved a team. We can, however, insist that the whistle blows the same way for everyone. That is the standard. Everything else is just a banner, waved when convenient.

****

About the author: Benjamin Joe Danso is an Associate PR Director at Touchpoint Magna Carta.

Ghana News.title: Public sector workers to receive 9% pay increase in 2027 and 10% in 2028
Ghana News.content:
Public sector workers are set to receive a 9 per cent increase in total remuneration in 2027, followed by a 10 per cent across-the-board salary increase in 2028.

The two-year agreement was reached between the government and organised labour following negotiations under the Public Services Joint Standing Negotiating Committee.

The Secretary-General of the Trades Union Congress (TUC), Joshua Ansah, says the 2027 adjustment comprises an 8 per cent increase in base pay, alongside an additional 1 per cent provision to address other conditions of service.

For 2028, the parties have agreed on a 10 per cent increase in base pay.

Mr Ansah explained that the additional 1 per cent provision in 2027 is intended to address existing inequalities in public sector allowances and improve fairness in remuneration.

He said the arrangement will particularly focus on protecting lower-paid and vulnerable workers.

"Beyond the percentage increases, fairness in the allowances remains a central concern. The additional one per cent provision is intended to help address existing distortions and inequalities in conditions of service, with particular attention to protecting lower-paid and vulnerable workers," he said.

He acknowledged that the agreement may not meet every expectation but described it as progress towards protecting workers' purchasing power.

"This agreement may not meet every expectation. It represents progress in our efforts to protect workers' purchasing power," he added.

Mr Ansah also indicated that organised labour and government would continue working together over the two-year period to address existing inequalities in public sector pay administration.

He stressed the need for fairness in the implementation of the agreement, particularly as the country transitions from the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission to an Independent Public Emoluments Commission (IPEC).

Ghana News.title: “The prison is built for human beings, not animals” – Peter Toobu backs Wontumi’s call for reforms
Ghana News.content:
Chairman Wontumi

The Member of Parliament for Wa West, Peter Lanchene Toobu, has called for a national conversation on prison conditions and the need to ensure that inmates are treated humanely, regardless of the offences for which they are serving sentences.

His comments follow former New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi’s call for sweeping reforms in Ghana’s prison system, including a dedicated prison hospital, improved welfare for prison officers, and regulated conjugal visits for inmates.

The proposals follow his remand on July 20, 2026, according to a statement issued on Tuesday by his spokesperson, Dr Palgrave Boakye-Danquah to mark his 100 days in detention.

Dr Boakye-Danquah said his visits to Chairman Wontumi had provided an opportunity for the politician to reflect on conditions within the Ghana Prisons Service, which he believes have seen limited structural improvement since 1962.

Chairman Wontumi is advocating a shift from a punishment-focused system to one that prioritises rehabilitation, welfare and productivity.

Speaking on Adom FM’s Dwaso Nsem, Mr Toobu said prisons were established not only to protect the public by keeping offenders away from society but also to reform them.

He argued that committing a crime should not strip an individual of their humanity, stressing that inmates deserve humane treatment while serving their sentences.

“The prison is built for human beings, not animals. People are sent to prison as a means of reformation and also for public safety because criminals are incapacitated,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Social expectations, political financing threaten judicial integrity – Valentin Kwasi Mensah
Ghana News.content:
Governance specialist Valentin Kwasi Mensah has warned that social expectations and political financing can undermine judicial impartiality in Ghana, arguing that threats to the independence of public officials extend beyond direct political interference.

Speaking at a JoyNews public lecture on the theme “Even Judges Must Eat – An Outside-In Provocation,” Mr Mensah said public officials often face demands from relatives, friends, former schoolmates, religious communities and political supporters that could influence their decisions.

“Requests for preferential treatment often arrive as appeals to loyalty or gratitude,” he said.

Mr Mensah cited his 2008 doctoral research at Oxford Brookes University, which examined cultural and institutional pressures through surveys and 35 interviews.

He referred to one participant, identified as PA2, who advocated limiting approaches to judges involving personal connections.

“He should be cut off from such things so that when he goes he reads the case and gives objective judgements,” the participant said.

Mr Mensah said the account illustrated concerns about pressure from personal relationships, but cautioned that it did not show all judges succumb to such demands.

He acknowledged the importance of family and community ties but warned that expectations around funerals, weddings, and other social events could put financial pressure on public officials, especially when lavish spending and reciprocal favours were expected.

Mr Mensah argued that improving salaries and working conditions was important but insufficient without clear ethical standards and effective enforcement.

He cited Articles 284 and 286 of Ghana’s 1992 Constitution, which address conflicts of interest and asset declarations respectively, stressing the need to ensure that public officials comply with applicable rules.

“Public office should never become a means of financing social status or rewarding personal networks,” he said.

Mr Mensah also raised concerns about political financing, warning that public institutions could become vulnerable to private interests when financial contributions to political parties are viewed as investments to be repaid through appointments, contracts or privileged access.

He said greater transparency in political financing, alongside credible oversight, could help address the risks.

“Transparent financing and credible scrutiny can help interrupt that cycle,” he said.

The JoyNews public lecture brought together stakeholders to discuss challenges facing Ghana’s judiciary and possible reforms to strengthen judicial independence, accountability and public confidence in the justice system.

Ghana News.title: Governance specialist calls for digital reforms to improve justice delivery
Ghana News.content:
Governance specialist Valentin Kwasi Mensah has called for greater transparency in judicial appointments and sustained investment in technology to improve justice delivery, citing declining public confidence in Ghana’s courts.

Speaking at a JoyNews public lecture on the theme “Even Judges Must Eat – An Outside-In Provocation,” Mr Mensah cited Afrobarometer’s 2024 survey, which found that 35% of Ghanaians trusted the courts somewhat or a lot, down from 57% in 2017.

He said the figures highlighted the need for reforms that would strengthen accountability and demonstrate fairness in the administration of justice.

“Such perceptions underline the need to rebuild confidence through visible fairness and accountability,” he said.

Mr Mensah noted that Article 144 of the 1992 Constitution outlines the processes for appointing judges to Ghana’s superior courts, involving different constitutional actors depending on the court.

He argued that while sharing responsibility for appointments could provide safeguards, the procedures must also inspire public confidence.

“Sharing responsibility creates safeguards, but procedures must also inspire public confidence,” he said.

He proposed publishing vacancies, establishing clear selection criteria and making appointment procedures more transparent to help the public assess whether merit guides the process.

Citing the United Kingdom’s experience, Mr Mensah referred to the Constitutional Reform Act 2005, which established a Judicial Appointments Commission that began operating in 2006, principally in England and Wales.

He said Ghana could draw lessons from the British model’s emphasis on merit and good character without necessarily adopting the same system.

Mr Mensah also called for sustained investment in digital systems to make court processes more efficient and accessible.

He proposed expanding electronic filing, searchable court records, digital payment systems and reliable hearing schedules to reduce administrative bottlenecks and improve the experience of court users.

“These could reduce missing files, unnecessary journeys, and opportunities for unofficial payments,” he said.

He also advocated case management systems that record adjournments and the reasons for them, enabling judges and court administrators to identify avoidable delays and improve efficiency.

Mr Mensah said citizens should be able to track the progress of their cases and access published judgments.

However, he cautioned that digital reforms would require regular maintenance, staff training, cybersecurity safeguards and appropriate judicial oversight.

He stressed that people without internet access or the skills to use digital platforms must also receive assistance.

“A computer system that excludes citizens cannot deliver accessible justice,” he warned.

The JoyNews public lecture brought together stakeholders to examine challenges facing the judiciary and consider practical reforms to improve the administration of justice.

Ghana News.title: Nacee announces star-studded second edition of KAVOD for November 8
Ghana News.content:
Award-winning musician, song writer and record producer Nacee is preparing to stage the second edition of his entertainment event, KAVOD 26, at the National Theatre in Accra on Sunday, November 8, 2026.

Scheduled to begin at 5 p.m., the event will combine live gospel music, theatrical performances and stand-up comedy, bringing musicians, actors and comedians together for a single production.

The musical lineup includes Nacee, Soul Winners, Cindy Thompson, Kofi Peprah, Yvonne Mends and Joe Mettle.

The theatrical segment will feature Vivian Jill, Killer Ntua, Clemento Suarez, Foster Romanus, Deaconess Abokoma, Jeneral Ntatia and DeLong, among others.

The comedy lineup includes Jacinta, Parrot Mouth, Jeffrey Nortey, Comedy Boy and Visa Boy, Adam Best and G.H. Pookie.

Building on the first edition

KAVOD returns after its maiden edition at the National Theatre on November 26, 2023, when Nacee introduced a format that extended beyond a conventional gospel concert.

The first edition combined music with a stage play inspired by the musician’s personal journey, exploring his humble beginnings, early struggles and eventual progress in the music industry.

The production also examined his work across gospel and secular music, his involvement in political campaign songs and the challenges he encountered while building his career.

Comedians Foster Romanus and Clemento Suarez led a notable segment featuring a fictional radio discussion. The scene explored public debate surrounding Nacee’s collaboration with rapper Guru on the song Boys Boys.

The production reached a climax when Nacee emerged from beneath the stage dressed in white and launched into a live musical performance. Finalists from the Aseda Open Verse Challenge also performed a medley of songs.

The maiden edition attracted several prominent personalities, including gospel musicians Sonnie Badu, Empress Gifty and Piesie Esther, alongside political figures and other entertainment industry stakeholders.

The 2026 edition will again bring together music, comedy and theatre, continuing the event’s approach of combining different forms of live entertainment in one production.

Tickets

Standard tickets are priced at GH¢200, while VIP tickets cost GH¢300. For tickets and enquiries, patrons can call 0597143961.

The event is being promoted under the tagline “KAVOD 26: Where Comedy Meets Theatre and Music.”

Ghana News.title: Fund judiciary adequately to protect judicial independence – Valentin Mensah
Ghana News.content:
Governance specialist Valentin Kwasi Mensah has called for adequate funding and resources for Ghana’s judiciary, arguing that judicial independence cannot be guaranteed without the financial and material capacity to deliver justice.

Speaking at a JoyNews public lecture on the theme “Even Judges Must Eat – An Outside-In Provocation,” Mr Mensah said judges could be independent in principle but struggle to perform their duties effectively if courts lacked adequate staff, functional computers and operational funds.

“Even judges must eat captures an important truth. Judges and court workers need decent conditions, while courts need buildings, records, equipment and functioning systems. Independence requires the means to do the work,” he said.

Mr Mensah noted that Ghana’s 1992 Constitution provides safeguards for judicial independence, including provisions under Article 127 on the independence of the judiciary and aspects of its financial administration.

He also cited provisions concerning judicial administrative expenses, conditions of service and the release of funds, alongside the legal framework governing the administration and financing of the Judicial Service.

However, he argued that constitutional safeguards must be matched by effective implementation and greater transparency in the allocation and use of public funds.

“Citizens should be able to see what courts request, what Parliament approves, what is released and how the money is spent. Institutions receiving public funds must explain both their needs and their results,” he said.

Mr Mensah referred to a 1988 study published by the Centre for the Independence of Judges and Lawyers, which distinguished between the freedom of judges to decide cases and the employment security and material conditions needed to sustain that freedom.

He warned that constitutional protections could lose their practical value if inflation weakened the purchasing power of judicial salaries or if approved funding commitments were not met.

His remarks highlighted the relationship between the financial security of judicial officers, the operational capacity of courts and the effective administration of justice.

The lecture, organised by JoyNews in collaboration with professional bodies, brought together stakeholders to discuss the state of Ghana’s judiciary and reforms needed to improve the delivery of justice.

Mr Mensah’s intervention focused on the need to ensure that courts have the personnel, equipment and funding required to function effectively, while maintaining accountability for the use of public resources.

Ghana News.title: Ghana–New Zealand Chamber seeks tourism partnerships between the two countries
Ghana News.content:
The Executive Director of the Ghana–New Zealand Chamber of Commerce, Mr Isaac Koumessina,

The Ghana-New Zealand Chamber of Commerce is exploring opportunities to strengthen tourism and business ties between Ghana and New Zealand by connecting tourism operators, guides and industry stakeholders in both countries.

The Executive Director of the Ghana–New Zealand Chamber of Commerce, Mr Isaac Koumessina, said the initiative would create opportunities for both countries to share tourism experiences, promote their attractions and develop partnerships within the sector.

Speaking on the sidelines of the recently concluded 2026 Inter Tourism Expo in Cape Coast, he said the Chamber was working to facilitate connections between Ghanaian tourism businesses and their counterparts in New Zealand.

Mr Kumesina said the Chamber’s involvement in the sixth edition of the expo followed an agreement with the organisers to collaborate on promoting tourism and business opportunities.

“When Inter Tourism Expo contacted us, it was an exciting opportunity for us to collaborate. We had an MoU signed, and then we decided that we have to support the Inter Tourism Expo, the sixth edition of the Tourism Expo,” he said.

He disclosed that the Chamber had held discussions with the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) on tourism and other sectors, including energy, as part of efforts to identify areas for cooperation.

According to him, GIPA had also requested the organisation of an event to facilitate engagement with stakeholders in New Zealand and explore opportunities for linking tourism attractions in both countries.

“Now, the GIPA also requested that we organise an event to get them into New Zealand. Then they can find out how many Ghanaians are in New Zealand, what are the tourism attraction areas in New Zealand, and how we can link both tourism attraction-related events between New Zealand and Ghana,” he said.

Mr Kumesina said the proposed engagement would also provide an opportunity to connect tour operators and guides in Cape Coast with tourism agencies in New Zealand, enabling them to showcase local attractions and explore potential partnerships.

He said stronger cooperation could help businesses in both countries benefit from tourism-related opportunities while expanding international exposure for Ghana’s tourism industry.

The Chamber’s initiative comes as Ghana continues to explore ways to attract more international visitors and strengthen tourism’s contribution to economic development.

Mr Kumesina also called for greater coordination among Ghana’s tourism agencies, citing New Zealand’s year-round tourism activities as a model Ghana could consider adopting to sustain visitor interest and create more business opportunities.

He said stronger collaboration among tourism stakeholders, coupled with targeted promotion, could help position Ghana as a destination offering activities and experiences throughout the year.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
