The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Mr Ike, who aspired to vie for the House of Representatives’ seat for AMAC/Bwari Federal Constituency, Abuja, for the 2027 general elections on the platform of Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), lost the bid in a primary poll.

Mr Olayinka, the FCT minister’s aide, through a post on X in May, allegedly mocked Mr Ike and leaked his confidential voter registration details on social media, in the aftermath of the actor’s loss.

The post allegedly showed details of Mr Ike’s voter registration transfer from Imo State to the nation’s capital.

Meanwhile, Mr Ike, through his lawyer L. T. Adeh sued Mr Olayinka and INEC in the suit marked: FHC/ABJ/CS/1272/2026.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He asked the court to declare that Mr Olayinka’s decision to publish his database on X without his approval “amounts to gross breach and violation of the applicant’s fundamental right to privacy and the protection of personal data.”

Mr Ike argued that Section 37 of the Nigerian constitution, Article 12 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and Sections 24 & 39 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 guaranteed his right to privacy and protection of personal data.

The actor asked the court to declare that INEC owed him and other voters a “statutory duty of care” to protect their private data against unauthorised access.

The applicant, therefore, prayed the court to award him N10 billion against Mr Olayinka and INEC as aggravated and general damages, to be paid jointly and severally for violating his fundamental right to privacy.

He sought a declaration that the press release by INEC dated 2 June, in reaction to the viral publication and circulation of his personal voter information and private data on social media by Mr Olayinka, amounted to a tacit admission of guilt and liability to him.

Mr Ike also sought an order directing Mr Olayinka to immediately retract and pull down the offensive post and publication on his social media X handle, @OlayinkaLere, containing screenshots of his personal voter information and private data.

He sought an order directing him to immediately tender an unreserved apology in writing for breach and violation of his fundamental right.

But responding in separate counter-affidavits, INEC and Mr Olayinka urged the court to dismiss the suit.

INEC stated that the subject of the post complained about by Mr Ike in the suit was neither classified, sensitive nor confidential information.

In the counter-affidavit sworn by Anthonia Makwe, an Assistant Director/Data Protection Officer in the Legal Drafting and Clearance Department, said that such information is displayed and published in accordance with the Electoral Act, 2026.

It stressed that the electoral body had the “statutorily and constitutional power to make available information of its voters to the general public without the consent of any registered voter.”

It said its statutory responsibility included the compilation, maintenance, display, publication, certification and management of the register of voters in accordance with the constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), the Electoral Act 2026, and the National Data Protection Act 2023.

It said what was alleged to be posted by Mr Olayinka on his X handle did not emanate from the commission.

“The 2nd respondent, as a data controller, has never breached its statutory duty of care, custody and protection of personal voter information and data, it owes the applicant and other Voters under its secured portal and restricted database, ” the commission also stated.

On his part, Mr Olayinka stated in his counter-affidavit he personally swore, Mr Ike’s suit was brought in bad faith.

He said the only information contained in the document he published was Mr Ike’s name and passport photograph, and that the information was already in the public domain.

He said contrary to Mr Ike’s claims, the information he published was not only in the public domain, it was also not accessed through any unlawful means.

Mr Olayinka stated that he did not owe the actor any duty of care and confidentiality and did not require his consent to publish his name and passport photograph that was already in the public domain.

He said Mr Ike, who brought himself to contest election into the House of Representatives, cannot be traumatised by the circulation of his name and passport photograph which he personally presented to the public when seeking to contest election, and as a Nollywood star.

He argued that information supplied in voter cards is not private data because by the provision of Section 19(1) of the Electoral Act, 2026, INEC is mandated to publish such information, not later than 90 days to the general elections.

He said contrary to Mr Ike’s deposition, the only information contained in the document published by him was his name and passport photograph.

He said the publication was done when Mr Ike led a team of hoodlums to INEC office to disrupt INEC’s activities immediately he declared his intention to contest the election.

According to him, the publication was to remind him of the recent change of his voter registration area.

He said it was to also draw the public’s attention to the statutory provision to avoid any breach of the law.

He said contrary to Mr Ike’s submission, the applicant who submitted his personal data and information to INEC and to the general public when he decided to contest could not feel unsafe and traumatised by the publication of his name and passport photograph.

Mr Olayinka said contrary to Mr Ike’s claim, INEC admitted in its press release that “there was no external breach of its CVR database, no hacking incident and no unauthorised external access to the commission’s ICT infrastructure.”

He argued that the purported injury suffered by Mr Ike was not caused by him who is not a data controller under the Nigerian Data Protection Act, 2023, and who does not owe him any obligation to safeguard his documents.

Mr Olayinka stated that the prayers in the suit, including N10 billion in damages, was in bad faith and “an indication that the applicant is a gold digger, who wants to reap where he did not sow.”

He insisted that he cannot pay damages for information that was already publicly accessible at the time of the publication.

He, therefore, urged the court to dismiss the suit in the interest of justice.

(NAN)

World.title: Niger Miners’ Saga: NSCDC death cell cleaned to destroy evidence, probe panel member says
World.content:
The cell of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) where 33 suspected illegal miners died in Minna, Niger State, was allegedly washed, disinfected and renumbered in an attempt to destroy evidence, a member of the federal government’s investigation committee has said.

Deji Adeyanju, a lawyer and human rights activist who served on the 10-member Independent Investigation Committee, disclosed this in a post on his social media account on Wednesday, citing findings in the committee’s report.

“NSCDC Cell was washed clean, disinfected, renumbered in an attempt to destroy evidence after the death of 33 miners,” Mr Adeyanju wrote.

The allegation raises further questions about the handling of evidence following the deaths of suspected illegal miners in NSCDC custody in Minna in September.

Panel recommends prosecution

The latest disclosure follows Mr Adeyanju’s earlier post announcing that the committee had submitted its report to the federal government and recommended prosecuting officers involved in the deaths for murder and other offences.

He also said the committee recommended a comprehensive overhaul of the NSCDC’s leadership, compensation for the victims’ families and the formalisation of artisanal mining.

On Wednesday, the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, said the committee had described the deaths as a preventable custodial tragedy caused by severe overcrowding, inadequate ventilation, prolonged exposure to extreme heat and dehydration.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In a statement on his official Facebook page, Mr Tunji-Ojo said the committee found that these conditions, not a disease outbreak, led to the deaths.

The minister added that the report had been transmitted to the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation for judicial action. He also warned that officers who attempted to conceal, disrupt, or destroy evidence would be held accountable.

Background

The federal government constituted the independent committee on 19 September following President Bola Tinubu’s directive for a full and transparent investigation into the deaths.

The incident followed the arrest of suspected illegal miners during operations in Minna on 15 and 16 September. Niger State NSCDC Commandant Suberu Aniviye and 20 other officers were subsequently suspended in connection with the incident.

On 27 October, TheCable reported that the committee had identified asphyxiation, or the deprivation of adequate oxygen, as the cause of death. Committee chairman Jonathan Kure said investigators inspected the detention facility, conducted autopsies and collected witness statements and forensic evidence.

The minister’s subsequent statement attributed the deaths to conditions inside the cell and described the incident as preventable.

The allegation that the cell was cleaned, disinfected and renumbered has not been independently verified by PREMIUM TIMES. The committee’s full report and any official response from the NSCDC on the specific allegation were not immediately available.

World.title: CBD COP17: Indigenous groups urge UN to halt wildlife carbon, biodiversity credits
World.content:
Indigenous Peoples and civil society groups have called on the United Nations to halt the monetisation of sacred animals and nature as “natural capital” for carbon and biodiversity markets, warning that the practice could contribute to wildlife extinction.

The groups made the call on Tuesday on the sidelines of the ongoing 17th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP17) in Yerevan, Armenia.

They expressed concern that animals such as buffalo, jaguars, orangutans and whales were being incorporated into offset schemes that, they argued, could allow oil and mining companies to portray themselves as environmentally responsible without addressing the damage caused by their operations.

“Alarmed that buffalo, jaguars, orangutans and even whales are being converted into offsets to greenwash oil and mining companies, Indigenous Peoples and civil society demand that the United Nations immediately stop monetising their sacred animals and nature as ‘natural capital’ for carbon and biodiversity markets because it will contribute to their extinction,” the groups said.

The concerns come amid contentious negotiations over Article 8(j) of the Convention, which calls on parties to respect, preserve and maintain the traditional knowledge, innovations and practices of Indigenous Peoples and local communities relevant to biodiversity conservation.

The provision also recognises the importance of the knowledge and practices of Indigenous Peoples and local communities to the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity.

Concerns over biodiversity financing

The dispute over nature-based financial mechanisms comes as delegates at COP17 continue negotiations on how to implement the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, which sets global targets for halting and reversing biodiversity loss by 2030.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Since negotiations began last week, major questions have remained over which countries and stakeholders should contribute to international biodiversity financing, how much funding should be mobilised and the mechanisms through which the resources should be channelled.

Parties also remain divided over language on reducing or phasing out incentives harmful to biodiversity, including certain agricultural subsidies.

Other unresolved issues include which commercial users of digital sequence information should contribute to the Cali Fund, arrangements for a new permanent body on Indigenous Peoples and local communities under Article 8(j), and how biodiversity action should align with climate commitments and other international obligations.

Against this backdrop, Indigenous representatives and environmental organisations have warned that carbon and biodiversity credit schemes could undermine conservation efforts if they allow companies to offset environmental damage rather than prevent it.

Indigenous groups reject monetisation of sacred animals

Aimee Robeson, executive director of Cultural Survival, said biodiversity conservation should not depend on assigning monetary values to animals and ecosystem services.

“If we truly care about biodiversity, we should not be tempted to monetise our relatives nor ecosystem services like carbon sequestration, because they have inherent value that cannot be reduced to a dollar amount,” Ms Robeson said.

She described market-based schemes as false solutions that could worsen existing environmental crises, arguing that they could lead to biodiversity loss and the degradation of ecosystems.

“There can be no sacrifice zones, no trade-offs and no offsets if we want life on Mother Earth to survive for generations to come,” she said.

Tom Goldtooth, executive director of the Indigenous Environmental Network, said Indigenous Peoples regard nature as a relative rather than a financial asset.

“For Indigenous Peoples, nature is not an asset class, she is our Mother,” Mr Goldtooth said.

He specifically rejected the use of buffalo in carbon credit schemes, describing the animals as central to Indigenous identity and heritage.

Mr Goldtooth recalled that commercial slaughter reduced the buffalo population from an estimated 60 million to 70 million in 1853 to only a few thousand by the 1880s.

He criticised proposals to use buffalo-related soil carbon storage to generate credits that could allow polluters to continue emitting greenhouse gases.

“Our buffalo, Tanka Oyate, are part of our genesis, not ‘bison bonds’. Carbon trading is an offensive scam that threatens the future of humanity. Bring back the buffalo, not colonialism!” he said.

Jaguar and orangutan offsets criticised

Wilmer Lucitante of UDAPT, Friends of the Earth-Ecuador and the Indigenous A’i Kofán Nation of the Ecuadorian Amazon also criticised the use of jaguar habitats to generate carbon credits.

He said monetising the animals could provide cover for extractive industries while failing to address the threats posed by oil drilling and mining.

“Turning our sacred jaguars into carbon credits is a false solution to climate change that accelerates their extinction, while greenwashing extractive industries. Instead of monetising wildlife, we need to stop oil drilling and mining in the Amazon,” Mr Lucitante said.

In Indonesia, Andine Fahira Lubis of the North Sumatra regional office of WALHI, also known as Friends of the Earth-Indonesia, raised concerns over biodiversity offsets involving the critically endangered Tapanuli orangutan.

With fewer than 800 individuals remaining, the species is considered one of the world’s rarest great apes.

Ms Lubis alleged that the orangutans were being used in biodiversity offset schemes associated with the Martabe Gold Mine in Sumatra, operated by PT Agincourt Resources, a subsidiary of Jardine Matheson.

The mine is located in the Batang Toru ecosystem, within Indigenous Peoples’ territories.

“Not only is the sheer hypocrisy of orangutan offsets staggering, but as our report clearly shows, offsets cannot redeem the irreplaceable,” she said.

Armenian mine raises further concerns

The debate also extends to mining projects in Armenia, the host country of COP17.

Nazeli Vardanyan, director of Armenian Forests, said the controversial Amulsar gold mine planned to use biodiversity offsets in areas associated with the Caucasian leopard and brown bear, species whose habitats could be threatened by the project.

She said civil society groups had campaigned against the mine for 20 years and that its approval shortly before the opening of the biodiversity summit had heightened concerns about the use of offsets to address environmental damage.

The groups warned that placing financial values on wildlife and their habitats could allow companies to claim conservation benefits while continuing activities that threaten biodiversity.

Cassandra Smithies, an offsets expert with the Global Justice Ecology Project, said the United Nations should not support schemes that allow extractive industries to use Indigenous territories and ecosystems as sources of carbon credits.

“Putting a price on nature will not save nature, it will destroy her,” Ms Smithies said.

She argued that Indigenous Peoples’ lands, animals and oceans should not be treated as carbon sinks for industries responsible for greenhouse gas emissions.

“The United Nations must not be complicit with green colonialism,” she said.

Conservation groups call for stronger commitments

While Indigenous representatives criticised the monetisation of nature, other conservation organisations at COP17 called for stronger commitments and more effective implementation of existing biodiversity targets.

Sue Lieberman, vice president of international policy at the Wildlife Conservation Society, said negotiations had made some progress but had yet to produce the level of ambition and concrete action required to meet the 2030 biodiversity targets.

She said delegates needed to strengthen commitments in the global review process and ensure that governments, communities and donors followed through on their pledges.

“The key is ambition. The key is to work with countries, communities, and donors to make sure everything they commit to happens,” Ms Lieberman said.

She added that conservation efforts must translate into practical action on the ground and in aquatic ecosystems, particularly at national and regional levels.

Alfred DeGemmis, the society’s director of international policy, said Armenia and a growing number of governments were supporting civil society calls to identify subsidies that harm nature and redirect the resources towards conservation.

However, he said proposed language that could establish measurable milestones towards the 2030 targets remained unresolved in the negotiating text.

“Ministers are now expected to try to resolve this behind closed doors in the summit’s final days,” Mr DeGemmis said.

The competing positions highlight a broader question confronting delegates at COP17: how to mobilise the financing needed to protect biodiversity while ensuring that financial mechanisms do not undermine conservation, Indigenous rights and the integrity of ecosystems.

World.title: Russia woos African leaders at Moscow summit
World.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin gives a speech during the Russia-Africa economic and humanitarian forum at the Gostiny Dvor conference centre in central Moscow on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Igor IVANKO / POOL / AFP)

A summit with nearly two dozen African leaders opened in Moscow Wednesday, with the Kremlin describing their countries as “natural allies” against the West.

The two-day Russia-Africa summit, the third since 2019, comes as Moscow grapples with heavy Western sanctions over its Ukraine offensive and as it provides security assistance to several African governments.

Moscow has courted ties with Africa since the Soviet era, and has long looked to the continent as a counterweight to what it sees as Western domination over international affairs.

“We are natural allies in building a multipolar world order,” Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said of the summit, referring to a system where political power is no longer concentrated in the West.

Russian President Vladimir Putin meanwhile said that that multipolar world was quickly becoming a reality, in an “irreversible” trend.

“The era when the fate of entire continents was determined by a narrow bloc of states is irrevocably gone,” he said as he opened a Russia-Africa economic forum, which gathered thousands of Russian and African business leaders in Moscow hours before the high-level summit began.

He told the delegations from 48 African countries, including 22 represented by their leaders, that Russia was “prepared to further expand the geographical reach of our agricultural product shipments”.

The pledge came as attacks in the Black Sea linked to the conflict in Ukraine continue to disrupt exports of grain from both Russia and Ukraine.

– ‘Neocolonialism’ –

Putin also announced that Moscow planned to “localise” the production of “effective Russian medicines and vaccines” on the African continent, and noted that the number of African students in Russia had swelled 50 percent since 2020.

The Russian president also stressed that his country was “open to sharing our modern competencies and high-tech digital know-how with our African friends”.

Putin’s criticism of what he calls Western “neocolonialism” in Africa has resonated on the continent.

That is especially true in the Sahel, where Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso have turned their backs on their former colonial ruler France in favour of closer ties with Moscow.

Among the around 20 bilateral meetings Putin was scheduled to have with African leaders in Moscow this week was one with his Malian counterpart Assimi Goita, whose government is using Russian paramilitaries to battle a jihadist offensive.

– DRC-Rwanda tensions –

Putin was also due to meet with Democratic Republic of Congo President Felix Tshisekedi, who is attending the summit as tensions between his country and neighbouring Rwanda continue to flare.

The Rwandan-backed M23 movement has seized swathes of the eastern DRC since taking up arms again in 2021, and, despite a US-brokered truce last December, fighting has continued.

Rwanda was to be represented at the Moscow summit by Prime Minister Justin Nsengiyumva.

The summit was expected to end Thursday with a final declaration on deepening cooperation between Russia and African nations, alongside a separate statement on cooperation in the field of artificial intelligence.

In all, 33 documents will be signed at the summit, focused in particular on economic cooperation, according to the Kremlin.

Russia will also seek to strengthen its diplomatic presence on the continent, where it aims soon to open a 49th embassy, in Liberia, the Kremlin said.

– Conscripted Africans –

Russia’s relations with African nations have meanwhile been clouded in recent years by numerous reports of Africans being forcibly conscripted by Moscow to fight on the frontlines in Ukraine.

Several African countries, including Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa, have publicly voiced alarm at the fate of their citizens recruited by Moscow.

In an open letter to the African heads of state and other officials attending the Moscow summit, the Amnesty International rights group voiced “deep concern regarding Russia’s forced and deceptive recruitment” of African nations.

The letter, published Tuesday, urged the officials to demand that Russia “cease any ongoing and future recruitment of people from Africa and other foreign nationals into its military forces”.

World.title: Some people are buried alive in Nigeria over lack of life-saving equipment – Medical expert
World.content:
Arinze Onwumelu (Dr Zo)

By Emmanuel Okogba

A Nigerian medical doctor based in Canada, Arinze Onwumelu, popularly known as Dr Zo, has raised concerns over the shortage of life-saving equipment in Nigerian hospitals, warning that patients with potentially reversible medical emergencies could die without receiving appropriate treatment.

Onwumelu made the remarks in a video shared on his Instagram account, @official_doctor_zo, where he called on Nigerians to hold government authorities accountable for gaps in the country’s healthcare system.

The doctor alleged that many government-owned hospitals lacked essential emergency equipment, including automated external defibrillators (AEDs), heart monitors and electrocardiogram (ECG) machines.

“In my opinion, some Nigerians are buried alive in Nigeria. Ninety-five (95) per cent of government-owned hospitals don’t have defibrillators, AEDs, heart monitors or ECG machines,” he said.

He questioned how medical personnel could determine the cause of a sudden collapse or identify a potentially treatable heart rhythm abnormality without access to appropriate diagnostic equipment.

“How on earth can you tell if someone slumped due to a heart attack or other forms of reversible arrhythmia?” he asked.

Onwumelu, who said he had worked in emergency departments in Nigeria before relocating to Canada, recalled his experiences at the Federal Medical Centre in Umuahia and the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital (UNTH).

He claimed that during his time working in the facilities in the late 1990s and early 2000s, he did not encounter automated external defibrillators or heart monitors in the emergency departments where he worked.

According to him, the absence of essential equipment made it difficult for healthcare workers to assess and manage some patients presenting with life-threatening conditions.

“If they bring somebody like Toluwanisings to the hospital, how are you going to know what is wrong? How do you determine whether the person can still be revived?” he asked.

The doctor also recounted an incident involving a 12-year-old boy who, he said, died at the Federal Medical Centre in Umuahia when essential equipment, including oxygen and a nebuliser, was unavailable.

He described the experience as particularly painful, recalling the grief of the boy’s mother.

“The silent cry of that woman is something I will never forget,” he said.

Onwumelu argued that the availability of appropriate emergency equipment, alongside trained personnel and timely intervention, could improve the chances of survival for patients experiencing certain medical emergencies.

He particularly highlighted the importance of defibrillators in treating some life-threatening heart rhythm disturbances, noting that prompt recognition and treatment can be critical in cardiac emergencies.

The doctor also rejected suggestions that he should personally purchase and donate the equipment to hospitals, insisting that the responsibility for providing functional public healthcare infrastructure rests primarily with government authorities.

“You people should hold your government accountable,” he said.

He questioned what he described as the contrast between public spending on political campaigns and the reported shortages of essential medical equipment in healthcare facilities.

Onwumelu further urged Nigerians to demand improved healthcare services and greater accountability from elected officials, arguing that the country had the resources to strengthen its health system.

He cited developments in other African countries as examples of the improvements he believes Nigeria should pursue.

World.title: Reps panel approves ₦100.5bn Yobe airport reimbursement
World.content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives Committee on Aids, Loans and Debt Management has recommended approval of a ₦100.5 billion promissory note programme to reimburse the Yobe State Government for constructing the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport in Damaturu.

The proposed reimbursement amounts to ₦100,509,017,234.55, following the Federal Government’s decision to take over the newly constructed airport.

Chairman of the committee, Abubakar Hassan Nalaraba, disclosed this while briefing journalists at the National Assembly, Abuja, on Wednesday, saying lawmakers had conducted due diligence and inspected the facility before recommending the reimbursement.

He said officials of the Federal Ministries of Aviation and Finance, alongside other relevant agencies, provided technical assessments and documentation on the project.

“After due diligence and considerations, and after undertaking comprehensive oversight of the airport, receiving the reports of technical officials at the Ministry of Aviation, Ministry of Finance and the accounting office, we recently considered and approved the reimbursement of the airport to Yobe State Government,” Nalaraba said.

He added that the committee found the airport’s infrastructure and equipment satisfactory, noting that professionals had certified the facilities as meeting the required standards.

The committee’s report stated that the Federal Ministry of Aviation inspected the completed airport and confirmed that the quality of work met the standards required for its takeover by the Federal Government.

It also found that the Yobe State Government had paid the contractors who executed the project, while the Bureau of Public Procurement certified that due process was followed.

According to the report, the committee examined submissions from the Yobe State Government, the Federal Ministries of Finance and Aviation, the Federal Executive Council and the Bureau of Public Procurement.

It also reviewed contract agreements, certificates of completion, evidence of payments to contractors, due-process reviews and the bureau’s certificate of no objection.

President Bola Tinubu had requested the National Assembly’s approval for the promissory note programme in a communication read on the floor of the House on October 13, 2026.

The request was made pursuant to the Debt Management Office (Establishment) Act, 2003, and the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007, which provide for legislative approval of the programme.

Promissory note programmes are used to settle outstanding Federal Government liabilities, including reimbursements to state governments for projects executed on behalf of the Federal Government.

Speaking on the airport’s economic significance, Nalaraba said the facility would add value to Yobe residents and create opportunities for investment.

“When you see a critical infrastructure being constructed in a state, I think it’s a value addition, first, to the people of the state. Secondly, it will attract some level of investment to the state and the nation at large,” he said.

A member of the committee representing Yobe State, Mohammed Mugbejajere, said the airport could serve as a cargo hub for the North-East, particularly for transporting agricultural produce and raw materials.

“Yobe, as you all know, is an agrarian state. We are into agriculture and a lot of raw materials are abundantly available in the state, where we expect that the cargo airport will be used as a hub, especially in the North-East region, where you have these cargo airports,” he said.

He added that the facility could help move agricultural products from the region to other markets.

However, journalists raised concerns about the commercial viability of airports in Nigeria, citing a report attributed to the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria indicating that only three of the country’s 22 domestic and international airports were commercially viable.

In response, Nalaraba said the committee relied on assessments by relevant aviation authorities, stressing that lawmakers were not technical specialists in airport operations.

“The Ministry of Aviation, FAAN, in my earlier statement, I said technical FAAN has all gone and satisfied that this airport is viable and is ready for commercial use,” he said.

He maintained that the project had undergone the necessary administrative and technical reviews before being presented to the National Assembly.

The committee chairman also clarified that the proposed reimbursement was not fresh funding for construction but repayment to Yobe State for money already spent on a project the Federal Government had decided to take over.

“This is reimbursement. This money has been spent. The Federal and state governments spent this money to construct that cargo international airport,” he said.

He added that the state government undertook the project despite aviation falling within the Federal Government’s exclusive legislative jurisdiction.

On safeguards against additional financial liabilities, the committee said the Federal Government’s takeover meant responsibility for the airport, including its future maintenance and development, would rest with the federal authorities.

The committee also indicated that the reimbursement would be a one-off payment, although detailed repayment arrangements were not fully explained during the briefing.

It recommended that the House approve the promissory note programme for the full amount of ₦100.509 billion, as claimed by the Yobe State Government and approved by the Federal Executive Council.

The proposed reimbursement puts the focus on how the Federal Government will manage the airport and whether it can attract sufficient commercial activity, particularly through agricultural cargo operations, to justify the public investment.

World.title: NNPCL to resume oil exploration in Borno
World.content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) has pledged to resume oil exploration activities in Borno State, while assuring the state government of steps to address delays in upgrading the Maiduguri Emergency Power Plant.

The commitments were made on Wednesday when Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, received the NNPCL management team, led by the board chairman, Engr. Ahmadu Musa Kida, in Maiduguri.

The meeting focused on energy development, the resumption of oil exploration in the state and the delayed completion of the emergency power plant upgrade.

Zulum stressed the strategic importance of resuming exploration in the Borno Basin, noting that the state had considerable commercial potential and shared borders with three countries.

He expressed optimism that renewed exploration efforts by the national oil company would help unlock the state’s hydrocarbon resources and stimulate economic development.

The governor, however, expressed concern over the slow pace of work on the Maiduguri Emergency Power Plant, describing the facility as critical to improving electricity supply in the state.

He said the materials required for the plant’s upgrade had been on site for about two years, yet the project remained incomplete.

Zulum urged the NNPCL management to intervene and remove the bottlenecks delaying the project, stressing that its completion was important to the socio-economic well-being of residents of Maiduguri and neighbouring communities.

Responding, Kida assured the governor of the company’s readiness to fast-track the resumption of exploration activities in the Borno Basin and address the challenges delaying the power plant upgrade.

He also commended Zulum for his continued support and efforts to create a conducive environment for investment in the state.

The meeting was attended by the Deputy Governor, Umar Usman Kadafur; Secretary to the State Government, Bukar Tijani; Acting Chief of Staff, Dr. Babagana Mallumbe; and other senior government officials.

Members of the NNPCL delegation included the Executive Vice President, Upstream, Mr. Udy Ntia, and the Executive Vice President, Gas, Power and New Energy, Mr. Olalekon Ogunleye.

World.title: Rivers rally shows Wike’s strength, says APC chieftain
World.content:
Wike

By Daniel Abia

PORT HARCOURT — A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Rivers State, Princewill Dike, has described the turnout at Tuesday’s Rainbow Coalition rally in Port Harcourt as evidence of the political influence and mobilisation capacity of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike.

Dike, who spoke at the Yakubu Gowon Stadium, venue of the rally to unveil coalition candidates for the 2027 general elections, attributed the large turnout to Wike’s political organisation, grassroots connections and ability to mobilise supporters.

He said the gathering had sent a message to those questioning the level of support enjoyed by President Bola Tinubu in Rivers State.

“The massive crowd at the gathering is an indication that the President has substantial political backing in the state, contrary to claims by antagonists of the FCT Minister’s political influence,” he said.

The activist expressed satisfaction with the rally, attributing its success to effective planning and the commitment of supporters who turned out to identify with the political movement.

He described Wike as a pace-setter, adding that the minister’s political achievements and mobilisation record would be difficult for opponents to surpass.

Meanwhile, Wike has announced that the proposed campaign rally of President Tinubu in Port Harcourt on November 7, 2026, will hold at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium.

Reacting to the announcement, Dike predicted that the presidential rally would attract a crowd comparable to that witnessed at the Yakubu Gowon Stadium, expressing confidence that the venue would be filled to capacity.

He said the turnout at Tuesday’s event had raised expectations for the presidential rally, while urging effective crowd management to prevent overcrowding and ensure public safety.

Dike also expressed delight that no casualty was recorded at the coalition rally, thanking God for what he described as the successful and peaceful outcome of the gathering.

World.title: Reps to grill INEC over 2027 election readiness, voter registration challenges
World.content:
House of Representatives

By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives has resolved to invite the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to appear before its committee to provide a comprehensive assessment of its preparedness for the 2027 general elections.

The resolution followed a motion sponsored by Mansur Manu Soro and Abdussamad Dasuki, which raised concerns over operational challenges facing the commission, particularly in the ongoing Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise.

The motion, initially seeking INEC’s appearance before the House, was amended to require the commission to brief the relevant committee on its readiness for the elections.

Under the resolution, INEC is expected to appear before the committee within seven legislative days and provide a detailed status report on its preparations for the 2027 general elections.

The lawmakers said the assessment should cover voter registration, Permanent Voter Card (PVC) production and distribution, election logistics, deployment of technology, recruitment and training of personnel, electoral security, risk assessment and funding.

They also called for information on budgetary appropriations, funds released, outstanding releases and the implications of any funding gaps for the commission’s preparations.

The House expressed concern over reports from CVR centres across the country indicating inadequate registration equipment, limited personnel, network challenges, prolonged waiting times and increased demand from citizens seeking to register or update their voter records.

According to the lawmakers, these difficulties could restrict the participation of eligible voters, particularly first-time voters, rural residents, persons with disabilities, students and workers.

They warned that failure to address the operational gaps promptly could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and threaten the peaceful conduct of the 2027 elections.

The lawmakers noted that the credibility, transparency and acceptability of the elections would depend significantly on INEC’s preparedness in areas such as voter education, logistics, technology deployment, personnel training, security coordination and timely funding.

They further observed that the recently concluded Ekiti State governorship election had provided useful lessons on election administration, technology deployment, logistics management and stakeholder engagement that could inform preparations for the 2027 polls.

The motion acknowledged INEC’s efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s electoral system but stressed the need for sustained parliamentary oversight to ensure that institutions entrusted with critical national responsibilities were adequately prepared, properly funded and accountable.

It also emphasised the importance of early institutional planning to ensure the timely procurement of election materials, deployment of technology, recruitment and training of election officials, effective voter education and coordination with security agencies.

The lawmakers said a comprehensive review of the commission’s preparedness would help identify potential weaknesses early enough for corrective action.

They added that addressing the identified challenges was necessary to guarantee free, fair, credible, inclusive and peaceful elections in 2027.

World.title: Four dead, 13 injured in Lagos truck-bus crash
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

Four persons, including a commercial bus driver, have died while 13 others sustained critical injuries in a collision involving a truck and a commercial bus on Alaro City Bridge, inward T-Junction, Epe, Lagos State.

The crash occurred on Wednesday morning when the truck rammed into a fully loaded commercial bus while both vehicles were crossing the single-lane bridge, trapping victims in the wreckage, according to eyewitnesses.

The General Manager of the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA), Mr Olalekan Bakare-Oki, confirmed that four people died in the incident, while 13 other occupants sustained critical injuries.

The truck driver also suffered severe injuries, with both legs reportedly severed, and was trapped in the wreckage.

LASTMA operatives, with support from the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), evacuated the deceased to a mortuary, while the Lagos State Ambulance Service (LASAMBUS) transported the injured to the nearest medical facility for emergency treatment.

Security personnel from the Epe Police Division also reinforced the rescue operations.

Bakare-Oki commiserated with the bereaved families, describing the loss of lives as deeply distressing, and wished the injured victims a speedy recovery.

He urged motorists to exercise caution, drive responsibly and comply with traffic regulations, particularly on bridges, narrow carriageways and other road bottlenecks.

The LASTMA chief reiterated the agency’s commitment to protecting lives and improving road safety through collaboration with other relevant agencies.

He also urged motorists to maintain safe following distances, observe prescribed speed limits and avoid dangerous driving manoeuvres, especially on bridges and constricted roadways where reckless driving could result in fatal crashes.

World.title: Ebonyi Assembly approves N150m political billboard fees
World.content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

The Ebonyi State House of Assembly has approved new levies for political billboards and posters in Abakaliki, fixing the fee for presidential and governorship candidates at N150 million, National Assembly candidates at N20 million and State House of Assembly candidates at N5 million.

The House also approved a request by Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru to obtain a N9.673 billion loan from Keystone Bank Limited to meet counterpart funding requirements for the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC).

On the billboard fees, the lawmakers unanimously adopted a resolution directing the immediate termination of all existing contracts relating to political billboards and posters within the Abakaliki capital city.

They also mandated the Commissioner for Capital City Development to take over the enforcement and collection of all levies relating to political billboards and posters.

The resolution followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by the Chairman of the House Committee on Capital City Development and Deputy Chief Whip, Hon. Arinze Lucas Chukwu, who represents Ishielu South Constituency.

Moving the motion, Chukwu expressed concern over the indiscriminate pasting of political posters and erection of billboards on public buildings, electric poles, streetlights, bridges and fences across the capital city.

He described the practice as environmental pollution that undermined Abakaliki’s appearance and deprived the state of internally generated revenue (IGR).

Chukwu said competing claims by different agencies over the collection of billboard levies had created confusion, revenue leakages and double taxation.

He argued that existing laws empowered the Commissioner for Capital City Development to regulate outdoor advertising within the capital territory.

Under the resolution, any political party, aspirant, group, organisation or individual seeking to erect a billboard or paste posters within the capital city must pay the approved levy into a designated government revenue account and obtain an official receipt before proceeding.

The House also resolved that the commissioner should designate approved locations for poster pasting and billboard erection and establish a task force to remove installations erected without proof of payment.

Defaulters would be required to pay a penalty of 50 per cent of the original levy, in addition to the applicable fee.

The lawmakers further directed the Chairman of the Ebonyi State Internal Revenue Service to terminate all contracts, concessions and arrangements with private consultants or agents for political billboards and posters in the capital city.

The agency was also directed to hand over all relevant files, data and authority to the Commissioner for Capital City Development.

Seconding the motion, the member representing Ivo Constituency, Hon. Onyebuchi Ogbadu, said the resolution would restore order and improve the state’s revenue generation.

The House directed its Committees on Capital City Development, Finance and Environment to monitor compliance and report back within 30 days.

The Speaker, Rt. Hon. Moses Ije Odunwa, put the motion to a vote, and it was unanimously adopted.

Assembly approves N9.673bn loan

In a separate development, the Assembly approved Governor Nwifuru’s request for authorisation to obtain a N9.673 billion loan facility from Keystone Bank Limited.

The governor’s letter, read on the floor by the House Leader, Hon. Kingsley Ikoro, stated that the facility was intended for the state government and local government councils to meet UBEC counterpart funding requirements.

According to the letter, Keystone Bank agreed to provide the loan at an annual interest rate of 17 per cent, with a management and commitment fee of 0.5 per cent.

Moving the motion for approval, Ikoro urged lawmakers to treat the request with urgency in the interest of educational development in the state.

Seconding the motion, the member representing Ohaozara East Constituency, Hon. Igu Chikezie Nwankwo, described the request as appropriate and critical to advancing access to education.

The member representing Ikwo North Constituency, Hon. Ifeanyi Nwakpu, also supported the request, highlighting its potential benefits.

Following deliberations, Speaker Odunwa put the motion to a voice vote, and the lawmakers unanimously approved the loan request.

World.title: Barau Counters Osinbajo, Defends Tinubu’s Economic Reforms
World.content:
…Blames poor communication for public discontent, cites NELFUND, highway projects

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Jibrin Barau, has challenged former Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo’s gloomy assessment of Nigeria’s economy and democratic governance, insisting that President Bola Tinubu’s administration is addressing longstanding structural challenges but needs to communicate its policies and achievements more effectively to Nigerians.

Barau acknowledged the validity of concerns raised by Osinbajo, particularly those relating to economic hardship, declining public confidence in democratic institutions and inadequate youth participation in electoral politics.

He, however, argued that the perception of poor government performance was partly attributable to the failure of political leaders to adequately explain their policies, interventions and ongoing development projects.

The Deputy Senate President spoke on Tuesday in Yola, Adamawa State, during a public lecture titled, ‘Democracy and Development: Rethinking the Leadership Question,’ organised to mark the 59th birthday of Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri.

Osinbajo, who served as vice-president between 2015 and 2023, had expressed concern about the growing dissatisfaction with democratic governance across Africa, despite nearly three decades of uninterrupted democratic rule in several countries.

Drawing on findings from Afrobarometer surveys, the former vice-president highlighted widespread economic anxiety, declining public confidence in government, rising living costs, unemployment, inadequate healthcare and diminishing youth participation in electoral processes.

He noted that although 64 per cent of Africans preferred democracy to other forms of government, only 38 per cent were satisfied with how democracy was functioning in their respective countries.

Osinbajo also cited survey findings indicating that 59 per cent of Africans considered their national economies to be in bad shape, while 51 per cent believed their economies had deteriorated.

He warned that persistent economic hardship and the failure of democratic institutions to meet citizens’ expectations could undermine public confidence in democracy, particularly among young people.

Responding to the presentation, Barau praised Osinbajo’s intellectual depth but questioned whether the gloomy picture reflected the full extent of government interventions and ongoing efforts to address the country’s challenges.

“I know he is a very good orator, a good public speaker and an intellectual to the core,” Barau said.

Explaining why he had decided to respond despite initially intending to avoid making a speech at the birthday celebration, the senator described Osinbajo’s presentation as thought-provoking.

“Having said that, I am compelled to make some comments on the paper. It is a very beautiful and thought-provoking paper,” he said.

Barau identified inadequate communication between political leaders and citizens as a major factor contributing to public dissatisfaction, arguing that governments needed to do more to explain the policies and programmes designed to improve living conditions.

He said: “What I want to say is this: one important reason for the gloomy picture portrayed by the surveys, particularly those conducted by Afrobarometer, is what the professor talked about and specifically observed: the issue of communication between the leaders and the led.

“There is no proper communication,” he said.

The senator maintained that although Nigerians were entitled to demand better living conditions and hold public officials accountable, citizens also needed adequate information about the challenges confronting the country and the measures being taken to address them.

He cited interventions in education and infrastructure as examples of the Federal Government’s efforts to tackle structural deficiencies that have constrained economic growth and limited opportunities for millions of Nigerians.

On education, Barau highlighted the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), introduced under Tinubu’s administration, describing it as an intervention designed to expand access to tertiary education, particularly for students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds.

He argued that access to education remained critical to addressing the long-term consequences of poverty, unemployment and social exclusion, especially in a country with a large and growing youth population.

“Before now, it was very difficult for a child who did not have the means to go to school. Now, everyone, except a child who does not want to go to school, can go to school in Nigeria with the NELFUND introduced by this administration,” he said.

The Deputy Senate President also underscored the importance of infrastructure development in stimulating economic activity, attracting investment and improving the standard of living.

He cited the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, the Badagry-Sokoto Highway and road projects across the North-east and North-west as evidence of ongoing efforts to address the country’s infrastructure deficit.

According to him, investments in roads, water supply and other essential infrastructure are necessary to connect communities, facilitate trade, reduce transportation bottlenecks and create conditions for sustainable economic prosperity.

He said: “When we talk about economic prosperity, you cannot achieve it without a certain level of infrastructure, including road networks, water supply and other essential infrastructure.

“This is what is happening currently in this country under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration. Roads are being constructed everywhere to propel the process of bringing economic prosperity. That is being done.

“It is a long journey, but it is being done. Yet, there is no proper communication.”

He urged political leaders and public officials at the federal and state levels to prioritise sustained public engagement, insisting that government policies could not achieve their intended impact if citizens remained inadequately informed about their objectives and implementation.

The senator also attributed part of the pressure on household incomes and the rising cost of goods and services to international economic developments, arguing that Nigeria’s current difficulties could not be considered in isolation from global events.

He pointed to the Russia-Ukraine war and conflicts in the Middle East as factors that had disrupted international supply chains, increased energy costs and raised production expenses across several economies.

Barau also cited tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic international oil transit route, as one of the factors contributing to volatility in global energy markets.

According to him, “The fact is that these challenges are not peculiar to Nigeria; they have an international dimension. The rising cost of living is partly attributable to conflicts in different parts of the world, including the Middle East, as well as the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine.

“These conflicts have disrupted global supply chains, driven up energy prices and increased the cost of goods and services worldwide.”

The senator, who is also the First Deputy Speaker of the ECOWAS Parliament, argued that developments in international energy and commodity markets could have significant implications for Nigeria, given the country’s exposure to global trade and the cost of imported goods and production inputs.

“Nigeria is not an island,” he said.

Barau’s intervention came against the backdrop of continuing public debate over the effects of Tinubu’s economic reforms, particularly the pressure on household incomes, transportation costs and prices of essential commodities.

While the Federal Government has defended its policy direction as necessary to address longstanding economic distortions, the scale of the immediate hardship has continued to generate public concern over the pace at which the benefits of the reforms would translate into improved living conditions.

Osinbajo’s lecture similarly drew attention to the wider democratic implications of persistent economic difficulties, particularly the possibility that citizens could lose faith in democratic institutions if governments failed to respond adequately to their expectations.

Barau, however, argued that bridging the gap between public expectations and government performance required political leaders to communicate more clearly, explain policy choices and provide credible information on the progress of ongoing interventions.

He called on public officials and other stakeholders to take collective responsibility for improving public understanding of government policies, stressing that effective communication should complement, rather than replace, tangible results.

For the Deputy Senate President, the challenge confronting Nigeria is therefore not only the implementation of policies to address economic and infrastructural deficits but also ensuring that citizens understand what the government is doing, why the interventions are necessary and how they are expected to improve their lives.

He maintained that sustained engagement between leaders and the electorate would be essential to rebuilding public confidence, strengthening democratic institutions and securing broader support for the country’s development agenda.

World.title: ADC PCC Alleges Plot To Shift Presidential Election, Insists on January 16
World.content:
Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council warned that reports of pressure on the Independent National Electoral Commission to shift the 16 January presidential election, just 80 days away, cannot be dismissed.

The ADC PCC said that plot to shift the presidential election was to be hinged on Ebola.

A statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, said, “If President Tinubu believes Nigerians want another four years of his government, he should face them at the ballot box, not seek more time through the back door.”

According to the ADC Presidential Campaign Council Director of of Strategic communications, “The Council has received information that the INEC Chairman is to be summoned to the Presidential Villa and instructed to shift the election.

“We are raising the alarm before that meeting takes place. President Tinubu must abandon any such attempt. Professor Joash Amupitan must refuse any instruction to change the timetable and immediately make any such approach public.

“The election date belongs to Nigerians. It must not be rewritten behind closed doors at the Villa”, the statement stated.

The ADC presidential campaign Council said that “Nigerians have endured three and a half years of soaring prices, shrinking incomes and relentless hardship.

“They have the right to judge this government at the ballot box on 16 January. A government that has made life this difficult for Nigerians must not be allowed to postpone its day of judgment.”

The ADC presidential campaign Council said that “Ebola is a serious public health concern. Health professionals must be free to contain it, and INEC must take every necessary step to protect voters and election workers.

“The NCDC Director General has said there is currently no reason to postpone the election. That position must not be twisted into a political excuse for delay.

“The Council puts INEC, domestic observers and international election monitors on notice: any proposal to change the timetable must be made openly, supported by published health evidence and subjected to public scrutiny. The Presidency must not use a health emergency to escape an electoral verdict.” Shuaib stated

World.title: No Shady Deal in Kwara Social Investment Programme, Says DG, Tejidini
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

Director General of the Kwara State Social Investment Programme (KWASSIP) Dr. Abdulwasiu Tejidini, has said that, there was no any shady deal in the financial operations of the agency.

He therefore said all the financial operations and approved funds disburshed to the beneficiaries were applied with the objectives of the mandate of the agency.

Dr. Tejidini in a statement issued in Ilorin, signed by the agency’s Press Secretary, Mrs. Yusuf Bola Shade, stated that the agency maintains records of beneficiaries across the 193 wards of Kwara State under programmes that includes Owo Isowo, Owo Arugbo, and the skilled and unskilled workers scheme.

Dr. Tejidini positions came on the sidelines of the recent called for a probe of the agency by the 52- youth coalition in the state that backed the call of the governorship candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) for 2027 election, Professor Abdulmumin Yinka Ajia to look into the financial operations of the agency since its inception.

The statement read, “The Kwara State Social Investment Programme (KWASSIP) has taken note of recent allegations concerning the management and implementation of its programmes.

“KWASSIP assures the public that funds approved and released to the agency have been applied in accordance with the objectives of its mandate.

“The agency maintains records of beneficiaries across the 193 wards of Kwara State under programmes including Owo Isowo, Owo Arugbo, and the skilled and unskilled workers scheme.

“The Kwapreneur programme has also supported beneficiaries in establishing and expanding businesses, creating employment opportunities, and contributing to economic activity in their communities.

“These outcomes reflect the agency’s efforts to promote sustainable economic empowerment and support livelihoods across the state”.

The statement added, “In response to economic challenges, KWASSIP has, at various times, provided assistance to businesses, individuals, and households affected by difficult circumstances.

“This includes support provided to businesses affected by the #EndSARS protests at Palms Mall, which enabled affected operators to resume activities and rebuild their livelihoods.

“The agency also recently disbursed ₦90 million to 12 young entrepreneurs to support business expansion, strengthen enterprise development, and promote job creation across Kwara State.

“KWASSIP remains committed to transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement in the delivery of its programmes. Its activities and records are available for appropriate review, in accordance with applicable procedures and requirements.

“The agency welcomes constructive criticism and public scrutiny. It is important that public discourse remains guided by facts, evidence, and a genuine concern for the welfare of the people, rather than political considerations or unsubstantiated claims.

“KWASSIP therefore urges all stakeholders to assess its performance on the basis of verifiable information, documented programme outcomes, and credible evidence.

“KWASSIP will continue to work with relevant stakeholders to ensure that its interventions reach intended beneficiaries and contribute meaningfully to the social and economic development of Kwara State”.

World.title: Israel Election Count: Netanyahu’s Bloc Leads With 54 Seats, Eisenkot-led Bloc 49, Arab Parties 17
World.content:
Israel’s election count has revealed a political deadlock, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud-led bloc leading with 54 seats, while the bloc led by Yashar party chief Gadi Eisenkot has secured 49 seats and Arab parties hold 17 seats.

According to Times of Israel reports, with more than 84 per cent of ballots counted, neither side has secured the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority, leaving the formation of the next government uncertain.

The latest figures give the anti-Netanyahu bloc a combined 66 seats when the Arab parties are included. However, forming a coalition remains complicated by campaign promises from several party leaders not to partner with Arab-led parties.

The Joint List chief signalled readiness to support efforts to remove Netanyahu’s government, declaring: “We’re ready to pave the way to oust Netanyahu government.”

Despite the uncertainty, both Netanyahu and Eisenkot expressed confidence in their ability to form the next government following exit poll results released on Tuesday night.

The exit polls suggested that the election had produced a stalemate, with neither political camp able to form a coalition without making difficult political compromises.

The pro-Netanyahu bloc was initially projected to win between 51 and 52 seats, below the number it currently holds in the Knesset. Subsequent partial results increased its projected strength, although the latest count placed the bloc at 54 seats.

Meanwhile, reports indicate that Eisenkot’s bloc is exploring ways to use its votes, alongside those of the Arab parties, to replace Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana, a member of Likud.

No candidate has reportedly been agreed upon, but Yisrael Beytenu lawmaker Oded Forer and Yashar’s Elazar Stern have been mentioned as possible options.

Netanyahu’s Likud also performed strongly in Kiryat Shmona, Sderot and other communities severely affected by the war, according to reports by The Times of Israel.

Political parties across the spectrum celebrated their performances despite the inconclusive results, while several leaders urged patience until the final count is completed.

Although more than 84 per cent of ballots have been counted, the final outcome may take several days to emerge. Remaining votes include “double envelope” ballots cast by Israel Defense Forces soldiers, diplomats and other voters who did not vote at their assigned polling stations.

The final results will determine whether either camp can assemble a governing coalition or whether further negotiations will be required to break the political deadlock

World.title: Customs Hands Over N5.8m Seized Unregistered Drugs To NAFDAC In Sokoto
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

The Sokoto/Zamfara Area Command of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has handed over seized unregistered pharmaceutical products valued at N5,804,062.06 to the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) for further investigation and necessary action.

The handing over ceremony was held on Wednesday , October 28, 2026, at the Command Headquarters in Sokoto, in line with existing inter-agency collaboration and the directive of the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi.

Speaking during the ceremony, the Acting Customs Area Controller, Sokoto/Zamfara Area Command, DC Haliru Isah Abdullahi, said the items were intercepted by gallant patrol teams along the Illela-Sokoto road, following credible intelligence and the commitment of officers of the Command.

He listed the seized items to include 360 packages of anti-cold containing 50 cards each with 4 tablets per card, 500 packages of Amodiaquine containing 25 cards each with 3 tablets per card, 140 packages of Paracetamol containing 100 cards each with 10 tablets per card, and 100 packages of Quinine containing 10 cards each with 10 tablets per card.

Abdullahi said the importation of the unregistered drugs contravened Section 55 of the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023 and NAFDAC regulations, noting that the drugs posed great danger to the health of Nigerians as they were not certified for consumption.

He warned smugglers and dealers in unwholesome products that the Sokoto/Zamfara Command under his watch would not tolerate any form of smuggling, stressing that the Command remained vigilant and committed to safeguarding the health of citizens and the nation’s economy.

He commended the officers who made the seizure possible for their diligence and bravery, and appreciated NAFDAC for its continuous partnership with the Service.

“I hereby formally hand over these seized items to the NAFDAC team for further necessary action,” Abdullahi declared.

Responding, the Coordinator of NAFDAC, Sokoto State, Abdulsalam Lawan, commended the Nigeria Customs Service for the inter-agency collaboration that had helped in curbing the entry of fake drugs into the country.

Lawan noted that the agency and Customs had enjoyed wonderful collaboration which had led to the ridding of unwholesome products from the country, and urged the Customs Service to sustain the tempo.

He assured that NAFDAC would carry out further investigation on the seized products and take necessary action in line with its mandate to protect public health and ensure only certified drugs circulate in the country.

World.title: Religious, Media Leaders Mobilise Against Disinformation Ahead of 2027 Polls
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

Religious leaders and media stakeholders have been urged to intensify efforts to combat misinformation, disinformation and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI) in order to prevent religious tensions, communal crises and electoral violence ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general election.

The call was made at a two-day workshop organised by Alkalanci, a fact-checking and media literacy organisation, in collaboration with the Institute for Media and Digital Innovation (IMDIL), in Jos, Plateau State.

The workshop, themed ‘Scaling Faith-Based Resilience Against Disinformation and FIMI,’ brought together Christian and Muslim leaders to build their capacity to identify false information, promote responsible communication and strengthen community resilience against information threats.

Speaking at the opening session, Editor of Alkalanci, Alhassan Bala, warned that the proliferation of false information posed a serious threat to Nigeria’s security, social cohesion and democratic processes.

He noted that the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) to create deceptive images, videos and audio recordings had made it increasingly difficult for citizens to distinguish authentic content from fabricated material.

According to him, malicious actors could exploit such technologies to inflame religious and communal tensions, provoke violence and undermine public trust, particularly as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 elections.

Bala urged religious leaders to exercise caution and verify information before sharing it with members of their congregations, stressing that responsible communication remains critical to safeguarding peace.

“When in doubt, do not share,” he said, emphasising the need for verification before circulating information capable of misleading the public.

Also speaking, Cyber and Hybrid Threats Programme Lead at the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office’s Integrated Security Fund (FCDO-ISF) West Africa, Oriola Odetoye, reaffirmed the United Kingdom’s commitment to supporting Nigeria in addressing foreign information manipulation and other hybrid threats.

He explained that the intervention, implemented under the UK-Nigeria Security and Defence Partnership, is designed to strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to detect, respond to and counter information manipulation campaigns that could threaten national stability.

Odetoye described religious and community leaders as critical stakeholders because of their influence in shaping public opinion and either preventing or escalating tensions within their communities.

He disclosed that the programme would be expanded to Plateau, Kano, Adamawa and Benue States to complement ongoing federal-level efforts aimed at promoting peace and countering information-related security threats.

Representing the Jama’atu Nasril Islam (JNI), Haruna Tanko cautioned against the deliberate spread of false information for political, religious or personal gain.

He warned that misinformation could create unnecessary fear, deepen divisions and trigger avoidable crises, especially during election periods.

Tanko called on both Muslims and Christians to uphold the values of truthfulness, peace and responsible communication while also advocating accountable leadership and improved governance.

Similarly, Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Plateau State Chapter, Rev. Dunka Gomwalk, urged religious leaders to strengthen interfaith dialogue and encourage their followers to verify information before sharing it.

He warned that unverified social media posts and impulsive public comments could fuel religious tensions and undermine ongoing peacebuilding efforts.

Gomwalk expressed optimism that the workshop would produce practical strategies and collaborative approaches through which faith communities could promote mutual coexistence.

Kalanci’s Programme Manager, Bamas Victoria, highlighted the organisation’s ongoing efforts to strengthen community resilience through fact-checking training, media literacy initiatives and public awareness campaigns.

She explained that the programme equips religious leaders, educators and other stakeholders with practical skills to recognise information manipulation, verify follow-up training sessions conducted in different locations have enabled participants to transfer knowledge to their communities, thereby expanding the reach of counter-disinformation efforts.

She expressed confidence in sustained collaboration among religious leaders, civil platforms, and techniques for identifying propaganda and manipulative narratives.

Organisers said the initiative aims to empower faith leaders to become stronger advocates for truth, peace and responsible information sharing as Nigeria prepares for another electoral cycle in 2027.

World.title: AFD, BoI Sign $30m Deal to Unlock Finance for Nigeria’s Creative Sector
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The French Development Agency (AFD) and the Bank of Industry (BoI) have signed a $30 million financing agreement to expand access to credit for Nigeria’s creative industry, with at least 90 per cent of the facility earmarked for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs).

The agreement, which includes a €500,000 technical assistance programme, is AFD’s first credit line dedicated to cultural and creative industries anywhere in the world, positioning Nigeria as the beneficiary of a financing initiative targeting one of the country’s emerging sources of jobs and economic diversification.

The facility, signed in Abuja during the visit of AFD Chief Executive Officer, Christophe Lecourtier, is designed to improve access to finance for businesses in fashion, design, textiles, music, film and audiovisual production, video games and visual arts.

Women-led and youth-led enterprises, as well as first-time borrowers, are among the priority beneficiaries of the programme, which seeks to address financing barriers that have constrained the growth of creative businesses.

The initiative comes as Nigeria’s cultural and creative industries account for approximately five per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and provide livelihoods for more than 4.2 million people.

Under the agreement, the BoI will deploy the credit facility to eligible businesses, while the technical assistance component will strengthen the bank’s capacity to finance the sector through staff training and the development of financial products tailored to the needs of creative enterprises.

The programme targets the training of at least 70 per cent of relevant BoI staff, alongside the development of specialised financing products to better serve businesses whose needs may differ from those of conventional industrial enterprises.

The agreement was signed by BoI Managing Director, Dr Olasupo Olusi, and Lecourtier, who represented AFD, reinforcing the longstanding partnership between the two institutions.

Beyond expanding access to credit, the initiative is expected to promote financial inclusion, support skilled employment and strengthen the contribution of the creative economy to Nigeria’s sustainable and inclusive growth.

Its focus on smaller businesses could prove particularly significant for entrepreneurs seeking to expand production, acquire equipment, develop new products or reach wider markets but who struggle to secure affordable financing.

The facility also aligns with the Federal Government’s Destination 2030 ambition for the creative sector, as Nigeria seeks to diversify its economy and harness industries capable of generating employment and business opportunities for its growing population.

The €500,000 technical assistance component is expected to complement the lending facility by improving BoI’s capacity to understand and meet the financing needs of creative businesses.

For AFD, the agreement represents an expansion of its development financing partnership with Nigeria, while the BoI is expected to use the facility to support enterprise development, job creation and economic diversification.

The two institutions said the programme would help remove financial and non-financial barriers to the development of Nigeria’s cultural and creative industries.

World.title: Give Us Our Severance Package, Protesting WRPC Support Staff Tell NNPCL
World.content:
Sylvester Idowu in Warri

The support staff of Warri Refining and Petrochemical Company (WRPC) have accused the Refinery Coordinator, Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, (NNPC) Limited, Mr. Bayo Adenrele, of working against President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and trying to instigate violence against the administration.

The aggrieved workers claimed that Adenrele has stripped off royalties from host communities of WRPC, vowing that they can no longer tolerate the rubbishing of host communities.

Chairman of the support staff of WRPC, Dafe Ighomitedo, who spoke to newsmen at the entrance of WRPC Tuesday, during the continued protest of the support staff, said NNPCL had been telling the workers lies, upon lies since 2015.

Ighomitedo, stated: “This is the fourth week we have been here protesting for us to get our severance package, having the old contract expired 30th September. Unfortunately, it has been lies upon lies. We have been here since 2015 and this protest has been going on since 2015, but it always ends with deceit.

“The two palaces hosting this company (WRPC) went to Abuja, where they made promises to give the workers proper welfare. They laid off people and give us peanuts, we that remained, we’re still hopeful that someday, something good will happen, but no way. They told the masses that they are taking care of us, saying they are paying us N90,000 to N150,000. No pension, no medical, no transport, we don’t even have access to the plant clinic, when we are sick, it is so demeaning. We can no longer take it. We have been here since 5th October, till now they have not responded.

“The Refinery Coordinator (RC) for the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL), Bayo Adenrele, feels we are nobody and we have lost confidence in him. He has no integrity when it comes to the Support Staff of WRPC.

“He is working against this present government of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. He is doing this to instigate violence against the president. We have been peaceful for so long. The community has been rubbished for too long and we can no longer take it. Bayo Adenrele has stripped the community of all royalties. This time around, it won’t be business as usual.”

Ighomitedo demanded to have a meeting with the Executive Vice-President, Downstream at NNPC Limited, Dr. Mumuni Dagazau, insisting that he should come down to Warri to address the protesting workers.

“We want to see the Executive Vice-President, Downstream at NNPC Limited, Dr. Mumuni Dagazau. He should come and address us, because the RC is rubbishing his office and staining the image of the Group Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL), Bashir Bayo Ojulari. RC is telling people that we are outsourced. We have our letters and document. We were employed directly. Our case is peculiar. The Acting MD right now was once a Support Staff that was later converted, but now nobody wants to convert us,” he said.

One of the support staff, Akivie Kingsley, who spoke in the same vein, stated: “It has been promises and failed promises, what this people are owing us, is what I can’t even speak out. We are entitled to every welfare, but their promises have gotten to the point that we can no longer take it.

“If we are going on leave, no leave allowance. We have people that are already dead; we have two corpses in the mortuary as we speak; we have marriages that are crashing because of lack of finance.
