Children are off school, because we cannot pay their school fees and the RC expects engineers like us, with vast experience, to keep working in this kind of environment, with N90,000 salary, it won’t work. We are done with this slave contract.”

Another support staff of WRPC, who is a Lab Technician, Benjamin Iwuno, lamented that he had put in over 13yrs in WRPC, stressing that all his service years has been taken for granted, being paid peanuts and no health benefit.

“How do you explain to the government that you have over 300 personnel working with you and none of them is pensionable? They can’t have access to basic healthcare. Some of my colleagues have died on duty, no compensation.

“Can the N90,000 take somebody with family home? The management is telling us that we don’t mean anything to them. How is it possible that my boss will write my job as his appraisal and I get nothing in return? It is painful. I want my rightful benefit working in oil and gas company,” Iwuno said.

For Harriet Charles, the story was not different, she wept while narrating her experience with the WRPC for the past 14 years.

“I have been here for the past 14years, I wasn’t like this, if you get to my house now, I don’t have TV, because N90,000 cannot get me TV. My children are in school but cannot pay their school fees. I go begging sometimes, because the money they are paying me is so meagre, people think I earn plenty money because I work in a refinery, where is the money?

“I have to buy soup from people selling soup to manage with my children. I have lost close friends working in the same department with me. I need my severance package, so I can be able to take care of my children. My house rent is due. We need this money, we are dying,” she added.

The aggrieved workers carried banners with inscriptions such as ‘EVP Downstream, Dr. Mumuni Dangazaun, must act now’; ‘The RC, Engr. Bayo Adenrele, Has No Integrity’; ‘WRPC Support Staff were never outsourced, but employed directed by WRPC’ and ‘No EVP Downstream, No discussion.’

World.title: How fans will watch the Soweto Derby with R165
World.content:
The first Soweto Derby of the 2026/27 season kicks off on Saturday, 31 October at the FNB Stadium at 15:30. As always, it will be about much more than three Betway Premiership points, with bragging rights also at stake.

Supporters of Kaizer Chiefs and Orlando Pirates moved very swiftly to snap up all the available tickets within hours after sales opened on MyTicket.

WATCH THE SOWETO DERBY WITH R165

The cheapest adult ticket that includes traveling to the FNB Stadium costs R165. The deal features a Level 1 general admission ticket and return bus transport through Gautrain services.



Supporters who preferred to purchase a Soweto Derby match ticket without transport paid R140 for Level 1 seating. Level 5 tickets were also priced at R140, while Level 2 tickets went for R200.

Children also grabbed Soweto Derby tickets at lower prices. They started at R50. A children’s ticket with Gautrain return bus transport will cost R75, while the package with Rea Vaya transport will be R110.

ORLANDO PIRATES ARE FAVOURITES OVER KAIZER CHIEFS

Pirates, unlike Chiefs, have delivered a near-flawless start to the 2026/27 Betway Premiership season. The defending champions are serious title contenders alongside Mamelodi Sundowns.



Coach Abdeslam Ouaddou’s side have not tasted a loss in eight matches. Pirates have seven wins and one draw with 22 points in the bag.

The mighty Sea Robbers, also competing in the CAF Champions League group stage, have 19 goals scored and just one conceded. That combination of attacking firepower and defensive resilience has put Pirates in a strong position at the top of the standings as they look to challenge the reigning champions for the league crown.

Meanwhile, Chiefs, have somehow, had a not-so-bad season and have unbeaten start of their own. Coach Fernando Da Cruz’s team are fifth place after eight matches. The Glamour Boys have three victories and five draws with 14 points.



Although their resilience has made them difficult to defeat, the performances have made Da Cruz face the wrath of the Chiefs faithful. With 13 goals scored and eight conceded, Chiefs are showing signs of greater structure. Victory in Saturday’s Soweto Derby could just provide exactly the boost the club needs for confidence against a buckling and fearsome Pirates.

CAN KAIZER CHIEFS SHOCK ORLANDO PIRATES?

World.title: Wynberg Boys celebrate two Old Boys in Springbok squad
World.content:
Wynberg old boys Zachary Porthen and Yaqeen Ahmed have been selected for the 37-man Springboks squad for the second leg of the Nations Championship. Image: SA Rugby

Two Wynberg Boys’ High School old boys, Zachary Porthen and Yaqeen Ahmed, have earned call-ups to the Springbok squad for the second leg of the Nations Championship.

The announcement marks a special moment for Wynberg Rugby, with the school celebrating the selection of two former pupils for the same Springbok tour for the first time since Doug Hopwood and Lionel Wilson in 1965.

Porthen, who matriculated in 2022, and Ahmed, who left the Cape Town school in 2025, are among the 37 players selected for the upcoming leg of the tournament.



Uncapped players

Ahmed is one of six uncapped players in the squad, giving him an opportunity to make his Springbok debut.

Porthen, meanwhile, has already made his mark in South African rugby history.

On 1 November 2025, he became the youngest Springbok prop to take the field in the professional era when he played against Japan.

He currently has eight Test caps to his name.

Wynberg Boys’ High School has produced 16 Springboks – including currently uncapped Yaqeen Ahmed.

Schedule

The Springboks will begin the second leg of the Nations Championship against Italy on Saturday, 7 November, before taking on France on Friday, 13 November and Ireland on Saturday, 21 November.



Those matches will be crucial to their hopes of finishing the league stages in the strongest possible position ahead of the Finals Weekend, scheduled for London from 27 to 29 November.

The Springboks currently lead the Southern Hemisphere standings on points difference, tied with New Zealand on 15 points.

World.title: How Orlando Pirates can reach the CAF Champions League quarter-finals
World.content:
Orlando Pirates drawn in Group C of the CAF Champions League. Image: @CAFmedia/X

Orlando Pirates face a tricky CAF Champions League group following Wednesday’s draw.

The Buccaneers have been drawn in Group C alongside Moroccan side RS Berkane, Tanzanian giants Simba SC and Cameroonian champions Colombe Sportive.

Pirates will need to finish in the top two to qualify for the quarter-finals.



With the fixtures set to get underway in the coming weeks, head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou will need his experienced players fit and firing if the Soweto giants are to progress to the knockout stages.

How Can Orlando Pirates Reach the Quarter-Finals?

The Buccaneers must target maximum points against Colombe Sportive, who appear to be the least experienced side in the group at this level of continental competition.

Winning both home and away fixtures against the Cameroonian champions would give Orlando Pirates six valuable points and put them in a strong position to qualify.

Another team the Sea Robbers could target is RS Berkane. The Moroccan side reached last season’s semi-finals but have struggled for consistency recently as they find themselves amongst the bottom teams in the Botola Pro 1.

The Buccaneers will need to take advantage of any weaknesses, particularly when playing at home. Four points from their two meetings would be a positive return, while six would significantly boost their qualification hopes.

Simba SC, however, could prove to be Pirates’ biggest challenge. The Tanzanian giants are experienced campaigners in African football and will be determined to secure their own place in the quarter-finals.



Pirates must therefore make their home advantage count while remaining disciplined on the road.

Winning all three home matches and securing at least one away draw could give the Buccaneers a strong chance of progressing, although the final outcome will depend on results elsewhere in the group.

With a balanced approach and consistent performances, Ouaddou’s men have a realistic opportunity to reach the CAF Champions League quarter-finals.

Orlando Pirates last won the competition back in 1995.

Can Pirates go all the way?

World.title: Suliman Carrim wins R100k bail – but there’s a catch
World.content:
Suliman Carrim has been granted R100 000 bail by the Pretoria Magistrate’s Court after allegedly failing to appear before the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry. Image: National Prosecuting Authority (NPA)

North West businessman Suliman Carrim has been granted R100 000 bail, but he will remain in custody as he faces a separate criminal case in Limpopo.

The Pretoria Magistrate’s Court granted Carrim bail on Wednesday, 28 October, following his arrest for allegedly failing to appear before the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry.

Magistrate Marc Curlewis imposed strict conditions after the State argued that Carrim posed a flight risk.



COURT REJECTS FLIGHT RISK ARGUMENT

Carrim was arrested at OR Tambo International Airport on 15 October, shortly before he was due to board an international flight.

The State opposed bail, arguing that he could evade trial if released.

The court found that the prosecution had not established sufficient grounds to keep him in custody in this case.

Under his bail conditions, Carrim must surrender his travel documents, obtain permission before leaving South Africa and report to the Mmabatho Police Station every Monday.

He must also make arrangements to return to the Madlanga Commission to complete his testimony.

The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) warned that any breach of his bail conditions could result in his arrest and further detention.



WHY CARRIM REMAINS BEHIND BARS

Despite securing bail in Pretoria, Carrim remains in custody in connection with a separate case before the Musina Magistrate’s Court.

He faces charges linked to the alleged attempted theft of two vehicles and the use of fraudulent bank documents.

The case is scheduled to return to court on Friday, 30 October, for a bail application.

In the Madlanga Commission matter, Carrim faces a charge under Section 6(1) of the Commissions Act for allegedly failing to appear before the inquiry on 14 August.

The Pretoria court postponed that case to 8 December 2026 for disclosure of the docket.

World.title: Botswana man killed in Ukraine after joining Russian army through WhatsApp
World.content:
Pako Namogang, the 25-year-old Botswana national reportedly killed while fighting for Russia in Ukraine. Image: Ukraine’s Defence Intelligence.

A 25-year-old Botswana national has been identified as the first citizen of the southern African country to be killed while fighting for Russia in Ukraine, after reportedly joining the Russian army through a WhatsApp recruitment group.

Pako Namogang, born on 30 May 2001, was recruited through a group called “Work in Russia”, according to Ukraine’s Defence Intelligence Directorate (DIU), which released details of his identity and military service.

The agency said a Russian recruiter used the group to seek people willing to serve in the Russian army.



Namogang travelled from Johannesburg to Moscow on 6 July 2026 before signing a one-year military contract on 21 July.

He was reportedly killed in mid-August during fighting near Novoliubivka in Ukraine’s eastern Luhansk region, the DIU said.

Botswana man killed fighting for Russia

According to the Ukrainian intelligence agency, Namogang was accommodated in a hotel after arriving in Moscow before proceeding through the military recruitment process.



He subsequently received training before being deployed to Russian-occupied territory in Ukraine.

The DIU also alleged that intermediaries helped recruit Namogang and other foreign nationals into the Russian military.

The agency said it had published documents relating to his identity and military contract.



However, the circumstances surrounding his death have not been independently verified.

At least 25 Batswana recruited

The Ukrainian government’s “I Want to Live” project, which tracks foreign nationals serving with Russian forces, reportedly has information on at least 25 Botswana citizens who signed military contracts with Russia.

One of the recruits is reportedly being held as a prisoner of war by Ukrainian forces, while Namogang is the first Botswana national the project has identified as having been killed in the conflict.



The figures highlight concerns about the recruitment of African nationals into Russia’s war against Ukraine, sometimes through offers circulated on social media.

Botswana government warns young people

Botswana’s government had already raised concerns about the recruitment of its citizens before Namogang’s identity was announced.

According to Botswana’s state-owned DailyNews, International Relations Minister Phenyo Butale told Parliament on 25 August 2026 that nearly 22 Batswana had been drawn into recruitment schemes connected to the Russia-Ukraine conflict.



Butale warned that some citizens were being attracted by offers presented as employment, training or security work before finding themselves on the frontline.

He said Botswana had helped stop and return eight citizens who were intercepted at airports in Botswana, South Africa and Ethiopia.

The minister also cautioned young people against accepting foreign military employment or training offers without understanding the risks involved.



Namogang’s reported death adds to concerns over the vulnerability of African jobseekers to recruitment into overseas conflicts.

World.title: The longest and shortest drives between Kruger National Park camps
World.content:
Driving through Kruger? These camps are furthest apart. Image: wikimedia commons

Driving between rest camps in Kruger National Park can take anything from just over an hour to most of a day, depending on where you are staying.

The park’s vast size means visitors need to consider distances carefully when planning an itinerary, particularly if they intend to move between camps during a short holiday.

The following figures are taken from SANParks’ published distances chart. Journey times are estimates that allow for slower driving and game viewing, rather than uninterrupted travel at the maximum speed limit.



Route between camps Approximate distance Estimated driving time Longest: Punda Maria to Berg-en-Dal 415km 16 hours 35 minutes Berg-en-Dal to Shingwedzi 344km 13 hours 45 minutes Punda Maria to Skukuza 342km 13 hours 40 minutes Shingwedzi to Berg-en-Dal 344km 13 hours 45 minutes Punda Maria to Lower Sabie 342km 13 hours 40 minutes Skukuza to Lower Sabie 43km 1 hour 45 minutes Satara to Orpen 48km 1 hour 55 minutes Skukuza to Pretoriuskop 49km 2 hours Satara to Olifants 54km 2 hours 10 minutes Letaba to Satara 69km 2 hours 45 minutes Shortest: Olifants to Letaba 32km 1 hour 20 minutes

Why do drives take so long in Kruger NATIONAL PARK?

Kruger National Park has strict speed limits to protect wildlife and visitors. SANParks lists maximum speeds of 50km/h on tarred roads and 40km/h on gravel roads.

Actual driving times can be longer because of:

Wildlife sightings: Animals on or beside the road often cause vehicles to slow down or stop.

Animals on or beside the road often cause vehicles to slow down or stop. Road surfaces: Gravel roads and certain routes can take longer to negotiate than tarred roads.

Gravel roads and certain routes can take longer to negotiate than tarred roads. Stops along the way: Visitors may want to visit picnic sites, viewpoints or waterholes.

Visitors may want to visit picnic sites, viewpoints or waterholes. Route choice: The shortest route is not necessarily the most rewarding for wildlife viewing.

SANParks’ published distances chart uses an average speed of 25km/h when estimating journey times, taking game viewing into account.

Some tips for planning drives between camps

Visitors should avoid planning an itinerary around distances alone. A route of 50km may take considerably longer than expected if there are good wildlife sightings along the way.

It is also important to remember that visitors must reach their booked camp or exit gate before the applicable closing time. Plan to arrive with a comfortable margin rather than relying on the estimated journey time.

For longer journeys, consider booking overnight accommodation at an intermediate camp. This can make a trip more relaxed and leave more time for game viewing.



Before setting off, check the latest SANParks travel times and Kruger maps, and confirm whether any road closures or other restrictions affect your route.

World.title: Petrol and diesel prices: What motorists need to know for November
World.content:
South Africa's motorists are set for a temporary - but welcome - two-month long fuel price relief at the pumps. Image: pexels

South Africa’s motorists could see petrol prices edge lower and diesel prices drop by more than R1.50 per litre in November 2026, following the government’s temporary fuel levy cuts.

The latest Central Energy Fund (CEF) data shows that petrol and diesel remain significantly under-recovered, pointing to further increases if current market conditions persist without intervention.

However, the temporary fuel levy reductions announced by Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana during his MTBPS speech last Wednesday have changed the outlook, with the latest projections indicating potential price cuts across all four main fuel grades.



The CEF figures as of Tuesday, 27 October, show petrol 93 with an under-recovery of R1.27 per litre and petrol 95 under-recovered by R1.12 per litre.

Diesel 0.05% is under-recovered by R1.43 per litre, while diesel 0.005% has an under-recovery of R1.35 per litre.

How much could fuel prices drop in November?

Godongwana announced a temporary fuel levy reduction as part of a R10 billion relief package intended to ease pressure on consumers.

For November, the general fuel levy will be reduced by R1.50 per litre for petrol and R3 per litre for diesel.

Based on the latest CEF snapshot and the relief measures, the indicative November inland prices are:

Fuel type Oct price Nov projection Levy Potential change Petrol 93 R29.88 R31.15 (R1.50) -23c/l Petrol 95 R30.25 R31.37 (R1.50) -38c/l Diesel 0.05% R31.95 R33.38 (R3.00) -R1.57/l Diesel 0.005% R33.29 R34.64 (R3.00) -R1.65/l

These are projections rather than confirmed prices. The final adjustments will depend on the remainder of the month’s market movements and other pricing factors, including the slate levy.



Oil prices could wipe out petrol cuts

The outlook remains uncertain as international oil prices rise amid renewed tensions in the Middle East.

Oil climbed to around $115 per barrel during the week, while the rand traded at around R16.50 to the US dollar.

Both factors influence South Africa’s fuel prices and could erode the projected savings before the end of October.

A weaker rand, further oil price increases or a significant slate levy adjustment could turn the projected cuts into increases.

The new prices are scheduled to take effect at midnight on Tuesday, 3 November.

1. The international price of petroleum products, driven mainly by oil prices.

2. The rand/dollar exchange rate used in the purchase of these products.

World.title: On the road to LGE 2026: Discovering Mahikeng
World.content:
MAHIKENG - As eNCA hits the road ahead of the 2026 Local Government Elections, we’re exploring the cities and communities shaping South Africa.

Reporter Bafedile Moerane will be visiting Mahikeng, the capital of the North West, a city with a rich political and historical legacy.

Here are five facts about Mahikeng you may not know.

1. The provincial capital

Mahikeng serves as the capital of North West province and is an important administrative centre in the region.

2. Close to Botswana

The city lies near South Africa’s border with Botswana, making it an important location for cross-border movement and trade.

3. A town with a wartime history

Mahikeng became internationally known during the Siege of Mafeking, which began in 1899 during the South African War, also known as the Anglo-Boer War.

4. A connection to Sol Plaatje

Prominent South African writer, journalist and political activist Sol Plaatje documented events surrounding the siege in his Mafeking Diary, offering a historical account of the period.

5. A name with a history

The name Mahikeng is derived from a Setswana word meaning “place of rocks”, reflecting the rocky landscape associated with the area.

World.title: N2 wall divides ANC and DA as poll finds nearly 70% support it
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The proposed wall on the N2 in Cape Town sparked a heated exchange between the ANC and the DA during an election debate.

Both DA Cape Town Mayoral Candidate, Geordin Hill-Lewis, and ANC representative Jeremia Thuynsma weighed in on whether the project would improve safety or divert attention from the deeper social ills Capetonians face.

The clash followed the presentation of an eNCA MarkData poll.

It found that 69.6% of respondents were in favour of the wall, 19.9% were against, while 10.5% were undecided.

READ | WATCH | ANC takes aim at DA over Cape Town’s clean audit slip

Thuynsma questioned the purpose of the project, adding that if the city was serious about fighting crime, it would direct its resources to the areas crime most affects.

'The reality is that crime is a big problem in the entire Cape Flats, and he's not attending to it. He must be responsible for the answers that he gives. The wall on the N2 is just basically taking money from the resources that are given to the state to attend to our people's problems for a nice-to-have.'

Alongside tackling crime, he also called on the city to address the underlying causes of the scourge including unemployment, poverty and housing shortages.

'If we basically build houses in a community, allow the community to build the houses, that will be creating jobs where the projects are. You are fixing roads; let the community do it, because that is what EPWP was about...The more people work, the less possibility you have of them getting involved in crime.'

But Hill-Lewis rejected Thuynsma’s criticism. Using the survey results, he said those who voted in favour of the project are those who are concerned about their safety.

World.title: Sharks confirm Mbonambi exit

DURBAN - The Sharks have confirmed the departure of Springbok hooker Bongi Mbonambi.

According to a statement from the Durban-based club, both parties agreed to end his contract with immediate effect.

It follows reports that the double World Cup-winning hooker was set to return to the Stormers.

"The decision follows constructive discussions between both parties and has been reached on amicable terms," the Durban club said in a statement on Wednesday.

Mbonambi had been involved in a disciplinary dispute with the Sharks over an alleged breach of team rules.

Mbonambi is set to feature for the Stormers as early as this weekend against Ulster at Cape Town Stadium.

The 35-year-old is said to have signed a one-year contract with the Stormers, who he represented on 74 occasions between 2015 and 2021 before joining the Sharks.

World.title: These are Suliman Carrim's bail conditions
World.content:
PRETORIA - North West businessman Suliman Carrim might have reprieve in one matter, but his legal woes continue. On Wednesday he was granted R100, 000 bail at Pretoria Magistrate's Court.

He was arrested by the Commission’s Recommendations Task Team (CRTT) at the OR Tambo International Airport on 15 October while boarding a plane to the UAE.

His arrest was in relation to his non-appearance at the Madlanga Commission multiple time. Thus, violating the Commissions Act.

The 49-year-old applied for bail stating that his health might often make it hard for him to appear before the court for his trial.

For this matter in Pretoria, he has been granted R100,000 bail and his bail conditions are as follows:

World.title: Suliman Carrim granted R100k bail in Madlanga case
World.content:
PRETORIA – Controversial North West businessman Suliman Carrim has been granted R100,000 bail with strict conditions in the Pretoria Magistrate’s Court.

Carrim has been behind bars since his arrest at OR Tambo International Airport two weeks ago. He is accused of failing to appear before the Madlanga Commission despite being subpoenaed to testify.

The State argued that his planned overseas trip suggested he could flee the country. Carrim, however, maintained that he intended to return to South Africa.

In his ruling, Magistrate Marc Carlewis said the court had considered the nature and seriousness of the charge, the strength of the state’s case at this preliminary stage, and the potential consequences of a conviction, including the maximum penalty.

He said these factors did not establish a sufficiently strong incentive for Carrim to evade trial, particularly given his established ties to South Africa.

The magistrate acknowledged that the state had raised legitimate concerns about whether Carrim would attend future court proceedings. However, he found that these concerns did not establish that Carrim was likely to evade trial if released on appropriately restrictive bail conditions.

The court also considered Carrim’s residential and family ties to South Africa, as well as his property interests in the country. His residential address in Mafikeng was subsequently verified by the state.

READ MORE | Madlanga Commission welcomes Suliman Carrim's arrest

The investigating officer testified that Carrim was arrested while preparing to travel internationally and had initially failed to produce proof of a return booking. This raised concerns that he might not return to South Africa.

However, the state later confirmed that Carrim’s return booking was authentic and indicated that he intended to return to South Africa on 27 October 2026.

Carlewis acknowledged that having a return booking did not conclusively prove Carrim’s intention to return. Nevertheless, he said its verification materially weakened the inference that Carrim intended to leave South Africa permanently.

World.title: China says takes Mbappe apology 'seriously' after Mao remark
World.content:
MADRID - China said Wednesday it took "seriously" an apology from Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe after comments he made poking fun at Mao Zedong sparked a social media storm and saw Spanish football yanked off state TV.

Mocking former leader Mao, blamed by historians for millions of deaths, is taboo in China and the French player's remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure to anger Beijing.

In a clip of a video interview with French show The Bridge, since taken down, Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto "some guy, think he's a Chinese dictator", an apparent reference to Mao.

"My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset," the France captain said in a statement in French, Chinese and English on Tuesday.

Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing on Wednesday: "We take seriously the apology the individual concerned has made."

La Liga, which saw the broadcast of its matches suspended in China, said it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe's recent comments have caused among Chinese fans".

But that may not be the end of the matter.

Chinese beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year's World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe, said Tuesday it had scrapped its partnership with the player, as did dairy firms Mengniu and Milkground.

CMG, which oversees public broadcaster CCTV, said it had decided to suspend broadcasts of the world's second-richest football league after England's Premier League.

Mbappe's club also drew fire for not issuing any public apology, with "How much longer will arrogant Real Madrid keep playing ostrich" ranking fifth on search engine Baidu on Wednesday.

Real "has neither criticised nor warned Mbappe over his conduct, let alone imposed any disciplinary measures", the state-run Global Times said in an editorial.

Mbappe, 27, continued to face a torrent of criticism from Chinese web users on Wednesday, some of it racist.

"His remarks were hurtful toward China and the Chinese people, so they cannot be translated," wrote one user on social media platform Weibo.

Mbappe's original joke about Mao was not reposted or had been scrubbed, from China's tightly controlled social media.

Chinese social media app Xiaohongshu had meanwhile frozen Mbappe's account, where he has over a million followers.

The same was done on the Weibo app, with a notice stating that "the user has been banned from following due to violating laws or the Weibo Community Convention".

Some Chinese media reports said global brands like Dior and Hublot had removed their Mbappe-related content on Weibo.

An AFP search on Dior and Hublot's Weibo page with Mbappe's Chinese name produced no results.
