World.title: Liberian Activists Urge Freeze on New Mining Deals Until Decades-Old Law Is Rewritten
World.content:
A coalition of civil society groups says signing long-term contracts under Liberia’s 2000 mining law would lock in the weak oversight, lost revenue and pollution that have marked the sector for decades.

MONROVIA, Liberia — A coalition of civil society organizations in Liberia has called on the government to stop signing and ratifying new long-term mining contracts until the West African nation replaces its 26-year-old mining law.

The CSO Consortium on Minerals, Mining, and Inclusive Sustainable Development made the appeal on Monday, October 26, at a press conference in the capital. It urged President Joseph Nyuma Boakai and the national legislature to impose a moratorium on new Mineral Development Agreements (MDAs) — the contracts, typically lasting 25 years or more, that set the terms under which large mining companies operate and that carry the force of law once lawmakers ratify them.



“We strongly believe that entering into new or additional long-term mineral development agreements under an outdated legal framework risk perpetuating existing governance weaknesses,” the coalition said.

Its members include the Center for Transparency and Accountability in Liberia, Integrity Watch Liberia, the Sustainable Development Institute, Medica Liberia and ActionAid Liberia, among others.

Wealth that has not reached communities

Mining is central to Liberia’s economy. It accounts for about a fifth of gross domestic product and dominates exports, according to a March 2026 assessment by the Washington-based research group Forest Trends. Iron ore and gold are the main products.

Yet the coalition said decades of extraction have not delivered matching jobs, public services or development for the communities that host mines. It blamed weak enforcement, corruption, the export of unprocessed ore, poor transparency, environmental damage and the exclusion of local people from decisions.

The Forest Trends report reached similar conclusions. It found the government may be losing millions of dollars a year in uncollected mining revenue. Mining companies paid just over $844 million to the state between 2007 and 2023, according to figures from the Liberia Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (LEITI), the national arm of a global revenue-disclosure standard. Mining licenses now overlap more than two million hectares of forest in a country that holds about half of what remains of the Upper Guinean rainforest biodiversity hotspot.

A year of illegal mining and license violations

The call follows a year in which government inspectors repeatedly found companies mining outside the limits of their permits, or with no permit at all.

Liberia issues several tiers of mining license. Class C permits are reserved for Liberian citizens and allow only hand tools. Class B permits cover small commercial operations. Large industrial projects operate under MDAs.

In March, a committee of the House of Representatives suspended Hurine Mining Company in central Bong County after investigators found it had exceeded the limits of its Class B license.

In April, the Ministry of Mines and Energy closed JinXin Mining Company in Rivercess County for mining without a valid license on ground licensed to another firm. The ministry said JinXin had ignored an order in January to stop. Days later it shut Alex Gee Group of Companies in Grand Gedeh County, whose license had lapsed. Officers also dismantled an unlicensed site whose alleged Chinese operators fled before they arrived.

In June, officials in Gbarpolu County seized excavators working a Class C claim, where heavy machinery is banned. They also found Chinese nationals mining under another company’s license, outside its approved boundaries.

Mines and Energy Minister R. Matenokay Tingban has acknowledged that many small commercial license holders fail to account for the minerals they extract.

The problems are not new. In 2024, the then-minister sought legal advice on revoking licenses issued since 2018, citing letters from the presidency directing that license applications be routed through the Office of the President. In 2025, a ministry investigation found that two companies, Hamak Mining and its successor 79 Resources, had misrepresented their license status and owed the government more than $400,000 in fees.

Big miners under scrutiny

Concerns extend to the largest operators. An investigation by The Associated Press and The Gecko Project published this year found that Bea Mountain Mining Corporation, Liberia’s biggest gold producer, repeatedly leaked cyanide, arsenic and copper at levels the country’s Environmental Protection Agency said exceeded legal limits.

The investigation found the company failed to report a 2022 spill on time and had earlier blocked government inspectors from its laboratory. Bea Mountain exported more than $576 million worth of gold between July 2021 and December 2022.

Why the coalition wants a pause now

Liberia’s Minerals and Mining Law was enacted in 2000, before the country’s 14-year civil war had fully ended. Lawmakers opened public hearings on amendments in July. At those hearings, the Liberia Chamber of Mines, an industry body, warned that changes limited to small commercial licenses would not fix the sector’s deeper problems. It called for a full overhaul covering taxation, licensing, environmental protection and strategic minerals such as lithium, cobalt and rare earths.

In January, the legislature ratified an amendment to the contract of steelmaker ArcelorMittal, Liberia’s largest iron ore producer, extending it to 2050 with an option to renew for 25 more years. Some senators praised the deal as a model for renegotiating other contracts. Another senator abstained, citing the company’s record of unmet commitments to host communities.

For the coalition, that timeline is the core of the argument. Contracts signed under a law that government, industry and activists all describe as outdated will outlast any reform that follows.

What the activists want in a new law

The coalition drew up its proposals at a meeting with mining-affected communities on October 1 and refined them at an October 21 roundtable with government agencies, donors and companies. Its 10 recommendations include:

* Binding transparency rules for licensing, contracts and revenue, including public disclosure of who ultimately owns mining companies;

* Clear penalties for violations by companies and by officials, and legal remedies for affected communities;

* Enforceable benefit-sharing for communities, building on a 2018 land rights law;

* Requirements to process more ore locally and to prioritize Liberian workers and suppliers;

* Binding obligations for mine closure and land restoration;

* Measures to protect women, young people and people with disabilities, including against sexual exploitation and abuse in mining areas; and

* Tighter regulation of small-scale mining, including sand and quarry operations.

The coalition praised the Boakai government’s stated commitment to reform but said the new law “must go beyond updating existing provisions.”

The Ministry of Mines and Energy did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

World.title: Liberia: Grebo Leader Calls for Calm and Swift Probe Into Death of Samuel Gekor in Grand Gedeh
World.content:
MONROVIA – A prominent Liberian lawyer and leading figure in the Grebo community has called for calm and a swift investigation into the death of Samuel Gekor, a young Grebo man found dead on a cassava farm near Zwedru, the capital of southeastern Grand Gedeh County.

Gekor’s body was discovered in the Kanneh area of Electoral District Two after he had been missing for three days. The circumstances of his disappearance remain unclear.

Counsellor Kunkunyon Wleh Teh expressed deep sadness over Gekor’s death and extended condolences to his family and the wider Grebo community, one of Liberia’s major ethnic groups, concentrated largely in the country’s southeast.



Teh, a former student of Bishop Juwel High School in Zwedru, said he has spoken with Gekor’s family to offer his condolences and support.

While acknowledging the community’s grief, fear and frustration, and its legitimate demand for answers, Teh urged residents to remain calm, peaceful and law-abiding as the search for justice continues.

He called on the Liberia National Police and the Ministry of Justice to speed up the investigation, establish the facts surrounding the disappearance and death, and ensure that anyone found responsible is held accountable under the law. The family and the public, he said, deserve timely updates, transparency and credible answers.

“Every Liberian deserves the right to life, safety, and dignity, irrespective of tribe, county, or social standing. No family should be left without answers when a loved one dies under troubling circumstances,” Teh said.

He said the community’s responsibility at this moment is to stand with the family, promote peace and demand justice through lawful means, cautioning against letting grief and anger turn into actions that could endanger lives or deepen divisions.

“Justice must be pursued, truth must prevail, and peace must be preserved,” he said.

World.title: Investors, executives gather in Margibi as Liberia seeks new money for mining and energy
World.content:
MONROVIA – President Joseph Nyuma Boakai will open a two-day international mining and energy conference on Wednesday, as Liberia steps up efforts to attract foreign investment into the natural-resource sectors that underpin its economy.

The Liberia International Mining and Energy Conference and Expo (LIMEC 2026) runs October 28–29 at the Farmington Hotel in Margibi County, near Roberts International Airport outside Monrovia. Government officials, international investors, mining executives, energy developers and development partners are expected to attend.

Boakai is scheduled to deliver the keynote address, setting out his government’s plans for drawing investment and promoting responsible development of the country’s mineral resources.



Mining, chiefly iron ore and gold, is one of the West African nation’s main sources of export earnings, while chronic power shortages remain a major obstacle to industrial growth.

Held under the theme “Transforming Liberia’s Economy: Driving Development Through Sustainable Mining and Energy Investments,” the conference will feature panel discussions, presentations and exhibitions on investment opportunities in mineral exploration, production, renewable energy and related infrastructure.

Amara Kamara, president of the Liberia Chamber of Mines, said the gathering offers Liberia a chance to deepen ties with international investors, showcase its resources and build partnerships that could create jobs and drive growth.

He said the event’s value should go beyond investment promotion to opening doors for Liberian businesses, increasing local participation in the mining industry and ensuring that communities benefit from investments.

Kamara credited Mines and Energy Minister R. Matenokay Tingban and his ministry for coordinating with the Chamber of Mines and AME Trade Ltd., the international organizer, to stage the event.

Sponsors include Avesoro Resources, Mantrac Group, Huawei, CORICA Mining Services, Mansa Resources, Sarmin Metals, Westcrest Liberia, AGL Africa Global Logistics, the Liberia Electricity Corporation (LEC), the Liberia Petroleum Regulatory Authority (LPRA) and WBHO.

World.title: Minister of Health commends local pharmaceuticals companies
World.content:
Minister of Health Professor, Roma Chilengi, has commended local pharmaceutical companies for investing in domestic production.

Professor Chilengi says the developments will create employment opportunities, strengthen the healthcare system and support the Government’s Grow Zambia Agenda.

He said the investments demonstrate Zambia’s ambition to expand local manufacturing is achievable and is already translating into tangible results.

Professor Chilengi was speaking after an inspection tour of V.L. Health Net Services Limited and Medizam Healthcare Limited, local pharmaceutical companies.

He said the investments would also provide opportunities for graduates and future scientists to acquire practical skills and contribute to the country’s economic development.

Professor Chilengi further noted that increased local production would improve the availability of essential medical commodities within the country’s healthcare system.

Meanwhile, Professor Chilengi has announced that Zambia is expected to break ground for the construction of a cholera vaccine manufacturing facility this month, through a partnership between the Zambian and Chinese governments.

He said the Zambian Government, through the Industrial Development Corporation, IDC, would be the majority shareholder in the project.

Professor Chilengi said the initiative demonstrates the Government’s commitment to building local capacity in vaccine production, expressing optimism that Zambia would manufacture its first vaccine in the coming months.

And local Pharmaceutical companies have pledged to continue serving the people of Zambia by making quality healthcare services more accessible and affordable in line with the national vision.

World.title: Mundubile, 17 others bail application adjourned to tomorrow
World.content:
The constitutional bail application case involving National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) 2026 Presidential candidate Brian Mundubile, his running mate Makebi Zulu and 16 others has been adjourned to tomorrow, October 29, 2026.

Chief State Advocate, Chali Hambayi, explained that the matter could not take off this morning to afford time to the lawyers for the petitioners to respond to the affidavit in opposition that was filed by the state.

Ms Hambayi indicated to journalists at the High Court in Lusaka, that the court granted the adjournment based on the request.

“The matter of Brian Mundubile and 17 others was scheduled to come up for the hearing of the application for constitutional bail. However, the matter could not take off this morning due to the fact that the lawyers for the petitioners asked for an adjournment to afford them time to respond to the affidavit in opposition, that was filed by the state,” Ms Hambayi stated.

Meanwhile, the petitioners Lawyer Milner Katolo said the defence team was working to ensure that the affidavit is signed by the clients, so that it is filed and the matter proceeds.

The matter came up before a panel of three judges, chaired by Judge Derek Mulenga.

Mr Mundubile, Mr Zulu and 16 other accused are facing various charges, including treason, sedition and offences relating to the prohibition of terrorism, following the August 13, 2026 general election.

World.title: Over 760 thousand farmers receive redeeming codes
World.content:
Government says 761,666 out of a target of 1,024,434 small-scale farmers have already received their redeeming codes.

Delivering a ministerial statement in Parliament today on the update of farming inputs, Acting Minister of Agriculture, Situmbeko Musokotwane, says the progression rate represents 74 percent.

Dr Musokotwane stated that of those issued with codes, 670,371 farmers have successfully redeemed their inputs, accounting for 65 percent of the targeted beneficiaries.

He announced that significant progress has been recorded in the distribution of farming inputs for the 2026-2027 agricultural season.

He highlighted that the programme utilizes the e-voucher modality, which has been rolled out across all 116 districts in the country.

Dr Musokotwane explained that the system is designed to promote crop diversification, climate resilience, and increased private sector participation, ensuring the timely delivery of inputs such as fertilizer, maize seeds, and various crop protection chemicals.

He further revealed that to support the programme, his Ministry received 1,764 applications from potential agro-input suppliers, of which 805 have been approved to participate and distribute inputs in their respective districts.

The Acting Minister of Agriculture said the ministry continues to conduct training for both agro-dealers and staff at the provincial and district levels to ensure efficient programme implementation.

And Dr Musokotwane has said the government has integrated the Zambia Integrated Agriculture Management System (ZIAMS) with three mobile network operators to enhance service delivery and customer verification.

Dr Musokotwane added that ZIAMS has also been linked with the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) systems to facilitate better monitoring and support the national production target of 10 million metric tons.

He urged farmers who have not yet redeemed their inputs to do so promptly at participating agro-dealer outlets in their localities.

Dr Musokotwane further cautioned beneficiaries against sharing their secret codes with agro-dealers or any third parties.

“Farmers are urged to personally present their codes and ensure they receive the full entitlement of inputs due to them. Government remains committed to strengthening the systems and mechanisms that support our farmers,” Dr. Musokotwane stated.

World.title: Govt embarks on national urban planning for regenerating cities
World.content:
Government has embarked on a consultative meeting to discuss the National Urban Planning programme which is focused on regenerating cities across the country.

Local authorities from across the country converged in Lusaka, following a successful settlement selection process.

The consultative meeting, has brought together civil society organisations, chiefs, traditional leaders, Council Chairpersons, Town Clerks, Planning Directors and members of the general public to deliberate on strategies for sustainable urban renewal, slum upgrading and orderly land use management.

Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development, Senior Professional Officer for Urban Planning, Meembo Nchimunya, said the programme seeks to address rapid urbanization challenges and promote inclusive, resilient and well-planned cities in line with the National Urbanisation Policy.

“To improve the living conditions of our citizens, the views, needs and ideas of citizens must be heard and integrated into the planning process. This consultation is critical to ensure that no one is left behind in our urban planning agenda,” Ms Nchimunya said.

And Zambia Institute of Planners President, Busiku Sulwe, emphasised the need to adopt realistic planning approaches that reflect the current urban situation.

“We need to exercise approaches that accommodate existing urban realities. If we ignore the realities on the ground, we will perpetuate the very challenges we are trying to solve,” Mr Sulwe said.

Meanwhile, a member of the Zambia Homeless and Poor People’s Federation (ZHPPF), Alice Phiri, echoed her organisation’s commitment to working with the government.

“As ZHPPF, we are committed to working with the government throughout this consultation process and the actualization of the national urban planning programme. We represent the voices of the urban poor and we want to ensure our communities are part of the solution,” Ms Phiri said.

The meeting is expected to come up with a roadmap for the implementation of the regenerating cities initiative across the selected local authorities.

Chikumbi says football has benefited significantly from Government support through funding, infrastructure and human resources provided through the Ministry of Sport, Youth and Arts and the National Sports Council of Zambia.

He said the Government has supported football since independence, including funding clubs and providing financial support to national teams.

Chikumbi noted that the Government has also taken steps to promote gender equality in football by ensuring that male and female players receive equal winning bonuses.

He says the Chipolopolo are preparing for the next round of the Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, while the Copper Queens are working towards qualifying for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games.

Chikumbi added that the Government has continued to support national teams with travel arrangements and other resources, citing the provision of a chartered plane for the Chipolopolo ahead of their match against Uganda in India.

Meanwhile, Zambia Premier League Chief Executive Officer, Joseph Chimpampwe, says the Zambia Premier League was established as the professional and commercial arm of the Football Association of Zambia (FAZ) to allow the association to focus on football development and national teams.

Chimpampwe says the league oversees professional competitions, including the men’s MTN Super League, the women’s Super-Division and lower-tier leagues.

He says Government funding to FAZ is mainly directed towards the development of football and supporting the men’s and women’s national teams, while the association is working to raise additional resources.

Chimpampwe says the league is exploring ways to do more through sponsorships and partnerships to strengthen its operations and support football development.

He adds that the league is positioning itself to increase its contribution to the growth of football in Zambia.

World.title: Grade seven pupils warned against engaging in examinations malpractices

Mungwi District Education Standards Officer (DESO) Musa Mulemwa, has warned pupils against engaging in examinations malpractices.

He called on pupils in examination classes to desist from any form of examination malpractice so they can obtain results that genuinely reflect their academic capabilities.

“Approach examinations with confidence, thorough preparation and positive attitude to avoid engaging in examinations leakages,” he disclosed.

The DESO urged the pupils to uphold honesty and integrity to allow their hard work to speak for them.

” A qualification earned honestly is far more valuable than the one obtained through cheating,” Mr Mulemwa said.

And speaking earlier Peas Kabuta Secondary School Headteacher Edson Musowa declared the school’s readiness to record a single digit in grade 12 examinations.

Mr Musowa further encouraged Teachers and learners who did not receive awards to work extremely hard for their efforts to be recognised next year.

Meanwhile, Peas Kampinda Coordinator, Shadrick Mulenga said the event was being celebrated under the theme: Rooted in value, ready for the world: knowledge, character and service,”

Mr Mulenga noted that the theme goes beyond passing examinations but must produce individuals who are knowledgeable, disciplined, honest and ready to serve the nation.

” The school will always strive to develop learners who excel academically while upholding strong moral values,” he narrated.

World.title: Government urged to address water challenges at Maule Rural Health Facility
World.content:
A concerned resident of Maule Village, Perthias Sichula, has bemoaned the lack of a dependable water source at the health facility, saying the situation is putting patients and health workers at risk.

Mr Sichula told the media in an interview that the facility does not have reliable running water, forcing patients and health workers to fetch water from various unprotected sources in the surrounding area.

Mr Sichula has since appealed to government and other relevant authorities to urgently drill a borehole or connect the facility to a safe and reliable water supply.

He also expressed concern over the deplorable state of the road connecting Maule Village to Senga Market through Kalukanya, Moses and Nkatya villages.

Mr Sichula has called on the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development, through the Senga Hill Town Council and the Road Development Agency (RDA), to work on the road to ease the movement of people, goods and services.

Meanwhile, Senga Hill District United Party for National Development (UPND) Chairperson Lewis Muchindo has acknowledged the water challenge at Maule Rural Health Facility, saying the matter is known and that government officials are doing everything possible to address the matter.

Mr Muchindo said government is expected to address the water challenge through the 2027 Constituency Development Fund (CDF).

He said it is important for every health facility to have access to a reliable water supply, given the critical role water plays in the provision of quality healthcare services.

Mr Muchindo has since appealed to residents to remain patient, assuring them that a borehole will be installed at the facility.

He said the Government, under the leadership of President Hakainde Hichilema, has heard the concerns raised by the community and is doing everything possible to address the challenge, particularly for the benefit of patients and expectant mothers who require adequate water during childbirth.

Mr Muchindo further said the planned borehole project should include a water storage tank and taps to ensure that the health facility has a sustainable and accessible water supply.

The beneficiaries thanked Mr Kasambo and ZAPD, saying the support will go a long way in cushioning their welfare and improving mobility.

Community leaders commended the Member of Parliament for remembering the most vulnerable and for fostering inclusive development in the constituency.

World.title: Senegal: Senegal's Youth Olympics' Welcome Should Include Everyone
World.content:
guest column

When the Olympic flame is lit in Dakar on October 31, Senegal will become the first African country to host an Olympic event. Nearly 3,000 athletes from 206 countries will compete at the Youth Olympics under the motto “Africa Welcomes, Dakar Celebrates.” Organizers have promised to greet them with teranga, a word that refers to the Senegalese tradition of hospitality, sharing and generosity.

On September 24, Senegal’s President Bassirou Diomaye Faye told the UN General Assembly: “By welcoming the world’s youth, Senegal will be hosting much more than just a sporting competition.” He said hosting the Youth Olympic Games shows “our differences [are] a strength, our diversity a richness, and our common humanity the foundation of peace.”

These lofty values are, however, in stark contrast to a law adopted in March that provides for a 10-year maximum prison term for consensual same-sex conduct and punishes “promotion” of homosexuality, or financial or other support for lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender (LGBT) people and organizations.

A new Human Rights Watch report documents rights abuses under the amended law, including mass arrests, forced HIV testing, barriers to accessing legal representation, and degrading detention conditions.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Human rights defenders and lawyers said that the introduction of new offenses of “promotion” or “glorification” of homosexuality has led to fear and anxiety among legal professionals and contributed to an environment in which detainees struggle to secure legal representation.

The impact on LGBT people in Senegal has been devastating. A 22-year-old university student described children following him through his neighborhood singing a Wolof slur while adults looked on. “People started insulting me… I couldn’t even defend myself. I knew if I said something, they would all come after me. To come back home I had to wait until it is dark so no one would notice me,” he said.

Police and Gendarmerie have also tested detainees for HIV without consent, then used positive results to bring additional charges. Although a District court later dropped these charges, such practices have contributed to a broader climate of fear and mistrust around access to HIV-related services.

Health professionals said that the law and the arrests that followed had made people unwilling to seek needed care. “One-third no longer come in for appointments to seek HIV treatment,” a doctor in Dakar told Human Rights Watch. A psychologist at Cheikh Anta Diop University said campus consultations had tripled since March, many of them with young men experiencing severe anxiety, hypervigilance, withdrawal from social life, and obsessive behaviors driven by fear of being perceived and attacked as LGBT.

The new law also puts participants in the upcoming Dakar Youth Olympics, including athletes, staff, and fans -- both residents and visitors at risk.

Globally, many athletes are using the Olympic platform to champion inclusion and diversity, including on issues affecting LGBT people. Many have also openly supported their LGBT teammates, coaches, friends, and family members. At the most recent Winter Olympics in Milan a record 50 out LGBT athletes competed, reflecting that LGBT inclusion has become part of the contemporary Olympic movement.

Senegal’s new law also blatantly contradicts the Olympic Charter, which prohibits “discrimination of any kind” within the Olympic movement, explicitly including discrimination based on sexual orientation. Senegal’s government is a key member of the organizing committee for the Youth Olympics. As part of their agreement with the International Olympic Committee (IOC), Olympic hosts commit to prevent, investigate, and remedy human rights abuses related to the games.

The example of the 2021 Tokyo Olympics showed that the Olympic spirit can inspire governments to act positively on LGBT people’s rights. After promising to welcome the world with “omotenashi,” Japan’s tradition of hospitality, the Tokyo Metropolitan government adopted an anti-discrimination ordinance tied to the Games. A national bill protecting LGBT rights stalled in 2021, but two years later Japan passed its first national law on LGBT rights. Campaigners credit the Olympics with advancing efforts to protect LGBT people from discrimination.

Close 

President Faye has a landmark opportunity to follow Japan’s lead. As the Games open, he should make a public commitment that all participants, visitors and residents will be protected from discrimination and arbitrary arrest. He should order the release of those detained under the LGBT law and refer the law to the

Constitutional Council to review its alignment with the Senegalese Constitution and international human rights obligations.

The IOC should use its close working relationship with Senegal's government to call for action on the LGBT law before the games begin. Senegal can still reverse laws that expose its visitors, human rights defenders, journalists or lawyers to arbitrary arrest, harassment, violence, and discrimination.

One lasting legacy of the Youth Olympics that would be worth cheering is if the “teranga” welcome and safety can start with Senegal’s own citizens--no matter their sexual orientation or gender identity.

Larissa Kojoué is an LGBT rights researcher and Minky Worden is director of global initiatives, at Human Rights Watch.

World.title: Nigeria: Senator Questions Tinubu's Fresh Loan Request, Use of Previous Borrowings
World.content:
"The truth is that we have approved so much funds to be borrowed in the past... ," the senator said.

Anambra Central senator, Victor Umeh, has questioned the federal government's handling of previous loans, asking why contractors executing capital projects are still awaiting payment despite repeated borrowing approvals to fund projects.

Mr Umeh spoke on Channels Television's Politics Today on Tuesday in response to President Bola Tinubu's request for approval to borrow $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion.

He said the government has repeatedly framed borrowing as necessary to fund its budgets, yet it has failed to meet some of its financial obligations.



"The truth is that we have approved so much funds to be borrowed in the past, and on each occasion we've been told that this borrowing would be able to fund the budgets and these budgets have remained unfunded up till this day," he said.

Mr Umeh, who represents Anambra Central Senatorial District in the Nigerian Senate, noted that three budgets were running concurrently, while contractors handling capital projects had yet to receive payments.

"So if you borrow to finance a budget and you are not able to finance that budget, where has the money gone to? That is the question on the lips of everybody," he said.

He also said the latest borrowing request was likely to be approved, arguing that members of the ruling party would outnumber opposition lawmakers.

After reading the president's letter on Tuesday, Mr Akpabio referred the request to the Senate Committees on Local and Foreign Debts and Appropriations for further scrutiny. He directed the committees to report back within one week.

The senate is expected to take a decision on the request based on the recommendations of the committees.

But no loan request from the Tinubu administration has been rejected by the senate. All loan requests have had smooth sailing at the senate with minimal scrutiny.

Fresh borrowing

Mr Tinubu's request for fresh borrowings was contained in a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio during plenary on Tuesday.

The president's letter sought approval to process external loans worth $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643 under the 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.

He explained that the funds would finance projects in infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms.

According to the president, the projects were selected after technical and economic evaluations and are expected to contribute to the country's socio-economic development.

Close 

He said the borrowing was necessary to address Nigeria's infrastructure deficit and bridge the funding gap.

Mr Akpabio referred the request to the Senate committees on Local and Foreign Debts and Appropriations for consideration, directing them to report back within one week.

Previous borrowing approvals

The latest request follows other borrowing approvals granted by the National Assembly under the Tinubu administration.

In May, lawmakers approved a $516.3 million loan from Deutsche Bank AG for the construction of the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway.

The loan has a nine-year tenure, including a grace period of up to three years. Its interest rate is capped at the Secured Overnight Financing Rate plus 5.3 per cent annually. The facility is backed by insurance from the Islamic Corporation of Investment and Export Credit, the insurance arm of the Islamic Development Bank.

In March, the National Assembly approved a $6 billion external borrowing plan. The package included a $5 billion facility from First Abu Dhabi Bank to support the national budget and a $1 billion export finance facility arranged by Citibank for the rehabilitation of Tin Can Island Port and the Lagos Port Complex.

The latest request comes amid concerns over Nigeria's rising public debt and the cost of servicing government obligations.

The government maintains that borrowing is needed to finance infrastructure and other development projects. But Mr Umeh has questioned whether previous loans have translated into the funding of approved budgets and the payment of contractors.

World.title: Nigeria: Govt, Labour Congress Agree on Allowances, Arrears
World.content:
The Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, have reached an agreement on a series of measures to ease the economic difficulties facing workers, including a â¦70,000 transport intervention and the payment of 19 months' arrears owed health workers.

The resolutions were reached at a conciliation meeting held at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment yesterday, following an earlier meeting convened on October 22.

The meetings were organised to address concerns raised by the NLC over the rising cost of living, the implementation of the National Minimum Wage, petroleum pump prices, workers' welfare and outstanding allowances.

The agreement was signed on behalf of the federal government by Dr. Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi,

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Minister of Labour and Employment; Timi Yakubu, Director-General, Budget; and Dr. Garba Abdul S. U., Permanent Secretary (SWO), Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, while

NLC president, Joe Ajaero, and National Secretary, JNPSNC, Olowoyo Gbenga, stood for labour.

Under the agreement, the federal government will provide a transport intervention of N70,000 across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026.

The government also approved peculiar allowance with effect from May 1, 2026, while payment of the arrears is expected to begin in November and will be made in three equal monthly instalments.

In addition, the 19 months' outstanding allowances owed health workers is to be paid within three months, beginning in December 2026.

The meeting also agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted to commence work immediately.

However, the parties remained divided over the effective date for implementing the new minimum wage.

On the issue of tax relief for workers, the meeting resolved that the matter would be referred to the National Executive Council, as taxation is a statutory issue.

Meanwhile, the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security has submitted the list of beneficiaries and the cost implications of the proposed hazard allowance for agricultural officers to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission for verification.

The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template.

Similarly, the NSIWC is expected to complete an updated assessment of the cost implications of the proposed CONHESS adjustment within three weeks.

Close 

The assessment will enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to take a decision on the matter.

The federal government and NLC urged state and local governments to participate in the intervention process and implement the agreed measures.

The parties also agreed to reconvene after one month to review the level of implementation of the resolutions.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 28, 2026
World.content:
Ex-Wife of Zimbabwe's VP Chiwenga Freed After Seven-Year Trial Delay

Marry Mubaiwa, the former wife of Zimbabwean Vice-President Constantino Chiwenga, has been freed from remand after seven years on trial for allegedly attempting to impede his medical treatment in South Africa. A magistrate ruled that she had suffered mental, physical and financial prejudice due to delays in the proceedings after the State requested another postponement. Mubaiwa was accused of attempting to kill Chiwenga, while he was in hospital in Pretoria. The vice-president then went to China for four months of treatment. Her lawyer welcomed the decision but said it came too late, arguing that Mubaiwa's rights had been violated. Mubaiwa celebrated her release outside court, and said justice had been achieved and that she was proud of her lawyer. The State could still pursue a new trial.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Nigeria Inquiry Blames Overcrowding for 37 Detainee Deaths

An investigation into the deaths of 37 detainees in Nigeria's Niger State has found that severe overcrowding, poor ventilation, heat stress and dehydration caused acute respiratory failure. The detainees died in September while being held on suspicion of illegal mining. Investigators found that the mining sites were licensed. Fifty people had been held in a small cell without adequate water, sanitation or airflow, while officers allegedly ignored repeated calls for help. Adults and minors were detained together, and some detainees were held beyond lawful detention periods. Authorities have pledged to take legal action against those responsible, and the inquiry recommended compensation for bereaved families and survivors. The investigating committee also recommended $22,285 for each bereaved family and 10m naira for each survivor.

DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Surges Past 10,000 Cases

Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo have reportedly risen to 10,060, with 4,887 deaths since the outbreak was identified in mid-May. The outbreak involves the Bundibugyo virus, which has no approved vaccine or specific treatment, complicating efforts to contain its spread. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has described it as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. Kenya has reported nine infections, including two deaths. Nigeria also confirmed an infection in a Swiss woman who had visited Uganda. Clinical trials are underway to assess potential antiviral treatments and whether existing Ebola vaccines can protect against the strain. Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person. It can cause fever, diarrhea, and, in some cases, bleeding.

Egypt Orders Closure of Independent News Website Mada Masr

An Egyptian court has ordered the closure of independent news website Mada Masr after convicting its editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah, of operating without a licence. Attalah was briefly detained and released after the outlet paid a fine of $53,400. The court also ordered the confiscation of its equipment. Mada Masr, founded in 2013, is one of Egypt's few remaining independent news outlets. It is known for its investigations into corruption, human rights abuses and the powerful role of the military in the country. Mada Masr plans to appeal the ruling, which has drawn condemnation from international press freedom and human rights organisations. The case has intensified concerns about growing restrictions on independent journalism in Egypt, where the outlet has faced years of legal challenges.

Thousands Flee Ethiopia Conflict into Kenya

Approximately 36,000 people have crossed from Ethiopia into Kenya to escape fighting around the border town of Moyale, according to the UN Refugee Agency. The displaced, many of them women and children, urgently need food, clean water, shelter, sanitation and healthcare. Kenya's human rights commission estimates that around 40,000 people have sought refuge in the area, placing pressure on temporary shelters and host communities. The conflict, which spread across seven districts in southern Oromia, followed tensions over a flag dispute and the killing of a 13-year-old girl. Authorities and humanitarian organisations have been urged to coordinate assistance and protect those fleeing the violence.

Close 

Over 100 Reportedly Killed in Sudan Market Drone Strike

More than 100 civilians were reportedly killed in a drone strike on Tangong Market in Nyala, South Darfur, amid escalating attacks across Sudan. The strike also injured numerous people and set parts of the market ablaze, according to reports. Separately, a drone attack on an electricity substation in Omdurman disrupted power supplies across parts of Khartoum, Omdurman and El Gezira, affecting several drinking water stations. The attacks are part of a wider escalation of assaults on markets and civilian infrastructure, with the UN Human Rights Office recording more than 306 deaths from drone strikes in the first three weeks of October. Calls have been made for a humanitarian truce and a permanent ceasefire.

World.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Cases Top 10,000 in DR Congo Ebola Outbreak
World.content:
DR Congo has reported more than 10,000 Ebola cases and nearly 4,900 deaths. The outbreak involves a virus for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment, complicating efforts to contain its spread.

Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo reported that Ebola cases had risen to 10,060, with 4,887 deaths since the outbreak was identified in mid-May.

The outbreak involves the Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has described it as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history.

Where else have cases been reported?



Kenya has confirmed nine infections, including two deaths, after a patient traveled from DR Congo through Uganda to the capital, Nairobi.

Nigeria also confirmed an infection in a Swiss woman, the wife of a Swiss diplomat, who fell ill after visiting Uganda. Authorities are investigating where she contracted the virus. She was evacuated to Switzerland.

Why is the outbreak difficult to contain?

Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person. It can cause fever, diarrhea and, in some cases, bleeding.

Early symptoms can resemble malaria, potentially delaying isolation and treatment.

The lack of an approved vaccine or specific treatment against the Bundibugyo virus further complicates efforts to control the outbreak.

Are vaccines and treatments being tested?

Clinical trials of two antiviral treatment approaches have been underway since July.

Two further trials are investigating whether the Ervebo vaccine can protect against the Bundibugyo virus. The vaccine is currently approved and recommended only against Ebola virus, formerly known as Zaire ebolavirus.

Edited by: Wesley Rahn

World.title: Nigeria: Nigeria's First Methane Disclosure Raises Questions Over Repeated Figures, Missing Data
World.content:
An analysis of Nigeria's first public company-level greenhouse gas disclosure reveals repeated emissions figures, incomplete methane reporting, and inconsistencies in the list of companies that submitted data, raising questions about the reliability of the country's emissions baseline.

Nigeria has taken an important step towards improving transparency in its oil and gas sector by publishing company-level greenhouse gas emissions data for the first time.

The disclosure, released by the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI) in its 2023 oil and gas audit report, is expected to help citizens, regulators and investors understand how much pollution companies emit and whether the country is making progress towards its climate commitments.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

However, an independent review of the data has identified several issues that may undermine confidence in the disclosures if left unresolved.

Using the Emissions Monitoring and Accountability Tool (EMAT), an interactive platform that organises and compares emissions data published by NEITI, this analysis found repeated emissions figures across different companies, missing methane information, and inconsistencies in the number of companies reported as having submitted emissions data.

The findings do not suggest wrongdoing by any company. Rather, they highlight areas where Nigeria's emissions reporting framework could be strengthened to improve transparency, data quality and public confidence.

Repeated emissions figures

One of the most striking observations is that Chevron Nigeria Limited and the Shell Petroleum Development Company (SPDC) reported exactly the same methane emissions figures for 2022.

Both companies reported 173,578,759.2 kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent (COâe) and 6,943,150.368 kilograms of methane.

The values are identical across virtually all reported fields except for halons.

The figures appear in Appendix 12 of NEITI's 2022 and 2023 Oil and Gas Industry Reports, which contain Nigeria's first publicly available company-level greenhouse gas disclosures.

This became immediately visible because EMAT allows users to compare company data side by side, identical figures that may be difficult to notice in static tables.

The Chevron-SPDC entries are not isolated cases.

Another example is Aradel Holdings Plc, which reported exactly the same methane values in both 2022 and 2023: 133,522,033 kilograms COâe and 5,340,877 kilograms of methane.

Similarly, Network E&P reported 112 kilograms CO2e and 3.64 kilograms methane in both reporting years.

Repeated figures do not automatically mean the data are inaccurate. Companies with similar operations, shared production facilities, or common reporting boundaries could legitimately report similar emissions. However, exactly identical values reported to several decimal places warrant further verification against the original submissions.

Another case concerns Pillar Oil, where the same numerical value appears repeatedly across different greenhouse gases.

For example, in 2022, the value 1,610,170.7872 appears across several gases, including carbon monoxide, nitrous oxide, nitric oxide and sulphur dioxide. The same pattern appears in 2023 with 2,389,859.8050.

The published report does not explain why these different gases share identical values.

Missing methane information

The analysis also found that methane reporting is far from complete.

Of the 30 company-year records reviewed in Appendix 12, only 12 contain information across all three methane reporting fields.

The remaining 18 records contain missing information, and some of the omissions are difficult to interpret.

For instance, NAE reported 963,970 kilograms of methane in 2022 but recorded zero for the corresponding carbon dioxide equivalent.

In 2023, the company again reported methane emissions but left the carbon dioxide equivalent field blank.

Similarly, Chevron and Heirs Energies reported methane only as carbon dioxide equivalent in 2023 without providing the underlying methane mass.

Heirs Energies reported 217.4 million kilograms COâe, one of the highest methane-related figures in the dataset, yet the absence of the methane mass makes it impossible to independently verify the conversion.

In another case, Platform Petroleum appears on the reporting sheet, yet all of its methane fields are blank for both years.

The report provides no explanation of whether blank cells indicate that no emissions occurred, that no data were submitted, or that emissions were not calculated.

This distinction matters because a blank field is not the same as reporting zero emissions.

Inconsistencies in company reporting

The analysis also raises questions about how many companies actually submitted emissions data.

NEITI states that 15 out of 62 audited companies submitted greenhouse gas information, while 47 companies did not.

However, the appendix presents 15 companies on the reporting sheets, and 58 entries on the non-reporting sheet.

Taken together, the lists contain 73 entries, rather than the 62 companies referenced by NEITI.

Further review shows that Platform Petroleum appears on both the reporting and non-reporting lists.

In addition, some entries refer to joint venture interests or individual oil fields rather than clearly identifiable legal entities, making it difficult to determine exactly which companies reported emissions.

For example, the non-reporting list includes the NEPL (55 per cent) and Shoreline (45 per cent) interests in OML 30, while the reporting sheets separately list Esso's Erha and Usan fields.

A reconciled list that clearly distinguishes legal entities, operators, and production assets would significantly improve transparency.

Why this matters

Nigeria has committed to ending routine gas flaring by 2030 and reducing fugitive methane emissions from the oil and gas sector by 60 per cent by 2031.

Measuring progress towards these goals depends on reliable baseline data.

Because Appendix 12 represents Nigeria's first public company-level greenhouse gas disclosure, it effectively serves as the benchmark against which future emissions reductions will be measured. If the baseline contains gaps or inconsistencies, assessing future progress becomes more difficult.

Several practical improvements could strengthen future disclosures, including publishing the original reporting templates submitted by companies, clearly distinguishing between reported zeros and missing information, identifying the legal entity responsible for each reported asset, providing explanatory notes for unusual entries and maintaining a public log of corrections where errors are identified.

NEITI's response

NEITI was asked, through a Freedom of Information request, to respond to the issues identified in the analysis, including questions concerning the methodology used by companies, duplicate figures, missing or zero values, emissions intensity, the number of reporting companies, verification procedures, and the accessibility of the published data.

NEITI explained that under EITI Requirement 3.4, greenhouse gas reporting is encouraged rather than mandatory.

According to the agency, its reporting template requested companies to provide greenhouse gas emissions data and information on the methodology used, including emission factors, direct ground based sensors, satellite estimates, and other recognised approaches.

However, the template did not require companies to provide the Global Warming Potential values used, the specific IPCC or other scientific assessment from which those values were derived, or the time horizon used to convert emissions into COâ equivalents.

The agency said it did not convert, normalise, recalculate or adjust the data submitted by companies. The published figures, therefore, reflect the information provided by the companies.

NEITI also said there is currently no established national verification framework for these disclosures and that its role is focused on transparency, collection, and publication rather than on independent technical validation or methodological harmonisation.

Close 

Regarding repeated entries and identical figures identified in the analysis, NEITI acknowledged the observations and said it would conduct an internal review.

The agency said necessary adjustments had been reflected in the published data. It added that the original company templates and internal validation records were not intended for public disclosure.

NEITI said that any corrections or clarifications resulting from its internal review would be reflected in the published dataset. It acknowledged the observations and said it would take the feedback into account as it updates the published information.

What happens next?

NEITI's first company-level greenhouse gas disclosure represents an important starting point for public scrutiny of emissions in Nigeria's oil and gas sector.

The data provide journalists, researchers, civil society organisations and policymakers with information that was previously difficult to access at the company level.

At the same time, the analysis shows that the value of the disclosure will depend on improvements in the way emissions information is collected, standardised, verified and published.

The immediate priority should be to establish a clearer and more consistent reporting framework that enables users to distinguish between zero emissions, missing information and non-applicable data; understand the methodology behind reported figures; identify the companies and assets covered; and reproduce emissions-intensity calculations.

As Nigeria works towards its methane-reduction commitments, the quality of the underlying data will be as important as the targets themselves.

The first disclosure has opened the window of transparency. The next challenge is ensuring that the information available through that window is complete, consistent and reliable to support meaningful public accountability.

This report was supported by the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development(CJID) as part of the Deepening Methane Emissions Transparency Initiative-Stream II

The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) is looking at this as good news."

CHINA EXPERT WARNS BEIJING WANTS AMERICANS — NOT THE CCP — TO SPREAD ITS MESSAGE

Williams pointed to a recent Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) trip, claiming that more than a dozen high-ranking members of the organization traveled to China to "produce favorable coverage of China and its regime," as an example of the Chinese government taking advantage of the "vulnerable Democratic Party" to promote itself in the U.S.

DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS OF AMERICA NEED TO ACTUALLY MEET THE CHINA THEY CLAIM TO LOVE

They don't come out and condemn this extremism because they may even be afraid of repercussions from the DSA and DSA voters."

A recent Gallup poll found that 43% of Americans have a positive view of socialism, for the first time since 2010.

Williams pointed to the rise of socialism among Americans and the possibility that at least six new DSA-affiliated lawmakers could enter Congress in January as reasons for concern about the direction of the Democratic Party.

TOP DEM TORCHES SOCIALISTS TAKING OVER HIS PARTY: 'THEY'RE ANTI-AMERICAN'

Malik Williams, a Democratic candidate for a seat in Texas' state legislature, called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and for legalizing marijuana during a Tuesday rally for U.S. Senate nominee James Talarico in Lubbock, Texas.

"We can legalize and tax THC and cannabis. We're gonna abolish ICE, we're gonna tax the rich and we're going to get my friend, the next United States senator from the state of Texas, James Talarico, elected!" Williams exclaimed to raucous applause.

Talarico, a Democrat running in a historically Republican state, has shied away from making such direct calls to abolish ICE while on the campaign trail.

JAMES TALARICO TORCHES BIDEN BORDER POLICIES IN STUNNING ATTACK AD AS PROGRESSIVE TRIES TO FLIP TEXAS BLUE

Talarico's recent remarks, however, depart from past comments. In January, during a primary debate with Rep. Jasmine Crockett, D-Texas, Talarico said it was time to "tear down" ICE.

"ICE shot a mother in the face. ICE kidnapped a 5-year-old boy. ICE executed a man in broad daylight on our streets just this morning. It's time to tear down this secret police force and replace it with an agency that actually is going to focus on public safety," he said.

FOX NEWS POLL: MAJORITY SAYS IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT HAS CROSSED THE LINE

Talarico also advocated for "hauling in" agents in front of Congress to testify on actions taken during enforcement actions.

Abolishing ICE is an unpopular opinion among Republicans nationwide, with 67% strongly opposing the idea, according to a July YouGov/The Economist poll. The same poll found 48% of Americans overall supporting ICE's abolition.

TRUMP WON THIS RELIABLY RED STATE BY DOUBLE DIGITS. NOW A DEADLOCKED RACE IS BRINGING HIM BACK

Texas voters, meanwhile, have a moderately negative view of the agency as a whole. Only 42% of the state views the agency as very favorable or somewhat favorable, compared to 47% of the state viewing ICE as somewhat unfavorable or very unfavorable, according to a February poll from The Texas Politics Project.

In introducing Talarico on Tuesday, Williams also stumped for a wide number of policies popular with the rising crop of democratic socialists while appearing to bash President Donald Trump and Talarico's Republican opponent Ken Paxton.

DEMOCRATS CAN TAKE THE LEAD ON ONE OF THE NATION’S TOP ISSUES – DATA CENTERS

"When we have embarrassing loser representatives that support a fascist, racist, rapist, war criminal, I say we deserve better! When the backbone of Texas, our ranchers and farmers, tell us that they do not want data centers and then our politicians, as they love to do, they force it upon us without consent, I say we deserve better!" Williams exclaimed to fanfare.

World.title: Trump's unusual legal gambit against Biden-era deportation rule pays off at Supreme Court
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The Supreme Court, with no noted dissents, has allowed an agreement between Texas and the Department of Justice ending a Biden-era immigration rule to go into effect.

The Biden administration adopted the rule in 2024, formally establishing procedures for immigration judges to temporarily pause certain deportation proceedings through a practice known as "administrative closure," including when migrants were pursuing immigration relief through other federal proceedings. The Supreme Court's move leaves in place a lower court ruling eliminating that rule, stripping away a procedure that allowed certain deportation cases to be put on hold.

Texas sued the federal government in June, arguing that the rule was adopted without proper legal authority.

The Department of Justice agreed with Texas, asking the judge overseeing the case to vacate the rule and prevent similar rules from being adopted in the future.

JUDGE WHO APOLOGIZED TO ACCUSED WOULD-BE TRUMP ASSASSIN LIGHTS UP DOJ IN HUNTER BIDEN FBI CASE

Opponents accused Texas and the Justice Department of colluding to eliminate the Biden-era rule, arguing that the two sides worked together despite being on opposite sides of the lawsuit.

On the same day the DOJ made its request, District Judge Reed O’Connor, an appointee of President George W. Bush, granted it.

TRUMP-APPOINTED JUDGE SLAMS DOOR ON DOJ AS COURT LOSSES PILE UP DAYS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS'

In August, however, three cities with large immigrant populations — Baltimore, Maryland; New Haven, Connecticut; and Columbus, Ohio — joined with Centro Legal de la Raza, an immigrant legal advocacy group, in an effort to intervene in the case and defend the Biden-era rule on appeal.

The cities argued that eliminating the rule could lead to residents being deported, reducing their tax revenues and giving them legal standing to challenge the agreement. O’Connor rejected that argument.

MAMDANI BLASTS FEDS FOR WAGING 'CAMPAIGN OF VIOLENCE AND TERROR' AGAINST NYC'S IMMIGRANTS

On Oct. 9, the three cities and Centro Legal de la Raza asked the Supreme Court to temporarily block the lower court's judgment while their appeal proceeded, accusing Texas and the federal government of engaging in "egregious collusion" to eliminate the Biden-era rule.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Federal lawyers argued that the cities and their allies lacked legal standing to challenge the agreement because they had not demonstrated the concrete injury required for a federal court to consider their claims.

World.title: Mahjong is the new tailgate game taking over college football for women — and even at home with head coaches
World.content:
It's not only college football that has been the focus of my attention over the past three months. It is also the new American pastime that has taken over the kitchen tables of Southern women and is making its way into tailgates on a weekly basis across the country.

It's not a new recipe, or a new table design. Instead, it's Mahjong.

A simple walk to Tiger Stadium on the campus of Louisiana State University during the opening weekend of the college football season certainly changed my outlook on the newest trend sweeping the the nation, one expensive set at a time.

LSU IS READY TO PARTY: LANE KIFFIN’S DEBUT BRINGS FIREWORKS TO DEATH VALLEY AFTER REVIVAL-LIKE BUILDUP

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

It started a few months earlier when I was first introduced to this game, thanks to a friend we'll just call "Sam" for the sake of keeping the wild world of Mahjong between the groups that play it.

I wouldn’t want to give away any secrets, and I would learn over time that this was on the same level as men getting together for a night of poker.

The one thing I did not expect to see while making my way into a college football game was four ladies sitting at a table within a tailgate playing this game while others around them were immersed in your normal pregame activities that included alcohol.

Did I just stumble into a whole new world?

What was it about this game that led to women, and men, finding themselves sitting at a table covered in a 'mat' playing with 'tiles' that were labeled differently and a rule pamphlet that was also used to stir up the same table of "craks," "bams" and "dots."

Yes, those are different items used to play Mahjong, which I still have no idea how to play.

Also, it had unbeknownst to me, the game had made its way to other tailgates across college football that included Ole Miss, Alabama and Indiana. Yes, I know for a fact it's being played at other tailgates across this country, even if I haven’t been able to see it firsthand just yet.

And why were there so many different colors involved, or why did every playing surface look different?

Turns out, I was on the cusp of being astonished at how much this was actually being played around college athletics.

No, I'm not just talking about the wives of coaches who might get together on a weekly basis to discuss life while playing this game.

A 'tile' game at a tailgate: I had no idea what I was getting into

I still remember, three or so months ago, when "Sam" told me i'd be surprised to know how many men participate in Mahjong as a way to decompress. More on that later, with a coaching twist.

Now, for full disclosure, I have yet to learn the intricate details of this game, nor have I sat down to play a round.

And, I'm not just talking about a hand of "cards." These were elaborate get togethers, with women hosting game nights usually on a rotating basis, while some outings will take place in a local studio or room that could also be used as a storefront.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S JERRY JONES? TEXAS TECH BOOSTER CODY CAMPBELL DEMANDS RETURN ON INVESTMENT

This turned into an investigative mission to find out how deep this whole Mahjong craze goes.

It just so happens that there are actual stores that sell "tiles," playing "mats," sets that include marketing agreements with the 'Grateful Dead'.

Yes, the band.

How would I know about this?

I'm sure by now you are wondering why in the world a sports writer would become so fascinated by a game that is played a majority of the time by women. It probably helps that "Sam" is so into this game that I have been running at system overload for months now, even though I enjoy hearing about these game nights that can most certainly be competitive.

So, what did I do?

This particular weekend had me in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, not far from home. Besides my algorithm on social media steering me toward different social media pages thanks to my curiosity, I needed to see what all the fuss was about.

One google search later I found myself taking a detour on the way to Bryant-Denny Stadium to the Tuscaloosa Mahjong Parlor, just off the boulevard near the University of Alabama campus. The nerves I felt walking into this store were almost as intense as interviewing a head coach following a game, wondering where my brain would take me in the press conference setting.

Luckily, Heather Fikes welcomed me into her store that is also home to a business ran by her husband, Steve, like I was just another friend on a random Friday afternoon.

The colors were something I had never seen before, with boxes of "sets" stacked eloquently throughout the store. There were also 'mats', travel cases and just about anything else one could imagine needed for such a hobby.

The awkward introduction by myself as a sports reporter looking to learn more about this game turned into a 45-minute conversation on nearly every single item for sale in this beautiful area designed just to sell the game known as "Mahjong."

And no, sorry guys, this hobby is not cheap.

I had to do a double-take when I heard that the colorful "Grateful Dead" set that caught my eye would cost over $400, which I immediately texted "Sam" about in full disbelief.

Not because it wasn’t worth it, but more so at how shocked I was to learn how this game had taken on a life of itself over the years, at least in the deep south, and if I get caught in the storm it can be pricey. But don't worry, guys there's a cheaper way.

I also didn’t know you could have a Mahjong "hookup" that could get you the same looking game equipment, but for a much cheaper price on what I would normally call the 'black market'.

It was also Heather's husband, Steve, that reaffirmed my thoughts that this game was essentially the same as poker is for men. A way for women to gather within their communities to either let off some steam, congregate to share details of their life, or actually get into the competitive spirit.

Yes, this can also get confrontational at times, with words being traded and attitudes checked at either the tailgate tent or the door to each hosting house.

Turns out, this was more relevant than I had imagined, and not just outside the college football stadium in this case.

Bringing the competition home, after a long day around the football facility

For the sake of not giving other coaches ammunition to use within the group texts within the community of each conference, I decided to hold-off on actually naming the coaches who were drawn into this game by their wives or significant others.

Also, there were coaches from six different conferences polled, so it would be hard to pin down a specific school.

Thanks to "Sam" giving me the idea, along with a few sources with insider knowledge, I started randomly communicating with a number of college football head coaches to gauge whether they had been pulled into this lifestyle.

"Dude, who told you I was playing?" one Power Four head coach responded to my question on whether they had ever played. "I use it as a way to relax, but unfortunately this damn game is addicting. I get home from the office and play a few rounds with my girls and wife.

"But man, I thought we were competitive on the football field. This is a whole different animal. I did win a round last month, though."

Then, it was another message to an unsuspecting coach within another conference.

"Alright, who gave me up? That's some bulls—," another Power Four coach jokingly replied. "Yea Trey, I probably play at least once every two weeks. When you sit down at the table, and you have all of those darn tiles, I was lost for the first couple weeks.

"I've got my wife over here talking smack, and then I'm getting it from my sister. Then, if I come home and she has friends over, I like to get at least one game in before heading upstairs. Every now and then I'm allowed to sit for a few rounds until it's time for me to leave the room so they can continue their night. If you're going to play, you better lock in, because they don't cut you any slack after a few practice rounds."

For full transparency, I sent inquiries to ten different head coaches over a two-day period asking if they had ever played Mahjong.

Amy Grant is opening up about her relationship with her husband, Vince Gill, after over 20 years of marriage, saying he will always stand up for her.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 65-year-old singer touched on her marriage to Gill, noting that while he is "kind, kind, kind," he will do anything to protect her.

"He does have a toggle switch, and if somebody does something to throw that switch, he can respond so quickly," she said. "And so he can see the field, and he's got a quick mind. And he is not afraid to put somebody in their place or be protective. And so, yeah, I mean, I feel so loved by him."

In March, Gill told the story of the time he confronted host Don Imus while on his radio show, and called him out for talking negatively about him and Grant.

AMY GRANT'S EMOTIONAL ACCOUNT OF DOCTORS AND NURSES SINGING OUTSIDE DOLLY PARTON'S HOSPITAL ROOM

He told the "Naked Lunch" podcast that Imus started out as a fan of his, but after he married Grant the radio host changed his tune and would say things such as, "Vince Gill, lost the Baby Jesus, married that Christian girl." While on his radio show, Gill waited until Grant's name came up and then took his chance to stand up for his wife.

"I said, ‘Well, if you ever met her, you'd never say an unkind word about her,’" Gill said. "‘I'm going to shoot you straight.’ I said, ‘I really only came on this show for one reason.’ I said, ‘We're either going to talk this out, straighten this out,’ I said, 'or I'm going to crawl across this desk, and I'm going to kick your a--.'"

Gill noted that on his way home from the interview, he caught Imus on the air and heard him say, "I don't know why I was giving that guy so much crap. I love that guy," adding that the two of them stayed friends until Imus' death in December 2019.

When speaking with Fox News Digital, Grant described all the ways Gill has shown up for her throughout their marriage, including when she had unexpected open-heart surgery in 2020, and when she had a bike accident in 2022, which affected her short-term memory.

What if this is as good as it gets?' And he said, 'Amy, anything could happen to any of us. An accomplished musician could have a stroke and never use their left hand again.' And he said, 'We're just going to take each day and it's enough.'"

She explained that his message of staying together no matter what, is something he has always conveyed, "whether spoken or not."

World.title: James Talarico faces off against Trump in dueling Texas rallies in election’s final days
World.content:
LUBBOCK, Texas — On the day a sitting president landed in their town for the first time in 34 years, people waited for hours in lines that stretched for blocks in this reliably red city.

But this crowd on the east side of the city wasn’t waiting for President Donald Trump. They wanted to see Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico.

“We’re all closet Democrats,” said Dr. Tim Jones, 66, an emergency room physician, laughing and gesturing to a sea of people around him in line before Talarico’s evening rally. “There are a lot of people who are finally upset at gas prices, diesel prices, inflation, lies, the war, all of it. It’s the corruption, tearing down part of the White House to build this vanity ballroom. I mean, it’s just pathetic. So people finally are deciding, ‘We’ll get out to vote.’”

Trump gave out hats at his rally in Lubbock on Tuesday. Kent Nishimura / AFP via Getty

Less than 3 miles away, a similar scene unfolded for Trump, who held a rally at the expansive Lubbock Memorial Civic Center as he sought to boost the Republican Senate candidate, state Attorney General Ken Paxton. In a new move, Trump brought out his secretary of state, Marco Rubio, who won one of the biggest rounds of applause of everyone Trump introduced.

The dueling rallies and the fount of voter enthusiasm in this city of fewer than 300,000 underscored the high stakes in a Senate race that has drawn hundreds of millions of dollars in spending and presents the biggest threat in years to the Republican Party’s grip on bright-red Texas. With just a week until the election, Talarico has held a narrow lead in polling. His trip to Republican turf is a sign he is trying to win Republican crossover votes he needs for a victory.

At their rally Tuesday, Democrats urged supporters to seize a once-in-a-generation chance to flip a statewide seat after three decades of Republican control. They panned the economy, high gas prices and closures of rural hospitals. Talarico repeatedly cast Paxton as corrupt and as a Trump sycophant. He called out Elon Musk, saying the tech billionaire — who has significant business interests in Texas — is trying to buy his own personal senator after having thrown more than $150 million into Paxton’s candidacy.

Talarico in Lubbock yesterday. Democrats hope he can help them win a Senate seat that has been in Republican control for decades. Kaylee Greenlee / Reuters

“We have an affordability crisis because we have a corruption crisis. But we can change that in this election, in this state, in this race,” Talarico said. “We are running against the embodiment of this corrupt system. We are running against the most corrupt politician in Texas.”

Republicans, meanwhile, showcased Trump, who cast Talarico as a Second Amendment-hating, meat-loathing extremist out of touch with everyday Texans. Minutes into his speech, Trump referred to him derisively as “Talafreako.”

He mentioned Talarico’s disappearance from the campaign trail earlier in the month, when he said he had the flu. Trump said he believed the reason either was a “mental problem” or he was “sick to his stomach” from eating meat.

While there are far more Republicans in Texas than Democrats, Republican strategists say they view the contest as a real fight at a moment when Americans are feeling anger and dissatisfaction toward Washington. Paxton has also battled his own personal scandals, creating a drag on his numbers. And Texas Republicans are still beset by infighting after a nasty primary campaign, when Trump endorsed Paxton over Sen. John Cornyn, who had the backing of much of the party’s establishment.

Paxton has leaned on Trump’s advocacy. Trump has visited Texas three times this month, holding a pair of rallies Tuesday.

“Is it not awesome and amazing to be onstage with the greatest president in my lifetime?” Paxton told the crowd as Trump stood behind him and looked on.

Paxton said he spent the day with Trump, starting with a campaign stop in Corpus Christi. He said that as they were arriving in Lubbock, Trump told him he doesn’t normally do two rallies for any candidate: “He said, ‘I must really like you.’”

“Mr. President, I really like you, too,” Paxton said.

In a potential sign that Republicans were looking to attract a greater cross-section of voters, Trump handed Rubio a speaking part at the rally, as he did earlier in the day in Corpus Christi. Rubio has generally held higher approval ratings than others in the administration, including Trump. He is also a possible candidate in the 2028 presidential election.

Rubio, who had stayed clear of midterm campaign rallies until Tuesday, took the microphone and kept it brief.

“Our enemies are weaker. Our country is stronger, and our people are safer because Donald J. Trump is the president of the United States,” he said at the Lubbock rally.

Trump called Talarico an “anti-gun extremist” and said he and Paxton are the only things standing between Talarico’s becoming a senator.

“They’ve got a lot of bad people,” Trump said of Democrats. “That’s why we can’t afford to lose to some freak.”

But Talarico has embraced the moniker, calling out that he had never seen so many “Talafreakos” packed into one room.

“Lubbock is ready for change,” he declared to deafening screams. More than 4,000 people signed up to attend the event Tuesday night, according to his campaign. “They are scared. They are terrified. They see what we see — that we’re about to win this election.”
