World.title: Rail Baltic construction focused on Tallinn-Pärnu section
World.content:
Rail Baltic Estonia is currently focusing primarily on the construction of the Tallinn-Pärnu section, which should reach its final stages by the end of 2030.

According to the new schedule, the main construction work on the Tallinn-Pärnu section will reach its final stages by the end of 2030, while construction will begin from Pärnu to the Estonian-Latvian border. The Tallinn-Pärnu section is scheduled to enter service by the end of 2032. The entire Estonian section will be completed by the end of 2034.

Currently, attention is focused on the Tallinn-Pärnu section. The first test runs should also begin at the end of 2030.

"Testing, to put it simply, means making sure that all these different components work together and that they do so safely. We are currently planning to use the Ülemiste-Tootsi section as the first test section. Whether it will be shorter or longer will become clear as work progresses, but at least the initial goal is to begin testing the Ülemiste-Tootsi section at the end of 2030," said Rail Baltic Estonia CEO Anvar Salomets.

Almost half of the project's funding is taken up by so-called preparatory work.

Anvar Salomets. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

"Building one kilometer of embankment costs approximately €7 million to €8 million per kilometer. If we now consider that the entire construction budget is €3.5 billion and we are building 200 kilometers, that comes to around €17 million per kilometer, meaning that embankment construction accounts for slightly less than half of that. The rest is the track superstructure, technical equipment, traffic management and electrification," said Rail Baltic Estonia board member Lauri Ulm.

A large share of the funding is expected to come from the European Union's Connecting Europe Facility, but agreements on the European Union's new budget are still being negotiated. Both Salomets and Ulm believe that the funding will be secured and that construction of Rail Baltica will not be canceled.

"Of course, this is still based on assumptions at present, as the relevant agreements on the new European Union budget are still being negotiated. In setting Rail Baltic Estonia's schedule, we are proceeding on the assumption that the state will ensure funding. As for what gives the state this confidence, I think perhaps the most important argument is that CEF funding has been applied for so far and has also been received. So what is expected from the next financial period is comparable in terms of the amounts involved," Salomets said.

"I do not see a scenario in which Rail Baltica is not built as a realistic possibility. It is a strategic project. It has also survived several governments, including those that are currently in opposition. I do not believe the Rail Baltica project could be halted. The state may, under any government, review priorities, deadlines and funding, which could have an impact primarily on the final completion date. But I think the question of whether Rail Baltica will be built or not was settled long ago. It will be built; the question is when," Lauri Ulm added.

The government has said that postponing the completion of Rail Baltica will make it possible to use approximately €660 million more from the European Union's new budget period.

World.title: Reform MP and former minister Liina Kersna not running in Riigikogu election
World.content:
Reform Party MP Liina Kersna announced on Tuesday that she is taking a break from politics, after 12 years, which included a stint as a minister.

This means she will not be running at the Riigikogu election in March 2027.

"I have always regarded the role of a politician as an extraordinary but temporary privilege to influence Estonia's life and future," Kersna noted via social media.

"At the same time, I have been aware of and understood what privilege blindness means. Although voters have entrusted me with a mandate to represent them in parliament on three occasions, for a total of 12 years, I have never identified myself as a lifelong professional politician. However, I can confirm that throughout those 12 years, I have always done my very best in every situation, feeling and bearing responsibility to Estonia and my voters," Kersna continued in her post.

Kersna said the past few years have been tough as she feels responsible for political decisions that she has had little or no opportunity to influence, adding she may seek a career change in academia.

"Perhaps I really am too sensitive for the job of a politician, but the constant sense of guilt that has accompanied it has exhausted me considerably," Kersna explained.

"In order to avoid getting bitter, blind to privilege and settling into the role of a two-dimensional politician, I have decided to take a break from politics. I will not be running for parliament next spring. I want, at least for a while, to be responsible solely for my own decisions and choices and to live a life outside day-to-day politics. I will probably apply for a postdoctoral position at a foreign university if the opportunity arises," she went on.

At the same time, Kersna encouraged people in education who have a vision to run for the Riigikogu.

"So that the voices of people in education get heard strongly in our Riigikogu, so that the quality of discussions there becomes more substantive. So that there is more education, wisdom, empathy, honesty, willingness to work, determination, respect, and clarity of thought, expression and purpose in our politics. All these qualities are very closely linked to education and being educated. Education is and must remain the foundation of our society," Kersna concluded.

Kersna was education minister 2021-2022.

Election day is March 7, 2027.

World.title: Bank profits up 9% on year
World.content:
Banks in Estonia earned just under €540 million in profit in the first nine months of the year, around 9 percent more than during the same period in 2025.

Data from the Bank of Estonia shows that banks earned €539 million in profit between January and September, an increase of approximately €42 million.

"The increase in profits was driven by growth in the loan portfolio and a rise in Euribor that boosted the interest income of the banks. Profits also benefited from a reduction in loan write-downs, which means that the banks put a lower estimate than before on their possible loan losses. The administration costs of the banks, particularly their staff costs, increased a little in contrast," the banks economist, Kristjan Mäe, wrote.

However, he said, the interest income of the banks has been growing notably faster than their interest expenses.

"The interest rates on long-term corporate loans and housing loans climbed by 0.5 percentage point over the year, while the average cost of funding for the banks rose by only 0.1 percentage point," Mäe said.

World.title: Estonia has run out of asphalt, says Tallinn deputy mayor
World.content:
Estonia is experiencing a shortage of asphalt as factories in Sweden and Lithuania are currently not supplying it to the country, Deputy Mayor Kristjan Järvan (Isamaa) has said

"I have to start with some sad news. Namely, Estonia has run out of asphalt," Järvan said at a Tallinn city government press conference on Tuesday.

The official said Estonia usually imports bitumen from two sources in Sweden and Lithuania.

"And for reasons still unknown, the Swedish company decided not to bring any more. It said that the ship that arrived three weeks ago would be the last this year. The next one will come in the spring. The Lithuanian company was delighted, immediately raised its prices, and then its factory broke down. This means that asphalt plants in Estonia can no longer obtain bitumen," the deputy mayor said.

Kristjan Järvan Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"What this means nationally is that those construction companies that have their own asphalt plants probably have their own contracts covered and, as usual, any surplus asphalt is put on the open market," he added.

Tallinn is affected by the issue as the second supplementary budget set aside money for roadworks this autumn.

"Now both of the City of Tallinn's partners have said that, unfortunately, the market situation is such that asphalt is simply unavailable. And this means that we are in a situation where we can happily announce that we have asphalt for resurfacing Liivalaia. We have to take a positive view of what we have," Järvan said.

Asphalting work on Liivalaia began on Monday, and Tallinn will grant an additional two weeks for this work, the deputy mayor added.

"But this also means that we will not take the risk of milling up Viljandi maantee and Vabaõhumuuseumi tee to lay new asphalt there. We will still avoid a situation where we have streets dug up for the winter and no asphalt to put down in their place," Järvan said.

Transport Administration: Bitumen is still being supplied to Estonia

The Transport Administration's Mart Arusoo told ERR that bitumen supplies have not completely stopped.

"Bitumen is still being supplied to Estonia, although its price has probably risen due to turbulence in oil prices. There will indeed be no more new bitumen deliveries from Sweden this year, but bitumen is still available from Lithuania," he said.

The agency is recalculating prices, but Arusoo said no problems had arisen at its sites yet.

This article was updated to add comments from the Transport Administration.

World.title: Estonian defense forces uniform sold online, but unauthorized public wear illegal
World.content:
While wearing Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) uniforms and insignia without the right to do so is illegal, they can still be bought freely online.

Under the Defense Forces Service Act, using the EDF uniform or insignia without authorization is banned, and illegal use is a misdemeanor offense the EDF itself can pursue.

This is in order to avoid for instance "false flag" efforts during times of crises, as well as cases of "stolen valor".

The regulation is set by a defense minister directive outlining each uniform element. Items like a regular officer's beret, sold by the volunteer Defense League (Kaitseliit) shop, meet that description. Online stores also offer various camouflage items: a summer scout cap, raincoat, shirt, vests and more. Reports have come in of uniforms worn in public by those lacking the right to do so.

The Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) can also verify, in public, whether an individual wearing EDF uniform is entitled to do so. The EDF can open misdemeanor proceedings where there is reason to believe the rules have been breached — for example based on information received, or where there is reasonable doubt about whether the wearer has the right.

There is no direct legal ban on buying or selling such products in civilian circulation, for instance via military surplus outlets, however, while retailing or producing them does not require a Defense Ministry permit.

At the same time, if a uniform was directly issued by the EDF, which makes it state property, selling or otherwise transferring it without authorization is prohibited, and the buyer of a standard EDF uniform or insignia is still liable if they wear it in public, even if the seller lacked the permit to sell.

In 2021 the Defense Ministry clarified that civilian wearing of the uniform was being banned due to its being official clothing worn in the course of service duties, including in combat. The ministry said it was vital a person wearing uniform, or clothing resembling it who was not a member of the military did not get confused with a service member carrying out duties.

The EDF considered this particularly important during any crisis or unrest, where illegal wearing of such clothing could, either inadvertently or deliberately, create a false impression of the actions of the EDF, the Defense League or the state. The concern also echoes what is often called "stolen valor" in the U.S. — the false impression created by wearing military uniform without entitlement.

World.title: Patient healthcare compensation claims on the rise, but many rejected
World.content:
Claims against healthcare providers have grown steadily in the nearly two years since the patient insurance system came into force, and so has the number of rejections.

"Looking at recent developments, the positive thing is that healthcare providers have adapted to the new regulation and everyone who must have patient insurance has signed a contract," Kairi Ruhno, service manager at the Health Board's (Terviseamet) healthcare services department, said.

Statistics also show patients are increasingly aware of patient insurance and are better able to use it.

"Whereas the previous healthcare quality expert committee got around 200 applications a year, in the first full year of the patient insurance system more than 400 compensation claims were filed with insurers. In the first ten months of this year, more than 660 applications have already been submitted," Ruhno said.

Ruhno stressed it is important to understand that not every treatment outcome that falls short of expectations automatically means a medical error occurred or an insurance claim can or should be made; simply that patients must have a clear and workable route to claim compensation for actual harm.

"Going forward, we see the greatest need for development in raising awareness. On the one hand it is important that healthcare providers understand the broader purpose of patient safety and the insurance system. On the other, patients' awareness of their rights and of how patient insurance works must increase, including which cases constitute an insured event and which do not," Ruhno went on.

Insurance market opening up

When liability insurance was introduced in Estonia over 20 years ago, in November 2004, there was only one option on the market, from insurers PZU. Now a PZU product and a new provider have been added, while market participants believe new insurers and products will ease the burden on healthcare providers and offer more flexible choices.

Liisi Murde-Parvell, a patient insurance expert at broker IIZI, said significant shifts have taken place, with Lloyd's entering alongside PZU and its terms now fully brought into line with the law. The arrival of new providers has ended PZU's monopoly, and brought prices down, though the market will take time to settle. "Pricing is difficult at the moment. The healthcare provider liability insurance product is entirely new, and there is very little earlier statistics to rely on. It is more other countries' practice," Murde-Parvell said.

Although premiums in the early years were high because of how the products were structured, she is optimistic. "This year the situation is already certainly considerably better and I believe next year it will be better still. There will probably be more new entrants by next year," Murde-Parvell said.

Because the statutory liability period is ten years, full statistics and clarity will take time to accumulate. "Complete knowledge of how many claims come and how many of them are actually justified will develop over years. And once it has developed, pricing will certainly be more transparent and easier to understand, and perhaps fairer too," she said.

Statistics: 75 percent of claims rejected

The Health Board publishes real-time statistics on its website on the application of patient insurance and the processing of claims.

From November 1, 2024 to October 27, 2026, a total of 1,148 compensation claims were submitted to insurers. Completed proceedings account for three-quarters: 863 claims have been reviewed, or 75.2 percent of all applications, while 285, or 24.8 percent, are still in progress.

Most claims are rejected. Of the 863 processed, 226 qualified as insured events, or 26.2 percent, while 637, or 73.8 percent, were not upheld. Across all claims submitted, upheld cases account for 19.7 percent and rejected ones 55.5 percent.

As many as 84.16 percent of compensated cases stem from direct medical error in diagnosis or treatment. Second among compensated cases are healthcare-associated infections at 9.5 percent, and wrong or unsuitable medicine or wrong dose at about 4.5 percent.

Nearly 59 percent of compensated cases fall into the middle damage category. Serious, irreversible or life-threatening harm accounts for about a third, 32.2 percent, of recognized claims. Minor harm accounts for under a tenth, 9.5 percent, suggesting claims are often not filed for lighter consequences or fall below the statutory compensation threshold.

A total of €1,077,228 has been paid out to patients. The average per compensated case is €5,886, and the largest single payout is €32,652.

The most claims were filed against emergency medicine departments, 180, which also produced the highest absolute number of insured events, 46. Family medicine is second by number of claims at 159, but its approval rate is exceptionally low: of 121 completed proceedings, only 12, or 9.9 percent, were recognized as insured events.

In orthopaedics, 34.6 percent, general surgery, 35.1 percent, obstetrics, 29.8 percent, and maxillofacial surgery, 31.6 percent, the approval rate remains steadily around a third.

More claims in 2026

As of 11 months into 2026, 664 compensation claims have been filed with insurers, exceeding the whole of 2025, 469 claims, by more than 41 percent.

Where only 29 claims, 6.2 percent, were unresolved in 2025, 256, or 38.55 percent of all applications, are in proceedings in 2026 — pointing to a multiplied workload for processors and to the fact that the speed of decisions cannot keep pace with the inflow.

Where family medicine was second by number of claims in 2025 with 56, in 2026 it has risen to first with 103. At the same time its approval rate has remained marginal.

The Health Insurance Fund (Tervisekassa) paid healthcare providers €6 million in 2025 to cover patient insurance costs, and €6 million is planned for 2026. Providers must add the same amount again from their own budgets each year, because the Health Insurance Fund covers up to 50 percent of the premium. That made last year's total insurance cost to the Estonian healthcare system an estimated €12 million.

World.title: Minister replaces Eesti 200 defector on Integration Foundation board
World.content:
Jašin was formerly a member of the coalition Eesti 200 party, but left it earlier this month to join the Social Democrats (SDE), who are in opposition.

According to the minister's directive, the proposal to recall Jašin, once touted as a possible future party leader, was made by Eesti 200 itself on October 15, the day after he left the party.

The party's letter is classified in the ministry's document register as being for internal use only, under a provision covering information containing personal data whose disclosure could significantly harm the data subject's privacy.

The replacement is not in itself unexpected: the foundation's board traditionally includes representatives of the relevant ministries, parties represented at the Riigikogu, and experts in the field, and Jašin had been from the second of these categories.

Via the same directive, Purga appointed Nikita Lumijõe to the same position for a three-year term. Lumijõe has been an Eesti 200 member since 2018 and works as an adviser to Education Minister Kristina Kallas, who is also Eesti 200's leader. SDE was in office with Reform and Eesti 200 until spring last year and has a representative on the XXX board in Henri Kaselo, formerly Kohtla-Järve's mayor.

Jašin was a member of Eesti 200 from November 19, 2018 until October 2, 2026, and joined SDE on October 14. Before the switch he had been discussed as a possible new leader of Eesti 200, and is a former Tallinn deputy mayor.

The Integration Foundation (Integratsiooni Sihtasutus) supports the development of an integrated and cohesive society as a competence center in the field, with both foreign residents of Estonia and Estonians living outside the country being in its target groups, the organization says on its website.

World.title: Isamaa lawyer: No ruling in criminal case to come before Riigikogu election
World.content:
A criminal case against opposition party Isamaa will not reach a court ruling before the March 2027 Riigikogu elections, the party's lawyer has said.

Jaanus Tehver, Isamaa's lawyer, said prosecutors are yet to decide whether to bring charges, but will do so soon.

The suspicions date to last November, when prosecutors notified Isamaa of a prohibited donation totaling €110,234 allegedly accepted between November 2020 and April 2024.

Tehver said he will file no further requests with the Prosecutor's Office and is waiting for the formal charges, which he expects given the prosecution's stated position since spring.

The Prosecutor's Office for its part said the defense has been given until next Monday to examine the evidence materials, after which prosecutors will decide how to proceed.

According to the suspicions, prohibited donations — mainly advertising services — totaling approximately €330,000 were made to Isamaa, of which the party allegedly accepted €110,234. Isamaa and all other suspects deny the allegations.

Tehver said that, purely in terms of timing, no ruling can now be issued ahead of the elections — at best, a preliminary hearing could be held, he added.

"This means that, until the Riigikogu elections, the best that can be said is that charges have been brought before the court and that the Isamaa party is accused of this or that crime," he said. "Unfortunately, we will not know the court's position on what it thinks of these charges before the elections. Regrettable, but what can you do."

"For me, the Prosecutor's Office's position is clear, and in a situation where they have made the decision that I believe they have made, there is no point in my submitting any further requests," Tehver added.

Isamaa's hairman Urmas Reinsalu said it was in the party's interest for clarity to come quickly, but said that the proceedings had not been an issue when recruiting candidates or preparing the election campaign. "Perhaps Isamaa's opponents are more interested in that. But in my opinion, this stirring up of dust already received a public verdict at the end of last year, when we presented our expert analyses and assessments," Reinsalu said.

Reinsalu added cases like this can work the other way too and exert a sort of rallying-round-the-flag effect, as supporters come to see the charges as unfounded – while charges would attract attention, this would not be enough to distract from offering a political alternative to the Reform Party-led government, he said.

Prosecutor's Office spokesperson Kauri Sinkevicius said that if charges are brought and the case goes to court, the court will take over responsibility for the proceedings, and can take circumstances such as the upcoming elections into account when scheduling hearings.

Background:

Last November the Prosecutor's Office notified Isamaa that it was suspected of accepting a large-scale prohibited donation totaling €110,234 between November 2020 and April 2024. Tehver has previously stated the party is suspected of having benefited from coordinated activity by major donor Parvel Pruunsild, Tõnis Palts and the nonprofit MTÜ Isamaalised, who provided advertising and analysis services, with the costs covered by MTÜ Isamaalised. Under the Political Parties Act, companies and nonprofits are prohibited from financing party activities or providing free benefits with monetary value.

World.title: Iraq seeks cooperation with Russia in oil, gas industries
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Deputy Minister of Oil for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber emphasized on Tuesday Iraq’s interest in developing cooperation with Russia in the oil and gas sectors.

Saber’s remarks took place during his meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of their participation in the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF), held between October 25 and 27 in Moscow.

According to Saber, Iraq seeks to leverage Russia’s advanced expertise and foster partnerships and joint ventures that optimally utilize natural resources and advance the energy sector.

Saber conveyed the Iraqi president’s and the prime minister’s greetings to Putin, emphasizing their commitment to promoting bilateral relations and broadening the scope of cooperation to serve the interests of the two countries.

The GECF addressed developments in the world’s gas markets and approaches to enhance cooperation among producing countries.

The forum also discussed strategies to attract investments and develop infrastructure to guarantee supply security and meet the growing demand for energy throughout the world.

World.title: Iraqi PM arrives in Damascus for an official visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi arrived in Damascus on Wednesday for an official visit to Syria, where he will meet President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

The trip marks the first high-profile visit by an Iraqi premier to Syria since the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024 and the establishment of al-Sharaa’s administration.

Al-Zaidi is accompanied by a high-level ministerial delegation aiming to strengthen economic, political, and security connections with the neighboring country.

The Iraqi prime minister’s agenda in Syria includes expanding commercial partnerships in trade, transport, agriculture, and water.

The two leaders are expected to focus on expanding oil export routes, following a memorandum of understanding signed earlier to revive a pipeline linking Iraq’s oil output to the port of Baniyas on the Mediterranean.

The discussions are expected to cover tightening control over shared borders and aligning counter-terrorism efforts. Al-Sharaa noted ahead of the visit that the border is secure and that intelligence and military coordination are actively underway.

The two leaders’ meeting is the second after they met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York last month.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Syria signals a broader strategy by both nations to transition neighborhood ties into sustainable developmental and security frameworks.

World.title: Trump tamed after US midterms? Europe doubts it
World.content:
Brussels – President Donald Trump may be facing a political pounding at the US midterm elections next month — but in Europe expectations are low that a big Democrat win would change much.

From the battlefields of Ukraine to the boardrooms of Europe, Trump has sent multiple shockwaves across the continent since returning to power last year.

During a head-spinning 22 months, the mercurial leader has turned spectacularly on Kyiv, imposed tariffs on allies and threatened to take Greenland.

Ahead of the November 3 polls it looks like American voters could punish Trump’s Republican party and hand control of one or both of the US House of Representatives or Senate to the Democrats.

But while the hope may be that Trump could be reined in by a hostile Congress, multiple officials at the EU and NATO told AFP they doubt a big loss would muzzle him on the international stage.

“We don’t think the unpredictability is going to change,” said one senior EU diplomat.

Publicly the European Union is keeping its cards close to its chest.

“We will not comment on any elections in the EU or abroad. Let’s wait for those and we’ll see where it goes,” said European Commission spokeswoman Paula Pinho.

Behind closed doors as well, officials say that the midterms are not featuring much in the bloc’s internal discussions.

“I suspect because a) it is difficult to really predict the result, b) one wouldn’t want to get too high hopes for change and c) not sure how much even a Democratic wave would impact foreign policy issues,” said a second senior EU diplomat.

– Ukraine, tariffs –

Ahead of the midterms, Trump has rattled Europe by yet again lashing out at Ukraine and cosying up to Russia as Washington has renewed its push to end the fighting.

While a Democrat win could usher in a more vocal pro-Kyiv majority in Congress, the EU is not expecting US support for Ukraine to ramp up again.

Officials in Brussels say they are focused on plugging a 70-billion-euro hole in Kyiv’s finances next year.

And while they’re pushing other countries like Britain, Canada and Japan to do more, they are certainly not counting on the United States.

Meanwhile, there is equally little optimism for any major reversal on the tariffs Trump has slapped on Europe.

Diplomats and officials point out that it took months to get Democrat President Joe Biden to roll back tariffs on EU steel after Trump’s first term — and even then limitations remained.

In a recent poll from the Washington-based Council on Foreign Relations, only one quarter of Americans backed removing all the tariffs on the EU.

– US forces in Europe? –

At NATO the story is much the same.

European allies are nervously waiting for the results of a Pentagon review of US forces on the continent that looks set to be unveiled in December.

The widespread expectation is that it will see the United States scale back its deployments, although the hope is the cuts will not be too severe.

Multiple diplomats at NATO said they didn’t envision the midterms having an impact on the review.

While a changed Congress could see US lawmakers more outspoken in support of the alliance, the direction of travel is already set with Europe stepping up efforts to take more responsibility for its defence.

“Whatever the outcome, we’ll keep going,” said one European diplomat.

– Trump unleashed? –

There is also a nagging fear that things could get worse after the midterms.

If Republicans cling on it could embolden Trump, meanwhile if they lose, he could seek to distract from his woes at home by stirring up things abroad.

“We have a history in America of presidents who get in trouble domestically turning more to the international stage,” said Bruce Stokes, a visiting fellow at the German Marshall Fund think tank.

From an escalation in the Iran war to a more concerted push on Ukraine, there are numerous ways the White House can keep worrying Europe.

“Trump has demonstrated they can’t stand not to be the centre of attention,” said Stokes.

“If that means he needs to do more on the world stage, positively or negatively, that may be what ends up happening.”

World.title: Anthropic’s record IPO faces some big questions
World.content:
San Francisco – No startup has ever grown so fast. In five years, Anthropic has become an AI giant valued at $1 trillion, and it is now aiming for a record-breaking stock market debut.

But it faces three threats: rivals that are catching up, prices that are collapsing, and bills that keep climbing.

Anthropic spells out the risks in its Wall Street prospectus, published Monday.

The first is commoditization: “the degree of differentiation among advanced AI models may narrow,” the company warns.

The San Francisco-based firm also says “substantially all of our revenue” comes from its AI tools. Unlike Google or Meta, it has no advertising empire to fall back on if business takes a hit, and no cloud business like Microsoft’s or SpaceX’s.

Investors have already grown nervous. In mid-August, shareholders were floating a valuation of $2 trillion.

But quarter-on-quarter growth slowed from 145 percent in the second quarter to 45 percent in the third, cooling expectations to around $1.5 trillion.

– Cheap and open –

So-called open AI models, which anyone can download and modify, are close behind closed models such as Claude or ChatGPT, which are available only through their owners’ paid services.

The performance of open models trails by only about four months on average, according to research institute Epoch AI.

They include Kimi K3.1 Pro from Chinese company Moonshot, which costs half as much as Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic’s current flagship.

And among paid models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google, none has stayed on top for long.

Anthropic also acknowledges it is holding itself back: its safety measures “could slow our capability gains relative to competitors that do not adopt similar constraints.”

Still, the company says each new version of Claude has boosted sales. More than 80 percent of its revenue last quarter came from models less than six months old.

– Prices collapsing –

When products look alike, prices fall. According to Morningstar, the price of having AI process the same amount of text, at the same level of performance, has dropped 97 percent, from $17 at the end of 2024 to 50 cents today.

Anthropic itself cut the price of Claude Opus by 20 percent in September, and OpenAI cut the price of one of its flagship models by a factor of five in July.

The effect is already visible at Vercel, a developer platform that routes requests across AI models.

In August, more than half of the text it handled was processed by open models, up from 13 percent in April.

Even so, Anthropic still captured nearly two-thirds of spending on the platform.

Even a 90 percent price cut would not shrink total spending on AI as long as usage keeps growing at its current pace, said Malik Ahmed Khan, a senior equity analyst at Morningstar.

– ‘Triple whammy’ –

Anthropic’s costs, by contrast, are largely locked in. To stay ahead, each new Claude model has to be bigger than the last, trained on more data using more computing power.

Since late 2025, the company has committed to paying at least $417 billion to rent chips and servers.

That is nearly 13 years of sales at its first-half 2026 pace, and the total could nearly double if cancellable or planned contracts are included.

These commitments are due no matter the state of its business, Anthropic warns.

The bet involves the entire industry: Google and Amazon are at once Anthropic’s shareholders, its suppliers and its resellers.

If AI turns out to be less profitable than expected, the International Monetary Fund fears a “triple whammy” from these intertwined investments: falling stock prices, debts that are harder to repay, and promised revenue that never materializes.

The independent research firm New Constructs called the listing “an unprecedented test of investor gullibility.”

To pay these bills, Anthropic is counting on money from the stock market, which is not unlimited.

SpaceX, Elon Musk’s rocket and AI company, raised record sums there in June, while Google and Meta, which are pouring fortunes into data centers, are also seeking fresh capital.

OpenAI, whose chief Sam Altman called a listing “ill-advised” this year, has chosen to wait until 2027, giving it time to see how Wall Street treats its big rival.

World.title: Tech stocks soar as SK hynix adds to rising AI confidence
World.content:
Hong Kong – Technology firms surged across Asia on Wednesday after blockbuster earnings from chip giant SK hynix helped boost optimism in the AI trade ahead of results from Wall Street titans Microsoft and Alphabet.

Oil prices rose as investors kept tabs on Israel’s election results, which could determine the future of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s war against Iran.

After a slight wobble this month in the tech realm caused by fresh worries about huge investment spending, profitability and company finances, AI-linked firms were back on the front foot.

SK hynix, which has been at the forefront of the chip boom, said Wednesday that third-quarter operating profit soared 632 percent to US$62.8 billion thanks to explosive demand for its advanced semiconductors.

The firm said it had now posted record revenue and operating profit for six straight quarters.

“While Wall Street argues over whether the AI arms race can keep financing itself, SK hynix has just reminded the market that somebody on the other side of all that capex is receiving the cheque,” wrote Stephen Innes at SPI Asset Management.

The reading added to optimism surrounding the sector after Anthropic, the mother company for Claude AI, said Monday in its IPO filing that first-half revenue surged about 1,300 percent and flagged heavy capital spending ahead.

That was followed Tuesday by Broadcom’s announcing jointly with Citi, Blackstone and Morgan Stanley a US$63 billion financing structure to build new capacity for Anthropic.

“The AI trade has undoubtedly received a healthy shot in the arm from Anthropic’s… filing, with its incredible revenue growth, improving compute economics and substantial commitments to future infrastructure investment reinforcing the longer-term opportunity across the AI supply chain,” said Pepperstone’s Chris Weston.

Shares in SK hynix soared almost nine percent Wednesday and South Korean rival Samsung, which reports Thursday, added more than eight percent. That pushed Seoul’s Kospi index up more than six percent.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 climbed more than one percent, with chipmaker Kioxia soaring more than 10 percent, while Advantest gained three percent and Tokyo Electron four percent.

Taipei was pulled sharply higher thanks to chipmaker TSMC’s strong performance, while Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore and Wellington were also well up.

The gains tracked advances in New York, where the Nasdaq added more than one percent.

Microsoft and Alphabet are due to report later in the day, while Amazon, Apple and Intel follow on Thursday.

However, traders are also awaiting the Federal Reserve’s policy decision Wednesday.

While it is expected to stand pat after last month’s hike, its post-meeting statement and comments from boss Kevin Warsh will be pored over for clues about its future plans. Markets expect a hike in December.

Crude prices jumped more than one percent as results from Israel’s general election rolled in.

While polls appeared to show Netanyahu’s governing Likud and the opposition neck and neck, the prime minister vowed to form a new coalition, adding that he could work with US President Donald Trump to eliminate the “existential threat” posed by Iran.

His comments came after opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot said the country had chosen change and that he would seek to form a new administration.

World.title: Billionaire Ambani’s Jio to debut after record India IPO
World.content:
Mumbai – India’s Jio Platforms makes its stock market debut on Wednesday after a record-breaking IPO, capping billionaire owner Mukesh Ambani’s years-long drive to diversify his conglomerate beyond oil refining.

Jio Platforms, which houses the country’s biggest wireless operator and is the digital services arm of Ambani’s Reliance Industries, raised about $3.2 billion at 1,119 rupees ($11.76) per share in India’s biggest-ever initial public offering.

The listing, one of the year’s most anticipated, attracted robust demand last week, with investors applying for more than 22 times the shares on offer.

In the run-up to its Mumbai debut, grey market platforms showed a premium of around 22 percent for Jio shares, although experts caution that such unofficial indicators can be unreliable predictors of early trading.

Nevertheless, most analysts expect decent listing gains despite a weak year for Indian equities.

Jio has a “proven execution record” and will see its cash generation “strengthening as the 5G investment cycle winds down”, analysts at financial services firm Emkay Global said in a note, calling the company “the digital engine of India”.

Launched a decade ago, Jio’s wireless service disrupted the market with steep discounts, rapidly winning customers from rivals Bharti Airtel and Vodafone.

With over 530 million subscribers, the firm currently makes most of its money from telecoms, but has expanded in recent years into digital services and artificial intelligence.

Experts say Jio is key to Reliance’s strategy to move beyond oil and underpins its future technology ambitions.

Local media have reported how it is considering a low Earth orbit satellite constellation to provide internet services from space — a venture that would see it compete with Musk’s Starlink, which has been trying for years to launch in India.

Musk accused unnamed Indian “oligarchs” this month of preventing Starlink’s rollout in the country, and referred to the Reliance chairman as “Prime Minister Ambani” and the “real boss of India”.

Reliance responded by noting that it had never “feared competition” and welcomed offerings from rivals in satellite communications, including Starlink.

World.title: US Fed expected to hold rates steady ahead of key midterm elections
World.content:
Washington – The US Federal Reserve will announce a decision on setting interest rates on Wednesday, with markets expecting the central bank to hold steady days ahead of crucial midterm elections, despite surging inflation.

The Fed will announce the decision of the 12 voting members of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) at 2:00 pm local time (1800 GMT) on Wednesday, with a press conference by Chairman Kevin Warsh to follow.

Policymakers voted at their last meeting in September to raise interest rates to a range between 3.75 and 4.00 percent — the first hike in three years — to tackle inflation.

The Fed has missed its long-term two-percent target for inflation for more than five years, with households and businesses battered by sustained price increases.

US President Donald Trump’s war on Iran, launched in late February, has sent energy prices skyrocketing and fueled domestic inflation, alongside his wide-ranging tariff policies.

Prices have also been driven by an investment boom in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and the build-out of huge data centers to support it.

The Fed’s decision comes six days ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party seeks to wrest control of both houses of Congress from Trump’s Republicans.

Trump’s handling of the economy has been a key issue throughout the campaign, with working-class households across the country struggling to make ends meet despite largely stable overall economic growth.

US consumer inflation came in hotter than expected in September, clocking in at 3.7 percent, edging back towards a three-year high established in May.

Still, key policymakers at the Fed — including Chair Warsh — have signaled that they did not see an urgency to raise rates again immediately.

Speaking in Bangkok earlier this month, Warsh said that US economic conditions had “broadly conformed” to policymakers’ expectations, fueling speculation that the Fed may pause at the October meeting.

Wendy Edelberg, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told AFP that all the signs pointed to a hold.

“I would be very surprised if they raised interest rates just for starters so close to the election, but also given that so many of them have signaled that they’re happy for a pause,” she said.

– ‘Don’t understand the logic’ –

For Edelberg, however, a decision to hold after raising rates in September would potentially be contradictory, given the labor market — the Fed’s other mandate — has been largely stable.

“In terms of the economics of it, I don’t totally understand the logic,” she said.

“If there was a reason to raise interest rates at the last meeting, I think that there’s just as compelling of an economic reason to raise interest rates at this meeting.”

The Fed has a dual mandate to maintain maximum employment while keeping inflation to its long-term target.

It achieves this goal largely using one tool: the economy’s key interest rate. Raising rates tends to cool inflation but can also dampen economic activity; lowering them can spur economic activity but also fuel inflation.

The US unemployment rate has been largely stable around 4.2 percent over the last year, with job growth mostly in positive territory — albeit driven by a few sectors.

Loretta Mester, former head of the Cleveland Fed, agreed that current economic conditions gave policymakers an opportunity to press ahead with rate hikes now.

“Take advantage of the situation you’re in today, which is pretty clear evidence of stability in the labor market, and clear evidence that inflation is still too high,” she said.

“Move, given that you know you want to be moving more, take the advantage of this meeting.”

Mester, who took part in FOMC meetings during her tenure at the Fed, insisted that the committee did not “take into account any kind of political issues” when it debated monetary policy.

– Attacks on Fed –

Still, Trump has loomed large over the Fed since he returned to power last year.

In his second term, he has led an unprecedented assault on the Fed’s independence, pursuing criminal charges against Warsh’s predecessor Jay Powell and attempting to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook as he demanded lower interest rates.

While the probe against Powell was dropped to smooth the way for Warsh’s Senate confirmation, the White House has recently renewed its drive to fire Cook — despite a Supreme Court decision that batted back an earlier attempt.

“I don’t think it’s going to stop because I think it’s in the nature of this administration to continue those attacks,” said Mester.

World.title: Meta, Snap head to trial in another case about social media’s harms
World.content:
San Francisco – Jury selection is expected to begin on Wednesday in Los Angeles for another landmark trial about the alleged harms of social media on young users, with Meta and, for the first time, Snap as defendants.

Thousands of lawsuits have been filed in recent years in local, state and federal courtrooms across the country with various claims about alleged harms to children and teenagers caused by social media companies.

The cases — the first of which went to trial earlier this year in Los Angeles — have taken twists and turns.

Meta and YouTube lost the first so-called bellwether case earlier this year, when a jury found them collectively liable for harming a young user known by the initials KGM, and ordered the tech companies to pay a combined $6 million penalty.

Meta said at the time that they “respectfully disagree” with the verdict.

Snap and TikTok settled with KGM ahead of that trial.

Months later, Snap, TikTok and YouTube settled another case that was set to go to trial in August; that plaintiff, known as RKC, then withdrew their remaining claims against Meta, allowing the Instagram and Facebook maker to avoid trial without a settlement.

TikTok and YouTube were previously named as defendants in the new case but both companies reached settlement agreements with the plaintiffs, known by their initials SJ and KDB, before the start of the trial, their lawyers said.

Meta reached a settlement agreement with one of the plaintiffs, SJ, but not KDB, according to their lawyers.

A California state judge consolidated both cases into a single trial.

If no additional settlements are reached before opening statements kick off on November 4, the new trial will move forward with both Meta and Snap as defendants.

Star witnesses are expected to testify beginning mid-November including Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Instagram chief Adam Mosseri, and Snap CEO Evan Spiegel.

Earlier this month, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion in a case where the company was found liable for deceiving users in the state about how their data was used in a case related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

A New Mexico jury previously found the social media giant liable for harms to children, leading to a combined penalty of $942 million.

In August, Meta agreed to pay more than $18 billion in penalties, in addition to making changes to Instagram and Facebook for teens, when it settled with 52 attorneys general several days into a trial held in California.

Part of that settlement hinged on YouTube and TikTok making similar changes to their own products, such as limiting daily screentime.

– ‘Addictive and problematic’ –

As regulators around the world grapple with reining in, or even banning, social media use for teens, American lawsuits have focused on allegations of addictive design and deceptive practices by social media companies.

Next month, lawyers for the two plaintiffs in Los Angeles — SJ and KDB — will argue that their clients were exposed to “addictive and problematic” social media apps when they started using them at 13 and 15, respectively, according to court documents.

SJ, a teen in Illinois, began to use Snapchat, the app created by Snap, compulsively and subsequently experienced mental health issues, an eating disorder and self harm, her lawyers claim.

KDB, now an 18-years-old from Mississippi, similarly developed compulsive use of both Meta and Snap, leading to worsening mental and physical health, according to her lawyers.

Meta has previously denied such claims.

“We will not back away from defending ourselves against baseless lawsuits,” Meta told AFP in July.

Snap intends to argue that it is different from other apps like Meta’s Instagram and Facebook because of Snapchat’s focus on primarily being a messaging platform.

“We believe the evidence will support that we have put our community first, and that these allegations fundamentally misrepresent the plaintiffs’ experiences on Snapchat and how our platform was designed,” a Snap spokesperson said in a statement.

World.title: 'They will fly': MEA on direct India-Taiwan flights after Pakistan blocks airspace over 'One-China' policy
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Wednesday indicated that direct air connectivity between India and Taiwan could be explored, amid reports that Pakistan has barred Taiwanese airlines from using its airspace under its âOne Chinaâ policy.

âMy sense is, if there are direct flights then they will fly,â MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said when asked about the possibility of direct flights between India and Taiwan.

The remarks came after Pakistan reportedly restricted Taiwanese carriers from using its airspace, in a move that highlights Islamabad's support for Beijing's position on Taiwan.

Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif confirmed the country's position to Bloomberg News, saying its aviation policy permits only mainland Chinese airlines to fly over its airspace.

âThe aviation division follows the One China policy â only mainland China is allowed,â Asif said.

âWe have permitted only Chinese airlines to fly over Pakistan,â he added.

Pakistan is the first country reported to have taken such a step against Taiwanese carriers. Bloomberg, citing flight-tracking data, reported that China Airlines Ltd and EVA Airways Corp had not flown over Pakistani airspace since the morning of October 25.





The restriction came to light after aviation observers noticed that some Taiwanese flights had begun taking longer routes to reach Europe, flying entirely over Russian airspace since the weekend.

According to Flightradar24 data, a China Airlines flight from Taipei to Rome on October 24 flew through Russian airspace, bypassing its earlier route through India, Pakistan and Turkmenistan.

The move comes as China continues to urge other countries to support its claim that Taiwan is part of its territory.

Beijing considers Taiwan a part of China, while Taipei maintains that the island is self-governed and rejects Beijing's claim.

Pakistan's decision also underlines its close ties with China, which Islamabad has described as an âiron-clad friendshipâ. The two countries have maintained an âall-weatherâ partnership since establishing diplomatic relations in 1951.

In January, Pakistan described Taiwan as an âinalienable partâ of China and reiterated its commitment to the One China principle.

World.title: 'People choose government, not vice versa': CJP backs INDIA bloc's November 1 rally
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) extended its support to the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan against alleged electoral irregularities.

In a statement, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said the exercise had raised serious concerns about the exclusion of eligible voters and accused the Election Commission of undermining the democratic principle that citizens, not governments, should decide electoral outcomes.

"The fundamental principle of democracy is that people get to choose their government, not that the government gets to choose its voters," Dipke said, adding that Kumar had "lost the trust required to oversee free and fair elections".

He also invoked BR Ambedkar's role in framing the Constitution, arguing that universal adult suffrage was intended to give every citizen an equal say in the country's future, regardless of caste, religion, gender, education or economic background.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"The idea was simple: bring more citizens into democracy, not keep them out of it," he said, calling on constitutional institutions to protect eligible voters' rights.

The CJP's backing comes as opposition parties step up their campaign against the SIR ahead of the November 1 rally.

On Wednesday, INDIA bloc representatives in Delhi alleged that the revision had disproportionately affected poor workers, tenants and residents of unauthorised settlements, and demanded that eligible voters' names be restored.

The opposition also cited alleged irregularities in voter records and sought a return to ballot paper-based elections. The bloc has maintained that the exercise risks disenfranchising legitimate voters.

World.title: 'India's businesses already hate all of you': Rahul Gandhi's 4-point reply to Nirmala Sitharaman's advice over Tata Group
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha

on Wednesday hit back at finance minister

with a 4-point response over the Tata Group row, questioning why Tata Trusts and

representatives were reportedly hosted at Union home minister

Amit Shah

's residence.

His remarks came after Sitharaman accused the Congress leader of politicising the Tata Group dispute and advised him to "refrain from seeing ghosts everywhere".

In a post on X, Rahul asked when "crony number 1" would enter the picture and which parts of the Tata Group he would get.

"Dear Mrs Sitarama. 1. Which "legal and commercial matter" required Tata Trusts and Tata Sons to be hosted at Amit Shah's residence?"

"2. When is crony number 1 going to appear in the game and which pieces of Tata is he going to get?" he said.

"Finally, all India's businesses except 3-4 of your cronies, already hate all of you and don't need any incitement," he added.

The exchange followed Rahul's earlier post accusing the government of "criminally destroying" the Tata Group and questioning business leaders' silence over the matter.

"Being the LoP Rahul Gandhi, I suggest you refrain from politicising every issue. Also, casually labelling commercial and legal matters as criminal is unacceptable," Sitharaman wrote on X.





The finance minister alleged that Rahul had "repeatedly decried" the achievements of Indian industry and its entrepreneurs. She also accused him of trying to "incite" business leaders to join him in "spreading distrust and toxicity".

Sitharaman contrasted the Congress's economic record with the BJP-led government's approach, accusing the former of suppressing entrepreneurs through its "stifling Licence-Quota Raj".

"For decades, your party had smothered the spirit of Indian entrepreneurs under the stifling âLicence-Quota Rajâ and inflicted poverty on crores of Indians. On the other hand, our government led by PM Narendramodi values Indian industry as a creator of jobs and a driver of economic growth. Our policies have been tailored to enable enterprise, support industry and encourage investment," she added.

She urged Rahul to engage constructively with the government rather than make allegations for what she described as "narrow political motives".

"The Constitution of India ensures justice to all its citizens and our Honourable Courts are entrusted with upholding it. History is witness to the shoddy manner in which you, your party and the PMs belonging to your party have demeaned the judiciary. So Rahul ji, refrain from seeing ghosts everywhere," Sitharaman said.

Earlier, Rahul had targeted Prime Minister

Narendra Modi

and home minister Amit Shah over the dispute, alleging that the Tata Group was being undermined and that business leaders were reluctant to speak out.

"Tata is being criminally destroyed, and no business leader dares say a word. How long will you stay silent? Until they own you? Indian business is not Modi and Shah's plaything. You lack courage. We don't. We will ensure justice for these crimes," he wrote on X.

World.title: 'India is very strong, watch Dhurandhar': Arunachal minister on ITBP chief's remarks on China border
World.content:
A file photo of ITBP personnel near Indo-China border. (ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India is âvery strongâ and its intelligence capabilities have grown significantly, Arunachal Pradesh minister Balo Raja said, citing the spy thriller Dhurandhar while questioning ITBP chief Shatrujeet Singh Kapur's reported remarks on continuing face-offs with Chinese forces along the border.Speaking to reporters in Itanagar on Tuesday, Raja, who holds the urban affairs, land management and civil aviation portfolios, questioned why a senior officer would make statements that could create an impression of India being weak."Why make statements like that when you are a DG? Why perceive yourself as weak? India is very strong. You must have seen the 'Dhurandhar' movie; watch it, and you will see how much India's intelligence capabilities have grown," Raja said.His remarks come amid a political controversy over Kapur's reported comments that face-offs at several locations along the frontier in Arunachal Pradesh were continuing.Addressing ITBP personnel at an event in Alwar, Rajasthan, on October 22, Kapur reportedly spoke about the confrontations along the India-China border and praised the force's newly raised Shaurya commando teams for their role in handling them.He also stressed the need to modernise weapons and equipment and strengthen the force's ability to respond to evolving security challenges, including drone warfare.Kapur said traditional methods of warfare were no longer sufficient to counter China, which he described as India's âbiggest adversaryâ.The reported remarks triggered political reactions, with opposition leaders seeking clarity from the Centre on the border situation and the circumstances surrounding the face-offs.The comments came as the ITBP stepped up its modernisation efforts, focusing on emerging warfare technologies, specialised training and improved operational capabilities.Earlier, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) clarified the government's position after reports of Kapur's remarks about continuing face-offs with the People's Liberation Army (PLA) in Arunachal Pradesh.During a briefing on Friday, the MEA said that the situation along the India-China border was occasionally disrupted when Chinese forces deviated from established patrolling patterns."Insofar as the specifics are concerned, I would refer you to the Ministry of Defence. As we have noted in the past, the situation in the India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns. Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control," the MEA said."The two sides have also agreed to discuss ways to improve understanding of the LAC in appropriate areas for better border management. I would also like to emphasise that the maintenance of peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations," it added.

World.title: 22 Indians, including 14 seafarers, killed in West Asia conflict: MEA
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India has lost 22 nationals, including 14 seafarers, in the ongoing West Asia conflict, the ministry of external Affairs (MEA) said on Wednesday.

According to MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, three Indians had been killed in Saudi Arabia.

âWe are deeply concerned about the ongoing conflict in West Asia. We have lost 22 Indian nationals in the conflict, including 14 seafarers. We remain in close touch with our community in the Gulf region for their safety and wellbeing. Three Indians have lost their lives in Saudi Arabia,â Jaiswal told reporters at a regular briefing in New Delhi.

The war began on February 28, following US and Israeli strikes on Iran. India has consistently called for a resolution through dialogue and diplomacy.

Tensions have escalated in recent days after Yemen-based Houthi rebels launched strikes on Saudi Arabia, opening another front in the eight-month-long conflict. Saudi Arabia is also among the Gulf states targeted by Iran for hosting US military bases.

India has expressed serious concern over Houthi attacks on the Kingdomâs civilian infrastructure and economic assets, warning that such strikes threaten regional stability and freedom of navigation through the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait.





The Iran-backed Houthis also attacked Saudi Arabiaâs East-West oil pipeline, a key route for crude exports that has become increasingly important since the conflict disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been under a virtual Iranian blockade since March.

The Houthi attacks have raised further concerns over the safety of the Bab-el-Mandeb, a strategic maritime chokepoint between the Horn of Africa and the Arabian Peninsula that connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Arabian Sea.

World.title: 'Commit to ballot paper': Congress dares PM Modi after his 'how many seats' swipe over MLC results
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister

on Wednesday took a swipe at the Congress over its dismal performance in the MLC polls held across four states. The grand old party which failed to win a single seat in the polls, hit back at PM Modi over his âballot paperâ remark and challenged him to commit to holding all future Lok Sabha and assembly elections using ballot papers.

The back-and-forth began when the Prime Minister in a post on X, wrote, "MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states - Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?"

Congress Rajya Sabha member Pawan Khera hit back at PM Modi, asking him to demonstrate confidence in the BJPâs prowess by committing to ballot paper voting in all future Lok Sabha and assembly elections.

In a post on X, Khera demanded the suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the restoration of 13.3 crore voters "deleted illegally".

"If Narendra Modi is so confident that EVMs have no bearing on election results, let him prove his confidence in the BJPâs electoral prowess through action, not rhetoric," he wrote.

"1. Commit to conducting all Lok Sabha and upcoming Vidhan Sabha elections by ballot paper going forward.





2. Suspend SIR and restore the 13.3 crore voters illegally deleted from the electoral rolls. 3. Terminate Gyanesh Gupta. 4. Repeal the law that gives life long immunity to Gyanesh Gupta," Khera wrote.

BJP national president Nitin Nabin also took a dig at the grand old party, saying the party would continue to struggle for survival under Rahul Gandhi's leadership. Addressing a gathering during the BJP's âLoktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hataoâ march in Delhi, Nabin said PM Narendra Modi would return to the Red Fort after the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.

Nabin also accused the Congress of opposing the cleaning of electoral rolls because it was distressed by efforts to remove alleged infiltrators.

âThere are voters who have died but whose names remain on the electoral rolls. There are also people whose names appear in the voter lists at two places. There are crores of such voters whose names are registered more than once, while the whereabouts of many others cannot be traced.

This is what is called a âghost voter listâ,â he said.

The remark came after the Congress drew a blank in Karnataka, where the BJP-Janata Dal (Secular) alliance swept all four legislative council seats despite the Congress being in power in the state. The results also saw the Congress lose its sitting Bengaluru Teachersâ constituency to the JD(S).

The prime minister's reference to ballot papers comes amid the opposition's repeated allegations of irregularities in electronic voting machines (EVMs) and demands for greater transparency in the electoral process.

The Congress suffered its biggest setback in Karnataka, where the BJP retained three seats and the JD(S) wrested Bengaluru Teachersâ from the ruling party.

JD(S) candidate A P Ranganath defeated sitting Congress MLC Puttanna by 908 votes, securing 10,810 votes against his rival's 9,902.
