World.title: AIMIM seeks transparent, time-bound plan to tackle El Nino impact
World.content:
The All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) urged the Telangana government to publish a dedicated summer drinking water plan for Hyderabad and the HMDA region, covering water availability, supply schedules, emergency sourcing arrangements and a public dashboard.

The representation was submitted by Hyderabad MP and AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi to Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka on Wednesday over the effects of El Nino, and the ensuing water paucity in the State.

Flagging the rainfall deficit, declining reservoir storage and groundwater depletion amid concerns over El Nino, Mr. Owaisi urged the government to take immediate measures to safeguard drinking water supplies. He also referred to complaints about water with an ‘unusual colour and smell’.

Mr. Owaisi sought priority water supply to hospitals, schools, hostels and other critical institutions, with ordinary deliveries within 24 hours and a six-hour response to critical institutional failures. He also called for the procurement of tanker capacity against the quantified deficit and the deployment of smaller vehicles with a capacity of 2.5 to 5 kilolitres to serve narrow lanes, particularly in the Old City.

On groundwater depletion, the Hyderabad parliamentarian requested that the September groundwater bulletin and the latest matched-station October readings be placed before the House and made available to the public.

On agriculture, the AIMIM chief called for a clear and dependable Yasangi irrigation schedule for each irrigation command, based on a joint assessment by the Agriculture and Irrigation departments. He also sought a support package covering compensation, seeds, inputs, alternative crops and marketing arrangements if a crop holiday was declared.

Mr. Owaisi called for an urban summer action plan, including drinking water kiosks at intervals of 300 to 500 metres along major roads, bus routes, markets, construction clusters and crowded public spaces. He called for employment support during the summer months and measures to protect vulnerable groups.

He urged the Chief Minister to place the representation before the Cabinet Sub-Committee constituted to address drought and El Niño conditions and issue the necessary orders at the earliest.

World.title: Equip yourselves with skills necessary for the changing world, expert urges students at AI seminar
World.content:
Keladi Shivappa Nayaka University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences Vice-Chancellor M.V. Dhananjaya has asked students to equip themselves with industry-relevant skills alongside academic knowledge to improve their employability.

He was speaking after inaugurating a one-day multidisciplinary international seminar on ‘Artificial Intelligence and Society’, organised by the Government First Grade College at Holehonnur in Shivamogga district, on Wednesday.

Pointing to the growing application of artificial intelligence (AI), Mr. Dhananjaya said the technology had made inroads into almost every sector, including agriculture. The national agricultural research system had also begun harnessing AI for various applications.

Agriculture accounted for nearly 41% of the country’s workforce, with about 141 million small landholders depending on the sector for their livelihood. Technological interventions, including precision application of fertilisers and data-driven farming, could help improve agricultural productivity and resource utilisation, he said.

Referring to the digital infrastructure created for agriculture, he noted that several corporate companies were developing technology-based solutions for the sector. Students needed to understand these developments and acquire the skills required to make effective use of emerging technologies.

Mr. Dhananjaya expressed concern over the gap between the skills imparted by educational institutions and those expected by industry. Despite a large number of graduates entering the job market, many struggled to secure employment because they lacked the necessary skills.

Referring to the National Education Policy introduced in 2020, he called for greater collaboration among departments and institutions. Universities should begin by strengthening networking within their own departments and making effective use of the infrastructure already available before exploring external partnerships.

Emphasising entrepreneurship, he urged students to prepare themselves to become job providers rather than merely job seekers. Several funding opportunities were available to support innovation, entrepreneurship and skill development, and students should learn how to access them.

Delivering the keynote address, Praveen G. Saptarshi, visiting professor at Salisbury University in the United States, said artificial intelligence should address real-world problems rather than become an instrument in the hands of those in power and capitalists. Expressing concern over current developments in AI, he said society needed to intervene to ensure that knowledge gained through human experience received due importance in the age of artificial intelligence.

Prashanth Jayaram, a senior technologist in the United States, said AI had made life easier. However, people should move beyond relying on ready-made answers and develop the ability to find creative solutions to problems.

Basavaraj N. Jagadale, head of the Department of Electronics at Kuvempu University, college principal Pratibha K.R., seminar organising secretary Chayashree K, seminar coordinator Nagaraj Naik S. and others were present. Many research scholars from Karnataka and outside participated in the conference.

World.title: GBA to launch new campaign focusing infra fix from November 1
World.content:
Even as the Freedom from Waste campaign is under way, the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) will launch a new campaign, titled “Ward One”, from November 1, focusing on addressing infrastructure issues.

Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said on Wednesday that, under the campaign, the corporations would undertake a month-long drive to address local civic issues, with priority given to repairing roads and improving junctions.

“Initially, one ward in each division will be selected for improvement. Ward-level officials will be provided with a checklist to systematically assess sanitation and infrastructure deficiencies. The assessment of requirements will begin on Thursday,” he said.

The drive will bring together parastatals and all associated departments, including Bangalore Electricity Supply Company (Bescom), Bangalore Development Authority (BDA), the Traffic Police, railway agencies and Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB). A ward-level committee comprising officials from all departments will be formed. The committees will coordinate the required works, monitor progress, and prepare an execution plan based on the time needed to complete sanitation and infrastructure improvements in each selected ward.

The drive will cover sanitation, road and junction repairs, drains and storm-water drains, drinking water supply, sewerage, streetlights, public transport, lakes, parks, waste management, tax collection, protection of government property, and traffic management.

“Assistant engineers, junior health inspectors and marshals will inspect roads and public spaces, identify pending issues, and map each problem to the department responsible for resolving it,” Mr. Gowda said.

According to a GBA source, during the first seven days, one ward in each division will be selected for the implementation of improvement works. Based on the outcomes on the ground and the lessons learnt, the drive will be expanded to other wards. The GBA aims to cover all wards.

Mr. Gowda said the rains had subsided and that infrastructure works could be taken up throughout November. He said priority would be given to improving and upgrading junctions.

The exercise will involve identifying junctions in each ward that are notorious for traffic problems and preparing dedicated plans to upgrade them. The plans will incorporate inputs from the Traffic Police, commuters, and local residents. Mr. Gowda added that better road conditions and improved junction management could help reduce traffic bottlenecks.

“To collect such micro-level details, we need time and dedicated staff. So, the first week of the drive will be dedicated to understanding the implementation challenges, and the plan will be tweaked accordingly,” a GBA source told The Hindu.

Need others to act

When asked about the progress of other drives undertaken earlier, Mr. Gowda said the debris-clearance drive was ongoing and that the works were being followed up. Meanwhile, the footpath-clearance drive had been completed to an extent, he said, while acknowledging that the “encroachments” had returned.

“No work can be done 100% in this system, but when we work together, a certain degree of success can be achieved. Now, the onus should also be shared by local leaders, who must take action on the ground to ensure that the work is sustained and becomes a continuous process,” he said.

World.title: HC summons HR&CE Commissioner
World.content:
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court has summoned the Commissioner of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department on a contempt petition filed for non-compliance of the court order to remove encroachments from Kalyana Pasupatheeswarar Temple lands in Karur.

A Division Bench of Justices P. Velmurugan and K.K. Ramakrishnan also directed the HR&CE Commissioner to file a status report in the case.

The Commissioner and seven other officials were suo motu impleaded as respondents in the contempt petition. The court posted the matter for hearing to November 5.

The court was hearing the contempt petition filed in 2024 by A. Radhakrishnan alleging non-compliance of the 2022 court order, directing the authorities concerned to issue proper notices to all the parties who were said to be in possession of the properties.

On receipt of such notices, the parties were directed to file their objections, along with documents available with them, to the authorities. The authorities were directed to consider them and pass appropriate orders on merit and in accordance with law, the court had directed.

If the authorities decided on the basis of the civil court decrees as well as materials available that these parties were encroachers of the temple properties, they had to be removed by the authorities, after affording them sufficient opportunity of hearing and by following due process of law. The exercise should be completed in 12 weeks, the court had directed.

World.title: Campaign intensifies in Puttaparthi, Dharmavaram as elections approach
World.content:
The municipal elections in Dharmavaram and Puttaparthi have thrown a litmus test of political strength in Sri Sathya Sai district, with the ruling NDA seeking to consolidate its position, while the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) attempting to defend its local influence. Tensions during nominations in Dharmavaram and an increasingly intense campaign in Puttaparthi have brought the rivalry into sharp focus.

Dharmavaram came under a tense start to the nomination process on October 16, when supporters of the TDP and YSRCP clashed near the municipal office. Police resorted to a lathicharge to disperse the rival groups after a heated confrontation turned into stone-pelting. Over a thousand cadres of both sides gathered near the nomination centre, prompting additional security deployment.

Meanwhile, Puttaparthi presented a different political picture. The TDP-led alliance and YSRCP have stepped up campaigning, with candidates reaching out to voters through neighbourhood visits and promises to address civic problems.

The alliance backed Jana Sena Party (JSP) candidate Mekala Eswar for the chairperson’s post, with local MLA Palle Sindhura Reddy and former Minister Palle Raghunath Reddy campaigning in his support. Mr. Eswar has promised to prioritise drainage and drinking water problems, while YSRCP candidate Boya Vanam Avinash has also intensified his campaign, making the contest a direct test of the opposition’s local appeal.

World.title: Youth held for murder for gain in Thoothukudi district
World.content:
The Thoothukudi South Police have arrested a youth, who allegedly murdered a woman when she resisted his attempt to rob her of the gold chain on Wednesday.

Police said C. Sasikala, 47, of Kandan Colony is living alone here as her husband Chithiraivel, is working in a teashop in Ernakulam, Keralam. Her son Niranjan is living in Shankar Colony here with his family.

A stranger, who entered the house of Sasikala on Wednesday afternoon, tried to snatch her gold chain, weighing 4 sovereigns. When she resisted, he attacked her with a machete he was carrying. He escaped with the gold chain.

With multiple cut injuries, Sasikala screamed for help. As the neighbours found her lying in a pool of blood, they alerted Mr. Niranjan. Even before he arrived at the spot, Sasikala succumbed to her injuries.

Deputy Inspector General of Police, Tirunelveli Range, R. Thirunavukkarasu, and Superintendent of Police R. Siva Prasad visited the spot. Fingerprint experts and sniffer dog were pressed into service to collect evidences. Police also collected CCTV camera footages to identify the culprit.

Thoothukudi South Police, who registered a case, arrested K. Vignesh Kumar, 24, of Anna Nagar here in connection with the murder for gain.

Further investigations are on.

World.title: Three youths arrested for possession of Tapentadol tablets in Vriddhachalam
World.content:
The Vriddhachalam police arrested three youths and seized 88 Tapentadol tablets from their possession at Vriddhachalam on Wednesday. The arrested were identified as Adithya, 19, and Tholkappiyan 20, of Tittakudi and Hari Prasad, 23, of Perambalur.

According to the police, a team was conducting vehicle checks near the Vedappar temple when they found three youths riding triples on a motorcycle. On seeing the police, the trio attempted to flee. The team intercepted them and found 88 Tapentadol tablets in their possession.

Preliminary investigations by the police revealed that the tablets had been ordered online and bought for illegal sale. The trio was produced before a local court and remanded to custody. A search has been launched for another accused who is at large.
