Meanwhile, the Centre for the Promotion of Imports from developing countries (CBI) has launched a year-long programme in Armenia. The initiative aims to help 21 Armenian producers of dried fruit and nuts develop their export potential and enter markets in the Netherlands and other EU countries.

World.title: “Gossip, myths and manipulation” – fifth day of hearings on banning opposition parties held in Georgia
World.content:
Georgia opposition ban trial

On 27 October, Georgia’s Constitutional Court held the fifth day of hearings on the merits of a lawsuit filed by the ruling Georgian Dream party seeking to ban five opposition parties. At this stage, the court is hearing arguments from the parties involved in the case.

The lawsuit names the United National Movement, Coalition for Change, Lelo – Strong Georgia, Gakharia for Georgia and the Federalists. Georgian Dream argues that these parties have violated Article 23 of the Constitution, which prohibits political parties whose aims include overthrowing or forcibly changing the country’s constitutional order. One of the arguments is that the parties refuse to recognise the legitimacy of the current authorities. The lawsuit also accuses them of organising attempts to overthrow the government. The United National Movement faces additional accusations of undermining Georgia’s independence and violating its territorial integrity. The lawsuit holds the party responsible for the August 2008 war with Russia over South Ossetia, when it was in power. All five opposition parties reject the accusations. Hearings are scheduled to continue through 30 October. The court must deliver its final ruling by 24 June 2027.

At the 27 October hearing, three representatives of the United National Movement appeared before the court: Ana Tsitlidze, Levan Bezhashvili and Alika Kuprava.

Ana Tsitlidze spoke for the longest time. She criticised the legal grounds for the lawsuit and the evidence presented, and questioned the judges’ impartiality. She argued that the case was politically motivated and that banning the parties would restrict political pluralism.

Tsitlidze spoke at length about high-profile criminal cases from the period when the United National Movement was in power in Georgia. She also addressed corruption allegations, relations with international partners and the events of the August 2008 war.

Whenever she mentioned a particular official by name, the presiding judge urged her to be more restrained and interrupted her speech.

With these statements, one of the parties defending itself in the case, the United National Movement, concluded its presentation to the court.

At the end of their speeches, none of the party’s representatives used the standard legal phrase: “I ask the court to dismiss the claim.” Instead, each speaker ended by appealing to the judges’ conscience.

The judges seemed to find it extremely difficult to hide their irritation at this unusual conclusion.

On 28 October, the Constitutional Court will begin hearing arguments from representatives of the Coalition for Change. They have announced in advance that they have prepared an extensive set of documents and will need a full day to present their case.

Below are the main points from the 27 October hearing.

Ana Tsitlidze: “Political gossip, myths and manipulation”

Ana Tsitlidze said the court must draw a clear line between the state’s legitimate powers and the use of constitutional procedures to target political opponents. In her view, the lawsuit filed by the ruling Georgian Dream party lacks legal grounds and amounts to nothing more than “political gossip, myths and manipulation”.

Tsitlidze said she was not trying to shield the United National Movement from responsibility for its political or legal record. On the contrary, she was ready to discuss every decision the party had made in the past, including those that were difficult to defend.

However, she argued that Georgian Dream’s lawsuit had no legal basis and relied on a selective interpretation of historical events.

“If maintaining a critical attitude towards the government and questioning the legitimacy of elections can become grounds for banning a party, then political pluralism in Georgia is over and the country has become a one-party dictatorship.”

Judge interrupts Tsitlidze: “How can you say that a man was killed?”

When the discussion turned to the circumstances surrounding the death of Nugzar Putkaradze, a Batumi City Council member who died in November 2021, presiding judge Revaz Nadaraia interrupted Ana Tsitlidze.

Putkaradze represented the United National Movement in Batumi City Council, in the Ajara region. He died of a heart attack. A few days before his death, his party said that representatives of the ruling party had been putting him under “unbearable pressure”.

“There is concrete evidence that Georgian Dream put pressure on him. This evidence has been made public. Nugzar Putkaradze was offered $100,000 to betray the National Movement and switch sides to Georgian Dream. In the end, he suffered a heart attack and died,” Tsitlidze said.

“How can you say such a thing? Think about your words! This is a very serious allegation. How can you make such statements from the podium in a courtroom? On what grounds are you claiming that a man was killed?” Judge Nadaraia asked.

“But the entire argument put forward by the parliamentary investigative commission, which prepared a report for this court, was based precisely on the claim that the National Movement had allegedly killed people as part of systematic crimes,” Tsitlidze replied.

Tsitlidze on controversial actions by the United National Movement in power and double standards

Ana Tsitlidze recalled several high-profile cases from the previous government’s time in office, including the Aprasidze family case, the case of Roin Shavadze, the murder of Sandro Girgvliani and the death of Yuri Vazagashvili.

She argued that the possible crimes of individuals should not automatically be grounds for banning an entire political party.

Speaking about the case of Roin Shavadze, Tsitlidze said she also had questions about it.

Shavadze was a former military officer who fought in the August 2008 war with Russia. He was arrested in Batumi on 24 August 2008, shortly after the war, and later killed. The case involved allegations of torture and extrajudicial killing. The circumstances remain the subject of political and legal disputes.

“The Roin Shavadze case was a problem for the United National Movement. I myself support reopening the investigation.

“But how can this case be used as grounds for banning the National Movement when the lead investigator was Resan Kontselidze, who later became a Georgian Dream MP? Moreover, the deputy prosecutor at the time was Vasil Roinishvili, who is now a Constitutional Court judge,” Tsitlidze said.

Turning to the Sandro Girgvliani case, Tsitlidze pointed out that the presiding judge was Levan Murusidze, who was later appointed as a judge for life by Georgian Dream.

In January 2006, when the United National Movement was in power, Sandro Girgvliani, a young man, and his friend were abducted and brutally beaten by people linked to senior Interior Ministry officials following a dispute at a cafe in Tbilisi. Girgvliani later died from his injuries. Four former senior officials were convicted in the case. However, their subsequent pardons and early releases sparked public outrage.

“Georgian Dream divides the careers of judges Murusidze and Chinchaladze into two periods. Their work before 2012, when Georgian Dream came to power, is portrayed as criminal because it helps build the case for banning the opposition. Yet the same judges’ work after 2012 is presented as a model of integrity and independence. This is a double standard, and such double standards undermine the very concept of justice,” Tsitlidze said.

In her view, Georgian Dream’s use of past misconduct within the judicial system as grounds for banning a political party is contradictory, especially since people who continue to work within that same system are not being held to the same standard.

Tsitlidze on Zurab Adeishvili and former officials from his circle now sitting in judgment on the opposition

Ana Tsitlidze noted that Zurab Adeishvili, a senior official under the United National Movement government, is mentioned 25 times in Georgian Dream’s constitutional lawsuit.

Adeishvili was an influential figure in President Mikheil Saakashvili’s administration. He served as Georgia’s chief prosecutor from 2004 to 2008 and as justice minister from 2008 to 2012.

The plaintiffs argue that his actions were so systematic and unconstitutional that the entire party should be banned.

Tsitlidze said she had never met Adeishvili in person. However, Constitutional Court judge Vasil Roinishvili knew him well: when Adeishvili was justice minister, Roinishvili served as deputy chief prosecutor.

Tsitlidze challenged the judges with the following question:

“How can someone be banned from political activity on the basis of the actions of a person they have never even met, while a former senior official from that very same system is now allowed to sit on the court and take part in constitutional justice?”

Tsitlidze on fake prison videos, planted drugs and weapons, and violations of privacy

Ana Tsitlidze cited criminal cases from the period when Georgian Dream was already in power. These included staged prison videos and cases involving drugs and weapons allegedly planted on people.

She noted that well-known figures Tamaz Elizbarashvili and Lado Bedukadze had spoken about prison footage being staged.

On the issue of drugs and weapons being planted, she recalled the December 2024 arrest of Giorgi Akhobadze, an active participant in pro-European protests. Akhobadze was charged with acquiring and possessing drugs. He was later acquitted, and the court ordered his immediate release in the courtroom.

Tsitlidze also raised the issue of violations of privacy.

One of the arguments in the lawsuit is that the United National Movement committed systematic crimes by distributing recordings of people’s private lives while in power. Tsitlidze argued that those responsible for publishing private recordings of journalists and politicians during Georgian Dream’s time in office should also be held accountable.

Tsitlidze: UNM accused of corruption as Georgian Dream officials jailed for corruption

Ana Tsitlidze noted that the plaintiffs accuse the United National Movement of corruption, despite serious questions surrounding senior officials from the ruling Georgian Dream party itself.

She cited the cases of former Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili, former State Security Service chief Grigol Liluashvili and former Defence Minister Juansher Burchuladze, all of whom have been convicted of corruption.

Given these cases involving members of their own party, Tsitlidze said, it was unclear why the plaintiffs believed the United National Movement should be banned over individual cases of corruption within its ranks.

Georgia’s international partners and sanctions

Tsitlidze criticised the argument that the opposition had worked with international partners to persuade them to impose sanctions on Georgia’s current authorities.

She said that engaging with international partners was a normal part of political activity, while decisions on sanctions were made by the partners themselves.

Tsitlidze’s closing words to the judges “The choice of which path to take is yours”

“I am not asking you to dismiss this lawsuit. Georgia’s history has never been one-dimensional. We have had people like Antsukhelidze and Sergo Ordzhonikidze, Ilia and Berbichashvili. The choice of which path to take is yours,” Ana Tsitlidze concluded.

“Would it not have been better to simply state, instead of making rhetorical remarks…” the presiding judge began, cutting himself off mid-sentence as he tried to hide his irritation. “You are asking the court to dismiss the lawsuit, are you not?”

“We are not asking for anything” Tsitlidze replied.

Levan Bezhashvili “The rule of law must not fall with those in power”

The speeches by the two other United National Movement representatives, Levan Bezhashvili and Alika Kuprava, were relatively brief.

“Today, you are deciding not only the fate of political parties, but also whether the Constitution will remain a check on government power in Georgia or become entirely dependent on the will of those who hold that power,” Levan Bezhashvili told the Constitutional Court judges.

“History does not remember who held more power at any given moment. It remembers what people did with that power. Your decision will be judged by whether you defended the rule of law at the moment when it was most difficult to do so. A party may be defeated, a politician may leave office, but the rule of law must not fall with those in power,” Bezhashvili stressed.

Reactions to the hearing

Badri Japaridze, one of the leaders of Lelo – Strong Georgia, told journalists that when it was his party’s turn to speak, its representatives would use every legal means available to expose what he called Georgian Dream’s real aim: to eliminate the opposition in the country.

Maia Kopaleishvili, a member of the Coalition for Change, told journalists that Georgian Dream had presented nothing but hearsay in its lawsuit.

“The hearings of the parliamentary temporary investigative commission, which form the basis of the lawsuit, are built on gossip and cannot provide sufficient grounds to accuse a political party of unconstitutional activity,” Kopaleishvili said.



Representatives of the United National Movement who addressed the court. Photo: Batumelebi, 27 October, Batumi.

World.title: Month after Russia’s ban on Georgian drinks, Russian experts to inspect laboratories in Georgia: what are risks?
World.content:
Russia’s Rosselkhoznadzor to inspect Georgian laboratories

From 2 November 2026, specialists from Russia’s agricultural watchdog, Rosselkhoznadzor, will visit Georgia to inspect Georgian laboratories, the agency said in a statement.

The Russian specialists will examine Georgia’s phytosanitary certification system for fruit and other plant products intended for export to Russia. They will also inspect a laboratory that tests such products for pesticide and agrochemical residues.

Phytosanitary certification confirms that plant-based products meet the requirements of the importing country. Laboratory tests for pesticide and agrochemical residues, meanwhile, detect the presence of these chemicals in products.

According to Rosselkhoznadzor, the visit follows an invitation from Georgia’s National Food Agency. The agency said the aim was to develop a common approach to monitoring products subject to quarantine controls.

The Russian agency did not specify which laboratory its specialists would visit. It also remains unclear whether the inspection will lead to any changes in the conditions for exporting Georgian products to Russia.

The Georgian side has yet to provide official information. Georgia’s National Food Agency promised JAMnews it would clarify the details, but subsequently stopped answering calls.

Background: the context for the planned visit by Russian specialists to Georgia

The planned inspection of laboratories in Georgia coincides with Russia’s ban on imports of several Georgian-made drinks.

The restrictions cover both alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages. They affect seven major Georgian companies, including producers of Coca-Cola and Nabeglavi water in Georgia. The companies affected by the ban account for around 75–80% of Georgia’s wine exports to Russia. Russia’s embargo on Georgian drinks came into force on 10 October.

Later, from 20 to 22 October, Rosselkhoznadzor specialists visited Tbilisi to attend a regional seminar organised by the World Organisation for Animal Health. During the visit, they also discussed bilateral co-operation with representatives of Georgia’s National Food Agency.

Following these meetings, Rosselkhoznadzor announced on 22 October that it would allow two Georgian dairy processors to access the Russian market from November. The agency also said it was ready to inspect six Georgian fish and seafood producers interested in exporting their products to Russia.

The statement also noted a 26% increase in Russian exports of live pigs to Georgia, while onion supplies had tripled. Meanwhile, Georgia’s exports to Russia of products such as blueberries, apples, plums and mandarins continue to grow.

Figs are among the products whose exports to Russia are also increasing.

According to Rosselkhoznadzor, Russia had imported 70,500 tonnes of fruit and vegetables from Georgia by 24 October 2026.

Imports increased across several product categories:

Nectarines — 17,900 tonnes, up 7.8%;

Apples — 15,300 tonnes, up 17.5%;

Blueberries — 9,500 tonnes, up 46.7%;

Plums — 6,700 tonnes, up 74.2%;

Mandarins — around 3,400 tonnes, up 59%;

Figs — more than 1,900 tonnes, up 21.2%;

Watermelons — 1,400 tonnes, up 59.5%.

What are the risks? — expert assessments

Khatia Dekanoidze, one of the leaders of the Unity – National Movement party, sees the invitation to Russian specialists as a sign that relations with Moscow are entering a new phase.

In her view, the decision raises questions about the reliability of Georgia’s own inspection systems. It also gives Russia additional leverage to exert economic pressure on the country.

“How can you invite a Russian expert to Georgia and give them the authority to inspect our products? What does this tell us? That they do not trust the food safety standards we have established ourselves. It also makes Georgia’s economy even more dependent on Russia. We know that Russia turns economic leverage into a tool of blackmail — as it demonstrated just a few weeks ago when it imposed an embargo on goods produced in Georgia.”

Teona Akubardia, a security expert, also points to risks to national security. She says Russia could selectively restrict access to its market for Georgian products and use that leverage for political purposes.

“There is a risk that Russia will be able to grant or deny access to its market at its own discretion. The state will have no means of protecting itself. With the process of integration with the West frozen, Russia will use this leverage even more actively for political purposes, seeking to bring Georgia fully under its control. This poses a threat to national security. Moreover, the Georgian Dream party is not only failing to neutralise this threat but is creating additional risks under the current circumstances.”

Russia’s Rosselkhoznadzor to inspect Georgian laboratories

World.title: Foreign tourist spending in Azerbaijan rises 72% during F1 weekend - Visa
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 28. During the Formula 1 weekend in Baku, spending by foreign tourists visiting Azerbaijan rose by 72% compared to the average for the previous three weekends.

This is reported in an analytical study conducted by Visa Consulting & Analytics (VCA), a division of Visa.

The report notes that growth was recorded in the hospitality, transportation, restaurant, and retail sectors.

According to the data, spending by tourists from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, the United Arab Emirates, the United States, and the United Kingdom rose by 104% during the race days compared to the same period the previous week.

An increase in spending on hotels and transportation was recorded

During race week, foreign visitors’ spending on hotels rose by 81% compared to the previous week. Spending on transportation during the race weekend rose by 91% compared to the previous weekend.

Spending on sporting goods also increased. Specifically, spending in this sector rose by 120% when comparing September 24 (the day of practice sessions) to September 25 (the day of qualifying).

Spending at restaurants on race day, September 26, was 29% higher than on the previous Saturday.

62% of tourists stayed in the country longer

According to the analysis, some of the visitors who arrived in Azerbaijan during the race weekend extended their stay in the days following the event. Long-stay visitors accounted for approximately 62% of the total number of participants and stayed in the country for an average of more than 12 days.

Nurlan Hajiyev, CEO and Regional Manager of Visa in Azerbaijan, stated that major sporting events have a broad economic and cultural impact.

“Major sporting events are powerful economic and cultural occasions, and this year’s race week in Baku demonstrates how their impact can extend to the broader economy and beyond the event itself. Our spending data shows that foreign tourists spend money in various sectors during Race Week, including lodging, transportation, dining, and retail, supporting local businesses and contributing to Azerbaijan’s tourism economy,” said Nurlan Hajiyev, CEO and Regional Manager of Visa in Azerbaijan.

What data does the analysis draw upon?

Visa’s analysis is based on aggregated payment transactions by Premium and standard cardholders in Azerbaijan. The study covers spending related to the race in Baku on September 24–26, 2026.

Total international spending is calculated by comparing figures from the race weekend with the averages for three weekends: September 3–5, 10–12, and 17–19. Growth in the five major tourist markets is based on a comparison of figures for the same days, September 24–26, with the previous week.

Hotel spending is compared between September 21–27 and the previous week, while transportation spending is compared between the race weekend and the previous weekend. Restaurant spending is calculated based on data from race day and the previous Saturday.

Visa operates in the digital payments sector and facilitates payment transactions between consumers, businesses, financial institutions, and government agencies in more than 200 countries and regions.

Since 2016, Azerbaijan has hosted one of the most prestigious motorsport tournaments in the world. The first Formula 1 race held in the country was named the European Grand Prix. The winner of that race was German driver Nico Rosberg. In subsequent years, the first to cross the finish line were Daniel Ricciardo (Australia), Lewis Hamilton (United Kingdom), Valtteri Bottas (Finland), Sergio Pérez (Mexico), Max Verstappen (Netherlands), Oscar Piastri (Australia), and Max Verstappen, who outpaced all his rivals and claimed the top spot on the podium. Only in 2020 was the Azerbaijan Grand Prix canceled due to the coronavirus pandemic.

In this year’s milestone 10th race, 20 drivers from 10 teams competed for the win. First place went to British driver George Russell of the Mercedes team. Dutch driver Max Verstappen of Red Bull finished second, while his teammate Isack Hadjar took third place.

The race track is 6 kilometers long. The Baku circuit, one of the longest on the Formula 1 calendar, features 20 turns. The track begins at Azadliq Square, curves around the Government House, then runs around the Icheri Sheher for 2.2 kilometers before reaching the Maiden Tower, after which it exits onto Oil Workers Avenue and ends at the starting point. The track, which is run counterclockwise, was designed by the renowned German architect Hermann Tilke.

World.title: Kazakhstan proposes six-month LPG export ban from Nov. 14
World.content:
Photo: Ministry of Energy of the Republic of Kazakhstan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 28. Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy has proposed introducing a six-month ban on the export of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), propane, and butane from the country by road and rail starting November 14, 2026, according to a draft ministerial order published for public discussion.

The draft was published on October 28, with public discussion scheduled to continue until November 12, 2026.

The draft order, titled "On Certain Issues of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Transportation," aims to ensure sufficient supplies of LPG for Kazakhstan's domestic market throughout the restriction period. It provides for certain exceptions to the proposed ban.

According to the document, the proposed measure would continue the export restrictions approved by Kazakhstan's Interdepartmental Commission on Foreign Trade Policy and Participation in International Economic Organizations.

The draft was prepared pursuant to paragraph 7 of the protocol of the commission's meeting on March 5, 2026, and in accordance with Article 18 of Kazakhstan's Law on Regulation of Trading Activities, Article 29 of the Treaty on the Eurasian Economic Union, and Section 10 of Annex 7 to the treaty.

The document identifies ensuring supplies of LPG to Kazakhstan's domestic market during the ban period as the measure's main objective.

The draft states that its provisions are not expected to have negative socioeconomic, legal, or other consequences or adversely affect national security.

World.title: Turkmenistan, IMF discuss expanding economic policy consultations
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 28. Turkmenistan and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have discussed prospects for expanding expert consultations and exchanging assessments and experience on economic policy.

This was reflected in a press release published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Turkmenistan following a meeting between Deputy Foreign Minister Ahmet Gurbanov and Anna Bordon, IMF mission chief for Azerbaijan and Turkmenistan, held in Ashgabat today.

According to the ministry, the sides emphasized the importance of expert engagement and consultations in building a deeper mutual understanding of economic policy issues. They also expressed mutual interest in continuing regular dialogue and developing cooperation.

The meeting comes amid ongoing engagement between the IMF and Turkmenistan on improving the availability and quality of economic data. On September 11, the IMF Executive Board reviewed the country's obligations under Article VIII, Section 5 of the fund's Articles of Agreement, which requires members to provide information needed for the IMF's work.

According to the board's statement, some key data, including information on international reserve assets, official gold and foreign exchange holdings, and the balance of payments, remained outstanding. The board encouraged the Turkmen authorities to address the reporting gaps and indicated that it would review progress within six months.

The IMF has also highlighted the importance of improving the availability and consistency of economic data used to assess Turkmenistan's performance. In its June 2026 assessment, the fund's staff noted that official GDP growth estimates were difficult to reconcile with other available indicators and therefore used its own estimates. The IMF estimated economic growth at 3.6% in 2025 and projected growth of 2.4% in 2026.

In an exclusive interview with Trend published in February, Bordon identified medium-term and program-based budgeting, stronger fiscal reporting and planning, and improvements in governance and statistical capacity among the fund's cooperation priorities for the year.

"These efforts aim to help translate hydrocarbon wealth into more diversified, resilient, and inclusive economic growth over the medium term," Bordon said.

Additionally, she said the fund's policy advice focused on strengthening fiscal management, improving public spending efficiency, modernizing monetary and exchange rate frameworks, and improving the quality and transparency of economic statistics.

The IMF's recommendations have also covered the financial sector. Bordon said they included strengthening the Central Bank of Turkmenistan's role in price and financial stability, reinforcing regulation and supervision, and reducing reliance on central bank financing for development purposes.

Trend's analysis suggests that the latest meeting takes place against a backdrop of two related challenges: the need to improve the quality and coverage of economic data used to assess the country's performance, and the need to strengthen policy frameworks for managing public finances and financial stability. Further expert consultations could help address these issues.

World.title: Russell Brand tells jury friends won't defend him over sex crime allegations
World.content:
Russell Brand has told a jury his friends and family have turned their back on him since a documentary aired allegations of his sexual offending, and would not defend him in court.

The actor and comedian is on trial in London's Southwark Crown Court charged with three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault.

The 51-year-old is accused of committing the crimes against six women in the United Kingdom between 1999 and 2009.

Mr Brand has pleaded not guilty to all counts and maintains he never took part in non-consensual sexual activity.

The prosecution has previously told the jury the six women did not know each other and came forward independently after seeing allegations about Mr Brand in a documentary and news articles.

On Wednesday, Mr Brand took the stand as his defence case opened, telling the jury he blamed the documentary for the allegations against him.

Mr Brand told the court the documentary had a "devastating" impact on his life and relationships with his friends and he could not convince anyone to give evidence on his behalf in court.

Mr Brand's lawyer Ian Winter KC asked Mr Brand: "Will they touch you with a bargepole?" "No," Mr Brand replied.

"I don't call it a documentary, I call it a TV show," Mr Brand later told the court.

Brand denies rape in hotel room

The court has previously heard evidence from a woman who claims Mr Brand raped her at a political conference in 1999.

One of the images of Russell Brand from 1999 tendered as evidence on Thursday. (Supplied: Metropolitan Police)

Mr Brand told the jury the "vivacious" and "loquacious" woman had consented because he was speaking to her during sex to "elicit approval", a practice he said he usually followed with women.

"Consent is fundamental, essential, necessary and indeed in many ways more important than sex itself," he told the court.

Mr Brand also denied all other charges against him, including allegations that he grabbed the breasts of a woman before allegedly dragging her into a toilet at a bar and raping her.

Mr Brand told the jury he did not do that and found it "disgusting behaviour" which was not only "obviously criminal but vulgar".

"I invited her to go into the lavatory to fool around," he told the jury, adding she was "happy to do so".

Mr Brand told the jury he was not famous or well-known at the time of the alleged offending, and did not reach "staggering fame'" until he married Katy Perry in 2010.

Brand admits being 'promiscuous' but denies having goals with women

He told the jury he was "extremely promiscuous" when he was younger, and at the time of the alleged offending, but denied claims, made by a witness earlier in the trial, that he had a goal of sleeping with 5,000 women in his lifetime.

Under cross examination, prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC put to Mr Brand that he was not prepared to leave any situation with a woman "without some sort of conquest".

"The way that's been characterised is so nefarious, unpleasant and ugly, that it's difficult to answer in earnest," he replied.

Mr Brand told the jury while he did not previously have much recollection of these events, after reviewing new disclosures, watching video interviews of the complainants and visiting some of the locations where the alleged crimes took place, he could now remember some of the events.

"My entire life has been consumed by these events, these allegations, these accusations, the impact of these allegations and accusations," he told the court.

"I have devoted myself to these matters."

Mr Brand chose to stand for several hours as he gave evidence with his hands clasped behind his back.

The judge praised the actor and comedian for speaking loudly and told him "not to be shy" when it came to describing his sexual encounters.

Outside court, Russell Brand told reporters it would be a day of "truth and justice" as his defence case began. (Reuters: Toby Shepheard)

Outside, as Mr Brand entered the crown court to give evidence, he told reporters it would be "inappropriate" to say much about the case.

"Other than I'm very grateful that today is the day for truth and justice,' he said.

"And we are blessed that as yet we have a system that can accommodate such things."

The trial continues.

World.title: Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami after fleeing Brazil
World.content:
Flavio Bolsonaro has arrived in the United States, less than a week after losing Brazil's presidential election.

Mr Bolsonaro, who is the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, had been facing a number of legal battles in Brazil and had been ordered by a court to surrender his passport earlier this week.

But the senator instead disappeared, prompting intense speculation that he had fled to the United States.

Mr Bolsonaro, who loses his immunity from prosecution when his Senate term ends in February, had said on Monday after the order to hand in his passports that he had no plans to ​flee.

"I have never thought about leaving the country," he said.

"I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this travesty, which ​is a clear attempt ⁠to intimidate me."

Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro could be seen being escorted out of Opa-locka Executive Airport, shielded by umbrellas. (Reuters: Eva Marie Uzcategui)

But Mr Bolsonaro and his family later disappeared, leading to intense online speculation he planned to fly to the US.

Argentina's migration department said they entered northern Argentina late on Tuesday evening.

They then travelled to Ecuador before flying on a Gulfstream G400 private jet to Miami.

Mr Bolsonaro, who ran on a populist platform, was widely expected to win Sunday's election but suffered a shock defeat to leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

In pictures published on Thursday, Mr Bolsonaro can be seen disembarking a plane at Opa-locka Executive Airport near Miami, Florida.

Mounting legal challenges

The decision to grant Mr Bolsonaro a US visa will likely to deepen the rift between the US and Brazil, two of the Americas' most populous countries.

US President Donald Trump told reporters earlier this week that he would approve of Mr Bolsonaro coming to the United States, after his State Department said it would give them entry visas.

On Monday, a court ordered Flavio Bolsonaro hand over his passport. (Reuters: Agustin Marcarian)

Mr Lula has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaro family to help return them to power.

Mr Bolsonaro's father, Jair Bolsonaro, also fled to Florida after losing the 2022 presidential election to Mr Lula before returning to Brazil three months later.

Jair Bolsonaro is now serving 27 years in prison for plotting a coup after supporters stormed government buildings in the capital Brasilia.

Flavio Bolsonaro, an incumbent senator for Rio de Janeiro, is under investigation by Brazil’s Supreme Court for alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion in two cases.

The court had ordered Mr Bolsonaro to hand over his regular and diplomatic passports by noon Tuesday, just two days after he lost the vote to Mr Lula.

It remained unclear whether he had complied, but allies said he also had an Italian passport.

ABC/wires

World.title: Tales from Outer Suburbia and Addition among Screen Music winners
World.content:
The ABC children's animation series Tales from Outer Suburbia was one of the biggest winners at the 2026 Screen Music Awards.

West Australian composers Josh Hogan and Ned Beckley took home four awards: Best Music for Children's Programming, Best Opening Title Television Theme, Best Soundtrack Album, and Best Original Song Composed for the Screen, the latter shared with Joni Hogan.

MasterChef, My Kitchen Rules and Travel Guides helped longtime collaborators Adam Gock and Dinesh Wicks continue their winning streak in the Most Performed Screen Composer — Australia category.

The pair also won Most Performed Screen Composer — Overseas for their work on Con Girl, Lego Masters and Married at First Sight.

Million Dollar Secret won Best Music for Unscripted or Reality Television Series, with Gock and Wicks among the team of composers recognised alongside Adam Sofo, Brontë Horder, Cassie To, David Bruggemann, Lydia Davies, Mitch Stewart and Rory Chenoweth.

Red Dog and Two Hands composer recognised

Red Dog composer Cezary Skubiszewski received the award for Distinguished Services to the Australian Screen in recognition of his incredible body of work spanning more than 30 years.

Cezary Skubiszewski recieved the 2026 award for Distinguished Services to the Screen. (APRA AMCOS: Tomek Sikora)

Australian documentary Sentient won Best Music for a Documentary, recognising Helena Czajka's score.

Christopher Larkin took out Best Music for a Video Game or Other Interactive Media for his work on the highly anticipated Hollow Knight: Silksong.

Finn Clarke was named Emerging Screen Composer of the Year, following his 2025 win for Best Soundtrack Album.

The charming rom-com Addition won the highly contested Feature Film Score of the Year award for composers Piers Burbrook de Vere and first-time winner Rose Mackenzie-Peterson.

First-time winners were also recognised across several categories, with Lego — Project Vehicles winning Best Music for an  for Benjamin Lam, Trading Cards earning Best Music for a Short Film for Nicholas Gardiner, and The Witchy Girls (Episode 6) taking out Best Music for a Television Comedy for Georgina Darvidis, Matthew Sheers and Peter Corrigan.

Screen composers make statement about AI

During the ceremony, composers, musicians and industry leaders wore special badges in solidarity, opposing the use of Australian creative work to train AI without creators’ consent, licensing or fair compensation.

The government is currently considering whether to allow technology companies to use copyrighted material to train AI models.

The initiative was spearheaded by composer Antony Partos and the Australian Guild of Screen Composers.

One participating composer was Nigel Westlake, best known for his score for the Australian classic Babe.

Westlake discovered that 180 of his compositions had been included in AI training datasets without his knowledge.

Among them was a requiem he wrote after the death of his son in a road rage incident in 2008.

“Our creative industries cannot become collateral damage in the race to attract AI investment,” Partos said in a statement.

Nigel Westlake is among the composers opposing technology companies using their work to train AI models without consent. (Supplied: APRA AMCOS)

Veltheim leads orchestra for final year as music director

The ceremony took place in Brisbane's Fortitude Music Hall on October 28, 2026, and was hosted by Rob Collins, Claudia Karvan OAM and Ayesha Madon.

In his final year as music director, composer and performer Erkki Veltheim led a live orchestra through selections from nominated scores.

The Screen Music Awards, presented by APRA AMCOS in collaboration with the Australian Guild of Screen Composers (AGSC), celebrate excellence and innovation in screen composition.

World.title: Defence official claimed she flagged plans for social media ban request
World.content:
A senior Department of Defence official said she had approval from a government minister to try to block the public release of her evidence to a parliamentary hearing due to concerns about "vile" social media commentary.

Deputy secretary Celia Perkins said she had approval from Assistant Defence Minister Peter Khalil when she told a parliamentary committee hearing last month that she did not "consent" to her evidence appearing on social media.

The request was swiftly rejected by committee chair senator Jess Collins, on advice from parliamentary officials.

"It is our right as senators and members of the public to disseminate the evidence that is provided by the witnesses today in the manner in which we see fit," Senator Collins said.

Jess Collins rejected the request on advice from the Senate Clerk. (ABC News: Callum Flinn)

Emails between Defence officials ahead of the hearing, obtained by the ABC through a Freedom of Information (FOI) request, reveal Ms Perkins told colleagues she raised her plans to make the statement with Mr Khalil and Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles's office two days before the hearing.

"(Department secretary Meghan Quinn) is fully supportive, as is AMINDEF. I discussed today in a meeting with AMINDEF and staff from DPMO and his office," she wrote in the email.

"I'll pass the opening statement to them tomorrow."

AMINDEF refers to Mr Khalil, and DPMO is the Deputy Prime Minister's office.

The ABC understands Mr Marles's office provided no input to Ms Perkins's statement before she made it. Comment has been sought from both Mr Khalil and Mr Marles.

The senior defence official claims Peter Khalil approved her plans to request that videos of hearings not be posted on social media. (ABC News: Ian Cutmore)

During a Senate estimates hearing this week, Senate Clerk Richard Pye was asked about the advice he provided the committee after Ms Perkins request.

"It's absolutely not something that a witness can do," he said.

"It was profoundly unhelpful, I thought on the day, for the matter to be raised in that way without any notice to anybody, not through the secretariat, not to the chair and not to other members of the committee."

But he added that there were genuine concerns about the effect of footage from committee hearings on social media.

"This is not to minimise the fact that there are some people who have been very bruised by their experiences before Senate and House committees and the treatment of footage that has come out of those," he said.

Concerns over 'vile' commentary

The emails reveal some of the reasoning Ms Perkins put forward before her request.

In an email to Ms Quinn a week before the hearing, she raised her plans.

"You may recall after the last hearing we had some unpleasant social media posts and reactions," she wrote.

"I also want to test with you this idea: I'd like to add an explicit statement that the Defence witnesses appearing do not consent to our evidence being reproduced in edited format on social media platforms."

She said the main argument was that she had to maintain a "safe workplace" for Defence staff, and that online commentary could be "distressing".

"Social media posts using footage from previous hearings in edited and embellished formats had generated significant vile, personal commentary that was distressing for staff and invited online bullying," she said.

Labor MPs deploy AI to tackle online abuse Labor MPs are turning to an AI tool to strip hundreds of thousands of abusive comments and threats from their pages but want social media companies to take responsibility.

Ms Perkins also suggested the posts could raise security concerns, including assisting foreign espionage.

"As senior leaders in Defence — we actively discourage security clearance holders from a social media presence that identifies us and our roles — and these post (sic), designed to invite outraged responses, increase the personal risk from malign online actors, including cyber and foreign intelligence threats."

While Ms Perkins's request was immediately shut down, the Secretaries Board, made up of all federal government departmental secretaries, soon after took up the issue, suggesting new standards were needed to guide the use of evidence given to parliamentary hearings online.

This week Steven Kennedy, head of the Department of Prime Minister and Cabinet, told estimates he did not support censoring footage, but did have concerns.

"Conduct that demeans, intimidates, humiliates or personally targets witnesses is inconsistent with the behaviour code for parliamentarians," he said.

World.title: At least 64 dead as high-speed trains collide in Spain
World.content:
At least 64 people have died in a crash between two trains in central Spain, local officials have confirmed.

The high-speed trains collided near the city of Toledo in the La Castilla Mancha region on Wednesday morning, shutting down the line connecting ‌Madrid to the southern Andalusia ‌region, rail operator ‌Adif said.

"Traffic ‌on the Madrid-Andalusia ‌high-speed rail line ‌has been suspended following ‌a rear-end ‌collision between two trains," it said on X.

397 passengers were on board the Renfe train and 147 passengers on the IRYO train at the time of the crash. (AP Photo: Manu Fernandez)

Regional spokesperson Esther Padilla previously said the death toll was "very likely" to increase.

She said 147 people were on board the Iryo train and 397 were on the Renfe train, and that several carriages had plunged down an embankment.

An official briefed on the accident shared that an Iryo express train was stopped at a signal when it was struck by a Renfe high speed train.

An aerial view of the crash site after two high-speed trains collided on Wednesday morning. (Guardia Civil via Reuters)

Ms Padilla told state broadcaster TVE that one train ran into the tail of the other, which was stationary, knocking two of its carriages off the track.

She said it was not known what had caused the crash, which occurred on a flat stretch between the towns of Urda and Los Yébenes.

Two cars were derailed in the crash. (AP: Juanma Jimenez/Europa Press)

Spanish Health Minister Mónica García told TVE that emergency workers were focusing on rescuing survivors and bodies from the two most damaged cars, and that injured passengers were being sent to different hospitals in the area.

"It was a high-speed impact, so we are expecting this to be a tragedy," she said.

Urda Mayor Manuel Galán told TVE that civil protection authorities had asked that the town prepare a sports pavilion to attend to injured passengers.

A military emergency brigade was deployed to help emergency services, firefighters and police to the crash site.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez cancelled his agenda for Wednesday to focus on the crash. In a post on social media he said he was “dismayed by the serious train accident in Toledo.”

In January this year 45 people were killed and 120 others injured when an Iryo train derailed at high speed into the path of an oncoming train run by Renfe AVE, near Adamuz in southern Spain.

Two high-speed trains collided near Adamuz in January this year. (Reuters: Ana Beltran)

The accident is still under investigation. A preliminary report by Spain's Civil Guard in February pointed to defects in the track, rail or weld between two sections of track as the main hypothesis for the accident, but kept seven other theories open.

Reuters/AP/ABC News

World.title: Hundreds stranded as 'cruise for life' operator goes bust over fuel costs
World.content:
Around 200 passengers who paid to live on a cruise ship while travelling the world have been abruptly left in a Cambodian port after the company ran out of money.

US-based operator Villa Vie Residences, which markets its residency programs as luxury alternatives to current retirement options, announced it had suspended operations after two and a half years of continuous travel.

In a statement on Tuesday, local time, Villa Vie blamed the "extraordinary" fuel costs following the Iran war for halting operations.

Passengers were given just seven hours to pack their bags and leave during a scheduled stop in the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville, according to Long Dimanche, deputy governor of Preah Sihanouk province.

He said in a statement 203 guests and 156 crew had arrived aboard the Bahamas-flagged ship from Thailand on October 23 and had been due to go on to Vietnam.

"The sudden order to disembark has left many retirees and remote workers homeless thousands of miles from their home countries," he said.

Some passengers took flights out while others remained in the city, he said, adding that the ship itself was due to refuel and leave on October 31.

An ocean-view villa inside Villa Vie's residential cruise ship. (Supplied: Villa Vie Residences)

Inside Villa Vie's 'continuous' voyage

Passengers aboard the 200-metre-long Odyssey cruise ship, equipped with a 24/7 medical centre, spa and fully contained villas, are sold on a "worry-free" life at sea.

Residents have the option to buy or rent rooms for a holiday or for life, with basic cabins starting at about $85,000.

The cruise departed Northern Ireland in October 2024 for a continuous voyage; some passengers sold everything they had to pay for it.

At the beginning of this year, the residential cruise ship dropped anchor at multiple ports on Australia's east coast.

Randy Cassingham, a passenger on board who runs a cruise blog, wrote that the disembarkation order followed a "cascade of problems".

Under a post entitled "Abandon Ship!", he said its Belfast launch was delayed by four months, while the ship never reached its capacity of 650 residents, peaking at around 350.

Loading Instagram content

He said it was not a "luxury" ship but affordable until the company started "begging for money".

Villa Vie said in its statement that per-cabin monthly fuel expenses had gone from an average of $1,800 to an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia.

"The company cannot simply pass increases of that scale on to residents, and the resulting shortfall has placed its current operating model under unsustainable financial pressure," it said.

Mr Cassingham accused the company of doing "absolutely nothing to help" stranded passengers.

Villa Vie said it was working to find temporary accommodation for residents.

"Villa Vie Residences recognises that this is a difficult and disruptive period for residents, crew members and employees, and is working to support those affected as plans develop," it said.

AFP

World.title: 'We haven't got it right': Collingwood to review AFLW
World.content:
Collingwood has pledged to thoroughly review the wreckage of its AFLW program, admitting "we haven't got it right".

The day after announcing that women's coach, Sam Wright, is about to leave, the Magpies said they would bring in a consultant to help with the strategic review.

Collingwood is a perennial AFLW under-achiever, winning only one game so far this season to be second-last.

Including the last two seasons, their record is five wins and 29 losses.

With Wright about to leave and captain Ruby Schleicher about to return home to WA, there are also reports of a mass player exodus once the season ends.

Collingwood AFLW coach to step down Coach Sam Wright becomes another casualty in Collingwood's horror season, saying he will leave the AFLW club.

"Our AFLW program is an integral part of Collingwood, and we are committed to ensuring it is positioned for sustained success," president Barry Carp said in a club statement.

"The board, together with the executive team, acknowledges that we haven't got it right — we take responsibility for that and are committed to getting better, both on and off the field.

"Engaging an expert outside Collingwood is important for us to provide a broader perspective, challenge our existing approaches and identify what needs to improve or change."

He added the expert would work with their AFLW sub-committee to ensure the women are set up for long-term success.

Collingwood's woeful AFLW season Former AFLW player and coach Lauren Arnell has criticised the standard of Collingwood, while emphasising the responsibility of coaches to "put on a show" to grow the game.

"We have a responsibility to our players, coaches, staff, members, supporters and the wider game to listen to feedback and be prepared to make meaningful, considered changes across the club to build a stronger AFLW program for everyone at Collingwood," Carp said.

Wright will coach Collingwood for the last time on Sunday against Essendon at Windy Hill. It will also be Bombers coach Natalie Wood's last game.

St Kilda are also looking for a new AFLW coach after Nick Dal Santo's departure, and expansion team Tasmania are the fourth team in the market.

World.title: Sex offender on the run after escaping from gym
World.content:
Authorities are searching for a sex offender who escaped government custody while at a gym in Ipswich, west of Brisbane.

Denzel Dynevor, 25, was with Forensic Disability Services officers at a gym in Eastern Heights when he ran out an emergency exit at about 11:20 on Tuesday morning.

He has not been seen since.

Members of the public are being asked not to approach the man.

Dynevor is described as a First Nations man about 160 centimetres tall with brown eyes and dark brown hair.

He was last seen wearing a black singlet, blue shorts and black shoes, but could have since changed his clothing.

Anyone who may have seen him, or has any information that may assist police, is being urged to immediately contact police.

Forensic Disability Services Queensland manages adults who have been detained on forensic orders.

World.title: ‘Twisted mass of metal’: At least 64 dead in ‘apocalyptic’ high-speed train crash in Spain
World.content:
Breaking WorldEuropeTragedy ‘Twisted mass of metal’: At least 64 dead in ‘apocalyptic’ high-speed train crash in Spain David Crowe Updated October 29, 2026 — 2:05am ,first published 8:51pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. London: Two trains have collided on a high-speed line in central Spain in a crash that has killed at least 64 people and injured dozens of others. One train crashed into the rear of the other just after 9am local time on the line south of Madrid, forcing at least three carriages off the tracks and down an embankment. Emergency services work at the scene of a collision between two trains in Urda, Spain. AP Photo/Manu Fernandez One passenger told Spanish newspaper El Mundo the scene was “apocalyptic” because of the scale of the destruction, as medics removed bodies from the smashed carriages. The greatest damage appeared to be to the rear three carriages of an Iryo train travelling south, which was rammed from behind by a Renfe AVE train also heading south from Madrid.



“It’s hard to imagine anyone is still alive in those three cars,” passenger Sebastián Herrero, a 46-year-old from Seville, told El Mundo. “It’s just a twisted mass of metal. It’s as if a bomb had gone off.” Herrero told the newspaper he was travelling in car 7 of the Iryo train that had departed Madrid for the south. Of the nine carriages, he said, four or five were derailed when the Renfe AVE crashed into the Iryo train. “It’s a perfectly straight stretch of track,” he said. “It’s impossible to understand how there was no warning.” Spain’s Transport Minister Óscar Puente said that the accident was caused by what he called the “inexplicable” order from a central command centre for Spain’s trains after a security system had failed. He said the train engineers were not to blame.



Puente said that at 8:30am the security system on a stretch of 63 kilometres stopped working due to a computer malfunction, causing all trains on that stretch to stop. But the central command told the RENFE train to start running again without any speed restrictions, and it ended up colliding with the stopped IRYO train at 8:53am. Puente said that the train should never have been told to start moving again since there was still a “stop signal” active that line. And if it had, at least it should have been told to go at reduced speed. Puente said they were still studying information to see how fast the train was going, but it could have been at 200km/h for that stretch of the track. “I am not attributing responsibility to anyone, I am just stating the facts,” Puente said. Passenger, Jesús Jerónimo, 54, told newspaper El Pais that he was travelling in car 2 of the Renfe AVE service heading south to Seville. “I felt a really brutal acceleration and I slammed into the seat in front of me,” he said.



Early reports indicate the Renfe AVE train had 397 passengers and the Iryo had 147 passengers. While early reports put the death toll at 10 and then 30 people, the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha later said there at least 64 dead. The update was issued shortly before 2pm on Wednesday (just before midnight in Australia). The president of Castilla-La Mancha, Emiliano García-Page, said more than 80 people were injured, 50 of them seriously. View post on X A young woman on the Iryo train, Eduarda, told news outlet Cadena Ser that some passengers had been trapped beneath the trains. “There were many people screaming because they couldn’t get out – it was horrific,” she said.



She told the news outlet, in an account also published by El Espanol, that the Iryo train she was on was in motion at the time of the crash. Spanish media reported that the Iryo train had sent an alert to the rail control centre saying it was stopped due to a failure of the LZB track signalling system, leading to speculation it was at a standstill when struck by the Renfe AVE train. Spain’s rail system operator ADIF said the crash occurred on Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo. Rail service was suspended between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia. The Castilla La Mancha regional government confirmed the death toll had risen to 30 people, after an earlier warning by spokeswoman Esther Padilla that the “number will surely rise”. Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez wrote on X that he was “shocked” by the “serious train accident”.



View post on X “Emergency services are working on the ground to assist those affected and ensure their safety, in coordination with all the involved administrations,” he wrote. “My affection, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families.” The collision comes nine months after an accident between high-speed trains belonging to the same operators on the same line. In January, 45 people died in southern Spain when a train jumped the track and hit an oncoming train. The crash was the deadliest in Spain since a 2013 crash that killed 80 people.



The crash on Wednesday could be worse than the January tragedy, El Pais reported. “The government confirms that there are many dead in the train accident and points to human error,” the newspaper said. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, who has clashed at times with Sanchez on migration policy, sent a message of sympathy to Spain. “In these such difficult hours, the Italian Government is close to Spain and the Spanish people for the dramatic railway accident that occurred near Toledo,” she wrote on X.



“My thoughts and those of our entire government go to the families of the victims, to the injured, and to all those who are working tirelessly in the rescue operations.” French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen were among the other world leaders to post tributes to the victims on X. World.title: James Hird joins AI firm after missing out on Essendon coaching job
World.content:
TechnologyAI James Hird joins AI firm after missing out on Essendon coaching job David Swan October 29, 2026 — 12:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. AFL great James Hird has taken a full-time job with a Melbourne artificial intelligence company – two months after Essendon chose Mark McVeigh over him as senior coach. The Brownlow medallist will run a new sports division at Affinda, which is backed by Toll founder and former Essendon chairman Paul Little. Hird will keep his role as director of coaching at VFL club Port Melbourne, which he does after hours and on weekends. James Hird has been appointed global head of Affinda Sports, an Australian AI company. Joe Armao “This is very much a full-time role, but I will continue my role with Port because it’s something I love,” Hird told this masthead. “I was disappointed, you know, thoroughly disappointed,” he said of missing out on the Essendon job. After the decision, he sat down with Affinda chief executive Tim Toner. “I was sort of like, well, why don’t we create something in sport that hasn’t really been done.”



Founded in Melbourne in 2012 and run by Toner and his brother, Ben, Affinda sells software that pulls information out of documents, as well as software that law firms use to compare contracts. Toner said it had customers in 85 countries. It was valued at $220 million after raising $25 million in February, The Australian Financial Review reported. Little put $15 million into that round. Ex-Essendon president Paul Little says there is already some optimism in the business community. Getty Asked whether Little had a role in his hiring, Hird said: “Not so much bringing me in, but when I spoke to Paul maybe a year ago about AI and sport, he mentioned that, would I like an introduction to Tim.” Hird said he “put my hand up and said yes, please”. Little became Essendon chairman in 2013 and backed Hird through the 12-month ban he accepted from the AFL that year under a settlement over the club’s supplements program.



Asked why clubs should trust him with their performance data given the supplements saga, Hird pointed to security. “The data is kept on their servers and with them, we’re providing a tool that they can use within their club and within their safety and within their security,” he said. (Left to right) James Hird and Affinda CEO Tim Toner. Joe Armao Toner said Affinda already had “multiple customers” among sporting organisations in Australia and overseas, but would not name them. “In the sporting world, there’s a lot more sensitivity around disclosure, particularly around what they’re doing with AI,” he said. He said sporting organisations had been approaching the company for about 18 months. Affinda initially paid them less attention than its corporate clients, he said, until bigger and better-known clubs started asking what AI could do. Hird said he had been using AI at a basic level for about 18 months, in his coaching and in analysing games for television. As he and Toner talked, he said, the possible uses grew. “The use cases just sort of bounced from five to 50.”



Related Article Analysis

AFL 2026 ‘What people don’t realise’: Candid Hird opens up after missing out on the Essendon coaching role Clubs already collect GPS data, Champion Data statistics, gym results, daily wellness data and training and match vision, he said, and AI could help bring it together. He recalled 8am meetings as a coach, deciding which players could train and how much: “Can they have 100 kicks, can they have 20 kicks, can they have 50 kicks.” It could help on game day, too. “In a coaches’ box, it’s very chaotic, and if you can reduce some of that chaos and some of that noise, there’s no doubt you can think more clearly as a coach,” he said. When Hird started playing, he said, “the only data you got was your kicks, marks and handballs”. He described Affinda’s work as “complementary” to Champion Data, the AFL’s official statistics provider, which is 49 per cent owned by the league. Toner said clubs that moved early would pull ahead. “I think what we’ll see in the next 12 months is the first mover advantage is real,” he said. “I think there’ll be a lot of clubs and teams playing catch-up if they’re not really at the front of that wave.” The Business Briefing newsletter delivers major stories, exclusive coverage and expert opinion. World.title: The Israeli elections have produced a deadlock. What happens now?
World.content:
WorldMiddle EastIsraeli-Palestinian conflict The Israeli elections have produced a deadlock. What happens now? Matthew Knott Updated October 28, 2026 — 9:45pm ,first published 9:31pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Follow our live coverage of the Israeli election here. The Israeli elections have, at least for now, produced a deadlock, with neither the pro nor anti-Benjamin Netanyahu blocs able to form a majority in their own right. The latest results show Netanyahu’s bloc winning 54, the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot on 47 and the Arab parties on 19. The key number is to reach at least a 61-seat parliamentary majority, although it is technically possible to govern in minority. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressing his supporters after the polls closed. Getty Images What happens once the votes are counted?



Israeli President Isaac Herzog will consult all the party leaders to inquire who they could support as prime minister. Based on these discussions, he will give one of the party leaders a chance to form a governing coalition. This is expected to be Netanyahu, given his Likud party has easily won the most seats in the Knesset, the Israeli parliament. This is not always the case, however. In 2021 Naftali Bennett became prime minister despite winning only seven seats in the elections. The president’s chosen candidate will have 28 days, and an additional 14 days if they ask for it, to form a government. If not, then someone else will be given a chance. Why is it so complicated? Seats in the Knesset, are allocated by proportional representation to national party lists, with parties needing to pass a threshold of 3.25 per cent of the national vote to secure seats. About a dozen parties are widely thought to have a chance of crossing the threshold, so the final tally and seat allocation will take time. People embrace and wave flags amid falling confetti as they celebrate early exit poll results for Israel’s general election in Tel Aviv. AP



What are the possible outcomes? Netanyahu convinces at least one of the opposition parties to cross over and support his government, allowing him to reach a parliamentary majority. For example, he could ask Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party to serve in a national unity government alongside him. He could also look to find potential defectors from within the opposition parties to help him reach a majority. Eisenkot tries to form a minority government reliant on the support of the Arab parties. Given his bloc has fallen far short of a majority, this would create an unwieldy government prone to collapse. The positions of the Joint List – a collection of far-left Arab parties including the remnants of the Communist Party – on the Israeli-Palestinian issue in particular sit well outside the mainstream of Jewish public opinion in Israel. If no one can command a majority then Israelis will have to return to vote again. Netanyahu will remain in power as prime minister in the interim period. Herzog, however, has said he is not keen to put Israelis through another round of elections. What are the key players saying? In his speech to supporters after polling booths closed, Netanyahu said: “The right-wing bloc has a clear, decisive majority among the Zionist public, among the Jewish public and all those who support the state.” For this reason, he said Israelis “need a right-wing, national, strong government. That’s what has to be done.” As yet, he has shown no sign of abandoning his ultra-Orthodox and far-right coalition members.



Yair Golan, leader of The Democrats party. Bloomberg Left-wing Democrats leader Yair Golan implored the opposition to form a government with the support of the Arab parties. “Anyone who tries to erase the voices of Arab citizens is surrendering to Netanyahu and giving up on Israel,” he said on social media. “We have a majority. We have responsibility. And we have an opportunity to form a government of change in partnership with Israel’s Arab citizens. A government that will serve all Israeli citizens.” Eisenkot vowed to do “everything to fulfil the people’s will,” saying that calling another election would be “a mistake”.



Gadi Eisenkot celebrating the exit polls with supporters in Tel Aviv. AP He said he would “do everything in my power to build a Zionist, pro-IDF [Israeli Defence Forces] enlistment government”, while warning Netanyahu not to play with national security for political gain. United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas said: “If we join a government of change, we will be able to see substantial changes, not just empty talk.” How would another round of elections work? What happened in the 2019-2022 period could be a guide to Israel’s immediate future.



When Israelis voted in April 2019, Netanyahu’s Likud party and the Blue and White alliance led by former military chief Benny Gantz finished tied on 35 seats each. Neither could form a majority so Netanyahu remained as prime minister until Israelis voted again in September. Loading Again, the results were virtually a tie, so Israelis headed to the polls again in March 2020. This time Gantz agreed to a power-sharing arrangement, but he was never able to take up the prime ministership because the Knesset was dissolved before he had a chance. At the March 2021 elections, Likud was again easily the biggest party but opposition leaders Yair Lapid and Naftali Bennett cobbled together a governing majority with the support of the United Arab List. That government lasted for around 18 months before it fell apart, triggering new elections and Netanyahu’s return to power. World.title: The late-night letter that blindsided Melbourne principals over classroom support
World.content:
PoliticsVictoriaEducation The late-night letter that blindsided Melbourne principals over classroom support Caroline Schelle Updated October 28, 2026 — 9:24pm ,first published 7:50pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Principals and parents are reeling from a state government decision to cut $3400 a year in disability support per eligible student in mainstream schools. In a letter to state school leaders late on Tuesday, just six weeks before the end of the school year, the state government announced plans for a major shake-up to taxpayer-funded disability support provided in classrooms. Mainstream schools will receive less funding to cater for children with disabilities. Getty Images The letter spells out changes to tighten criteria for disability support, a 2.5 per cent drop in “student-level funding rates”, and a reduction of $850 a term, per student “in mainstream schools only” from next year. The cuts are designed to curtail the ballooning cost of providing disability support in the state’s schools, which has risen by 16 per cent a year since 2021.



“This is unsustainable, and it risks affecting support for children who need it most,” a government spokesperson said. Related Article Exclusive

School funding A Melbourne school classified 90% of students as having ‘extensive’ needs. Now it could face a $23m bill The changes will apply from term 1 next year. The state government said the changes would mean more money for the students who needed it most. A government spokesperson said there was no overall cut to school funding, which would be used for explicit teaching reforms, targeted literacy and numeracy interventions, tutoring and services to help students remain engaged in education.



The letter said overall funding for disability inclusion would grow to $2.2 billion in 2029. The criteria for students receiving disability support will also change, with new definitions of academic performance and benchmarks for being able to do tasks independently. The government has not clarified what criteria would be used to determine which students are eligible for taxpayer-funded supports. The move shocked teachers and principals, who said they weren’t consulted, and has devastated families of students with disabilities. Melbourne mother Christine, whose 16-year-old son has autism, a mild intellectual disability and ADHD, said the extra help her son received in school was vital.



“For families like mine, these cuts would be life-changing,” she said. Her son is in a mainstream secondary school, where he has had the most success as a student. “I genuinely believe that without disability inclusion support from the beginning, my son may have fallen out of the school system altogether,” she said. Related Article Exclusive

Schools ‘Over the line’: The leaked memo linked to Melbourne school’s $23m disability funding scandal “We tried a specialist school environment, which worked for a while, but his biggest successes came through mainstream schooling, where he had the opportunity to experience and participate in the wider world.”



The support from his aides was critical in helping him to navigate school, and stay connected to learning, she said. “With teachers already stretched managing diverse needs in large classrooms, this support is not a luxury – it is essential,” she said. Association for Children with a Disability chief executive Karen Dimmock said families were devastated by the new criteria, which she said would mean less money for schools to spend supporting students with disabilities. “The majority of this funding is spent on individual education support staff,” she said. “This is an incredible workforce that does everything from help children with physical access to those with low vision or are hard of hearing, or helping students to maintain focus.” The disability advocate said it was a lot of money for schools to lose.



“This is just devastating,” Dimmock said. “The difference this funding makes to a child every day in the classroom is invaluable.” Australian Principals Federation president Andrew Cock said a student’s disability didn’t become less complex because the department changed its funding formula. “The support they need remains, regardless of what the budget says,” he said. He said schools couldn’t deliver more inclusive education with less funding.



“The expectations on principals haven’t changed, the needs of students haven’t changed, but the funding available to support them is being reduced,” he said. Principals were left to manage the consequences of these decisions, without meaningful consultation from the government, he said. “Funding decisions must be driven by student need, not simply financial targets.” The Australian Education Union said the decision should be reversed. “The … decision to cut funding for children with disability attending public schools is a disgrace and must be reversed immediately,” Victorian branch president Justin Mullaly said.



He said it would pull support from one in every six students who were receiving disability inclusion support at a public school. “I would like to know how the government proposes that the affected students are going to get the support they need to learn with this support pulled out from under them.” Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

Brisbane motorists are being urged not only to drive safely on Halloween – Bicycle Queensland wants them to not drive at all, to give children a rare chance to retake the streets.

Bicycle Queensland chief executive Dr Matthew Burke said Halloween, which this year falls on a Saturday, was not the time to drive through the suburbs.

“It’s one of the few nights of the year when children are allowed to take over neighbourhoods, running and riding between homes,” he said.

Pedal Party, which organises rides through Brisbane’s streets, is joining with Bicycle Queensland for a Halloween-themed event in 2026.

Burke said children once played in Australian streets every single night, not just on Halloween.

World.title: Rubbing the Australian XI up the wrong way
World.content:
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Regarding the overnight Test action, Don Bain of Port Macquarie isn’t sure “whether the sports reporter was being intentionally punny when he opined that crowd commentary at Newlands, home of sandpapergate, might be ‘abrasive’.” Such wordsmithery can occur in all codes. Granny just heard noted rugby league intellect Denan Kemp accuse the management of NRL halfback Sam Walker of “Playing chicken with the Roosters.”

Still (kinda) in Cape Town, Richard Ansoul of Tanunda (SA) recalls that “as an impecunious student, our daughter, Claire Ansoul, won a Herald competition to name a themed dream team of Australian cricketers (all left-handers, Masons etc) in season 1987-88. As winner, she received a double pass to the Tests. Her motley team consisted of men who had all been filmed on the field, picking their nose. Look out for her in the stands at Newlands.”

David Baird of Burradoo is feeling pretty ticked-off right now: “I’d like to see a downtick in the word ‘uptick’. Ironically, I’d like to see an uptick in the word ‘increase’.”

“Gail Grogan (C8) brought back fond memories of reading the Herald aboard the train,” writes Lawford Steele of Scarborough. “Gail said ‘It was awkward folding the pages’ and I remembered being complimented on my skill at being able to flick, turn and fold the broadsheet Herald to the required size without upsetting adjacent commuters.”

Merran Loewenthal of Vienna, Austria, has more on the Halloween alternative (Martin Luther Day) for David Morrison (C8): “In Germany and Austria and most Catholic European countries, November 1, All Saints’ Day, is a national holiday, if you happen to be of the Lutheran faith, you are also entitled to enjoy a holiday on Reformationstag, October 31!”

The crash on Wednesday could be worse than the January tragedy, El Pais reported. “The government confirms that there are many dead in the train accident and points to human error,” the newspaper said. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, who has clashed at times with Sanchez on migration policy, sent a message of sympathy to Spain. “In these such difficult hours, the Italian Government is close to Spain and the Spanish people for the dramatic railway accident that occurred near Toledo,” she wrote on X.



“My thoughts and those of our entire government go to the families of the victims, to the injured, and to all those who are working tirelessly in the rescue operations.” French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen were among the other world leaders to post tributes to the victims on X. World.title: James Hird joins AI firm after missing out on Essendon coaching job
World.content:
TechnologyAI James Hird joins AI firm after missing out on Essendon coaching job David Swan October 29, 2026 — 12:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.
